data.text:
# Y4VS8 — Rich text removed: plan and design ruling

## Ruling: `PenTextContent` is deleted, not narrowed

2.17's `TextContent = StringOrVariable` is *exactly* `PenValue<String>`. Keeping
`PenTextContent` would leave a one-case enum whose sole payload is `PenValue<String>` —
pure indirection. `TextData.content`, `NoteData.content`, `PromptData.content` and
`ContextData.content` all become `PenValue<String>?`, which is the same type every other
string-or-variable property on those nodes already uses (`fontFamily`, `fontWeight`,
`fontStyle`), so text content now flows through `PenVariableResolver.resolve(_:from:)`
with no bespoke path.

`PenTextSpan` is deleted. `PenTextStyle` is deleted too: it is dead code (no reference
anywhere in Sources or Tests) whose docstring says it exists to be "shared by text nodes
and rich text spans" — the sharing is what is going away. That empties
`Models/PenTextStyle.swift`, so the file goes.

## Decode behaviour for an array

`PenValue<String>` throws `DecodingError.typeMismatch` on a JSON array. That is the right
answer: a 2.17 document carrying styled runs is malformed, and 2.8–2.10 documents are
rewritten by the version gate before the decoder ever sees them.

## Migration rule

`PenRichTextMigrationRule` keys on the *shape* (`content` is an array), not the node type,
because a `ref` node's `descendants` override has no `type` key. The 2.9 schema uses
`content` only for `TextContent` (text, note, prompt, context), so this is unambiguous.

Concatenation, in order, no separator; a run whose `content` is missing or not a string
contributes nothing. One `.warning` / `.migration` diagnostic per node carrying the id.

## Known wrinkle: a `$` at the head of a multi-run concatenation

A single run `{"content": "$headline"}` concatenates to `"$headline"` and decodes to
`.variable("headline")` — correct by accident and worth keeping. But runs
`["$price", " today"]` concatenate to `"$price today"`, which decodes as
`.variable("price today")`. The format has no `$` escape, so there is no fix at this
layer; `PenVariableResolver` already restores an undefined `$name` as a literal, so it
degrades to the right pixels.

## GoldenParity finding

`parser-text-content`'s golden differs from the 2.9 original in three places, only one of
which is rich text:

1. `rich-text`'s `content` — Pen drops it, we keep "Bold Italic Colored". Deliberate: the override.
2. Pen writes `fontFamily: "Inter"` on the three text nodes that had none — the document
   default font, same class of save-time stamping as the existing `fontWeight: "normal"` rule.
3. Pen omits `textGrowth: "auto"` where the original wrote it — `auto` is the default.

(2) and (3) are general Pen save behaviour, not rich text, so they go in
`GoldenParity.normalized(_:)` next to the `fontWeight` rule rather than into the
rich-text override. The override then asserts exactly the content difference and nothing
else, so any other drift still fails.

## icon_font becomes icon — done

Renamed the `icon_font` node type to `icon` (keys `iconFontFamily`→`library`,
`iconFontName`→`icon`; `weight`/`fill` unchanged) end to end: model
(`PenNode.Kind.icon(IconData)`, `NodeType.icon = "icon"`), a new
`PenIconMigrationRule` (registered first in `PenLegacyMigrator.rules`, no
diagnostic — nothing is discarded), and every consumer (layout, variable
resolution, import prefixing, React emitter, editing/CRDT sync, renderer).
Font machinery (`PenIconFontRegistry`, codepoint tables, `PenIconFontRenderer`)
kept its name per the brief — it's genuinely about fonts, not the node.

New/renamed files:
- Sources/Woodcase/Migration/PenIconMigrationRule.swift (new)
- Sources/Woodcase/Models/PenNode+IconData.swift (was PenNode+IconFontData.swift)
- Sources/Woodcase/CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Icon.swift (was ReactEmitter+IconFont.swift; emitIconFont→emitIcon — it emits SVG icon components, not font glyphs, so it's node machinery, not font machinery)
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenIconMigrationRuleTests.swift (new, 7 tests)

Golden parity: "parser-icon-font" enabled and passing. MAE unchanged (5.27,
same as before — icon rendering pixels don't move). React emitter output is
byte-identical (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 touched zero .golden files) — confirmed pure
rename, no behavior change.

CRDT property paths renamed too: "kind.iconFontName"/"kind.iconFontFamily" →
"kind.icon"/"kind.library" in PropertyDiff.swift and
CRDTDocument+PropertyCodec.swift, to stay consistent with the renamed Swift
properties. No test hardcoded the old strings, so this was safe, but it's a
wire-visible rename for any external CRDT client of Woodcase's editing layer
that isn't in this repo (Penumbra) — flagging in case Penumbra's editing UI
references those property-path strings directly.

Full suite green (1509 tests). swiftformat clean on every file we touched;
found the shared PropertyDiff.swift already had a pre-existing
`redundantType` lint violation at line 97 unrelated to our edit — left it
alone per "edit only the icon-related lines" (confirmed on `main` it predates
this branch).

Switch statements over Kind/NodeType edited (file:line) — for the follow-up
script-node slice's case:
- Sources/Woodcase/Models/PenNode.swift:126 (decode dispatch), :193 (encode dispatch)
- Sources/Woodcase/PenLayoutEngine.swift:422, :435
- Sources/Woodcase/PenVariableResolver.swift:456

- Sources/Woodcase/CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Nodes.swift:34
- Sources/Woodcase/CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Images.swift:39

Worktree: /Users/ben/git/Woodcase/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8159d4da187cf96f

Path viewBox landed on branch worktree-agent-aedc24fcf56fe3b51.

Model: new `PenViewBox` (Friendly, own file) decoding to/from the four-element wire
array `[x, y, width, height]`; `PenNode.PathData.viewBox` is optional and
round-trips. Wired into the CRDT property codec and PropertyDiff too — without
that a `kind.viewBox` edit op would be silently dropped.

Renderer (`PenShapeBuilder.svgPath`): with no viewBox, unchanged tight-bbox
stretch. With one, translate by (-x,-y) then scale by (nodeW/w, nodeH/h)
independently; overflow is drawn unclipped (nothing clips a path today, so this
needed no renderer change beyond the transform). A viewBox with a non-positive
dimension falls back to the tight-bbox path.

Parser: Pen's compact-relative output already parsed correctly — the two new
equivalence tests (`M0 0l100 0-50 100z` == `M 0 0 L 100 0 L 50 100 Z`) were green
on first run. Criterion scB needed no code change.

React emitter: an explicit viewBox is emitted verbatim plus
`preserveAspectRatio="none" overflow="visible"`, which the observed semantics
require; with no viewBox the output is byte-identical to before, so the goldens
did not move.

FINDING for the script/shader slice (CGyxg): `viewbox-experiment.pen` does not
decode as a whole. Its document-level probe rectangle carries a `shader` fill and
`PenFill.FillType` has no `shader` case, so the decode of that one node fails the
entire document — not just that node. The `script` probe is fine (`.unknown`) and
the `line` probe is fine. The MAE test therefore filters the top-level children
down to `root` before parsing; when shader support lands, delete
`loadRootOnly()` in `PenViewBoxSnapshotTests` and parse the file directly.

FINDING for the fixtures/MAE slice: Pen's `Export(["root"], "png", …, {scale:1})`
does NOT export the frame's box. It exports the union of the frame and everything
overflowing it, so the 900x300 root frame came out 900x340 with its origin 40 px
above the frame — the green triangle's viewBox overflow. Any future re-export of a
fixture with overflow will have the same offset.

No migration rule is needed for viewBox: it is a new optional key, absent from
every 2.8-2.10 file, and nothing else about paths changed between 2.9 and 2.17.

Full suite green (1526 tests). viewbox-experiment MAE 0.0146 against a threshold
of 5.0, the same threshold the other flat-vector fixtures use.

data.text:
Flat stroke keys landed on branch `worktree-agent-a501e65b315faa7f3` (not committed).

## Shape of the change

- `PenStroke` is gone. Every strokable payload (frame, text, rectangle, ellipse, path, line, polygon) now carries the five 2.17 keys directly: `stroke: PenFills?`, `strokeWidth: PenStrokeWidth?`, `strokeLinecap: PenStrokeCap?`, `strokeLinejoin: PenStrokeJoin?`, `strokeAlignment: PenStrokeAlign?`.
- New `PenStrokable` protocol (Models/PenStrokable.swift) is the single currency for consumers — renderer, React emitter, NodeDiffer, PropertyDiff, variable resolver and import prefixer all take `some PenStrokable` / `any PenStrokable` instead of a `PenStroke?`. No view/twin struct was introduced.
- `PenStrokeThickness` → `PenStrokeWidth` (own file). `PenStrokeAlign` cases are now `inner/center/outer`; `PenStrokeCap` is `butt/round/square`. `dashPattern` and `miterAngle` deleted from the model and the renderer.
- `DeltaProperty.strokeThickness` → `.strokeWidth` (StateDelta/StateEmitter/NodeDiffer/StateDefinitionTests); the target-neutral vocabulary would otherwise name a property the model no longer has.

## Migrator

`PenStrokeMigrationRule` appended to `PenLegacyMigrator.rules`. Beyond the key renames it copies two Pen.app behaviours, because the app's own re-saves are the oracle:

1. **Defaults are omitted.** `join: "miter"`, `align: "center"` and `cap: "none"` (→ butt) are written as nothing. Without this, golden parity for both enabled fixtures fails: Pen omits `strokeLinejoin` on `uniform-stroke` and `strokeAlignment` on `per-side-stroke` / the three `render-shapes-and-fills` rectangles that were `align: "center"`.
2. **A stroke with no `fill` is dropped entirely** (shadcn.lib.pen has ~60 of these). Safe: such a stroke had no paint and neither renderer nor emitter drew anything for it.

`dashPattern` / `miterAngle` each emit a `.warning` at stage `.migration` naming the node. The paint-less drop is silent by design — nothing visible is lost, and a warning per node would bury the two that matter.

## Consequence worth knowing: the alignment default flipped

2.9's `stroke.align` defaulted to `inside`; 2.17's `strokeAlignment` defaults to `center`. `PenStrokeRenderer` and `ReactEmitter.emitStroke` now default to `.center`. No fixture regressed — every legacy stroke on disk carries an explicit `align` except one per-side stroke in `woodcase-app.pen`, and per-side rendering ignores alignment. The React emitter maps `inner` and `center` to the same inset box-shadow, so no golden moved. Recorded in DocC (PenInteroperability "Stroke Alignment Default").

## Ref overrides now merge per-key

A 2.9 descendant override carrying a whole `stroke` object replaced the base stroke wholesale; the flat keys merge independently through `PenNodePatcher`'s JSON merge. One real difference: an override whose stroke had no `fill` used to *erase* the base's paint; now it migrates to nothing and the base stroke survives. Nothing in the suite depended on the old behaviour.

## Findings for other slices

- **`layoutIncludeStroke` does not exist in Woodcase.** The brief and the design doc both name it as a consumer to port; `grep -rn layoutIncludeStroke Sources Tests` is empty, and `PenLayoutEngine.swift` has no stroke reference at all. Layout never accounted for stroke width. Whoever writes the RapidPro brief should not promise it.
- **`scripts/mae-check` is fail-open on macOS.** It uses `declare -A` under `#!/bin/bash`, which is bash 3.2 on macOS: both declarations error out, the id→baseline lookup never happens, and the script reports a bogus "regression in `settings` 5.69 -> 5.73" (that 5.69 is *ratings*' baseline) before rewriting the baseline anyway. The pre-commit hook's MAE gate is therefore not actually comparing per-id. Worth its own task.
- **`Fixtures/tmp/lucide.ttf` is needed too**, not just `icon-test.html` — the gotcha entry has been corrected.
- MAE numbers are byte-identical to the baseline; `mae-check` only reshuffled row order (parallel test writes), and that reshuffle was reverted.

## Verification

`swift test --quiet` — 1538 tests in 143 suites, all pass. `swiftformat Sources Tests --config .swiftformat --lint` is clean for every file touched except a pre-existing `redundantType` on `PropertyDiff.swift:97`, a line this change does not touch. `swift package generate-documentation --target Woodcase` raises no warning for any new symbol.

# IAh3e — Group loses layout and size

## Summary

GroupData now carries only `children`, `effects`, `blendMode` (Friendly). Removed
`width`, `height`, `layout`, `gap`, `padding`, `justifyContent`, `alignItems`.
`PenGroupMigrationRule` (new, appended to `PenLegacyMigrator.rules`) drops those
keys from a legacy `group` node, emitting one `.migration`-stage diagnostic per
node listing only the non-default ones dropped (layout "none", gap 0, padding 0,
justify/align "start", width/height "fit_content" are silent).

Ported: PenLayoutEngine (group's `extractLayoutProperties` case only — always
`.none` layout, fitContent sizing, zero gap/padding, start/start
justify/align), PenVariableResolver (two call sites, group resolves only
`effects`+`children` now), ChangeCategory.categorizeGroup (always
`.renderOnly` — only effects/blendMode remain, matching Frame's pattern of
not diffing `children`), PropertyDiff.diffGroup/allKindKeys(.group) (now
`["kind.effects","kind.blendMode"]`), CRDTDocument+PropertyCodec's group
apply/extract cases (same reduction), ReactEmitter+Frame.emitGroup (fully
rewritten: group is always `relative`, each child gets its own
`position:absolute; left; top` wrapper div, mirroring how Frame handles
`layout:"none"` — group never emits flex classes since it has no layout of
its own). PenRenderer.originalNodeSize's `.group` case removed (falls to the
existing `default: .zero`, unchanged behavior since `fixedValue` was already
always nil for a group in practice).

## Golden parity

`parser-all-node-types` appended to `GoldenParity.enabledFixtures` and passes.
Two findings not in the brief (see project doc correction block):
- The pair has **no icon_font/icon node** — the icon rename was never a
  blocker here. `withKnownIssue` for ojfp4 was NOT needed.
- The pair's `path1` node exposed a **pre-existing, unrelated** difference:
  Pen.app rewrites path geometry compact-relative on save; `geometry` is a
  raw string (`PenNode.PathData`), so the two fixtures' strings differ even
  though they describe the same path. Canonicalizing that syntax is the
  path-viewBox slice's job (`PenSVGPathParser`), explicitly out of scope
  here (DO NOT BUILD: TZv76) — absorbed with a per-pair `GoldenParity`
  override rather than a general fix.
- Also found: Pen drops an empty `children: []` from `frame`/`group` on
  save. `GoldenParity.normalized(_:)` now treats empty and absent the same
  for both node types (this affected `frame1` too, not just `group1`).

## Layout MAE

Unchanged — `blur2`/`blur3`/`blur2-no-bg`/`blur3-no-bg` print identical MAE
to before (0.0, 0.097..., 7.66, 16.51). Deliberately did **not** touch
`PenLayoutEngine.layoutAbsoluteContainer`'s `contentSize: 0` hardcode (a
latent bug: an absolute/`.none` container with `fitContent` sizing — frame
*or* group — always reports its own size as `(0,0)` regardless of children,
because `resolveContainerSize` is always called with `contentSize: 0`,
never a real union bbox). Fixing it would make a rotated group's own
bounding-box nonzero, which — per `PenRenderer.applyTransform` — changes the
rotation-centering math and *would* move the blur2/blur3-no-bg group
rotation snapshots. `layoutAbsoluteContainer` is shared with Frame's
`layout:"none"` path, so it's also outside "group-only lines" for the
PenLayoutEngine.swift DO-NOT-BUILD restriction. Flagging as a real,
pre-existing bug for a future task, not fixing here.

## React goldens

Not regenerated — none of the `.golden` fixtures (`ScreenSettings`,
`ActionButton`, `HomeCollection`, `StatCard`, `TabBar`, `PencilListItem`,
`TextInput`, `ThemeProvider`, `ScreenLab`, all from `banking.pen`) contain a
group node, so `emitGroup`'s rewrite touches none of them — `swift test`
confirms (no golden diffs).

## Suite / lint

`swift test --quiet`: 1533 tests, 142 suites, all pass.
`swiftformat . --lint`: clean on every file this task touched (one
pre-existing `redundantType` in `PropertyDiff.swift:97` is in
`diffKind`'s untouched `default:` case, not mine).

`scripts/mae-check` has a pre-existing bug: `declare: -A: invalid option`
(bash/zsh version mismatch) and its "regression" line for `settings`
(5.69 -> 5.73, within the 7.0 limit) is unrelated to groups — `banking.pen`
(source of all WebView/React golden fixtures) has zero group nodes. The
script also non-deterministically **reordered** `performance/mae-baseline.csv`
(same values, different row order) and staged it; reverted with
`git checkout -- performance/mae-baseline.csv` before finishing — did not
commit that. Did not attempt to fix the script itself (out of scope for
this leaf).

## Deviations from strict red/green

Model+source+tests were largely written together rather than as fully
separate red-then-green passes for every assertion. Two groups of tests
are worth flagging:
- Genuinely red-before/green-after: all of `PenGroupMigrationRuleTests`
  (new type), `CRDTGroupPropertyCodecTests`'s "legacy key ignored" cases,
  `PropertyDiffTests.allKindKeysGroup`, `ReactEmitterTests.groupBasic` /
  `groupNilLayoutDefaultsNone` (old `emitGroup` never produced `relative`
  alone or per-child absolute wrappers).
- Green under both old and new code (documentation/lock-in, not
  discriminating): `PenModelTests`' "ignores legacy layout keys" (Codable
  already ignores unlisted keys), the new `ChangeCategoryTests` /
  `PropertyDiffTests.diffKindGroupBlendModeOnly` group cases (old
  `categorizeGroup`/`diffGroup` already fell through to the same result
  when only `blendMode`/`effects` differed), `PenLayoutEngineTests`'
  group-absolute-positioning test (89f0187 already defaulted a group to
  `.none` layout, so this was already true before this task).

Worth a job note flag for the "docs" leaf: PenEngine.md's group row/layout
section updated here (DocC group coverage); double-check nothing else
needs a Pencil→Pen pass in that same doc when that leaf lands.

# Y4VS8 findings — rich text removed

## Shipped

`PenTextContent` and `PenTextSpan` are gone; `content` is `PenValue<String>?` on
TextData, NoteData, PromptData and ContextData. `PenTextStyle` went with them (dead
code whose stated purpose was sharing style between nodes and spans), so
`Models/PenTextStyle.swift` is deleted outright. `PenRichTextMigrationRule`
concatenates a legacy run array into one string and warns once per node.

Full suite: 1516 tests, 141 suites, green. `swiftformat . --lint` clean for every file
this slice touched (11 pre-existing errors elsewhere, verified present on 96ef1b3).

## render-text MAE moved 4.746 → 4.514

Measured with `swift test --no-parallel --filter PenRendererSmokeTests`, before and
after (stash / pop). Every other smoke fixture is unchanged to three decimals. The
number is logged, not asserted, so nothing was loosened.

It moved *down*, which is the opposite of what the brief expected, and the reference
PNG explains why: `Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-text.png` **already has no rich
text in it** — there is a blank gap where "Bold and Italic" and "Underline
Strikethrough" should be. It was exported by a Pen build that already dropped the
runs. So Woodcase was drawing bold/italic ink into empty space before, and now draws
lighter regular-weight ink into the same empty space: less mismatch, lower MAE.

The consequence for the fixtures task: re-exporting `render-text.png` from Pen.app
will make this *worse*, not better, because Pen renders nothing there and we
deliberately render the words. render-text will keep a floor of ~4.5 MAE for as long
as we keep the words. That is a decision to take knowingly, not a threshold to chase.

## GoldenParity needed two normalizations that are not rich text

Enabling `parser-text-content` surfaced two Pen save behaviours the gate task's
normalizer did not yet know about, both general rather than rich-text-specific:

1. Pen stamps its default `fontFamily` — "Inter" — on a text node that names none.
   Nodes that already name a family keep it.
2. Pen omits `textGrowth: "auto"`, which is the default.

Both went into `GoldenParity.normalized(_:)` next to the existing `fontWeight:
"normal"` rule, with "Inter" named as `GoldenParity.penDefaultFontFamily`. The
rich-text override is therefore *only* the content difference: it asserts the
migrated node is "Bold Italic Colored" and the golden's is nil, then equalizes.

## A `$` at the head of a multi-run concatenation is unrepresentable

`["$price", " today"]` concatenates to `"$price today"`, which decodes as
`.variable("price today")`. The format has no escape for a literal `$`, so there is no
better rule available at this layer. A *single* `$var` run flattens correctly to a
variable reference, and `PenVariableResolver` already restores an undefined `$name` as
literal text, so the rendered result stays right either way.

## Pre-existing bug found: the font cache poisons ~20 MAE tests at random

One `swift test` run in three fails `PenFontRenderingTests` plus every MAE test using
IBM Plex Sans, with `familyName → "SF Pro"`. `PenTextMeasurer.fontCache` (b2a13c7) is
process-wide and does not know about `TestFontRegistration`; whichever parallel test
asks for the font first caches the fallback. Not fixed here — out of slice, and it
touches shared code. Recorded in `project/gotchas.md`.

# CGyxg — Script node, shader fill and schema leftovers — findings

## Status

Both pending criteria are met:
- **2js** `viewbox-experiment` round-trips byte-stable modulo key order and fileToken —
  `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenScriptShaderRoundTripTests.swift`, both tests green.
- **FXc** Rotation pivot test passes —
  `PenTransformBuilderTests.rotationDoesNotPivotAtTopLeft()`, green **on the first run,
  against unmodified `PenTransformBuilder` code** (see the rotation-pivot finding below —
  the code was not changed).

Full suite: `swift test --quiet` → 1656 tests, 0 failures. `swiftformat --lint` clean on
every file this leaf touched (32 files: 4 new Sources, 1 new CodeGen file, 16 edited
Sources, 6 new Tests files, 3 edited Tests files, 2 project docs).

## Major finding: the rotation-pivot brief was wrong, and I did not follow it

The brief asked for a test proving `PenTransformBuilder` "rotates around the node's
top-left corner as the 2.17 schema states," and to fix it (loudly) if it doesn't.

It doesn't — `PenTransformBuilder` pivots at the rect's center, and always has. I did
**not** change it, because I measured the alternative first: swapping the pivot to
`(0,0)` and re-running `PenSnapshotTests`'s `render-transforms-and-effects` test (an
80×80 rectangle rotated 45°, checked against Pen.app's own rendered PNG) moved its MAE
from **1.12 to 10.77** against an **8.0** threshold. Center pivot is what Pen.app
actually draws. `PenRendering.md` already said "applied around each node's center
point" — that was already correct; the schema's "top-left corner" phrase describes the
*position anchor* (`PenLayoutEngine`'s rotated-bbox expansion keeps a rotated node's
declared `x`/`y` fixed as the expanded bbox's top-left), not the CG transform's pivot.

Recorded in three places:
- `PenTransformBuilderTests.rotationDoesNotPivotAtTopLeft()` — the regression test,
  with the MAE numbers in its doc comment.
- `project/2026-08-29-pen-2.17-migration.md` — a correction block under the change
  table (row 10), in place per doc practice.
- `project/gotchas.md` — a new dated entry: a schema doc comment can describe the
  position anchor, not the render pivot; check against a real Pen.app MAE fixture
  before "fixing" a renderer to match schema prose.

## Other deviations from the brief

- **GoldenParity.enabledFixtures**: did *not* append `"viewbox-experiment"` there — it
  requires both a `Fixtures/<name>.pen` (2.9) and `Fixtures/v2.17/<name>.pen` half, and
  `viewbox-experiment` has no 2.9 original. Appending it would fail
  `GoldenParityTests.enabledPairsExist(basename:)` for every fixture in the list, not
  just this one. Instead added `GoldenParity.goldenOnlyFixtures` (currently just
  `"viewbox-experiment"`) and `GoldenParity.assertCleanParse(_:)`, which asserts the
  golden parses with no node falling back to `.unknown(typeName:properties:)` — proving
  the script/shader/etc. probes in the file all decode to their typed `Kind` cases. New
  test: `GoldenParityTests.goldenOnlyFixturesParseCleanly(basename:)`.
- **TDD sequencing**: for a change this wide (new enum cases in two exhaustive
  model enums, touching ~20 consumer files with exhaustive `switch`es), true
  red-then-green per file wasn't practical inside one whole-module Swift build — the
  module doesn't compile at all until every switch has its new case. I front-loaded the
  model + consumer implementation to reach a compiling baseline, then wrote and ran the
  test suite (all green). Every new type, fill case, and node case still has its own
  test; I did not skip coverage, only reordered when in the pass it was written.
- Added `PenShaderUniform.vector` array resolution in `PenVariableResolver` and prefix
  handling in `PenImportResolver+Prefixing` for shader uniforms — brief only named the
  file for the script side, but the shader side needed the identical treatment for
  correctness (a `$`-referenced shader uniform would otherwise not resolve, and would
  not get alias-prefixed on import), so I added it at the same low cost.

## What's wrong in the brief (explicit)

1. The rotation-pivot ask (above) — asked to make a change that breaks rendering
   fidelity against real Pen.app output. Verified empirically, not changed, loudly
   documented.
2. "Append viewbox-experiment to GoldenParity.enabledFixtures" — literally doing this
   breaks the existing `enabledPairsExist` gate (see above); the brief itself flagged
   this ambiguity ("say which"), so this isn't really a bug in the brief, just resolved
   in favor of the helper-extension option.
3. Everything else in the touch-point list (PenNode.swift, PenLayoutEngine ~422/435,
   PenVariableResolver ~456, PenImportResolver+Prefixing ~79, PenNode+Editing ~69,
   EditOperation+Codable ~60/113, ChangeCategory ~103, CRDTDocument+PropertyCodec
   ~228/420, PropertyDiff ~83/304, PenRenderer ~491/646/662/678, ReactEmitter+Nodes
   ~34, ReactEmitter+Images ~39) was accurate in *kind* (right files, right shape of
   change) even though — as warned — none of the line numbers matched after the stroke/
   group/richtext slices merged.

## Files

New:
- `Sources/Woodcase/Models/PenNode+ScriptData.swift` — `PenNode.ScriptData`, `PenScriptInput`
- `Sources/Woodcase/Models/PenFill+ShaderFill.swift` — `PenFill.PenShaderFill`, `PenShaderUniform`
- `Sources/Woodcase/CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Script.swift` — `emitScript`
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenScriptDataTests.swift`
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenShaderFillTests.swift`
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenImageFillOptionalURLTests.swift`
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenScriptShaderConsumersTests.swift`
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenScriptShaderRoundTripTests.swift`

Edited (production): `Models/PenNode.swift`, `Models/PenFill.swift`, `PenLayoutEngine.swift`,
`PenVariableResolver.swift`, `PenImportResolver+Prefixing.swift`, `Rendering/PenRenderer.swift`,
`Rendering/PenFillRenderer.swift`, `Editing/ChangeCategory.swift`, `Editing/EditOperation+Codable.swift`,
`Editing/PenNode+Editing.swift`, `Sync/CRDTDocument+PropertyCodec.swift`, `Sync/PropertyDiff.swift`,
`CodeGen/ComponentAnalyzer.swift`, `CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Nodes.swift`,
`CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Images.swift`, `CodeGen/React/ReactEmitter+Styles.swift`.

Edited (tests): `PenTransformBuilderTests.swift` (new pivot test), `PenViewBoxSnapshotTests.swift`
(dropped `loadRootOnly()`), `GoldenParity.swift` + `GoldenParityTests.swift` (golden-only fixtures).

Edited (docs): `Documentation.docc/Woodcase.md`, `Documentation.docc/PenEngine.md`,
`Documentation.docc/PenRendering.md`, `project/2026-08-29-pen-2.17-migration.md`, `project/gotchas.md`.

Worktree: `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/.claude/worktrees/agent-ab8764dbe5c119184`, branch
tip includes a clean `git merge main` (no conflicts — nothing had been implemented yet
when the merge landed) on top of the stroke/group/richtext slices.

# VLEHU — Documentation and rename

## Summary

Brought the prose docs into coherence with the landed 2.17 model. All 18 changed files are
comment/prose-only — no production code logic changed.

- **DocC pages**: Woodcase.md topic groups now list all 5 concrete migration rules
  (`PenIconMigrationRule` and `PenGroupMigrationRule` were missing). PenEngine.md gained a
  `### Groups` subsection (parity with the existing Strokes/Rich text subsections) and a
  `fileToken` paragraph under the version-gate section. Verified the version-gate table against
  `PenParser+VersionGate.swift`/`PenFormatVersion.swift` — accurate as written, no changes needed.
- **Pencil → Pen rename**: `PenInteroperability.md` retitled "Pen Interoperability"; all prose
  "Pencil" references across every DocC page, README, AGENTS.md's project-owned head, and ~15
  Swift doc-comment sites (PenIconFontRegistry, PenLayoutEngine, PenVariableResolver,
  PenShapeBuilder, PenFillRenderer, PenID) now say "Pen" or "Pen.app" (app-specific rendering
  claims use "Pen.app", matching the style already used by the migration-era prose).
  `Sources/WoodcaseCommand/WoodcaseCommand.swift`'s "Render Pencil .pen files" abstract was left
  alone — CLI is owned by leaf 8ToLQ. The `pencil` MCP server name and the docs.pencil.dev URL
  were left alone per the brief.
- **README**: states Pen.dev, the 2.8–2.17 (+ newer 2.x with diagnostic) read range and that it
  always writes 2.17, that legacy files are migrated on load with diagnostics reported through
  `PenDiagnosticCollector`, fixed a stale "13 node types" (now 14 — `script` was added), and
  dropped a stale "rich and plain text" renderer claim (rich text was removed in 2.17).
- **AGENTS.md project-owned head**: "Pencil.dev" → "Pen.dev"; per a mid-task instruction from the
  coordinator, updated the schema-file bullet to point at `./local/Pen-Schema-2.17.md` (the app's
  own 2.17 schema) with `Pen-Schema.js` (2.10) / `Pen-Schema-v2.js` (2.17 dev docs) named as the
  older copies — these files are gitignored and were not created in this worktree.
- **Stale-term sweep**: grepped the whole tree for `dashPattern`, `miterAngle`, `PenStroke `,
  `icon_font`, `iconFontName`/`iconFontFamily`, `PenTextSpan`, "rich text", `2.9`, `2.10`,
  `Pencil` — every remaining hit is a legitimate migration-history reference (describing what the
  old key/type was called), not a stale claim about current behavior.
- **Pre-existing DocC warnings fixed as a side effect**: the baseline `swift package
  generate-documentation --target Woodcase` had 8 warnings unrelated to the 2.17 work (broken doc
  links in `ReactHarnessBuilder.swift`, `EditableDocument(+Expansion).swift`, `LayoutCache.swift`,
  and `CRDTArchitecture.md`, plus a dangling reference to a `UndoController` type that doesn't
  exist anywhere in the codebase). Fixed all of them (comment-only) since the job criterion is
  "no missing-symbol warnings" with no scope carve-out. Final run: **0 warnings**.
- **Test fixture setup**: copied `Fixtures/tmp/icon-test.html` and `lucide.ttf` from the main
  checkout per the documented gotcha (gitignored, not created by any test) — without them one
  WebView test times out. `swift test --quiet`: 1656/1656 pass.

## Deviations from the brief

1. Fixed 8 pre-existing DocC warnings outside the five named concept pages (ReactHarnessBuilder,
   EditableDocument, EditableDocument+Expansion, LayoutCache, CRDTArchitecture.md) — comment-only,
   done to satisfy the literal "no missing-symbol warnings" criterion.
2. Added a `### Groups` subsection to PenEngine.md that wasn't explicitly requested by name, for
   parity with the existing Strokes/Rich text subsections and because the brief lists "groups as
   pure containers" as a concept to describe.
3. Addressed the coordinator's mid-task addition to AGENTS.md's local/ file list.

## What's wrong in the brief

- **"the migrator and its six rules"** — there are five concrete `PenMigrationRule` types
  (`PenVersionMigrationRule`, `PenStrokeMigrationRule`, `PenIconMigrationRule`,
  `PenRichTextMigrationRule`, `PenGroupMigrationRule`), confirmed against
  `PenLegacyMigrator.rules` and the design doc, which describes each slice adding exactly "one
  rule." No sixth rule exists or is implied anywhere — script/shader nodes are new in 2.17 and
  need no legacy translation. This looks like a simple miscount in the brief, not a
  design-doc/code disagreement worth a correction block.
- No other design-doc claim contradicts the landed code; PenViewBox, stroke migration, icon
  migration, script/shader round-tripping, and the rotation-pivot finding all match their
  doc-comment and DocC descriptions exactly. No correction block was needed in
  `project/2026-08-29-pen-2.17-migration.md`.

data.text:
Done in worktree agent-a9732813355649696 (branch worktree-agent-a9732813355649696), not committed.

`layoutAbsoluteContainer` now computes the union of its children instead of
`contentSize: 0`, so a `fit_content` container with `layout: "none"` — a frame,
and every group — sizes to its children. Union = max over enabled children of
(child.x + childRect.width) / (child.y + childRect.height), measured from the
container's own origin: a child at a negative offset overhangs and cannot grow
the box leftward or upward; a rotated child contributes its rotated bounding box
(that is the rect the engine writes for it, and what a flex parent already
counts); disabled children take no space; padding is not reserved; fixed and
fill_container are untouched, and fit_content(fallback) still falls back when
the union is zero.

FINDING that changed the plan: the brief predicted the blur2/blur3 rotation
snapshots would move. They must not — blur2-no-bg sits at MAE 0.0, a
pixel-perfect match with Pen's PNG, and a group sized to its union with the
usual centre pivot would move its content by (-87.6, +211.4). A group is an
ANCHOR, not a box. blur2.pen's group stores x=-111.42492757477771, y=100.000…04,
rotation=-315 over a 299x299 union; those are exactly where the group's local
origin lands when a 299x299 group at (-49.5,-49.5) is swung 45 degrees about its
own centre (agrees to 1.4e-14, Pen's own float noise). So Pen pivots at the
bounds centre when the user rotates, then BAKES the result into x/y; at render
time rotation replays about that anchor. The rival model (x/y = union top-left,
centre pivot) puts the diamond's centre at (38.08, 249.50) instead of (100,100),
i.e. off the 200x200 artboard — blur2-no-bg.png shows a full-bleed diagonal
split, so it is centred.

Implemented accordingly: `applyRotationExpansion` exempts a group (its rect is
the UN-rotated union), and `PenTransformBuilder` pivots a group at its rect's
origin rather than the centre. This is a rotation-pivot change, which the brief
listed under DO NOT BUILD, but its own escape hatch ("if the evidence says Pen
sizes a group some other way — e.g. rotation pivots at the declared box —
implement what Pen does and document it") covers it, and without it the group
cannot have a real size at all.

MAE: nothing moved. All eleven PenSnapshotTests figures are identical to the
digit — blur1 1.4115625, blur2 7.65750625, blur3 16.5103625, blur2-no-bg 0.0,
blur3-no-bg 0.09728125, transforms-and-effects 1.1222287132289934, and the rest.
No threshold touched, no reference PNG regenerated. blur3/blur3-no-bg were
predicted to move and did not: their groups carry no rotation, and a group draws
no content, so its rect reaches the render only through the pivot and the shape
path for effects.

data.text:
Baseline measurement, before any change (2026-08-29, this machine, main @ 2f47240)

`swift test --filter "WebViewTestHarness"` — the `Icon font renders glyphs via file URL`
test renders at `viewportSize: CGSize(width: 400, height: 600)` and writes
`/tmp/pen-exports/webview-regression/icon-test.png`.

    sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight -g dpiWidth /tmp/pen-exports/webview-regression/icon-test.png
      pixelWidth: 800
      pixelHeight: 1200
      dpiWidth: 72.000

So today's harness returns a CGImage at **2x the viewport points** (400x600 pt -> 800x1200 px),
which is the host's screen backing scale: `WKSnapshotConfiguration.snapshotWidth` is set to the
width in *points* (400) and `takeSnapshot` rasterizes at the display's backing scale. That matches
`PenRenderer.render(..., scale: 2, ...)` on the Woodcase side of every MAE comparison. Any
re-implementation must produce 2x, not 1x.

Fixed by keying the font cache on a registration generation. Branch
worktree-agent-a9bdc916c52f4ad67 (not committed).

DESIGN. New public `PenFontRegistry` owns a monotonic `generation` counter that
names the fact "the set of fonts Core Text knows about". `FontResolutionCache`
stamps every entry with the generation it was resolved under and discards the
whole cache the first time it is touched at a newer generation. `resolveFont`
reads the generation *before* resolving and passes it to `setFont`, which drops
a write whose generation is already stale — that closes the window a plain
"invalidate on registration" check leaves open (thread A probes availability,
thread B registers, thread A writes the fallback).

Every registration site now calls `PenFontRegistry.didRegisterFonts()`:
`PenIconFontRegistry.ensureRegistered`, `GoogleFontResolver.registerFont`, and
`TestFontRegistration`. The first two are production paths, so this was a live
production bug, not only a test-ordering one.

OPTION (b) — "never cache a fallback" — WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED.
`swift test --quiet --no-parallel --filter "PenFontResolutionBenchmarkTests"`,
median of 10, 3 runs:

  resolve-absent-10000   before ~10.8ms   with (b) ~4000ms   (~370x)
  measure-mixed-2000     before ~57ms     with (b) ~800ms    (~14x)

An absent family is the common case in a real .pen (a design naming a font the
machine does not have), and `fontFamilyAvailable` on a missing family makes Core
Text run a full fallback cascade, ~400us a call. At 200 text nodes that is 80ms
per layout pass against RapidPro's 4ms budget. (b) also turns out to add nothing
over (a): once the generation is trusted, "F was absent at generation G" is
itself a valid cached fact.

INSTEAD, the gap (a) leaves — a registrar outside Woodcase that never calls the
hook — is covered by observing `kCTFontManagerRegisteredFontsChangedNotification`
on the local notification centre, which Core Text posts whenever anyone changes
the font set. It is free at steady state and covers exactly the case the hook
cannot (a GUI host app), while the hook covers exactly the case the notification
cannot (a headless process with no run loop). Documented as belt-and-braces, not
as a replacement for the call.

FINAL NUMBERS (same command): resolve-present ~8.3ms, resolve-absent ~9.5ms,
measure-mixed ~31ms — at or better than baseline, no memoization lost.

TEST FONT REGISTRATION was already deterministic and needed no change:
`TestFontRegistration.once` is a lazy static, so `swift_once` makes
`registerTestFonts()` a barrier, and all three suites that need the fonts
(PenFontRenderingTests, PenWoodcaseAppTests, WebViewRegressionTests) call it
from `init()`, which runs before their test bodies. No other suite measures text
from a bundled family — `PenLayoutRootFillContainerTests` and the analyzer/
emitter suites that load woodcase-app.pen never reach `PenTextMeasurer`. The
nondeterminism was entirely the shared cache. swift-testing has no process-wide
before-all hook; a `SuiteTrait` would only repeat what `init()` already does, so
none was added.

VERIFICATION. `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenFontRegistrationCacheTests.swift`
reproduces the race deterministically by writing a private copy of
IBMPlexSans-Regular.ttf with its family renamed to "Woodcase Font" via
equal-length byte substitution in the `name` table (offsets stay valid; Core
Text accepts it). Nothing else in the process ever registers that family, so
"resolve before registration" is exact rather than order-dependent. Red before
the fix: `CTFontCopyFamilyName(after) -> "SF Pro"` instead of "Woodcase Font".

Full suite, 5 sequential `swift test --quiet` runs: 1691 tests, 160 suites,
PASSED 5/5 (94s, 65s, 53s, 46s, 43s). Previous failure rate ~1 in 3.

The `project/gotchas.md` entry "The memoized font cache makes ~20 MAE tests fail
at random" is deleted.

NOTE FOR THE INTEGRATOR: `PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests` is gated on an Xcode
app host and so never runs under `swift test` — the memoization had no coverage
in CI. The new suite runs unguarded and does the same job; the guard on the old
one looks unnecessary (PenFontRenderingTests does the same CoreText work with no
guard) but I left it alone as out of scope.

data.text:
Implementation findings (2026-08-29)

DONE. `Tests/WoodcaseTests/WebViewTestHarness.swift` is rebuilt on SleepyHollow
(pinned at 35c1b0cf43fc46da840628649b057378c5f72147) and no longer imports WebKit.
Full suite passes twice; sorted performance/mae-test.csv is byte-identical to
performance/mae-baseline.csv on every run (25/25 rows, `diff` empty).

What replaced what:
- WKWebView + WKWebViewConfiguration        -> PageHost(options:) + LoadOptions + ViewportSize
- loadFileURL(_:allowingReadAccessTo:)      -> PageHost.load(_:)  (see below)
- the __READY__ WKUserScript poll           -> InjectedScript(.documentEnd, .page) + host.messages(named:"ready", in:.page)
- the WKScriptMessageHandler error capture  -> ConsoleCapture via ConsoleOperation (pull) and the console message stream (push, for the timeout path)
- Timer.scheduledTimer timeout              -> a TaskGroup race between the ready stream and Task.sleep
- WKSnapshotConfiguration + takeSnapshot    -> ShotOperation(region:.viewport, scale: ShotScale(factor: 2)) -> ShotImage -> ShotCapture(decoding:).image

Three things in the plan did not survive contact:

1. WaitCondition cannot be used for __READY__ here. `.predicate("window.__READY__ === true")`
   works in isolation, but WaitEngine re-checks it from the HOST, on the main actor, every
   50 ms. Woodcase's suite saturates the main actor, and a full `swift test` starved that
   poll into two unearned timeouts (StatCard at budget 5 s, the icon-font harness test at
   budget 10 s). Reverted to the old design's page-side push (setTimeout + postMessage);
   the retired code's comment about Timer vs Task.sleep was warning about exactly this.

2. SleepyHollow has no read-access root for file URLs and needs none. Nothing in its
   API mentions loadFileURL/allowingReadAccessTo; PageHost.load calls
   webView.load(URLRequest(url:)). Measured: that loads a file: document AND its relative
   subresources in sibling/parent directories. `allowingReadAccessTo:` is now unused.

3. swift-argument-parser had to move 1.7.1 -> 1.8.2. SleepyHollow's `sleepy` target uses
   @Option(defaultAsFlag:), added in 1.8; `swift build` builds every product in the graph,
   so plain `swift build` failed until `swift package update swift-argument-parser`.

Scale: unchanged at 2x (400x600 pt -> 800x1200 px), now fixed by ShotScale(factor: 2)
rather than inherited from the host display.

Also needed: `#if canImport(WebKit)` -> `#if os(macOS)` in the two caller test files,
since SleepyHollow is macOS-only while WebKit imports on iOS too.

One test added (a behaviour the old harness had and nothing covered): an uncaught page
error surfaces as HarnessError.javaScriptError rather than a timeout. Its message is only
asserted non-empty — WebKit sanitizes ErrorEvent.message to "Script error." for a file:
document, which was true of the old harness too.

data.description: Agent-first CLI editing of .pen files and a read-only live viewer. Decisions and the verb set are in project/2026-08-29-viewer-editor-plan.md; the agent-experience evidence is in project/2026-08-29-pen-mcp-tire-kick.md. Read both before claiming. Strict TDD on every leaf.
data.title: Woodcase Viewer & Editor

data.description: Library-level pieces the CLI is a thin consumer of. All in Sources/Woodcase/Editing (or a new Editing/Agent-facing folder, one type per file), Foundation-only, DocC at 100%.
data.title: Editing core

data.description: EditOperation.updateKind replaces a node's whole kind; agents want to set one property. Add a `setProperties` operation carrying a [String: AnyCodable] keyed by the same property paths LWWPropertyMap already uses ("kind.width", "common.name"), applied through PenNodePatcher-style merging, with an inverse, dirty-tracking classification via ChangeCategory, and CRDT emission as per-path LWW writes. Unknown keys and type mismatches are typed EditingErrors naming the key.
data.title: Path-based property patch operation

criteria.label: setProperties on a rectangle's fill leaves every other property untouched and round-trips through materialize()
An unknown property key fails with an error naming the key and the node
The CRDT emits one LWW write per path and two peers converge

data.description: A resolver from an address string to a node id: id, name path from any ancestor ("Dashboard/Header/Title"), instance path into a ref's expanded tree ("Orders/Value", resolved to the component child id for storage in descendants), and a within-batch tag ("@hero"). Ambiguity is a typed error carrying every candidate as an id plus its full name path; no match is a typed error that lists near misses (same leaf name elsewhere). Also a name-path formatter for the reverse direction, used by every error message and by tree output.
data.title: Node addressing

criteria.label: Each of id, name path, instance path and tag resolves in a fixture with nested refs
A duplicate name yields an ambiguity error listing all candidates with full paths
A miss yields an error that names near misses

data.description: A stable hash per node subtree (properties, children order, descendant hashes) and one for the document, computed from the flat store and exposed on EditableDocument. A mutating operation may carry an expected revision for each node it touches; a mismatch is a typed conflict error naming the node and both revisions. Document-level revision is what the activity log records.
data.title: Revision tokens

criteria.label: Editing a child changes the ancestors' revisions and no sibling's
An operation with a stale expected revision fails with a conflict naming the node
Revisions are stable across encode/decode of the same file

data.description: Applies an ordered list of operations (the JSONL grammar in the plan) to an EditableDocument in memory: each op resolves its addresses (including @tags created earlier in the batch), applies, and records a per-op result; a failure skips the op and marks every later op that references its tag or target as cascaded; independent ops continue. The result is a report (line, status, error, created name→id tree). Atomic mode discards everything on the first failure. Also the retry: given a prior report, re-run only its failed and cascaded lines.
data.title: Batch applier

criteria.label: A batch with a bad op in the middle applies the independent ops before and after it
An op referencing a failed op's tag is reported as cascaded, not failed
Atomic mode leaves the document unchanged after any failure
Retry re-applies exactly the failed and cascaded lines

data.description: PenFileTransaction: open a .pen under an exclusive advisory lock (flock on the file), parse, hand an EditableDocument to a closure, write the result atomically (temp file + rename, same directory) in the canonical form migrate already writes (sorted keys, two-space indent), release. A held lock is waited on with a bounded timeout, then a typed error. Unchanged documents do not rewrite the file (mtime stays).
data.title: File transactions

criteria.label: Two concurrent transactions on one file serialize; neither loses the other's edit
Output bytes for an unchanged document are identical to the input
A lock held past the timeout fails with a typed error, not a hang

data.description: Operations whose consequence exceeds their target refuse without an explicit flag and explain: deleting a reusable node that has instances (lists them; `detach` applies detachRef to each first), an override or descendant patch that matches no node in the component (error, never a silent no-op, with candidates), moving a node into its own subtree. Each guard is a typed EditingError with the information the CLI needs to print the remedy.
data.title: Consequence guards

criteria.label: Deleting a component with two instances fails naming both; with detach it succeeds and both are plain frames
An override addressed to a nonexistent descendant fails listing the component's overridable nodes

data.description: A TreeRow model and formatter: for a document (or subtree), one row per node with id, type, name (or an unnamed marker), resolved layout rect in the parent's space, and a clip flag (partially/fully outside its parent), computed from PenLayoutEngine after variable resolution for a chosen theme; optional expansion of refs with path addresses ("SAjDU/B0M8B8/uKX6O") that resolve back through the addresser; optional property columns; depth limit; and a JSON form. This is the read that replaces most screenshots.
data.title: Settled tree view

criteria.label: Rows for a fixture match its known layout rects and flag a deliberately overflowing child
Expanded rows carry path addresses that the resolver accepts
Unnamed nodes are marked and named nodes are shown by name path

data.description: An append-only JSONL event log at ~/.woodcase/activity.jsonl ($WOODCASE_HOME overrides the directory), one event per applied operation: timestamp, identity (PeerID name), absolute file path, op kind, node ids and name paths touched, the inverse EditOperation (from EditableDocument+Inverse), document revision after. Written by the file transaction on commit. A reader that tails it (with an offset) and filters by file and identity, for the CLI and the viewer. Rotation at a size threshold.
data.title: Activity log

criteria.label: Every applied op in a batch produces exactly one event with the resulting document revision
The tail reader resumes from an offset without re-reading

data.description: Sources/WoodcaseCommand grows one command file per verb, each a thin adapter over the core: no decisions in the adapter. Conventions from the plan: --json on every read, the sleepy-style exit codes, name→id tree on every mutation, errors that name the path and the remedy, --as/$WOODCASE_AS. Tests in WoodcaseCommandTests drive the commands against fixture copies in a temp directory.
data.title: CLI verbs

data.description: `woodcase tree <file> [<node>]` prints the settled tree view; --depth, --props, --json, --expand, --theme. `woodcase get <file> <node>` prints one node as .pen JSON (or expanded), with its revision. data.text:
Handoff from the planning session (2026-08-29, Claude Fable 5 with Ben). The plan doc and the tire-kick note carry the decisions; this note carries what is *not* in them.

**Codebase facts that shape the first leaves**
- `EditOperation.updateKind` replaces a node's whole kind — that is the gap the patch leaf closes. `LWWPropertyMap` (Sync/) already keys registers by property path ("kind.width", "common.name"): use that vocabulary for `setProperties` rather than inventing one. `PenNodePatcher.patchNode(_:with:)` is the existing property-dict merge to build on.
- Frames without a `layout` key are horizontal flex in both Pen and Woodcase (`PenLayoutEngine.swift:328`, `data.layout ?? .horizontal`). Only the document root is coordinate-placed, so auto-placement in `add` applies to root-level inserts only.
- `EditableDocument+Inverse.swift` already computes inverse ops — the activity log and `undo` reuse it; don't write a second inverse.
- `migrate` (`PenFileMigrator`) defines the canonical write form (sorted keys, two-space indent); file transactions must emit the same bytes so an unchanged document is byte-identical.
- The Swift toolchain fails inside the Bash sandbox; run `swift build`/`swift test`/`swiftformat` with the sandbox disabled, one call at a time (`project/agents/harness.md`).

**Sibling repos**
- `../PixelPeeper` already exposes a `PixelPeeper` library product beside the `peep` executable — the vision-helper leaf depends on it as a pinned GitHub revision, never a path. `../SleepyHollow/Sources/sleepy/ShotCommand.swift` holds the existing grid implementation (`ShotGrid`) to generalize. The `sleepy` binary is not on PATH in this environment.
- `../agents/modules/cli-design.md` (uncommitted there as of this note) is the house CLI-design module distilled from this work; Ben will commit, `make sync`, and `agents add cli-design` here. Once it renders into AGENTS.md, it is the rule for every verb.
- Penumbra must reload on file change (file is truth) — a Penumbra job, filed when the CLI lands (plan § Handoffs).

**Ben's rulings during planning**
- No NIO ("pretty heavy"); `serve` is a hand-written HTTP/SSE server on Network.framework.
- Activity log at `~/.woodcase/`, not XDG.
- Exit codes: sleepy's table verbatim.
- Viewer HTML is not built until the Pen design prototype (leaf A80Hf, labeled decision) is signed off — do that prototype in Pen via its MCP and write a second DX note.

**Scratch state**
- `local/tirekick.pen` is an untouched 2.9 scratch copy (Pen never saved the session); delete or reuse freely. Pen files for reference live in `~/Local/Pen/` (read needs the sandbox off).

**Suggested first move**
`job claim --next` lands on the patch leaf. Patch, addressing and revision tokens are disjoint in files and are fan-out candidates per `project/agents/delegation.md`; the batch applier waits on all three. Strict red/green on each.

Correction to the handoff: `cli-design` is now a pair, like jobs/harness — `cli-design` (kind: file → `project/agents/cli-design.md`) plus `cli-design-brief` (inline). Enabling here is `agents add cli-design cli-design-brief`; then add a `project/agents/cli-design.md` line to the docs list in the project-owned head of AGENTS.md.

Rulings for dispatch (2026-08-29, integrator):
- The lenient CRDT codec (CRDTDocument+PropertyCodec: unknown key ignored, undecodable value silently sets nil) is a footgun for agents; the leaf builds a *throwing* NodePropertyCodec in Editing/ (path vocabulary = PropertyDiff's, "common.*"/"kind.*") and the CRDT codec delegates to it so there is one vocabulary. Errors: EditingError.unknownProperty / propertyTypeMismatch (pre-carved in 6bd7ff6).
- setProperties carries [String: AnyCodable]; a value of .null clears the property. Inverse = setProperties with the prior values of exactly the same keys. CRDT emission = one SetProperty per key (reuse processLocalUpdateKind/UpdateCommon's shape). ChangeCategory via categorize(old, new) before/after.
- Operation is atomic: validate every key first, apply none on any error.

Rulings for dispatch (2026-08-29, integrator):
- A segment matches a node by id or by name (ids also appear as segments in tree --expand paths like "SAjDU/B0M8B8/uKX6O"); segments are consecutive parent→child; the first segment may be any node in the document. Unnamed nodes are addressable only by id.
- When a segment resolves to a ref node and segments remain, the remainder resolves inside the referenced component's tree (recursing through nested refs) and the result is the descendants key Pen stores: component-child ids joined by "/" from the outermost ref inward (Pen-Format.md: "children of nested instances… prefix with the containing instance's ID and a slash"). Result type distinguishes .node(id) from .instanceDescendant(refID:, descendantKey:).
- "@tag" resolves through a caller-supplied [String: String] tag map; a missing tag is addressNotFound.
- Errors are pre-carved in 6bd7ff6: ambiguousAddress(candidates: [NodeAddressCandidate]), addressNotFound(nearMisses:). The name-path formatter marks unnamed segments; pick a marker and document it.

Rulings for dispatch (2026-08-29, integrator):
- Do NOT reuse EditableDocument.contentHash(for:) (Layout): it uses Swift's per-process-seeded Hasher and mixes in layout rects, so it is neither stable across runs nor content-only. Leave it alone; the new thing is `revision`.
- Revision = 64-bit FNV-1a over (canonical JSON of the node with children stripped — JSONEncoder .sortedKeys, no whitespace — followed by each child's revision in order), rendered as 16 lowercase hex chars. Document revision = FNV-1a over root revisions in rootOrder plus canonical JSON of version/themes/imports/variables. Foundation only; no CryptoKit.
- Expected revisions travel beside the operation, not inside it: `apply(_ op: EditOperation, expecting: [String: String])` checks every entry first and throws EditingError.revisionConflict(nodeID:expected:actual:) (pre-carved in 6bd7ff6) before applying anything; a nodeID absent from the document is nodeNotFound. This keeps the leaf out of EditOperation.swift, which the patch leaf owns. Also `applyLocal(_:expecting:)`.
- Computed on demand, no cache — the performance-budget leaf measures later.

data.text:
Design settled after reading the seams (patcher, 2026-08-29).

NodePropertyCodec will be table-free where it can: it encodes the node's
PenNodeCommon / kind data struct to a [String: AnyCodable] via JSONEncoder,
patches the one key, and decodes back — so the wire shape is by construction
the .pen file's own JSON shape, and a bad value fails as a real DecodingError
that becomes EditingError.propertyTypeMismatch. Valid kind paths come from
PropertyDiff.allKindKeys(kind) so there is literally one vocabulary.

Three wrinkles found in the existing seams:
1. Swift name != JSON key for two fields, uniformly across every kind:
   `fills` encodes as "fill" and `effects` as "effect". The path vocabulary
   uses the Swift names ("kind.fills"), so the codec keeps a two-entry
   translation table.
2. PenNode.RefData has custom Codable that flattens `rootOverrides` into
   top-level keys, so the generic dict trick cannot address it. `.ref` gets
   an explicit three-path implementation.
3. Existing CRDT codec bug: encodePenValue(.variable("x")) emits .string("x")
   with NO "$" prefix, while encodePenValueString emits "$x". PenValue's own
   Codable and every .pen file use "$x". Delegating to the new codec fixes
   PenValue<Double>/<Bool> to the "$x" form. Symmetric before and after, so
   CRDT convergence is unaffected; it makes CRDT setProperty payloads
   interchangeable with .pen JSON, which setProperties needs.

2026-08-29 rulings from Ben for the unattended stretch: push to origin after each integration; the viewer design prototype (A80Hf) is done in Pen and exported to PNGs under project/ without waiting, but the .pen save and the sign-off remain Ben's; every other decision on the frontier is the integrator's, logged as job notes.

data.text:
Revision tokens implemented and tested. New files, all under Sources/Woodcase/Editing/ (plus a docc section and a test file):

- Sources/Woodcase/Editing/FNV1a.swift — `FNV1aHasher` (internal), an incremental 64-bit FNV-1a hasher. `combine(_:)` folds in `[UInt8]` or `String` (UTF-8), `finalize()` gives the raw `UInt64`, `hexString` gives 16 lowercase hex chars.
- Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+Revision.swift — `revision(of:)`, `documentRevision`, `apply(_:expecting:)`, `applyLocal(_:expecting:)`. Canonical JSON via a private `JSONEncoder` (`.sortedKeys`, `nonConformingFloatEncodingStrategy = .convertToString(...)` so a stray NaN/Infinity can't make revision computation throw).
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/RevisionTests.swift — 14 tests: FNV-1a vectors (empty string, "a"), hex format, missing-node nil, ancestor-propagates/sibling-untouched, reorder changes parent, documentRevision changes on variable add / stable when unchanged, apply(expecting:) match/stale/missing-node (document verified unchanged in both failure cases), applyLocal(expecting:) match/stale, and revision stability across parse→EditableDocument→materialize→encode→reparse (parser-variables.pen fixture).
- Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/EditingDocuments.md — added a "Revision Tokens" section with a code example, cross-linked from prose to `contentHash(for:)` to explain why they're different.

Verification: red first (14 compile errors, exactly the missing symbols — FNV1aHasher, revision, documentRevision, apply/applyLocal(expecting:) — confirmed via `swift test --filter RevisionTests`), then implemented; all 14 new tests green on first run after implementation (no red-then-green iteration needed beyond the initial compile-error red). `swiftformat . --lint` clean (auto-fixed 2 files once: numeric-literal grouping and a Sendable conformance the formatter flagged as redundant on the non-public FNV1aHasher — removed). Full suite: `swift test --quiet` — 1715 tests / 162 suites passed. `swift package generate-documentation --target Woodcase` — zero warnings/errors.

Files touched are exactly the ones this leaf owns: FNV1a.swift, EditableDocument+Revision.swift (both new), EditingDocuments.md (docc addition), RevisionTests.swift (new test file). Nothing in EditOperation*.swift, EditableDocument+Properties/+Apply/+Inverse.swift, NodeAddress*.swift, or the Sync codec was touched. EditingError.swift untouched — reused the pre-carved revisionConflict/nodeNotFound cases as instructed. No CLI verbs added.

Deviation from brief: none of substance. Minor: `applyLocal(_:expecting:)` is written without `@discardableResult` to match the existing `applyLocal(_:)`'s signature exactly (the brief's "same guard" reading).

What's wrong in the brief: nothing found — the pre-carved EditingError cases, the flat-store shape, and the `PenNode` standalone-encode assumption all held as described. One thing worth flagging for the integrator: `nodes[id]` in the flat store already has children stripped to `nil` (via `withEmptyChildren()`), so `revision(of:)` encodes `nodes[nodeID]` directly with no extra stripping step — the brief's phrasing ("encode the PenNode ... with children stripped") reads as if stripping were something revision(of:) needs to do; it's already true of the stored value, which simplified the implementation.

- Unnamed marker is `#<id>`; `#` also works as an explicit id-escape on any segment.

covered by tests; full suite 1753 tests green, swiftformat --lint clean.

New: Sources/Woodcase/Editing/NodePropertyCodec{,+Write,+JSON,+Shapes}.swift and

CRDTDocument{,+LocalProcessing,+PropertyCodec}, EditingDocuments.md.

The CRDT codec's 584 lines of hand-written switches are gone — it is now 82
lines delegating to NodePropertyCodec with try?, so the lenient face and the
throwing face share one vocabulary.

Three things the integrator should know:

1. WIRE-SHAPE FIX (behaviour change, no test needed changing). The old
   encodePenValue emitted a PenValue<Double>/<Bool> variable as "x" with no "$",
   while encodePenValueString emitted "$x". PenValue's own Codable and every
   .pen file use "$x". Delegating to the typed Codable unifies on "$x". Old and
   new are each symmetric, so CRDT convergence is unaffected; what changes is
   that a setProperty payload is now interchangeable with .pen JSON, which
   setProperties needs.

2. NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT. A strict vocabulary on PenNode.Kind.unknown would have
   silently dropped a remote setProperty for a key that replica had not seen,
   diverging two peers on an unrecognised node type. An unknown kind has no
   schema to check against, so any kind.* key is now accepted there;
   paths(for:) still lists only the keys it carries. Two regression tests in
   CRDTSetPropertiesTests cover it, one via setProperties and one via updateKind.

3. PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED. A whole-kind type swap does not converge through LWW
   property writes: PropertyDiff emits "kind.type", and neither the old codec
   nor the new one can apply it (a type change is updateKind's job, and the
   receiving peer still holds the old kind). Unchanged by this leaf; worth a
   backlog entry.

Codable already round-trips, covered by a test.

Shape: PenFileTransaction.run(at:timeout:_:) / .read(at:timeout:_:), body is
@MainActor @Sendable (EditableDocument) throws -> Value, returns
Outcome<Value>{value, didWrite, url}. flock(2) on the .pen file itself (LOCK_EX for
run, LOCK_SH for read), polled with LOCK_NB every 10 ms up to the timeout; never a
blocking flock. Unchanged documents are not written — encodeForFile(materialized)
vs encodeForFile(parsed) — so bytes and mtime both stay. Writes go to a temp
neighbour, take the original's permissions, then rename(2).

Two design points beyond the brief. (1) rename(2) replaces the inode, so a waiter
holding a descriptor for the old inode could win a lock on a file no longer at the
path and lose the other transaction's edit; acquire() therefore re-opens the path on
every poll and re-checks st_dev/st_ino after each successful flock. (2) The lock is
advisory and is documented as such: Pen.app writing the file without asking is not
blocked.

Verification: full suite green, 1724 tests, `swift test --quiet`; `swiftformat . --lint`
clean; DocC builds with no warnings. All three acceptance criteria mutation-tested —
downgrading the write lock to LOCK_SH makes the concurrency test fail 5/5; stubbing
describesFile/permissions makes the FileLock tests fail. Criteria UJk/Nka/jsz marked
passed.

Gotcha recorded in project/gotchas.md: under the parallel full suite a 10 ms
Task.sleep can resume ~12 s late, so wall-clock assertions near the interval under
test are unreliable.

Left for the activity-log leaf (qoTVa): no recorder was built. The seam is
Outcome.didWrite plus the single private write(_:replacing:) commit point.

Ruling 2026-08-29 (Ben): `pen` validates our assumptions but is never a test-suite dependency — it may break or vanish, and consumers can't be made to install and log in. So scripts/pen-oracle is a fixture *generator* run by hand: its outputs (layout JSON, PNGs, Pen's canonical re-save) are committed as fixtures and the tests read those files only. No test shells out to `pen`; no test skips on missing login — there is nothing to skip. The "encodeForFile vs Pen's save" comparison is a committed fixture pair with a dated note of every difference, regenerated when Pen changes.

data.text:
Design settled after reading the seams (EditOperation, EditableDocument+Addressing/
+Revision/+Apply/+Inverse/+Layout/+Overrides/+Detach, NodePropertyCodec, PenID,
PenNode+RefData, PenDescendantOverride).

Grammar (Sources/Woodcase/Batch/BatchOperation.swift), one JSONL line per op:
  set          target, props, rev?
  add          parent?, node, at?, tag?, rev?
  cp           source, parent?, at?, tag?, props?, rev?
  mv           target, parent?, at?, rev?
  rm           target, detach?, rev?
  override     target (Instance/Descendant), props, rev?
  var          name, value (PenVariable) - add-or-update
  theme-axis   name, options - add-or-update

Decisions:
- Omitting `parent` means the document root. The CLI's literal `document` maps onto
  the absent field; an address string can never collide with it.
- `rev` guards the op's primary node: `target` where present, else `parent`. A
  root-level `add`/`cp` has no such node, so `rev` is checked against
  `documentRevision` instead. Checked through `apply(_:expecting:)` for node ops.
- `set` props use the `common.*`/`kind.*` NodePropertyCodec vocabulary;
  `override` props use raw .pen key names, because that is what Pen writes into a
  ref's `descendants` map. Documented in the grammar - the asymmetry is the file
  format's, not ours.
- Variable/theme-axis REMOVAL is not in the batch grammar: making the payload
  optional would turn a dropped field into a silent delete. Add/update only.
- `override` supports `props` only, not `node`: PenDescendantOverride's object
  replacement form is a raw .pen shape, and nothing in EditOperation can express it.

Atomic: run on `EditableDocument(from: document.materialize())`, capture the
TRANSLATED [EditOperation] per line, and on full success replay those onto the real
document. Replay (not hand-back) because EditableDocument is an @Observable
reference callers hold, and the copy has no crdtDocument or layout cache. Replaying
the translated ops rather than the BatchOperations keeps the generated PenIDs stable
between the trial and the real run.

Cascade: a failed line poisons its tag, its addresses as written, and the ids they
resolved to. A later line touching any of those (target, parent OR source) is
cascaded, and poisons the same way, so the chain propagates.

Read the seams. Key finding before writing a line: in CRDT mode `applyLocal` calls
`crdtDocument.processLocal` FIRST and then swallows any throw from `apply()` (it
reconciles and returns the ops anyway). So a guard that only lives in `applyDelete` /
`applyOverrideDescendant` would be silently bypassed by `applyLocal` — the delete would
still tombstone and replicate. Every guard therefore runs as a pre-flight in `applyLocal`
before `processLocal`, and again inside `apply` for the non-CRDT path.

Design:
- `EditOperation.DeleteNode.Instances` (`.refuse` / `.detach`), default `.refuse`;
  custom Codable so `instances` is optional on the wire.
- New `Editing/EditableDocument+Guards.swift`: `instanceIDs(ofComponent:)`,
  `instancesToDetach(for:)`, `validateOverrideTarget(_:)`,
  `overridableDescendantKeys(ofComponent:)` (recurses through nested refs, using
  `inspectComponent`), and a shared `descendantIDs(of:)` replacing the two private
  copies in +Apply and +Detach.
- Guard 1 covers the whole deleted subtree, counting only instances that SURVIVE the
  delete — instances inside the doomed subtree are not stranded.
- Guard 3 (cycle) already exists in `applyMove`; tests are regression pins.
- Detaching delete gets `deleteNode(_:) -> [DetachResult]` mirroring `detachRef(_:)`,
  and `completeDetachingDeleteInverse(detached:partialInverse:)` mirroring
  `completeDetachInverse`.

Design settled (before writing code):

- Rects from PenLayoutEngine are ALREADY parent-relative (`layout()` doc comment +
  layout-absolute.layout.json confirm it), so no conversion is needed. The brief's
  "convert to parent-relative" step is a no-op.
- `EditableDocument.computeLayout()` takes no theme, and `expandedDocument()` strips
  reusables (so component definitions get no rect). TreeView therefore runs its own
  side-effect-free pipeline: materialize -> PenRefExpander.expand(keepReusables: true)
  -> PenVariableResolver.resolve(theme:) -> PenLayoutEngine.layout. Same rects as
  computeLayout() for every non-reusable node; additionally gives components rects.
- Expanded node ids: an instance descendant is `refID/<descendantKey>`, which equals
  `ResolvedNodeAddress.address` exactly. The instance ROOT is the anomaly: its expanded
  id is `refID/<componentRootID>` (PenRefExpander.prefixIDs uses component.id), while
  its address is just `refID`. TreeView walks the FLAT store and derives expanded ids
  from a ref-id prefix chain, so it needs componentRootID (follow the ref chain through
  componentRegistry, mirroring PenRefExpander.expandRef).
- Row id = unique handle (flat id at top level, expanded id inside an instance);
  address = namePath at top level, id-path inside an instance. Both resolve.
- Identity columns (type/name/reusable/instance/childCount/address) come from the flat
  store (that is what an edit addresses); rect + property columns come from the settled
  resolved document (that is what is rendered).

Claimed. Read the harness, the regression suite, the SleepyHollow finding, and SleepyHollow's PageHost/PageHost+Scripting.

Findings so far (pre-measurement):
- `PageHost` supports repeated `load(_:)`: `isLoading` only forbids *concurrent* loads on one host, and `navigateAndSettle` resets facts/failure state per navigation. Injected scripts are WebKit user scripts installed at init, so they re-run on every document; the console capture buffers page-side, so it resets with the document. `messages(named:)` sinks are removed on stream termination, so per-render subscription on a shared host does not leak.
- The budget is fixed at `PageHost.init`, so a reused host must be keyed by budget.
- The likely dominant cost is the page, not Swift: every fixture HTML loads `babel.min.js` (3.0 MB) + `tailwindcss.js` (407 KB) and transpiles the emitted TSX in-browser, per test. Reusing one web content process should let WebKit's memory/bytecode caches carry that across loads.
- Second candidate: `loadDocuments()` re-parses the 244 KB .pen fixture and re-runs resolve + ref-expand + resolve per test, and `ComponentAnalyzer`/`PageAnalyzer`/`ThemeAnalyzer`/`ReactEmitter`/`PenLayoutEngine.layout` all re-run per test on identical input.

Added `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PhaseStopwatch.swift` (flag-gated on `WOODCASE_TEST_PROFILE`) and laps in `WebViewTestHarness.render` and both `compare*` helpers. Measuring the before profile next.

Done and verified. New files:
  Sources/Woodcase/Tree/{TreeRow,TreeReport,SettledTree,TreeView,TreeFormatter}.swift
  Tests/WoodcaseTests/{TreeViewTests,TreeFormatterTests}.swift
  Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/tree-overflow.pen

section + Topics group). No existing source file changed.

24 new tests; full suite 1859 tests pass (`swift test --quiet`, exit 0); swiftformat
clean.

Deviations worth the integrator's attention:
- `TreeView.rows(...)` THROWS (the brief's signature did not). An unresolvable `root`
  must raise addressNotFound/ambiguousAddress, not return an empty listing.
- `TreeFormatter.json(_:revision:)` takes the revision (the brief wrote `json(_:)`,
  which has nowhere to get it from). The wire shape is a public `TreeReport` struct so
  the CLI leaf decodes the same type the formatter encodes.
- `TreeRow.rect` is `PenRect?`, not four Doubles: reuses the existing struct rather
  than a twin, and `nil` beats a zero rect standing in for "no layout".
- Layout does NOT come from `computeLayout()` — see the earlier note. `SettledTree`
  runs materialize -> expand(keepReusables: true) -> resolve(theme:) -> layout.
- The text form gains a header line ONLY when property columns are requested, plus a
  `*` type prefix for a component definition and a `+N` name suffix for children the
  listing hides. Without properties it is rows only, ~55 chars.

Integration note for the CLI leaf: `tree` should pass `--json` through
`TreeFormatter.json(rows, revision: document.documentRevision)` and print

over `[TreeRow]`; the verb holds no decisions.

passed (exit 0). Nothing in this leaf touches existing sources, and gotchas.md already

Activity log built on branch worktree-agent-a1bf166672627a006.

New files: Sources/Woodcase/Files/{ActivityEvent,ActivityEvent+Codable,ActivityLog,ActivityReader,ActivityRecorder}.swift; Tests/WoodcaseTests/{ActivityEventTests,ActivityLogTests,ActivityReaderTests,ActivityRecorderTests}.swift; Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/WoodcaseActivityLog.md. Modified: Files/PenFileTransaction.swift (the seam), Files/PenFileError.swift (doc broadened — it now names the log too), Documentation.docc/{Woodcase,EditingDocuments}.md, README.md.

Shape. ActivityEvent is Friendly with custom Codable pinning the wire format: time (ISO-8601 UTC ms), identity, file, op, nodes, paths, inverse, revision, batch — sorted keys, unescaped slashes, one line. identity is a plain String (the --as name), NOT a PeerID: PeerID carries only a UUID rawValue and no display name, so a peer id would say nothing to a log reader; the CLI maps the same name to a PeerID where the CRDT needs one. op is ActivityEvent.Kind, derived from EditOperation with a caller override so undo/cp label themselves.

Seam. PenFileTransaction gained an OVERLOAD, run(at:identity:log:timeout:_:), whose body is (EditableDocument, ActivityRecorder). The existing run(at:timeout:_:) is unchanged and delegates to it with identity nil — deliberate, so the batch-applier leaf (Fmyjz) that is compiling against the old signature right now does not break. recorder.apply(op, expecting:, as:) takes the inverse first, applies, then reads name paths from whichever side of the edit still has the node, and stamps documentRevision per op. Events are appended only after write(_:replacing:) succeeds; identity nil, a throwing body, or a no-op transaction all append nothing.

Log/reader. flock(2) on the log file via FileLock; rotation at 8 MB renames to activity.<basic-ISO>.jsonl under the lock and recreates the live file immediately (the append loop retries, which also absorbs another process's rotation window). Reader takes no lock: it stops at the last newline, so a partial trailing line is never consumed. Page carries events/nextOffset/restarted/skippedLines. follow() (AsyncStream, polled) IS included.

Verification: swiftformat . --lint clean; swift test --quiet green, 1870 tests, exit 0; DocC builds with no warnings. Red confirmed first (20 "cannot find in scope" errors before the sources existed). Both criteria tested: three ops through the recorder -> exactly three events with the revision after each; the reader resumes from an offset without re-reading.

Foundation trap worth a gotcha (not filed, to avoid a conflict on gotchas.md with the other live leaves): Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true) TRUNCATES the fraction rather than rounding, so a Date built from x.123 formats as ".122". ActivityEvent assembles the milliseconds itself and rounds on both encode and decode so a line round-trips to an equal event.

data.text:
Batch applier built and green. 17 new files under Sources/Woodcase/Batch/, 5 test
files, 1 fixture, 1 DocC article; the only existing file touched is
Documentation.docc/Woodcase.md (topics index). Nothing in Files/, Editing/ or
TreeRow*.

Suite: swiftformat . --lint clean; swift test --quiet = 1888 tests / 175 suites
passed (97s). Batch tests alone: 55 passing. Red was confirmed first — the three
test files would not compile against the missing BatchApplier/BatchOperation/
BatchReport.

All four leaf criteria are covered by named tests:
  8Kj badOpInTheMiddle
  jnv cascadeByTag (plus cascadeByAddress, cascadeChain, cascadeBySharedTarget)
  sKt atomicDiscardsEverything (plus atomicAppliesOnFullSuccess,
      atomicReportsTheRealIDs)
  8WY retryReRunsOnlyWhatFailed (plus retrySeesEarlierTags, retryNoop)

Findings for the integrator:

1. PenID.remapIDs avoids collisions only WITHIN the subtree; it never consults the
   document. applyInsert's validateNoDuplicateIDs makes a collision loud rather
   than corrupting, but EditableDocument.detachRef has the same exposure and is
   unfixed. BatchApplier.remapped(_:avoiding:) redraws until disjoint from
   document.allNodeIDs.

2. EditingError.componentHasInstances exists but nothing throws it, so today
   {"op":"rm"} without "detach" on a component with instances succeeds and orphans
   the instances. The detach path is tested; the refusal is pending leaf zF7AK.
   Once that lands, a test for the refusal should be added here.

3. `set` and `override` cannot share one property vocabulary: a ref's descendants
   map is keyed by raw .pen names ("content"), not NodePropertyCodec paths
   ("kind.content"). Each verb now refuses the other's target with a message
   naming the right verb.

4. BatchOperation.decodeJSONL throws for a malformed line — that is a file that
   will not parse, not a report line. The CLI leaf should map it to a usage-class
   exit code, not to a per-line failure.
