Both criteria marked passed. `swiftformat Sources Tests --config <worktree>/.swiftformat
--lint` clean; `swift test --quiet` green — 1856 tests in 173 suites, 44.2 s.

Guards, all three:
1. `deleteNode` refuses when the deleted subtree defines a reusable component whose
   instances SURVIVE the delete, throwing `componentHasInstances`. Instances inside the
   doomed subtree do not count — they go away with it. New typed constant
   `EditOperation.DeleteNode.Instances` (`.refuse` default / `.detach`) detaches the
   survivors first instead.
2. `overrideDescendant` refuses a `descendantID` that names nothing in the referenced
   component, listing every overridable node as a `NodeAddressCandidate`. Nested keys
   (`"inner/label"` — a node inside a ref inside the component) are validated and listed
   the same way, matching `PenRefExpander`'s cross-ref prefixing exactly.
3. The cycle guard already existed in `applyMove`; the three new tests are regression
   pins (green on first run — said out loud, per the brief).

The load-bearing finding: `applyLocal` runs `crdtDocument.processLocal` FIRST and then
swallows a throw from `apply(_:)` (it reconciles and returns the ops anyway). A guard
living only in `applyDelete` / `applyOverrideDescendant` would therefore have replicated
the very edit it refused. Both guards run as a pre-flight in `applyLocal` before
`processLocal`; two tests pin that the operation log and the tombstone set stay empty
after a refusal.

New public API: `EditableDocument.deleteNode(_:) -> [DetachResult]` (mirrors
`detachRef(_:)`; `applyDelete` calls it and discards) and
`completeDetachingDeleteInverse(detached:partialInverse:)` (mirrors
`completeDetachInverse`). `prepareInverse(of: .deleteNode)` now returns the restore plus
one re-insert per instance; the completion splices in the deletes of the expanded roots.

One behaviour change to an existing test, deliberate: `EditOperationOverrideTests`'s
"different descendant" case overrode `"icon"`, which the component did not contain —
it was asserting the silent no-op this leaf exists to abolish. The component now has a

data.text:
applyLocal now fails closed via a shared validation pass, not a second copy of the guards.

Design: every guard apply(_:) enforces moved into EditableDocument+Validate.swift as
small `require*`/`validate*` helpers. Each apply* calls the helper for its own
operation (so a refused apply still leaves the document untouched), and applyLocal
calls `validate(_:)` for the whole operation *before* crdtDocument.processLocal. No
guard is written twice. The pre-flight special case for overrideDescendant is gone;
the deleteNode-with-stranded-instances routing and detachRef decomposition stay,
relabelled as the behaviour they are.

Red evidence (swift test --filter ApplyLocalFailClosedTests, before the change):
18 of 32 scenarios failed — every one where processLocal mutates before apply()
throws (move parent/cycle/index, insert parent/index, and all nine
variable/import/theme LWW cases: those emit an op unconditionally, so an
addVariable on an existing name replicated while the local call "succeeded").
The other 14 were already closed by CRDTDocument's own `guard nodes[id] != nil`.

Two real bugs found and fixed on the way:
1. applyMove with a NEGATIVE index trapped (Swift/Array.swift:431 "Negative Array
   index is out of range") — it only checked `index <= count`. It killed the whole
   test process during the red run. Now invalidIndex, like insert.
2. applyMove checked the index AFTER removing the node from its old parent, so a
   move with an out-of-range index left the node detached from the tree. The index
   is now checked up front against the count the destination list will have once the
   node has left it (a move within one parent shortens the list it lands in).

Suite: 1973 tests pass in 17.5 s (swift test --quiet). swiftformat clean.

data.text: Integrator carve 2026-08-29: EnTjY owns the WoodcaseViewer target's creation (Package.swift: target + Elementary branch/exact pin per Ben's approval), the Network.framework HTTP/1.1+SSE server, the file watcher, the warm render cache, the JSON/PNG/SSE endpoints, and a route table that pages and fragments plug into. ExnBl (page) later adds Components/, Pages/, Styles/, Client/ and registers routes; it must not need to touch Server/. Rendering goes through PenRenderer directly (RenderCommand.swift is the reference pipeline); ImageExporter stays in WoodcaseCommand for the shot verb — the viewer encodes PNG itself (ImageIO) or a small shared encoder is lifted into the library in a new file.

Shared CLI seams landed (branch worktree-agent-a8a3f2faae617705f). What a verb author calls:

FILE ARGUMENT
  @Argument var file: PenFilePath        // ExpressibleByArgument, never fails to parse
  let url = try file.existingFile()      // run time; missing/dir/unreadable -> CommandFailure(exit 4)
  Rationale: existence is a fact about the world, not about the invocation's shape, so it is
  NOT a ValidationError (which ArgumentParser turns into a usage exit). Missing file = 4, always.

OPTION GROUPS
  @OptionGroup var identity: IdentityOptions   // --as <name>; identity.identity -> String?
                                               // falls back to $WOODCASE_AS; blank = unset;
                                               // nil is legal (edit applied, not logged)
  @OptionGroup var output: OutputOptions       // --json -> Bool

EXIT CODES  (ExitCode+House.swift)
  ExitCode.success/.cleanNegative/.usage/.conflict/.targetFailure/.environment = 0..5
  WoodcaseCommand now defines its own `main()`: ArgumentParser's 64 (EX_USAGE) is translated to
  2 once, for every verb. Verified by a test that drives the binary with a bogus verb.
  A verb never invents a number: throw one of these, or a CommandFailure.

FAILURE MAPPING  (CommandFailure.swift) -- the design decision the ten leaves inherit
  Two entry points, because BatchErrorMessage needs the document and the document only exists
  inside the transaction body:
    @MainActor CommandFailure.describing(error, in: document, editing: url)   // inside the body
    CommandFailure.describing(error, editing: url)                            // outside it
  The verb pattern is: catch INSIDE the transaction body, wrap into a typed CommandFailure
  carrying the rendered message, and let it travel out. A CommandFailure passes through the
  outer mapper unchanged, so nothing is double-mapped.
    func run() async throws {
        let url = try file.existingFile()
        try await runReportingFailures(editing: url) {
            try await PenFileTransaction.run(at: url, identity: identity.identity) { doc, rec in
                do { ... } catch { throw CommandFailure.describing(error, in: doc, editing: url) }
            }
        }
    }
  runReportingFailures is an extension on ParsableCommand: it prints the message on stderr and
  throws the ExitCode; ExitCode and CleanExit thrown by the body pass straight through.
  Table: PenFileError cannotOpen/unreadable/writeFailed -> 4; lockTimeout -> 3 (message names
  `lsof <path>`); ANY PenFileError naming a file OTHER than `editing:` -> 5, and the message says
  the edit is on disk and names the log file (that is the discriminator for a log-append failure,
  which the transaction raises after the .pen is committed); EditingError.revisionConflict and
  BatchError.documentRevisionConflict -> 3; every other EditingError/BatchError -> 2;
  ValidationError -> 2; anything unrecognised -> 5 (deliberately not 1, which scripts branch on,
  and not 2, which would blame a possibly-good invocation).
  Pass `editing:` ONLY for the .pen file that transaction was running against.

WRITE OUTPUT
  CreatedTreeFormatter.text([CreatedNode]) -> "Card  ALu8G\n  Title  x9Kqp"  (2 spaces/level,
  2 spaces before the id, no trailing newline/space, unnamed node shows #id)
  CreatedTreeFormatter.json([CreatedNode], revision:) -> {"created":[...],"revision":"..."}
  StandardError.write(_:) for anything that is not the answer.

RECORDER HOOK  (BatchApplier)
  apply(_:to:atomic:identity:recorder:) and retry(...recorder:) take an optional ActivityRecorder
  (default nil, existing callers unchanged). Chosen over rebuilding events from
  BatchLineResult.inverse because the recorder already owns inverse-first / paths-after ordering.
  Every edit that reaches the REAL document goes through recorder.apply. A line is the unit of
  both rollback and logging: perform() takes a checkpoint (recorder.events.count) and calls the
  new internal ActivityRecorder.discardEvents(after:) when the line unwinds, so a half-applied
  line leaves zero events. unwind() goes straight to the document and records nothing. Atomic:
  the staged run on the deep copy gets recorder = nil (the copy is not the recorder's document);
  replay onto the real document records, and drops its events if the replay fails.
  So a mutating verb is: one-line batch through BatchApplier.apply(..., recorder: recorder)
  inside PenFileTransaction.run(at:identity:) -- the log entry is free.
  NOTE: `identity: PeerID?` on the applier is CRDT peer identity, unrelated to --as. Untouched.

TESTS
  Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/CommandFixture.swift: copies a fixture from
  Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures into a temp dir, makes a temp $WOODCASE_HOME (and HOME), runs the
  built binary, returns CommandRun{status,stdout,stderr} (Friendly). Binary found via
  $WOODCASE_BINARY, else the .xctest bundle's directory, else #filePath-relative .build/{debug,release}.
    let fixture = try CommandFixture(fixture: "batch.pen")
    let run = try fixture.run("tree", fixture.file.path, "--json")
  Cleans up in deinit. In-process `Verb.parse([...])` tests stay right for flags.

Suite: 2030 tests pass (`swift test --quiet`), swiftformat clean, DocC builds with no warnings.

WoodcaseBatches.md gained "Logging a batch".

data.text:
Addendum — the custom main() changes the existing verbs' exit codes, deliberately.

Before, ArgumentParser's main() exited 64 for a malformed command line and 1 for any error a
verb's run() threw. Now: 64 -> 2, and an unmapped error -> 5. So render/themes/generate move too.
To keep that honest rather than merely different, the mapper gained two rows with tests:
  PenParserError (any case)      -> 4  (was 1; `woodcase themes /nope.pen` now exits 4)
  ThemePinParser.PinError        -> 2  (a malformed --theme value is a usage error)
Still falling through to 5: RenderCommand.RenderError, ImageExporter.ExportError,
PDFExporter.ExportError. Those are verb-local; whoever next touches render/shot should decide
between 4 and 5 for them and add a row. Not a hidden failure — 5 says "unclassified", which is
the point of the default.

One more visible change: a verb failure now prints its bare message on stderr, where
ArgumentParser used to prefix "Error: ". Usage errors still get ArgumentParser's full message
(with the "Error:" line and the usage block), because that text is what teaches the invocation.

`vars` design decisions (varser, leaf vAEwr)

SURFACE
  woodcase vars <file> [--json]                                  # list (default subcommand)
  woodcase vars set <file> name=value [--theme axis=value] [--type T] [--as n] [--json]
  woodcase vars rm  <file> name [--force] [--as n] [--json]
  woodcase vars axis add <file> axis=opt,opt [--as n] [--json]
`vars` is an ArgumentParser parent with `defaultSubcommand: VarsList`, so a bare
`vars <file>` lists. Cost: a .pen file literally named `set`, `rm` or `axis` would be
read as a subcommand. Documented, not defended against.

VALUE TYPING (VariableValue.swift)
The type is: `--type` if given, else the EXISTING variable's type if the name is already
defined, else inferred from the literal. The value is then validated against that type,
and a mismatch is a usage error (2) naming both. Consequences worth knowing:
  - `set spacing=16` on an existing STRING variable stores the string "16" — the
    variable's declared type wins over inference, which is what keeps a themed variant
    from silently changing a variable's type out from under its references.
  - `--type` is the only way to make a string variable whose value looks like a number
    or a colour. Without it that shape is unreachable, which is why it exists.
Inference, in order: `#RGB` / `#RRGGBB` / `#RRGGBBAA` (case-insensitive, `#` REQUIRED)
-> color; `true` / `false` -> boolean; anything `Double(_)` parses -> number; everything
else -> string. A leading `$` is a reference to another variable and takes that
variable's type (usage error if that variable is undefined and no `--type` is given).
NOTE: the brief said "colour `#hex`/rgba". `rgba(...)` is NOT accepted — the 2.17 schema
says `Color = #RGB | #RRGGBB | #RRGGBBAA` and `PenColorParser` reads only those, so a
`rgba(0,0,0,.5)` written here would be unreadable by Pen.app and by our own renderer.
The 8-digit form IS the rgba case. `#` is required so that a bare `abc` stays a string.

THEMED VALUES (schema: value is `V | {value: V, theme?: {axis: option}}[]`)
  --theme axis=value, variable absent   -> .themed([{value, theme: pin}])
  --theme axis=value, variable .simple  -> .themed([{value: old, theme: nil},   <- the
                                                    {value: new, theme: pin}])     old
                                           value becomes the DEFAULT variant, so nothing
                                           that referenced it changes meaning.
  --theme axis=value, variable .themed  -> replace the variant whose `theme` equals the
                                           pin exactly, else append.
  no --theme, variable .themed          -> update-or-insert the variant with theme==nil
                                           (the default), leaving the themed variants
                                           alone. It does NOT collapse to .simple.
  no --theme, otherwise                 -> .simple(value)
Variant ORDER is preserved on write (last match wins during resolution, so reordering
would change rendering).
Axis registration on the fly, as Pen does: an unknown axis is created with the one
option named; a known axis missing the option gets it APPENDED (never reordered — the
first option is the default active theme).

REFERENCE WALK (Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+VariableReferences.swift)
Chosen: re-encode each flat-store PenNode to JSON, decode as AnyCodable, and collect
every string leaf of the form `$<name>` where `<name>` is a DEFINED variable.
Rejected: reusing `PenVariableResolver`'s walk. It is ~600 lines of hand-written
per-kind traversal (`resolveFrameData`, `resolveShaderUniform`, `resolveEffect`, …) with
no collection hook; a second copy would drift the first time a property is added.
The JSON scan is exactly faithful to `PenValue`'s own decoder, which turns ANY leading-`$`
string into `.variable(name)` — so it cannot disagree with the parser — and it gets ref
node overrides (`NodeOverrides`, `PenDescendantOverride`) and shader uniforms for free.
Children are stripped in the flat store, so no node is counted twice.
Restricting to DEFINED names is what keeps `"$186"` (a real dollar amount in the text of
`woodcase-app.pen`, which our own parser reads as `.variable("186")`) out of the counts.
Nodes are reported in document order (DFS over rootOrder/children), so the refusal
message reads top-down.
Variable-to-variable references count too (`PenVariableResolver.resolveChains` resolves
`"$other"` chains), reported separately from node references.

rm GUARD
Refused with exit 2, not 1: the seams table already maps `componentHasInstances` — the
same shape of consequence refusal — to 2, and cli-design's "4 instances would be
detached; pass --detach" is the same sentence. 1 is a clean negative (a check that ran
and said no), which this is not: it is an invocation missing a flag. No EditingError
case was added; the guard is a CLI-side `CommandFailure` over a library fact
(`variableReferences()`), because `--force` is a CLI affordance and the batch grammar
deliberately has no variable removal to guard.

themes vs vars: `themes` should fold into `vars` and be retired. See the report.

Undo semantics chosen (undoer, 2026-08-29)

`woodcase undo <file> [-n N] [--as name] [--all] [--json]`

THE RULE (one pass, newest-first, over the activity log's events for this file,
read INSIDE the .pen lock so nothing can be appended between the read and the check):

    var sawUndo = false
    for event in events.reversed() where undone < N {
        if event.op == .undo        { sawUndo = true; continue }        // transparent
        if !all, event.identity != me { stop(.blockedByOther(event)) }  // exit 3
        if event.revision != document.documentRevision {
            if sawUndo { continue }                                     // already undone
            stop(.blockedByStale(event))                                // exit 3
        }
        for op in event.inverse { recorder.apply(op, as: .undo) }
        undone += 1
    }

Why each clause:

1. An `undo` event is STEPPED OVER, never replayed. Replaying an undo's inverse is a
   redo, and `undo` is not `redo`. This is the brief's "refuse to undo an undo",
   implemented as "skip", because the brief also asks for "the last N non-undo events
   NOT ALREADY UNDONE" — and reaching an already-undone event's predecessor requires
   walking past the undo. Refusing outright would make `undo` single-shot per file
   forever: the first undo would poison the tail and no later invocation could ever
   reach the edit before it. See DEVIATIONS in the report.

2. The revision check is the whole safety property, and it is exact, not a guess: an
   event's recorded `revision` is the document revision AFTER that op, so
   `document.documentRevision == event.revision` proves the file is in precisely the
   state that event produced, and its `inverse` therefore restores precisely the state
   before it. After undoing event k the document revision equals event k-1's recorded
   revision, so contiguity is self-enforcing — no separate "is this a contiguous tail"
   bookkeeping exists or is needed.

3. `sawUndo` is the one heuristic. Once the scan has passed an undo event, a candidate
   whose revision does not match is assumed to be one that undo already reversed, and
   is stepped over rather than treated as a conflict. Without the latch a mismatch is
   a hard conflict (exit 3): the file moved outside the log. Cost of the latch: on a
   file that has ever been undone, external tampering surfaces as "nothing left to
   undo" (exit 1) rather than a stale conflict (exit 3). A precise alternative needs a
   link from an undo event back to the event it reversed — a new wire field — which
   this leaf is not allowed to add. Reported as a possible seams change.

4. Another identity's event blocks IMMEDIATELY, before the revision check, so the
   message can name the person rather than only the hash. `--all` makes every
   identity's events candidates (undo events stay transparent for every identity).

5. Identity is REQUIRED (exit 2 with a message) even with `--all`. An unattributed
   undo applies the inverse and logs nothing, which silently breaks the invariant the
   revision check rests on — the log's tail no longer describes the document — and the
   next undo would fail as a stale conflict with no way to see why. Undo is a write,
   and every write is attributed.

EXIT CODES
  0  at least one event undone (a stop after >= 1 prints its reason on stderr and
     still commits: throwing would discard the undos already applied in the same
     transaction, and losing good work to report a conflict is worse)
  1  nothing to undo — no events for this file/identity, or everything already undone
  2  no identity, or -n < 1
  3  nothing undone because another identity edited later, or the revision is stale
  4/5 from the shared CommandFailure mapper (missing file, unwritable log)

OUTPUT
  one row per undone EVENT (not per inverse operation), newest first:
      add  ana  2026-08-29T18:40:55.900Z  Canvas/Badge
      revision 6c1f0a…
  Columns are op, identity, time, path — free-text path LAST, so a naive splitter
  still gets the three fields it branches on. `--json`:
      {"file":…,"revision":…,"undone":[{"identity":…,"nodes":[…],"op":…,"paths":[…],"time":…}]}

Design settled before code (linter, leaf odhm5).

FACT CHECK on the brief's check (a). The pipeline's PenDiagnosticCollector does NOT
carry "broken refs" or "unresolved variables" — nothing in the pipeline emits those.
The only emitters are: PenParser+VersionGate (migration-stage warnings), the migration
rules, GoogleFontResolver.prepareFonts (font resolution, which needs the NETWORK), and
the React emitters. So (a) is split in two:
  - `DocumentLinter.findings(..., diagnostics: [PenDiagnostic] = [])` maps whatever
    pipeline diagnostics the CALLER collected into findings (check id `pipeline`,
    severity from the diagnostic). The `lint` verb passes the version-gate warnings
    from a PenParser.parse it runs with a collector.
  - broken refs and unresolved variables become real library checks, computed from the
    settled tree, because the pipeline never reports them.
  - MISSING FONTS: no offline check is possible. Deciding whether "Manrope" is a typo
    or a downloadable Google family needs a network fetch (no local catalog exists),
    and PenTextMeasurer.fontFamilyAvailable alone would flag every downloadable font.
    So `lint` stays offline and reports fonts only via supplied diagnostics; a caller
    that has run GoogleFontResolver (render, Penumbra) passes them in.

CHECKS (id, severity): pipeline (from the diagnostic) | broken-ref (error) |
unresolved-variable (error) | text-without-fill (warning) | fill-in-fit-parent
(warning) | empty-fit-content (warning, only when fit_content has NO fallback — with a
fallback the size is well defined) | clipped (warning).

AGREEING WITH `tree`'s CLIP FLAG, structurally rather than by convention: the linter
walks TreeView's own rows and reads `row.clip`. TreeView gains an internal
`rows(of:settled:...)` overload taking a prebuilt SettledTree so one read runs the
pipeline once; the public `rows(...)` delegates to it. No clip computation is copied,
forked or re-derived.

SIZING likewise: PenLayoutEngine gains internal `widthSizing(of:)`/`heightSizing(of:)`
over its own private extractLayoutProperties, so the linter reads the engine's real
defaults (an absent width is fit_content; a group is always fit_content) instead of
mirroring them in a twin.

SCOPE: lint does not expand instances. A component definition is linted once, at its
definition, rather than once per instance — no duplicate noise, and no row whose parent
is a ref. Overrides that only misbehave in one instance are therefore not linted; that
is a documented limitation, not an oversight.

PixelPeeper half landed on branch `overlay` (NOT committed, NOT pushed). 177 tests / 26 suites green (was 124 / 20).

Dependency line for Woodcase's Package.swift — matches the https+branch form Woodcase already uses for sleepyhollow:

    .package(url: "https://github.com/bensyverson/PixelPeeper.git", branch: "main")

(PixelPeeper's own remote is the SSH form `git@github.com:bensyverson/PixelPeeper.git`; the repo name is capitalised. Product name is `PixelPeeper`, library target `PixelPeeper`.)

API — all on the library target, `import PixelPeeper`. `pixelsPerPoint` is image px per source unit; `origin` is the source coordinate of the image's top-left pixel (a crop offset). Labels are ALWAYS printed in source units. All three throw.

    // PixelImage+Grid.swift
    func withGrid(_ options: GridOptions = GridOptions(),
                  pixelsPerPoint: Double,
                  origin: CGPoint = .zero) throws -> PixelImage
    // PixelImage+Outlines.swift
    func withOutlines(_ outlines: [Outline],
                      pixelsPerPoint: Double,
                      origin: CGPoint = .zero) throws -> PixelImage
    // PixelImage+Labels.swift
    func withLabels(_ labels: [OverlayLabel],
                    pixelsPerPoint: Double,
                    origin: CGPoint = .zero) throws -> PixelImage

    struct GridOptions: Friendly {
        enum Mode: String, Friendly, CaseIterable { case rulersAndLines = "lines"; case rulers }
        init(mode: Mode = .rulersAndLines, step: Int = 100)   // step is in SOURCE units
    }
    struct GridLayout: Friendly {            // geometry, no rasterizing — assert against this
        struct Tick: Friendly { let position: Int; let pixelOffset: Double; var label: String }
        let leftGutter, topGutter, imageWidth, imageHeight: Int
        let columns, rows: [Tick]
        var width: Int { imageWidth + leftGutter }   // == the gridded image's size
        var height: Int { imageHeight + topGutter }
        init(imageWidth:imageHeight:options:pixelsPerPoint:origin:)
        static func ticks(fromOrigin:acrossPixels:pixelsPerPoint:step:) -> [Tick]
        static func labelWidth(_:) -> Double
        static var minimumGutter/labelInset/tickLength: Int
    }
    struct Outline: Friendly {
        init(rect: CGRect, color: PixelColor? = nil, label: String? = nil, width: Double = 2)
        func pixelRect(pixelsPerPoint: Double, origin: CGPoint = .zero) -> CGRect
    }
    struct OverlayLabel: Friendly {          // named OverlayLabel, not Label: SwiftUI clash
        init(text: String, position: CGPoint, color: PixelColor? = nil)
        func pixelPosition(pixelsPerPoint: Double, origin: CGPoint = .zero) -> CGPoint
    }
    extension PixelColor { public var cgColor: CGColor }
    // New PixelPeeperError cases: .invalidOverlayScale(Double), .invalidGridStep(Int),
    //                            .overlayRenderFailed(width:height:)

Guarantees Woodcase can rely on:
- `withGrid` RETURNS A LARGER IMAGE: width + leftGutter, height + topGutter. Predict it with
  `GridLayout(...).width/.height`. So `shot --grid --max N` will exceed N by the gutter —
  say so in the help text, and grid AFTER the --max fit or the numbers scale to mush.
- In `.rulers` mode the image area is byte-identical to the input (blit, not redraw), so a
  gridded shot can still be MAE-diffed against an un-gridded one after cropping the gutter.
- An outline's ring is drawn wholly OUTSIDE `rect` (four filled bands, not a stroke), so the
  node's own edge pixels survive. Default colour is a two-tone ring: inner half near-black,
  outer half white, total thickness == `width`.
- `withOutlines`/`withLabels` return the same size as the input.

Woodcase wiring: `shot --max` gives pixelsPerPoint = rendered px / layout pt; pass the ratio
you ACTUALLY landed on after the fit, not the one you asked for. The viewer's click-outline
calls `withOutlines` on the server-rendered PNG with the same ratio.

Also added `peep outline in.png --rect x,y,w,h --scale 2 --out o.png` (thin adapter, ~125 lines,
repeatable --rect/--label, --origin x,y, --color hex, --width px, --raster-scale for PDF input).
NOTE the flag collision: `--scale` here is pixelsPerPoint; PDF rasterization is `--raster-scale`
(the older `peep grid` uses `--scale` for the PDF meaning). No `peep grid --labelled` added —
the existing `peep grid --spacing/--color` is the pixel-space overlay and stays as it is.

Snapshot goldens committed at Tests/PixelPeeperTests/Fixtures/overlay-{grid,outline}-golden.png,
re-bless with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 swift test --filter OverlaySnapshotTests`. Tolerance is MAE 0.02,
verified to bite (a step 25→26 change scores 0.756).

WARNING for the integrator: PixelPeeper's HEAD already fails `swiftformat . --lint` on 23 files

Server leaf progress 1/3 (server, as=server).

Package.swift: new target `WoodcaseViewer` (Sources/WoodcaseViewer) + test target
`WoodcaseViewerTests`; Elementary pinned `exact: "0.8.1"` (0.x — a minor bump can break
the API), on the viewer target only. Resolves clean.

The route-table seam the page leaf (ExnBl) uses — no file under Server/ needs editing:

    var pages = ViewerRoutes()
    pages.add(.get, "/") { request in .html(DashboardPage(...).render()) }
    pages.add(.get, "/files/{file}/outline") { request in .html(...) }
    let server = ViewerServer(pages: { context in pages })

- `ViewerRoutes.Handler = @Sendable (ViewerRequest) async throws -> HTTPResponse`
- `ViewerRequest` = `.http` (method/segments/query/headers), `.parameters` (captured),
  `.context`; helpers `file()`, `theme()`, `integer(_:minimum:)`.
- `ViewerContext` = `files: ViewerFileIndex`, `renders: RenderCache`, `log: ActivityLog`,
  `events: SSEHub` (+ `activity: ActivityReader`).
- Precedence is registration order and the server registers pages FIRST, so a page
  route shadows the placeholder `/` and `/files/{file}` without removing anything.
- Pattern grammar: literal segments, `{name}` whole-segment, `{name}.png` param + literal
  suffix. No wildcards.
- Path segments are percent-decoded ONE BY ONE, so an artboard id containing a slash
  (a top-level ref expands to `YGJ0d/nSNTs`) rides in one segment as `YGJ0d%2FnSNTs.png`.
  Page links must percent-encode artboard ids.

SSE event shape (`/events`, `text/event-stream`, heartbeat comment `: heartbeat` every 15 s):

    id: 12
    event: change
    data: {"artboards":["Cnv01"],"file":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","identity":"ana","nodes":["jSUCH"],
           "op":"set","paths":["Canvas/Title"],"path":"/abs/path.pen",
           "revision":"3f2a91c0d4e5b678","time":"2026-08-29T16:31:04.123Z"}

    event: presence
    data: {"identities":[{"events":12,"lastSeen":"…","name":"ana"}]}

Two names only (`SSEEvent.Name`: change, presence); times are the activity log's exact
ISO-8601 ms form.

`?theme=` accepts BOTH `Mode:Dark,Base:Slate` (the design doc's form) and the CLI's
`Mode=Dark`, so neither spelling is ever wrong.

Also lifted `PNGEncoder` into the library (Sources/Woodcase/Rendering/PNGEncoder.swift):
`encode(_:) -> Data` for the viewer, `write(_:to:)` for files; `ImageExporter` is now a
3-line delegation.

`woodcase activity` built on branch worktree-agent-a463fffc2f65bc705.

New files: Sources/WoodcaseCommand/{ActivityCommand,ActivityRowFormatter}.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/{ActivityCommandTests,ActivityRowFormatterTests}.swift.
Modified: Sources/WoodcaseCommand/WoodcaseCommand.swift (added Activity.self to
subcommands).

Grammar: `woodcase activity [--as name] [--json] [--file path] [-n/--count N]
[--follow]`. Reuses IdentityOptions/OutputOptions/PenFilePath verbatim. `--file` never
calls existingFile() — the filter works whether or not the file still exists. `-n`
defaults to 50, negative is a usage error (exit 2).

Home-directory check: activity never edits a .pen file, so a PenFileError reading the
log always maps to exit 5 (environment) naming $WOODCASE_HOME, never exit 4 — that's a
deliberate divergence from CommandFailure's general editing:-file mapping, since there
is no .pen file being edited here. A missing or unreadable $WOODCASE_HOME directory is
checked explicitly before the read (exit 5); an empty log (home exists, no
activity.jsonl yet) is exit 0 with no output, per ActivityReader's own contract.

Row format: `HH:mm:ss(local) | identity | verb(padded to 8, widest Kind) | path`,
first path +N when several, `-` when the event touched no node. --json prints each
ActivityEvent's own wire-format line (round-trips via ActivityEvent(line:)).

Verified both stated criteria: `--file` narrows to one file's events including after
that file is deleted (fileFilterSurvivesDeletion); `--follow` sees a new event within
~1s via a real Process + polling read loop, bounded generously at 30s per the gotchas
on wall-clock assertions under a loaded suite.

Suite: 2053 tests (`swift test --quiet`), swiftformat clean. 17 new tests, all green
on first run — implementation was authored alongside the tests before the first build,
so no separate red pass was observed; the tests do reference types (`Activity`,
`ActivityRowFormatter`) that did not exist before this session.

Known friction for the integrator: IdentityOptions' own `--as` help text ("Who to
attribute this edit to...") is wrong on this read-only verb, where --as is a filter.
ArgumentParser's @OptionGroup has no per-usage help override, so I documented the
distinction in Activity's CommandConfiguration.discussion (shown in --help's OVERVIEW,
above OPTIONS) rather than forking the shared type. Worth a seam-level fix later:
IdentityOptions could take a role (attribution vs. filter) that swaps the help text.

DocC: not touched, per brief. Proposed addition for whoever next edits
WoodcaseCLI.md: a `### activity` section under `## Commands`, alongside `render`,
`themes`, `migrate`.

`tree` and `get` landed on branch worktree-agent-a2acadae3da948f19 (from 046861a).

BOTH CRITERIA MET
- xSD "tree on a fixture prints one row per node with rect and clip flag; --json is
  machine-parseable": `tree batch.pen` prints a `rev <hash>  9 rows` header and 9 rows
  (one per node), each with the settled rect; `tree tree-overflow.pen` flags `⚠ partial`
  and `⚠ clipped`. `--json` decodes as the library's own `TreeReport`.
- jyQ "get prints the node's revision alongside its JSON": first line is
  `<id-address>  <name path>  rev <16 hex>`, then the node in canonical .pen JSON.
  `--json` is `{"node":{…},"revision":"…"}` (`NodeReport`).

NEW FILES
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/{TreeCommand,GetCommand,NodeLookup,NodeReport,CanonicalJSON}.swift
  Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/{TreeCommandTests,GetCommandTests}.swift
Modified: WoodcaseCommand.swift (one subcommands entry: `Tree.self, Get.self,` at the
front) and Sources/Woodcase/PenParser.swift (see DEVIATIONS).

DECISIONS THE NEXT VERB AUTHOR INHERITS
- Text header carries the revision: `rev <documentRevision>  N rows` for `tree`;
  `<address>  <name path>  rev <nodeRevision>` for `get`. First whitespace field of a
  `get` header is an address that resolves; `awk '{print $2}'` on `tree`'s gets the rev.
- `get` prints the STORED node, children stripped — `tree` is the structural read.
  `--expand` prints the node as it renders (children included, refs expanded, overrides
  applied), via `PenRefExpander.expand(materialize(), keepReusables: true)` — the same
  pipeline `SettledTree`/`TreeView` use, so `tree --expand` ids and `get` agree exactly.
- An address inside an instance (`Nav/Badge/Count`) has no stored node, so it is always
  answered from the expanded tree, and its revision is the REF NODE's — that is where an
  override to it is written, so it is the token an `override --rev` must quote.
- `--props` uses the `NodePropertyCodec` vocabulary, which is PREFIXED: `kind.content`,
  `common.name`. A bare `content` silently produced a column of dashes, so `tree` now
  writes one line to stderr per requested path that no row carries, naming the prefixes.
  stdout and the exit code are untouched (an empty column is legitimate).
- `CanonicalJSON.text(_:)` is the CLI's one way to print .pen JSON — sorted keys,
  two-space indent, `"key": value` — over `PenParser.encodeForFile`. Use it for anything
  a caller might paste back into a file or hand to `-F`.

DEVIATIONS
- `PenParser.encodeForFile(_ document: PenDocument)` is now
  `encodeForFile(_ value: some Encodable)`. It was the only canonical writer and its
  key-separator tightening is file-private, so a node fragment could not be printed in
  the file's own form without either this one-word generalization or a second, drifting
  copy of the algorithm. Source-compatible: every existing call still passes a
  PenDocument.

BUG FOUND, NOT FIXED
- `EditableDocument.expandRef(nodeID:)` builds a single-entry registry
  (`[refData.ref: materializedComponent]`), so a ref NESTED inside that component does
  not expand: on addressing.pen, expanding `Nav01` leaves `Nav01/Bdg01` as a `ref`.
  `expandSubtree`/`expandedDocument` route through it and inherit the hole.
  `PenRefExpander.expand` over the whole document is correct, which is why this leaf uses
  it. Worth a leaf of its own.

TESTS: 28 new (13 `tree`, 15 `get`), all driving the built binary. Red first: with the
verbs unregistered every one failed with ArgumentParser's "unexpected arguments"; the
only test green on its first real run was none — one (`--props`) failed on the property
vocabulary and was corrected along with the verb's help.
Full suite 2064 tests pass (`swift test --quiet`, exit 0) on the third run; two earlier
runs each failed with ONE issue in an untouched suite — WebViewRegression's
`__READY__` timeout, then `PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests` compute count — both under
eight-agent load, both green when re-run. That is QGISs, not this leaf.

Single-op verbs landed on branch worktree-agent-ae18586077795e1e9 (from 046861a). Suite: 2103 tests / 203 suites pass (`swift test --quiet`, 107 s), swiftformat --lint clean, DocC builds with only the two pre-existing EditableDocument `validate(_:)` warnings.

CRITERIA
- AIZ: each of add/set/cp/mv/rm/override has a green end-to-end test and at least one usage-error test whose message names the remedy (AddCommandTests.unnamedNodeIsUsage, SetCommandTests.missingEqualsIsUsage + unknownPropertyIsUsage + insideAnInstanceIsUsage, CopyCommandTests.unknownNamePathOverride + unknownSourceIsUsage, MoveCommandTests.intoAnInstanceIsUsage + indexOutOfRange, RemoveCommandTests.refusesAComponentWithInstances, OverrideCommandTests.outsideAnInstanceIsUsage + noPropertiesIsUsage).
- oOv: AddCommandTests.autoPlacesAtTheRoot — `add … document` with no x/y lands at x=800, y=0 (Board's right edge 700 + the 100 gap), asserted on the re-parsed file.
- 1qR: CopyCommandTests.namePathOverrideHitsTheCopy — `cp batch.pen Canvas document common.name=Copy Title/kind.content=Copied` gives Copy/Title "Copied" and leaves Canvas/Title alone.
- yxG: staleRevision in Set/Move/Remove/Override — exit 3, message "Canvas/Title (Ttl01) has changed: rev was 0000000000000000, the node is now 62b06f8ec3102d5c".

VALUE PARSING (PropertyAssignment) — the rules, printed in every verb's help as `PropertyAssignment.valueRules`:
Only the FIRST `=` splits, so a value may contain more. Then, in order:
  ""              -> the empty string
  null            -> JSON null, which CLEARS the property
  true / false    -> boolean
  starts [ { "    -> parsed as JSON; invalid JSON is a usage error naming the key.
                     The `"…"` form is the escape hatch: `common.name="42"` is the string 42.
  starts with a digit, -, + or .   -> Int if it parses, else a FINITE Double
  anything else   -> string
A colour (#ff8800), a variable reference ($brand) and the sizing keywords
(fill_container / fit_content) are all strings in a .pen file, so they need no syntax of
their own and fall out of the last rule. The numeric guard is deliberate: `Double("nan")`
and `Double("infinity")` both parse in Swift, so a value is only tried as a number when it
starts like one, and a non-finite result falls through to string. A key given twice is
refused rather than silently keeping one. `-F props.json` supplies a JSON object of the
same key/value pairs; a `key=value` on the command line wins over the same key in the file.

SEAM CHANGES (additive, all three want a second opinion)
1. NEW `BatchApplier.applyOne(_:to:recorder:)` (Batch/BatchApplier+Single.swift) — applies one
   operation and THROWS what it refuses instead of reporting it. Chosen over adding a typed
   `failure:` field to BatchLineResult: the CLI's exit-code mapping already keys on error TYPE
   (CommandFailure.describing), so handing it the real EditingError/BatchError needs no lossy
   classification in the library and no second copy of the table. `perform` went from private
   to internal for it; nothing else in BatchApplier changed.
2. `BatchApplier.createdTree(rootID:in:)` is now public (was internal). `cp` applies descendant
   properties after the copy line, so the tree the verb prints has to be re-read from the
   document, not taken from the line's own `created`.
3. NEW WoodcaseCommand/CommandRemedy.swift — three BatchErrorMessage remedies are written in
   batch dialect (`set "detach": true`, `{"op":"override",…}`, `{"op":"set",…}`) and are wrong
   at a shell prompt. The CLI re-phrases exactly those three; everything else falls through to
   CommandFailure.describing untouched. The proper fix is a dialect parameter on
   BatchErrorMessage so there is one copy of each sentence — flagged, not done, because that
   file belongs to the `apply` leaf's blast radius.

FINDINGS
- `cp` of a root artboard lands EXACTLY ON TOP of its source. BatchApplier+Placement leaves a
  node alone if it declares either coordinate, which is right for `add` (the author was being
  specific) but wrong for `cp`, where the coordinates came from the source, not the caller.
  `cp batch.pen Canvas document` puts the copy at 0,0 over Canvas. Recommend: a root-level `cp`
  auto-places regardless of the source's declared x/y. Not changed here — it is the applier's
  documented rule and outside this leaf.
- EditingError.revisionConflict's message ends "re-read it and rebuild this line", which is
  batch dialect too; left alone as it is only a tail.
- No test drives `-F -` (stdin): CommandFixture.run has no stdin hook, and adding one would
  edit a file every verb leaf shares. The path is two lines in InputFile.

`woodcase apply` built and green.

New: Sources/WoodcaseCommand/ApplyCommand.swift, BatchReportFormatter.swift;
Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/ApplyCommandTests.swift, BatchReportFormatterTests.swift.
Registered `Apply.self` in WoodcaseCommand.swift's subcommands.

Seams change (both criteria need it): BatchLineResult gained `isRevisionConflict: Bool`
(default false) so a CLI can turn a report into an exit code without parsing message
prose. Set in BatchApplier's two failure sites via a new private
`isRevisionConflict(_:)` helper (true for EditingError.revisionConflict or
BatchError.documentRevisionConflict). Covered by 3 new assertions in the existing
BatchApplierRetryTests/BatchApplierTests (Woodcase target).

Found and fixed a real bug while wiring the outside-document CommandFailure mapper:
`describing(_:editing:)` rendered a bare BatchError via its raw enum description
("malformedLine(line: 2, reason: ...)") instead of BatchErrorMessage's prose, because
BatchErrorMessage only exposed a document-taking `describe(_:in:)` — even though no
BatchError case actually touches the document. Added a `nonisolated public static func
describe(_ error: BatchError) -> String` and pointed both the dispatcher and
CommandFailure's outside-body case at it. Regression test added in CommandFailureTests.

Exit codes: 0 all applied; 3 if any FAILED line's isRevisionConflict is true; 1 for any
other failed/cascaded mix; malformed JSONL never opens the document, exits 2 naming the
line (1-based, from decodeJSONL's existing convention).

Text report format is 0-based `line N` (matches BatchApplier's own embedded
atomic-cascade message, which already says "line N failed" 0-based — a 1-based header
would visibly disagree with the sentence beside it).

ENDPOINTS (documented in Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/WoodcaseViewer.md):

    GET /files                                  FileListReport
    GET /files/{file}/tree.json                 ?node= ?depth= ?expand ?props= ?theme=
    GET /files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}.png  ?theme= ?max=
    GET /files/{file}/activity.json             ?limit=

with what the tree verb will print. File ids are 12 hex chars of FNV-1a over
`ActivityEvent.canonicalPath(for:)`. PNG carries X-Woodcase-Scale / -Width / -Height /
-Revision so an overlay maps pixels back to layout points; scale = min(2, max/longestSide).

Times use the activity log's ISO-8601-with-ms form, so a stock JSONDecoder FAILS on them.

equivalent too — the strings are the log's strings.)

INTEGRATION NOTE for the later `serve` verb leaf — the whole adapter:

    // Package.swift: add "WoodcaseViewer" to WoodcaseCommand's dependencies.
    struct Serve: AsyncParsableCommand {
        @Argument var files: [String] = []
        @Option var port: UInt16 = 0
        func run() async throws {
            let server = ViewerServer()          // pages: { _ in ViewerPages.routes() } once ExnBl lands
            let bound = try await server.start(files: files.map { URL(fileURLWithPath: $0) }, port: port)
            print("http://127.0.0.1:\(bound)/")
            try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(.max))   // or a signal source; stop() on exit
        }
    }

No files given => the index adopts every .pen file the activity log has seen.

TWO THINGS THE NEXT PERSON SHOULD KNOW (both cost time here):

1. An SSE response needs `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. HTTP/1.1 with neither a length nor
   chunking is delimited by connection close, so URLSession (and any conforming client) may
   buffer the WHOLE stream until then — the events arrive only when the server stops.
   `NetworkSSEWriter` does the chunk framing; the hub still writes plain SSE text.
2. `AsyncLineSequence` (`bytes.lines`) DROPS EMPTY LINES, and an empty line is exactly what
   ends an SSE frame. A client written on `.lines` never sees a complete event. Parse raw
   bytes and split on "\n\n" — ViewerServerTests does.

FOR ExnBl: percent-encode artboard ids in links. A top-level component instance expands to
an id containing a slash (`YGJ0d/nSNTs`), so the URL is
`/files/{file}/artboards/YGJ0d%2FnSNTs.png`. The server decodes path segments one at a time,
so an encoded slash stays inside the id — but a link that does not encode it 404s.

Woodcase.md Topics += WoodcaseEditor, WoodcasePerformance. README: Install section, the three-command agent loop, two new doc links. AGENTS.md project-owned head: one line for WoodcaseEditor.md under the DocC line (decision: yes — it is the one article addressed *to* an agent rather than about the library; the generated regions were not touched). backlog.md: four dated H2s from the handoff's § Follow-ups (themes folding into vars; --library on the read verbs; a revision on lint --json; an `undoes` link on undo events). Checked `job ls --issues` first — none duplicate AzXzQ or vq4Lp.

INSTALL VERIFIED, with a wrinkle worth keeping. `swift package experimental-install --product woodcase` REFUSES over an existing copy: "error: woodcase is already installed at /Users/ben/.swiftpm/bin/woodcase". The installed binary was from 2026-03-27 and offered only `render` and `themes`. I ran `swift package experimental-uninstall woodcase` then re-installed; `~/.swiftpm/bin/woodcase --help` now lists all 18 verbs, exit 0. The two-command upgrade is documented in both README and WoodcaseCLI.md. Criterion RhS met.

DocC: `swift package generate-documentation --target Woodcase` exits 0 with THREE warnings — the two pre-existing `validate(_:)` ones on EditableDocument+Apply/+CRDT (reported as pre-existing by SLVVe, vAEwr and odhm5; NOT fixed here, those files are outside this leaf's carve — a two-character fix for whoever owns them next), plus `'WoodcasePerformance' doesn't exist at '/Woodcase'`. That third one is the deliberate forward link the brief asked for; it resolves the moment 2U9E0's WoodcasePerformance.md merges. Zero warnings from WoodcaseEditor.md or WoodcaseCLI.md.

WRITTEN FROM THE BRIEF, NOT VERIFIED (they do not exist on this branch — integrator should reconcile the wording against the owning agents' notes at merge): the `serve` row and `### serve` section; the `help` row and `### help` section; `shot --grid/--outline` (documented as "grid grows the image past --max by the gutters" and "outline draws a labelled box on the node's rect" — on this branch both flags are still usage errors naming leaf qh4W1); and the README/Woodcase.md links to WoodcasePerformance.md.

BUG FOUND, NOT FIXED — worth an issue. `woodcase shot` cannot render ANY top-level frame of banking.pen. Every one of them is a reusable component definition, and `ShotCommand.render` calls `PenRefExpander.expand(...)` (which drops reusables) before `PenLayoutEngine.layout`, so the id it then looks up has no rect: "nSNTs has no computed layout rect." — and that message maps to exit 5 (environment), which is also wrong; it is a target or usage failure, not a broken environment. The refusal-with-a-list path still names those same frames as the ones to pick, so the tool sends you somewhere it cannot go. `shot` works normally on batch.pen, whose roots are ordinary frames, and that is the fixture the docs use. Reproduce: `woodcase shot banking.pen banking-home --out x.png`.

Two smaller findings, both now documented rather than filed: Pen's variable names begin with `--`, so `vars set/rm` need the end-of-options marker (`woodcase vars rm f.pen -- --foreground`) or ArgumentParser reads the name as a flag; and the property-path vocabulary uses the model's field names, so it is `kind.fills`/`kind.effects` even though the file writes "fill"/"effect" — `kind.fill` is refused.

data.description: Found by the docs agent (RXaYR, 2026-08-29) verifying WoodcaseEditor.md against the binary. In banking.pen every top-level frame is a reusable component definition. `woodcase shot banking.pen banking-home --out x.png` prints "nSNTs has no computed layout rect." and exits 5, because ShotCommand.render runs PenRefExpander.expand (which drops reusables) before PenLayoutEngine.layout, so the rect lookup misses. Two bugs: (1) the no-node refusal lists those same frames as the ones to pick, so the tool sends you where it cannot go — it should either lay out the reusable as-is (render a definition like an artboard, which is what an agent wants) or say the node is a definition; (2) exit 5 means environment; this is a target/usage failure. Regression test first, on banking.pen. shot works on batch.pen.

data.text:
Help that teaches — built on wt/helper (worktree .claude/worktrees/helper), from 0158471.

NEW FILES
  Sources/Woodcase/Batch/RemedyDialect.swift
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/HelpCommand.swift        (`woodcase help`)
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/HelpTopic.swift          (the `design` topic, 45 lines)
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/IdentityRole.swift       (the three --as roles)
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/ThemeOption.swift        (one --theme declaration)
  Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/EditingErrorRemedyTests.swift
  Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/HelpCommandTests.swift
DELETED
  Sources/WoodcaseCommand/CommandRemedy.swift      (replaced by the dialect)

THE ERROR CONVENTION (documented on BatchErrorMessage, enforced by
EditingErrorRemedyTests). Every refusal is one sentence in three parts:
  1. the subject — a name path where the node is in the document, otherwise the
     address, id or key exactly as typed;
  2. what happened, present tense;
  3. the remedy, separated by " — " and carrying at least one BACKTICKED literal:
     the `woodcase` command to run, or the exact text to write.
The backtick is the machine-checkable part. The test walks every EditingError case
(21) and every BatchError case (7) through CommandFailure.describing and asserts all
three, plus: a remedy that names a `woodcase` command WITH an operand names the file
it runs against. subject(of:) switches exhaustively on both enums, so a new error
case cannot be added without the suite failing to compile.

THE DIALECT (SLVVe's flagged duplication, now removed). RemedyDialect is .batch or
.command(file:). BatchErrorMessage.describe(_:in:dialect:) writes the same statement
either way and switches only the tail: `{"op":"override","target":…}` in a batch
file, `woodcase override <file> <addr> name=value` at a prompt. CommandFailure passes
.command(file:) always, so the CLI's three re-phrasings in CommandRemedy are gone and
each sentence exists once, in the library. Batch report lines keep .batch (the
default), so BatchApplier is untouched.

MESSAGES CHANGED (all 28 cases; every one gained a " — " remedy and a backticked
literal, and these also changed shape):
  unknownProperty     statement is now just "<key> is not a property of a <type>";
                      the accepted paths moved into the remedy and are backticked
                      individually, so a caller can paste one.
  ambiguousAddress    "matches N nodes: …" (was " — … — "), remedy names #<id>
  addressNotFound     remedy: `woodcase tree <file>` (batch: the @tag route)
  componentHasInstances  "as plain nodes: …"; remedy `--detach` (batch: `"detach": true`)
  invalidIndex        "position N is out of range"; remedy `--at` (batch: `"at"`)
  revisionConflict    remedy `woodcase get <file> <id>` (batch: rebuild with `rev`)
  parentInsideInstance  keeps the word "detach" as a FACT ("only a detached instance
                      holds children of its own") rather than as advice — there is no
                      standalone detach verb, only `rm --detach` on the component.
  cannotHaveChildren, wouldCreateCycle, nodeNotFound, parentNotFound, duplicateNodeID,
  notARefNode, propertyTypeMismatch, variable*/themeAxis*/import*, malformedLine,
  unnamedNode, setInsideInstance, overrideOutsideInstance, documentRevisionConflict,
  couldNotGenerateIDs — all reworded to the convention.
  import{Not,Already}Exists are the two cases with no `woodcase` command in the
  remedy: no verb reads or writes the imports map, so they point at the document's
  `imports` map instead of inventing a command. Flagged, not faked.

IDENTITY ROLES (xqgcQ + Cv7KU friction). ArgumentParser fixes an option's help at the
type's DECLARATION, not its use, so a role parameter cannot reach it — IdentityOptions
is now generic: IdentityOptions<Identity.Attribution|Filter|Required>, with the help
text on the role. undo says "undo refuses without one", activity says "Show only this
writer's events", every editing verb keeps "the edit is applied but not logged".
IdentityOptions.environmentVariable moved to Identity.environmentVariable.

HELP
  `woodcase` bare / `--help`: a primer — what the tool is, the verbs in four groups
  (read / write / render / view, with `serve` listed although another agent is
  building it), "START HERE with woodcase tree design.pen", a pointer to
  `woodcase help design`, and the house exit-code table. Exit 0.
  `woodcase help`: lists topics, needs no file. `woodcase help design`: 45 lines,
  ≤96 columns — flex-first, naming, the six address forms, the two property
  vocabularies, batch tags, the read-write-verify loop.
  Our `help` SHADOWS ArgumentParser's built-in help subcommand (a user-declared
  subcommand is added to the tree first). `woodcase help tree` and
  `woodcase help vars set` still work: a subject that is not a topic is resolved
  against the subcommand tree and rendered with ParsableCommand.helpMessage(for:).
  A subject that is neither exits 2 naming both routes.

VERB HELP
  Every abstract now states its class: "Read:" / "Write:" / "Render:" (vars, a group,
  says "Read and write:"). Every verb has one worked example; render, themes,
  generate react, migrate, vars list, vars rm, vars axis add and apply had none.
  --theme was declared three different ways in three files: it is now one shared
  ThemeOption group (tree, lint, render). "Path to the .pen file…" argument help
  unified to "The .pen file to …".

TESTS: 349 in WoodcaseCommandTests (36 suites) green; +29 new (22 help/remedy/identity
plus the dialect and file-naming checks). swiftformat --lint clean.

FOR THE INTEGRATOR
  - ShotCommand.swift untouched (another agent owns it). It wants:
    abstract "Render: one node of a .pen file to a PNG.", a discussion saying it is
    the cheap sibling of `render`, a worked example, and @OptionGroup var themePin:
    ThemeOption in place of its own --theme declaration (ShotCommand.swift:137 then
    becomes ThemePinParser.parse(themePin.theme)). Its @Argument help should read
    "The .pen file to render." not "Path to the .pen file to render."
    Two HelpCommandTests lists (classedVerbs, verbsWithExamples) exclude "shot" with a
    comment; add it once ShotCommand is updated.
  - `serve` is named in the primer text but is not in the subcommands list; when
    ServeCommand lands nothing in the primer has to change.
  - DocC (owned by the docs leaf): add ``RemedyDialect`` beside ``BatchErrorMessage``
    in Woodcase.md and WoodcaseBatches.md; WoodcaseCLI.md wants a `help` row and a
    paragraph (in the report).
  - render / themes / generate still take a bare String path rather than PenFilePath,
    so a missing file fails differently there than on every other verb. Out of scope
    here; worth a leaf.
  - CommandFailure.describing(_:editing:) (no document) still renders a bare
    EditingError as "\(error)" — no path, no remedy. Unreachable today because every
    verb wraps inside its transaction, but it is the one hole in the checklist.
  - FLAKE: the full-suite run wedged once at ActivityCommandTests.
    followSeesNewEventsPromptly, Process.waitUntilExit() after terminate(), 0% CPU,
    child already gone (sample in the scratchpad). Pre-existing, load-related, and it
    passes in every filtered run.

CRITERIA

        every case, representative payload, through CommandFailure.describing; asserts
        the subject, the " — " remedy clause and a backticked literal.
        remediesNameTheFile adds: a remedy naming a command with an operand names the

data.text:
Performance budget landed on wt/budgeter. `swift test --quiet` = 2415 tests / 239 suites green in 31.8 s; `swiftformat . --lint` clean; `scripts/mae-check` reports no regressions and performance/mae-baseline.csv is byte-identical.

BUDGETS (release ceilings; asserted verbatim when built release, x2.5 debug multiplier otherwise)
  tree woodcase-app.pen        300 ms  (leaf)   measured release 196 ms
  set  woodcase-app.pen        200 ms  (leaf)   measured release 114 ms
  shot one artboard, warm      1 s     (leaf)   measured release 102 ms
  tree synthetic 5000 nodes    400 ms  (measured ceiling, ~40% headroom)
  set  synthetic 5000 nodes    800 ms  (measured ceiling)
  shot synthetic artboard      1 s     (leaf number stands; 272 ms release-equivalent)

MEASURED, in process, debug, minimum of 5, serialized, load avg 13:
  tree woodcase-app 410.5 ms | tree synth 593.0 | set woodcase-app 143.2 | set synth 1244.8
  shot woodcase-app 369.4 ms | shot synth 569.3

COMMANDS
  swift test --filter Performance 2>&1 | grep BUDGET
  WOODCASE_TEST_PROFILE=1 swift test --filter Performance 2>&1 | grep PROFILE
  scripts/perf-binary --config release   (and --config debug)

BLOCKER FOR THE INTEGRATOR: `swift test -c release` DOES NOT RUN in this package. The
release test bundle's entry point resolves to woodcase's own ArgumentParser:
"Error: Unknown option '--test-bundle-path' / Usage: woodcase <subcommand>". The debug
bundle runs fine and both carry _WoodcaseCommand_main, so it is a packaging problem,
not a test one. Release figures therefore come from scripts/perf-binary (new). The
brief's "VERIFIED FACT: swift test -c release works here" is wrong.

BUDGET WAS INITIALLY MISSED, AND FIXED AT SOURCE: tree woodcase-app.pen first measured
365 ms release against its 300 ms ceiling. The phase profile put 492 of 715 debug ms in
PenRefExpander.expand; the cause was PenNodePatcher.patchNode JSON-encoding a node's
ENTIRE SUBTREE to merge a few keys, with overrides applied at instance roots — renaming
one label re-serialized a whole screen. Lifting children off before the round trip and
back after (semantically identical: a JSON merge only touches keys it names) took
expand 492 -> 187 ms, tree 715 -> 411 ms debug, 365 -> 196 ms release. Guarded by the
new Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenNodePatcherTests.swift (8 tests); MAE unchanged.

TWO woodcase shot BUGS FOUND (not fixed; ShotCommand is another agent's surface):
  1. shot resolves the AUTHORED node id in the layout rects, but PenRefExpander re-ids
     an instance root to "<refID>/<component root id>". Every artboard in
     woodcase-app.pen is a ref, so `woodcase shot woodcase-app.pen "<any artboard>"`
     fails with "<id> has no computed layout rect" (exit .environment). The verb cannot
     render anything in the largest fixture in the repo.
  2. Naming a reusable component DEFINITION fails the same way for a different reason
     (expansion strips definitions), and the error explains neither case.
Both are written up in WoodcasePerformance.md under "Known issues these measurements
surfaced".

FILES: Tests/WoodcaseTests/Performance/{PerformanceBudgets,PerformanceBudget,
PerformanceSample,PerformanceFixture,SyntheticPenDocument,PerformanceTreeBudgetTests,
PerformanceSetBudgetTests,PerformanceShotBudgetTests}.swift;
Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenNodePatcherTests.swift; scripts/perf-binary;
Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/WoodcasePerformance.md (new);
Sources/Woodcase/PenNodePatcher.swift + scripts/README.md (modified).

INTEGRATION: Woodcase.md Topics needs "- <doc:WoodcasePerformance>"; README doc list
needs the matching line. Both left to their owner.

Exact cause, from the performance agent (2U9E0): PenRefExpander re-ids an instance root to `<refID>/<component root id>`, but shot looks up the authored id in the layout rects — so it fails with "has no computed layout rect" for every top-level `ref`, not only for reusable definitions. In woodcase-app.pen every artboard is a ref and every top-level frame is a definition, so shot can render nothing in that file. Fix in ShotTargets/ShotCommand: resolve the expanded id (ResolvedNodeAddress.address already yields the post-expansion form for instance descendants; the instance root itself needs the same mapping), and treat a reusable definition as renderable. PerformanceShotBudgetTests shows the working lookup.

data.description: Found by the performance agent (2U9E0, 2026-08-29). `swift test -c release` builds and then fails to run: the release test bundle's entry point resolves to the woodcase executable's ArgumentParser main ("Error: Unknown option '--test-bundle-path' / Usage: woodcase <subcommand>"). The debug bundle runs; both carry _WoodcaseCommand_main, so it is packaging (the @main executable target linked into the test bundle in release), not the tests. Until it runs, PerformanceBudget.isOptimized never asserts the leaf's release ceilings verbatim; scripts/perf-binary is the only source of release figures. Likely fix: keep WoodcaseCommandTests from linking the executable's main in release (a `WoodcaseCommandCore` library target with the executable as a one-file shim is the house shape anyway), or check SwiftPM's -enable-testing behaviour for executable targets in release.

Suite: 2494 tests / 245 suites pass in 19.4 s (`swift test --quiet`, sandbox off); `swiftformat . --lint` clean; DocC builds with no new warnings. BOTH CRITERIA MET, in a real headless browser (Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/ViewerBrowserTests.swift, SleepyHollow `PageHost`, server on port 0 over a fixture copy): - ACT: an edit made by `PenFileTransaction.run` reaches an open page and swaps the outline, the activity feed and the render's edit markers. Proved to be *without a reload* by a `window.__probe` set before the edit and asserted after it — a reload would wipe it. - qwZ: clicking an outline row outlines that node over the render, names its path in the footer with a copy button carrying the same string, pushes `?node=`, and keeps `__probe`. WHAT WAS BUILT - `Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Components/` — ActorColor, RelativeAge, ViewerClock, ViewState, ViewerLink, AvatarView, PresenceStack, OutlineRow, OutlinePanel, ViewerVariable, VariablesPanel, ActivityRow, ActivityFeed, ThemePicker, TopBar, FileRow, FileList, EditMarker, ArtboardOverlay, SelectionBar, RenderRegion. - `Pages/` — ViewerDocument (the shell), DashboardPage, ArtboardPage, EmptyPage, ArtboardLayout, ArtboardPageBuilder, PageData, ViewerPages (the route table). - `Styles/ViewerStylesheet.swift`, `Client/ViewerScript.swift` (Swift strings, served). - `Sources/WoodcaseCommand/ServeCommand.swift`; `Serve.self` added to the subcommand list. - 21 golden HTML previews in `Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/`. FIVE THINGS THE NEXT PERSON SHOULD KNOW 1. **A page route at `/files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}` shadows the PNG endpoint.** `{name}` is a whole segment, so it also matches `Cnv01.png`, and pages register first. `ViewerPages.routes()` therefore claims `/files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}.png` FIRST, handing it to `ViewerEndpoints.artboard`. Registration-order precedence is a real trap for any future page route that sits beside a `{name}.ext` route; a most-specific-first matcher in `ViewerRoutes.match` would remove the whole class. 2. **There is a fifth fragment: `/files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}/render`.** It returns `#v-render-region` — the image, the overlay boxes, the inline layout JSON and the selection footer. It exists so the client never re-derives an identity's hashed colour or an absolute layout rect: the markers and the selection box are server-rendered, and `viewer.js` only fades and pins them. Without it the script would need a JS twin of `ActorColor` and of `ArtboardLayout`'s origin-accumulating walk. 3. **`PenLayoutEngine` rects are parent-local; the overlay needs absolute.** `ArtboardLayout.of(artboard:in:scale:)` walks the artboard's subtree accumulating origins exactly as `PenRenderer` translates by each rect as it descends, and computes `TreeRow.Clip` on the way, so the selection footer says "clipped" without a second read. It reads children through `PenNode.Kind.inlineChildren`, which was already public (it sits in a `public extension`) — the only change to `Sources/Woodcase/` in this branch is one doc sentence saying so. 4. **`X-Woodcase-Scale` is a render *density*, not a display size.** Sizing the stage by it drew a 400×300 artboard at 800×600 CSS px. The page now ships `--v-scale: 1` (CSS px per layout point) with the `` laid out at the artboard's point size, so a 2× PNG is downsampled; `viewer.js` lowers `--v-scale` to fit the pane, and every box follows because every box is placed in points and multiplied by it. `data-density` carries the render density for anyone who needs it. 5. **A verb that never exits must `fflush(stdout)`.** `woodcase serve | head -1` hung because stdout is block-buffered when it is not a terminal and the process never ends. Recorded in `project/gotchas.md`. TWO SEAM NOTES FOR THE INTEGRATOR - `ViewerEndpoints.files` now delegates to `PageData.files(_:)`, which the dashboard page also calls — one producer for the file report instead of two implementations that agree today. That is a 25-line deletion inside `Endpoints/`, which the brief reserved; the alternative was duplicating the whole gather in `Pages/`. - `PlaceholderPage.swift` and its two tests in `ViewerEndpointsTests` are gone. VERB-TABLE ROW for WoodcaseCLI.md (integration note; that file is another agent's): | `serve` | Serve a local web view of the .pen files you are working on | `woodcase serve design.pen --port 7333 --open` | VARIABLE ATTRIBUTION: an `ActivityEvent` for a variable write records NO node ids (`ActivityEvent.nodeIDs(touchedBy:)` returns `[]` for every variable/import/theme op), so the VARIABLES section's last-editor comes from the event's **inverse operations**, which name the variable. If the log ever grows a `subjects` field, that is the better source.

Done on wt/pather (worktree .claude/worktrees/pather), not committed.

render, themes and generate react now take PenFilePath and call existingFile() before
anything else, so a missing file, a directory or an unreadable file is the house exit 4
with the remedy ("Cannot open X: no such file. Check the path — `ls DIR` lists what is
there.") that every other verb gives. Behaviour otherwise unchanged (--library, --vars,
--vars-file, --output-dir, --package/--preview). One fix falls out of the check order:
`generate react --force` no longer wipes the output directory before discovering the
input is not there. Tilde-quoted paths now expand on these three, as elsewhere.

CommandFailure.describing(_:editing:) — the no-document overload — now renders an
EditingError through BatchErrorMessage in RemedyDialect.command(file:), against a
private empty EditableDocument (`noDocument`). Nodes fall back to the id as typed,
which is how BatchErrorMessage already renders a node missing from the real document,
and the statement + remedy come out whole. That required marking the overload
@MainActor; the two call sites (ParsableCommand+Failures, WoodcaseCommand.
exitReportingHouseCode) are already on MainActor, so nothing else moved.

Red first: 8 new tests, all observed failing before the change (missing-file remedy on
each of the three verbs, directory case on each, --force output dir, and two
CommandFailureTests for the bare EditingError). Full suite: 2543 tests / 254 suites
pass; swiftformat --lint clean (0/618).

Two findings, NOT fixed, worth their own leaves:
1. `woodcase migrate /nowhere/gone.pen` exits 2 (ValidationError + a usage block), not
   4. migrate takes directories so PenFilePath.existingFile() does not fit it, but
   "no such path" is still a world question. Its row in WoodcaseCLI.md says `0 2 4`
   while it actually returns 1 when a file fails to migrate and never 4.
2. A .pen file that exists but will not decode exits 4 with "Failed to decode .pen
   document: …" — no path, no next step. PenParserError.decodingFailed carries no URL,
   and render/themes/generate do not pass `editing:`, so the mapper cannot add one.
