data.text:
Most-specific-first route matching, on branch wt/router (worktree .claude/worktrees/router). Not committed.

What changed
- Route gains a public `specificity: Route.Specificity` (Friendly, Comparable), computed once in
  `init`. Specificity holds one `Rank` per segment — `.capture` < `.suffixedCapture` < `.literal` —
  and compares lexicographically left to right; equal-length equal-shape patterns compare equal, so
  ties fall through to registration order. Different segment counts (which can never both match one
  path) are ordered by count only to keep Comparable total.
- ViewerRoutes.match now scans every entry and keeps the highest-specificity method-matching one,
  strictly greater so an equally specific earlier registration keeps the path. 405/Allow and
  GET-answers-HEAD unchanged: `allowed` is still every path-matching entry under another method,
  and it was already only consulted when nothing matched.
- ViewerPages.routes() no longer registers `/files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}.png` — it holds page
  routes only. ViewerEndpoints keeps the single PNG producer.
- Docs: ViewerRoutes header ("Precedence is specificity, then registration order"), match(_:),
  add(contentsOf:), ViewerPages and ViewerEndpoints headers, and WoodcaseViewer.md § Adding pages
  (now a rank table plus the ties rule).

Red/green
- With the workaround removed and the matcher untouched, ViewerPagesTests.pngStillWins failed with
  Content-Type application/json (the page route captured "Cnv01.png"). After the matcher change it
  passes.
- The three new ViewerRoutesTests ordering cases (suffixed beats bare, literal beats capture, first
  differing segment decides) were red against the old matcher and green after.

Tests added
- RouteTests: ranksSegmentsByHowNarrowlyTheyMatch, comparesSegmentsLeftToRight,
  equalShapesAreEquallySpecific.
- ViewerRoutesTests: suffixedCaptureBeatsBareCapture, literalBeatsCapture,
  theFirstDifferingSegmentDecides, registrationOrderBreaksTies, plus a private `text(_:_:)` helper.
  The existing "first registered wins" case was reworded to "at equal specificity".

Suite: `swift test --quiet` — 2541 tests in 253 suites, 1 issue: PerformanceSetBudgetTests
"set transaction on a synthetic 5000-node document" (2626 ms vs a 2000 ms debug limit). It passes
alone — `swift test --quiet --filter PerformanceSetBudgetTests` reports 1767 ms — so it is machine
load under the parallel run, not this leaf. Everything else green. `swiftformat . --lint` clean
(0/617).

Also seen, unrelated: an earlier full run wedged for 6+ minutes at 0% CPU in
WoodcaseCommandTests/ActivityCommandTests.followSeesNewEventsPromptly (ActivityCommandTests.swift:259);
sampled, killed by pid, and the rerun passed it. Worth a look by whoever owns the activity verb.

Criteria: LLG and 2S0 both met.

New evidence 2026-08-29 (wave 3/4 agents): (1) ActivityCommandTests.followSeesNewEventsPromptly (ActivityCommandTests.swift:259) wedged two separate full runs at 0% CPU — Process.waitUntilExit() after terminate(), child already gone — sampled and killed by pid both times; rerun passed. Suspect: the test's teardown races the child's exit; use a bounded wait or kill -9 + waitUntilExit under a timeout. (2) PerformanceSetBudgetTests "set transaction on a synthetic 5000-node document" reported 2626 ms against the 2000 ms debug limit in one full run under 4-agent load (1767 ms alone) — min-of-5 is not enough when every sample is inflated; consider widening the debug limit, or making budgets advisory (print, and fail only under WOODCASE_BUDGET_STRICT=1 / release), and say which in WoodcasePerformance.md. (3) FileWatcherTests/ViewerFixtures hit FSEvents-timing failures once under load (helper agent). The integrator's own wedge samples are in the session scratchpad as wedge-*.txt.

shotter, 2026-08-29. Branch wt/shotter. Fixed; not committed.

TWO bugs, not one.

1. The one filed. `shot` looked the *authored* id up in the layout rects. Fixed at the
   source: new `EditableDocument.expandedID(of:)` (Sources/Woodcase/Editing/
   EditableDocument+ExpandedAddress.swift) maps a ResolvedNodeAddress to its
   post-expansion id — a ref becomes `<ref id>/<component root id>`, following ref
   chains through `componentRegistry` exactly as PenRefExpander does. ShotTargets uses
   it for the rendered node and for every --outline box. `shot` now expands with
   `keepReusables: true` (the design-canvas reading `tree`/SettledTree and Penumbra's
   DocumentPipeline already take), so a reusable definition renders as itself. The
   no-node refusal now lists top-level frames AND refs, marking definitions
   "(component definition)". A genuinely missing rect is now exit 2 with a remedy
   naming both the typed address and the resolved id (ShotTargets.missingRectFailure).

2. Found while making "--outline on a descendant of an instance" go green.
   PenLayoutEngine settles every rect RELATIVE TO ITS PARENT; only a top-level node's
   rect is in canvas coordinates (see Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/
   layout-deep-nesting.layout.json — a leaf four levels down reads x:0,y:0).
   `--outline` read one rect and treated it as absolute. Every box below depth 1 landed
   in the wrong place, and any artboard away from the origin refused its own
   descendants. New ShotFrame (Sources/WoodcaseCommand/ShotFrame.swift) walks the
   rendered node's subtree and composes the offsets; membership in that map is now what
   decides "is this node in the picture".

CHANGED AN EXISTING TEST. ShotCommandTests.outlineResolvesThroughARefInstance asserted
only exit 0 while the box was drawn at (0,0). In addressing.pen Dash1 flows Header and
Body in a row, so Body sits at x=800 and Nav01/Lbl01's composed x is 850 — outside
Dashboard's own 800-point width. Retargeted to shoot Dashboard/Body and added a pixel
assertion so it cannot pass for the wrong reason again.

Suite: 2543 tests / 255 suites, all pass (`swift test --quiet`). swiftformat clean.
scripts/mae-check clean.

FOR OTHER OWNERS (I did not touch these):
- Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Render/RenderCache.swift:192 `PenRefExpander.expand(parsed)`
  drops reusables, so the viewer lists ZERO artboards for banking.pen. Should be
  `expand(parsed, keepReusables: true)` to agree with `shot` and `tree`.
- Sources/WoodcaseCommand/NodeLookup.swift:93-100 hand-rolls the same ref→expanded-id
  mapping as a prefix scan over top-level nodes only. Should call
  `document.expandedID(of:)`.
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/Performance/PerformanceShotBudgetTests.swift `renderRoot(for:in:)`
  is a third copy, and its doc comment now describes a bug that is fixed.
- WoodcaseCLI.md wording proposed in the report; I did not edit it.

GOTCHA worth recording (I did not edit project/gotchas.md to avoid a conflict):
"PenLayoutEngine rects are parent-relative. Only a top-level node's rect is in canvas
coordinates; a nested node's x/y is its offset inside its parent. Anything that reads a
single rect out of the map and treats it as absolute is wrong below depth 1 —
`layout-deep-nesting.layout.json` is the cheapest proof."

Fixed on wt/expander (not committed; integrator merges).

Diagnosis confirmed and the fix goes further than the ticket: rather than widen
expandRef's registry and leave a second expansion implementation standing, the
editing layer now has no expansion of its own. EditableDocument+Expansion.swift
lost ~130 lines (expandRefsInNode, expandRefsInNodes, stripReusables) and all
three entry points delegate to PenRefExpander:

- expandRef(nodeID:) — PenRefExpander.expandRef over materializedComponents()
- expandSubtree(rootID:) — new PenRefExpander.expand(_:registry:) over the
  materialized subtree
- expandedDocument() — PenRefExpander.expand(materialize())

materializedComponents() rebuilds each reusable's subtree from the flat store,
because componentRegistry holds children-stripped nodes; it is the same set
PenRefExpander.buildRegistry builds from the file. Provenance no longer comes
out of the expansion: it is read off the ref nodes before it (collectProvenance),
which is all ComponentProvenance ever needed, and records exactly the same refs
as before.

Behaviour change worth knowing: expandSubtree no longer reads or warms the
ExpansionCache (it expands the whole subtree in one PenRefExpander pass).
expandRef stays cached, unchanged. No caller in Sources used expandSubtree.

Tests (red first, all three failed before the fix):
Tests/WoodcaseTests/EditableDocumentExpansionParityTests.swift
- expandRef on addressing.pen Nav01: no raw refs left, and Nav01/Bdg01/Cnt01
  carries the cross-ref override "3" (it was a raw ref, override landing nowhere)
- expandSubtree on Dash1: same
- parity: expandedDocument() == PenRefExpander.expand(doc) and each
  expandSubtree(root) == the matching child of expand(keepReusables: true), over
  every Fixtures/*.pen that has a ref (addressing, banking, expander-nested-ref,
  shadcn.lib, woodcase-app). The expandSubtree half was red on all five.

Performance: swift test --filter Performance, all six budgets pass after
(tree woodcase-app 409.7 ms / synthetic 591.5 ms, set 151.9 / 1267.2 ms).
Same command on the stashed baseline in the same minute: tree 769.0 / 719.0 ms,
set 168.2 / 1250.0 ms. No regression; expandRef is not on tree's path (tree runs
PenRefExpander directly), so the registry build costs it nothing.

Docs: EditingDocuments.md "Component Registry and Expansion" rewritten to say
there is one expander and that only expandRef is cached.

Full suite: swift test --quiet, 2540 tests / 254 suites, passed. swiftformat clean.

Adjacent hole found, NOT fixed (no issue filed — worth one): the ExpansionCache
is invalidated only for edits to a ref node or to the reusable root itself
(EditableDocument+Properties.swift, +CRDT, +Detach, +Overrides). An insert,
delete or move *inside* a component, or a property edit on a component's
descendant, leaves cached expandRef results stale. Pre-existing; unchanged here.

Fixed on wt/expander (not committed; integrator merges).

The applier now names why a root-level node holds the coordinates it does, as a
type rather than a bool: BatchApplier.RootCoordinates, .authored (an add's
subtree — the author wrote them, so either coordinate suppresses placement, as
before) or .copied (a cp's source coordinates — they describe the source, so
they never suppress placement). planAdd passes .authored, planCopy .copied.

A caller who wants the copy somewhere in particular passes common.x / common.y
in props: those are applied after the insert and win outright, on the axis they
name. So `cp Board document --set common.x=42` lands at (42, placed-y), not at
(42, the source's y) — the source's coordinates are never authorship. That is a
choice between two readings of the ticket; the alternative (mirror add's "either
coordinate" rule against props) leaks the source's y into the answer where the
caller cannot see it.

Tests (red first):
- BatchApplierCreationTests.rootCopyIsPlaced — `{"op":"cp","source":"Board"}` on
  batch.pen lands at (800, 0); was (500, 40), exactly on top of Board.
- BatchApplierCreationTests.rootCopyTakesGivenCoordinates — with
  props {"common.x":42} lands at (42, 0); y was the source's 40.
- CopyCommandTests.rootCopyDoesNotLandOnItsSource — `woodcase cp batch.pen Board
  document common.name=Loose` writes x 800 / y 0; was 500 / 40.

Docs: WoodcaseBatches.md "Placement" now states the add/cp split and the props
escape hatch; CopyCommand's discussion says the source's x/y describe the source.

Not touched, and someone should: WoodcaseEditor.md line ~267 says "Only a
root-level add (parent `document`) is coordinate-placed" and its `cp` paragraph
says nothing about placement — a cp at the root is coordinate-placed too. Left
alone to avoid colliding with whoever owns that article.

Full suite: swift test --quiet, 2540 tests / 254 suites, passed. swiftformat clean.

data.note: Landed on main as e154128 (pushed), 2550 green. Route.Specificity (public, Friendly & Comparable; literal > suffixed capture > capture, lexicographic, length as the total-order fallback); ViewerRoutes.match keeps the most specific method-matching entry with strict > so equal shapes fall through to registration order; ViewerPages holds page routes only. Decision (integrator): Specificity stays public — precedence is part of the contract a route registrant reasons about.

data.description: Found integrating wlAte (2026-08-29). PenLayoutEngine settles rects relative to the parent; anything that needs canvas coordinates walks the subtree composing origins — and that walk now exists twice: ShotFrame.rects(under:in:layoutRects:) in WoodcaseCommand and ArtboardLayout in WoodcaseViewer (which also computes TreeRow.Clip). Lift ONE walk into the library (e.g. PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects(under:in:layoutRects:) or a SettledTree accessor, whichever the layout cache already has the pieces for — check LayoutCache/SettledTree first) and make both consumers call it. In the same leaf, since they touch the same seam: (a) RenderCache.swift:192 calls PenRefExpander.expand(parsed) without keepReusables, so the viewer lists zero artboards for banking.pen while shot and tree treat a definition as renderable — switch to keepReusables: true so the viewer and shot agree on what an artboard is (a definition renders as itself); (b) NodeLookup.swift:93-100 hand-rolls the ref→expanded-id mapping as a prefix scan over top-level nodes — replace with document.expandedID(of:); (c) PerformanceShotBudgetTests.renderRoot(for:in:) is a third copy whose doc comment now describes a fixed bug — use expandedID. Regression tests: the viewer lists banking.pen's definitions as artboards; NodeLookup resolves a ref nested inside a component.

data.description: Found by the expander agent (AzXzQ, 2026-08-29), not fixed. EditableDocument's ExpansionCache is invalidated only for edits to a ref node or to a reusable component's ROOT (EditableDocument+Properties.swift, +CRDT, +Detach, +Overrides). An insert, delete or move inside a component, or a property edit on a component's descendant, leaves cached expandRef results stale. Exposure today: expandRef is used by detach and CRDT detach only (expandSubtree no longer reads the cache), so a detach after an in-component edit within one document lifetime can produce a stale clone. Fix: invalidate on any edit whose node has a reusable ancestor (walk parents to a componentRegistry member), with a regression test: edit a text node inside a component, then detach an instance, assert the detached clone carries the edit.

data.description: Ruling 2026-08-29 (Ben): agents must not be required to generate node ids, but an id they DO pass is honored as long as it is unique within the document; an omitted id gets a fresh, non-colliding random code (5-char alphanumeric, like Jobs). Today BatchApplier+Create regenerates EVERY id in an added subtree via PenID.remapIDs(in:) and the docs say "do not invent ids — they are regenerated on insert" (WoodcaseEditor.md § Adding a subtree, CreatedNode.swift, PenSubtreeDecoder.swift, BatchOperation+Grammar.swift line ~48). Change the contract: on `add` (and `apply` add lines), keep a supplied id if it is unique in the document and not duplicated within the subtree; generate for omitted ids; a supplied id that collides is refused with EditingError.duplicateNodeID (its message already says "leave id out and let add generate one" — keep it and make it true). Internal refs within the subtree (a ref inside the subtree pointing at another node in the subtree, descendants keys) must still be remapped consistently for the ids that were generated. `cp` still regenerates every id (a copy must not collide with its source). Update the grammar text, CreatedNode/PenSubtreeDecoder doc comments, WoodcaseEditor.md's paragraph and `woodcase help design` NAMES/ADDRESSES if it mentions ids. Tests first: add with a unique supplied id keeps it; a colliding one is refused with the remedy; omitted ids are generated; cp regenerates.

data.text:
Fixed on wt/cacher (not committed — integrator squashes).

One rule, one place: Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+ExpansionInvalidation.swift.
`invalidatingExpansions(touching:_:)` reads the touched nodes before AND after the
mutation and empties the whole ExpansionCache if either reading finds a ref, a
reusable component, or a node inside one (`expansionCanDepend(on:)`, walking
`ancestors(of:)`). Both readings are needed: a delete or a move out of a component
only looks like component work beforehand, an insert or a move in only afterwards.
Per-op subject lists live in `expansionSubjects(of: EditOperation)` and
`expansionSubjects(of: DocumentMutation)`.

Choke points wrapped (every write to the flat store passes one of them):
- apply(_:) — all local ops; applyLocal routes the flat store through it too.
  Split the switch out as private applyOperation(_:).
- applyMutation(_:) — every remote CRDT write; split as applyMutationToStore(_:).
  CRDTDocument emits a mutation for every parent it changes, so reconcile only
  re-derives from what the mutations already named.
- deleteNode(_:) / detachRef(_:) — public value-returning mutators that bypass apply.
- the applyLocal fail-closed catch block, which writes created nodes directly.

Removed the sprinkled invalidate calls (+Properties x3, +Overrides, +Detach x2,
+CRDT applyMutation) and, with them, ExpansionCache's now-dead reverseIndex,
invalidate(_:) and invalidateAll(referencingComponent:).

Tests: Tests/WoodcaseTests/ExpansionCacheInvalidationTests.swift, 10 cases —
property edit / insert / delete / move-out / move-in inside a component then
detach; CRDT local and CRDT remote (edit + insert) then detach; clearing
`reusable` re-collapses a cached expansion; and one guard that an edit outside
every component leaves the cache warm. 9 of 10 red before the fix, all green after.

swift test --quiet: 2575 tests / 258 suites, 0 failures. swiftformat . --lint clean.

walker: all three criteria done on wt/walker (worktree .claude/worktrees/walker). Not committed.

1. `PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects(under:in:layoutRects:)` is the one canvas-space walk
   (new file `Sources/Woodcase/PenLayoutEngine+AbsoluteRects.swift`, Foundation-only,
   DocC'd, 7 unit tests against `layout-deep-nesting`). `ShotFrame.swift` is deleted —
   it was a pure forwarder once the walk moved — and `ShotCommand` calls the library
   function directly; `ArtboardLayout.of` takes its x/y from the same call and keeps its
   own tree walk only for document order, the name path and `TreeRow.Clip` (a
   parent-local test). Rotation: origins only, as both walks already did; the doc
   comment says so.

2. `RenderCache.prepare` expands with `keepReusables: true`, so a reusable definition is
   an artboard as it already is for shot and tree. New `ComponentArtboardTests` (red
   before the change, verified by reverting): banking.pen now lists nSNTs, msdSu, jl9It,
   d4kAy, Dt9Jv plus the two placed refs; batch.pen's Cmp01 renders through both the
   PNG endpoint and the artboard page. Four existing viewer assertions changed from
   ["Cnv01","Brd01"] to +"Cmp01" (ViewerEndpoints, ViewerServer x2, ChangeCoordinator,
   RenderCache unknown-artboard message). WoodcaseViewer.md's "A reusable component is a
   definition, not a page, and is not an artboard" is rewritten to the new truth.

3. `NodeLookup.expanded` and `PerformanceShotBudgetTests.renderRoot` both use
   `EditableDocument.expandedID(of:)`; both private copies deleted. New
   `NodeLookupExpansionTests` (5 tests over addressing.pen, including a ref nested
   inside a component).

Two premises in the leaf description turned out to be wrong, recorded here so the next
reader does not repeat the search:

- The viewer listed **two** artboards for banking.pen, not zero: the expander clears
  `reusable` on a clone, so the two ref-placed screens (YGJ0d/nSNTs, 8ruxp/nSNTs)
  survived stripping. What was missing was the five definitions.
- NodeLookup's prefix scan was **not** a scan "over top-level nodes" — it recursed the
  whole tree — and I could not construct a case where it disagrees with `expandedID`.
  The nested-ref tests were green at birth; they are a regression net for the refactor,
  not a bug fix. The refactor still stands on its own: one mapping, not two.

Found while probing, NOT fixed (out of scope, worth a leaf): `woodcase tree --expand`
prints `Card1/Btn02` as the address of a ref nested one instance deep, but
`woodcase get <file> Card1/Btn02` fails with "matches no node in this document" —
`EditableDocument.resolve` does not accept the id-path the tree prints for a ref inside
an instance. Reproduce with a 3-node fixture: Page1 > ref Card1 -> reusable CardC >
group > ref Btn02 -> reusable BtnC.

Suite: `swift test --quiet` → 2579 tests in 260 suites passed (82.1 s), sandbox off.
`swiftformat . --lint` → 0/626 files require formatting. Two intermediate runs failed
only on PerformanceTree/PerformanceSet budgets under multi-agent load (tree 1.13 s vs
750 ms debug limit); those cleared on a quieter run and I did not touch tree or set.
Budgets left alone.

data.description: Found by the walker agent (urmCm, 2026-08-29), not fixed. `woodcase tree --expand` prints `Card1/Btn02` as the address of a ref nested one instance deep, but `woodcase get <file> Card1/Btn02` answers "matches no node in this document": EditableDocument.resolve does not accept the id-path the tree prints for a ref inside an instance. Reproduce: Page1 > ref Card1 → reusable CardC > group > ref Btn02 → reusable BtnC. A read must hand back addresses a write accepts (cli-design § Output), so this is a contract break. data.text:
Done on wt/migrator (not committed; integrator commits).

What changed
- NEW Sources/WoodcaseCommand/PenInputPath.swift — the file-or-directory argument,
  sibling to PenFilePath rather than a mode on it: PenFilePath's whole contract is
  "one .pen file" and existingFile() refuses a directory, so a `.fileOrDirectory`
  mode would have made its return type a lie for every other verb. existingTarget()
  runs when the verb runs and returns a typed Target (.file/.directory), not a bool.
  Missing path -> CommandFailure(.targetFailure, 4) with PenFilePath's exact sentence
  ("Cannot open <path>: no such file. Check the path — `ls <dir>` lists what is
  there."). A file that is not .pen -> CommandFailure(.usage, 2), naming what it
  wanted and where to look. Readability is deliberately NOT checked up front, unlike
  PenFilePath: migrate walks trees and must not refuse a whole run for one bad file.
- MigrateCommand.swift — inputs is [PenInputPath]; penFiles(in:excluding:) switches
  on existingTarget() instead of raising ValidationError (which ArgumentParser turned
  into exit 2 + a usage block for a perfectly good command line).
- MigrateCommand.swift — a run with failures now throws ExitCode.targetFailure (4),
  not .failure (1). Ruling: 1 is the clean negative a script reads as "the check ran,
  the answer is no"; a .pen file that could not be read, migrated or written is the
  same target failure every other verb returns for a file it cannot open. The failure
  still does not stop the run, and --dry-run still exits 0 when nothing failed.
- WoodcaseCLI.md — the `migrate` row already said 0 2 4 and is now TRUE, so it is
  unchanged; the section gains an exit-code table plus two worked shell examples
  showing which 4 is which (refused before any file is touched vs. after the run).

Tests (red first, then green)
- NEW Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/MigrateExitCodeTests.swift (5, CommandFixture,
  real binary): missing path -> 4 + remedy + no USAGE block; directory searched
  recursively -> 0; non-.pen -> 2; unmigratable .pen -> 4; --dry-run -> 0.
- NEW Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/PenInputPathTests.swift (6), mirroring
  PenFilePathTests.
- MigrateCommandTests: +1 (missing path is 4), and two existing expectations changed
  because the behaviour changed — non-.pen now CommandFailure(.usage) not
  ValidationError, and the failed-run code is now .targetFailure not any ExitCode.
- Intermediate red was informative, not just a compile error: with the new type wired
  in but the old `throw ExitCode.failure` kept, exactly the two exit-code tests failed
  with "expected 4, got 1".

Verification
- swift test --quiet: 2577 tests, 259 suites, 1 issue — PerformanceSetBudgetTests
  "set transaction on a 5000-node synthetic document", a debug-build budget on a
  machine running six agents' suites in parallel. Unrelated to this change.
- swiftformat . --lint: 0/626 files require formatting.
- Manual: `woodcase migrate /nowhere/gone.pen` -> 4 with the remedy sentence;
  `woodcase migrate README.md` -> 2 naming .pen; `migrate --help` renders.

For the integrator
- Two flags, neither in scope for this leaf:
  1. ActivityCommandTests.followSeesNewEventsPromptly (line ~259) HUNG a full-suite
     run for 12 min at 0.6% CPU, blocked in NSConcreteTask.waitUntilExit on the
     spawned `activity --follow`. Sampled, killed by pid, reran clean — so it is
     intermittent, and it wedges the suite rather than failing it. Worth a job.
  2. `migrate` over a directory holding no .pen file exits 0 via
     CleanExit("No .pen files found."). Documented as-is, not changed.

Diagnosis: the refusal was RIGHT, the message was wrong. A .pen fill's `type` is
`"color"` (2.17 schema line 39: `Fill = ColorOrVariable | { type: "color"; ... }`);
`"solid"` has never been a fill type. `PenFill.FillType` is
color/gradient/image/mesh_gradient/shader. So `kind.fills=[{"type":"solid",...}]`
had to be refused — but three things made the refusal read as self-contradictory:

1. `PenFills.init(from:)` decoded the array with `try?` and, on failure, fell back to
   decoding a *single* fill. That threw away "element 0's type is misspelled" and
   reported the fallback's typeMismatch, which the codec collapsed to `actual: "array"`
   — the very form the message had just listed as accepted. Same bug in `PenEffects`.
2. `NodePropertyCodec+Shapes`'s table was hand-typed prose beside the decoders, so it
   had drifted: `padding` was documented `[horizontal, vertical]` while the schema and
   `PenPadding` both read a 2-array as `[vertical, horizontal]` — the message told
   callers the opposite of the truth.
3. `PropertyAssignment.valueRules` — printed in every mutating verb's `--help`, and
   mirrored in WoodcaseCLI.md — offered `{"type":"solid"}` as its JSON example. That is
   almost certainly where the reported command's shape came from.

Fixes: fills/effects decode an array *by shape* and raise the array's own error; a new
`PenPropertyShape` assembles every `expected` from the decoding types themselves
(`PenFill.fillTypeNames`, `PenEffect.effectTypeNames`, `PenPropertyShape.oneOf(_:)`
over the `String` enums, now `CaseIterable`); a new `PenDecodingFailure` renders the
`DecodingError` as `[0].type: "solid" is not an accepted spelling`; `PenCornerRadius`
and `PenPadding` decode messages rewritten wire-facing; the `set` remedy no longer
repeats the whole expected shape.

Now:
  kind.fills on Canvas/Cards (Crd01) takes a color string, a fill object, or an array
  of either (a fill object's type is one of color, gradient, image, mesh_gradient,
  shader), for example [{"type":"color","color":"#FFD166"}], but the value given is an
  array ([0].type: "solid" is not an accepted spelling) — correct the value;
  `woodcase get batch.pen Crd01` shows what the node holds now

Anti-drift guard: `StructuredPropertyShapeTests` writes every `PenPropertyShape.example`
in the table through `NodePropertyCodec.setting`, so a stale example fails the suite.

Suite: 2574 tests / 258 suites pass (43.8 s). swiftformat clean. Branch wt/filler,
not committed.

Done on wt/decoder (not committed). An undecodable .pen file now fails the same way on
every verb, with the path, the decoder's real objection and a next command:

    Cannot read /w/broken.pen: not a .pen document — children[0].id should be a string
    — check the file's JSON with `python3 -m json.tool /w/broken.pen`.

How: `PenParserError.decodingFailed` and `.unsupportedVersion` gained a `url: URL?`
(breaking, pre-launch; every match site updated) and a public `url` accessor; an
internal `PenParser.parse(_:from:diagnostics:)` attaches it, and `parse(contentsOf:)`
routes through it. `PenFileTransaction` now lets a `PenParserError` through instead of
flattening it into `PenFileError.unreadable` — that is what makes tree/lint (transaction)
and render (direct parse) print one sentence. New `DecodingReason` (library) turns a
`DecodingError` into "children[0].id should be a string"; new `ParserFailureMessage`
(CLI) adds the remedy. `BatchOperation.decodeJSONL`'s private duplicate of the
DecodingError renderer is retired in favour of `DecodingReason`.

Deviation the integrator should know: the brief's remedy for the version gate,
`woodcase migrate <path> --dry-run`, is wrong — migrate goes through the same gate and
fails identically, so it is a plausible-wrong-answer. The version case says "update
Woodcase, or correct the \"version\" key with `python3 -m json.tool <path>`" instead.

Follow-up for the migrator (MigrateCommand was off-limits here): its per-file report
prints "<path>: error: Cannot read the .pen input: …" because `PenFileMigrator.migrate`
takes `Data` and so has no URL to attach. Giving that call the URL (or having the report
drop its own prefix when the error names a file) would tidy it.

swift test --quiet: 2588 tests / 259 suites pass, 66 s. swiftformat clean.

Done on wt/namer (worktree .claude/worktrees/namer), not committed.

Contract changed: `add` (and `apply` add lines) now keep an id the caller supplied and
draw one only for a node that omitted it; `cp` still draws every id.

New: Sources/Woodcase/Editing/SubtreeIDPlan.swift — the three steps as one typed plan
(validate supplied / draw omitted / rewrite internal refs + descendants keys), with two
front doors: `keeping(_:avoiding:)` (add, can refuse) and `regenerating(_:avoiding:)`
(cp, cannot). `PenID.remapIDs(in:)` is now a thin wrapper on `regenerating`, so detach
and CRDT get ref-rewriting too.

Id grammar (from local/Pen-Schema-v2.js Entity: "Unique string; MUST NOT contain '/'"):
any non-empty string with no `/`. Exposed as `PenID.isValid(_:)`. A supplied id that
breaks it is `EditingError.invalidNodeID(id:)` (new case); one already in the document
or repeated in the subtree is `duplicateNodeID`, whose remedy sentence is now true.

Also: `PenSubtreeDecoder` marks an omitted id as `unsuppliedID` ("") instead of
generating one; `EditableDocument.validateNoDuplicateIDs` now catches ids that collide
only within the subtree (was a real hole — regression test added, watched red);
`BatchError.couldNotGenerateIDs` retired as unreachable (the plan draws against the
document's ids, so the retry loop it guarded is gone).

Bug fixed on the way: a `cp` of a subtree holding both a component and an instance of it
left the copied instance pointing at the *original* component.

Docs: BatchOperation.grammar, AddCommand help, `woodcase help design` (new IDS block),
WoodcaseEditor.md § Adding a subtree, WoodcaseBatches.md § Creating nodes, WoodcaseCLI.md
§ add, CreatedNode + PenSubtreeDecoder doc comments, DocC topic curation.

swift test --quiet: 2590 tests, 258 suites, passed (37.8 s / 70.1 s on two runs).
swiftformat . --lint: clean. One gotcha appended (nested #require will not compile).

data.text: Concrete lead 2026-08-29 (integrator): after killing wedged test helpers, three orphaned `.build/debug/woodcase activity --follow` processes were still alive (children of ActivityCommandTests.followSeesNewEventsPromptly, spawned via Process; the helper's death does not kill them). With them running, ViewerPagesTests.recentEditsShowOnThePage failed twice in a row with "batch.pen is locked by another process; gave up after 5s" and passed immediately after they were killed by pid. So: (1) the follow test must terminate its child in a defer/teardown that survives cancellation, and the child should exit when its parent dies (e.g. poll getppid() or watch stdin EOF) — that also removes the waitUntilExit wedge; (2) a 5 s lock budget in a viewer test is still a wall-clock assertion under load; consider a longer budget or asserting the typed outcome. New shape reported by the filler agent: ViewerServerTests/ViewerPagesTests fail fast with NSURLErrorTimedOut on loopback under 5-agent load (~2 runs in 5) — distinct from the wedge.

The refusal was right ("solid" is not a fill type; it is "color"); three faults fixed: PenFills/PenEffects swallowed the array's own error, the shapes table was hand-typed and had drifted (padding order was reversed), and valueRules taught {"type":"solid"}. data.text: Deterministic reproducer 2026-08-30 00:xx (integrator, quiet machine, main at d7bdce2 + the decoder branch staged): `swift test --skip "Viewer"` dies twice in a row ~10 s in with exit 1, no "Test run with" summary, no issue, no crash/signal text; the last suites finishing are FileLockTests ("A writer blocks a reader, which then times out"), PenVersionGateTests, PenWoodcaseAppTests. No kill()/killpg in Sources or Tests; ServeCommandTests touches no signals. Logs: scratchpad/skipviewer2.log (non-quiet, 3144 lines) and skipviewer3.log. Also seen tonight: full runs stopped externally as "killed" while in background; a full run wedged 10 min in PenTextMeasurer (CoreText); ViewerPagesTests recentEditsShowOnThePage failing "locked by another process; gave up after 5s" until orphaned `woodcase activity --follow` children (one leaked per run by ActivityCommandTests.followSeesNewEventsPromptly) were killed; NSURLErrorTimedOut on loopback in ViewerPagesTests. data.text: HANDOFF 2026-08-30: read project/2026-08-30-handoff-viewer-issues.md — 15 commits landed (viewer page + serve, help, budgets, docs, and the wave-4/5 issues), QGISs running alone, wt/namer (Kvliv) done and queued behind it, then aZADN and HgtJR. Suite unstable tonight: only a plain full `swift test --quiet` verdict counts; kill orphaned `woodcase activity --follow` children by pid after any killed run.

DONE 2026-08-30 (flaker, branch wt/flaker, not committed). Four symptoms, four causes, two of them product bugs. Full write-up: project/2026-08-30-suite-stability.md.

(1) SILENT EXIT 1 = an out-of-memory kill. `sample` on the "hung" helper: 40.2 GB peak, 100% CPU, in CRDTConcurrentMoveTests.threeNodeCycleAttempt -> applyRemote -> invalidatingExpansions defer -> expansionCanDepend -> EditableDocument.ancestors(of:). `applyRemote` applies a batch one op at a time and passes through a CYCLIC parents map mid-batch (A->B, B->C, C->A); ancestors(of:) had no visited set and grew an array forever. Product bug on the multiplayer path. Fixed: ancestors(of:) and isDescendant(_:of:) stop at the first repeated id (Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+Queries.swift). Regression test EditableDocumentCycleSafetyTests. NOTE THE DEVIATION: the brief said don't touch Sources/Woodcase/Editing (wt/namer). The root cause was there; the change is 6 lines in one file, EditableDocument+Queries.swift. Check for conflict with wt/namer before merging.

(2) THE WEDGE IS REAL AND SEPARATE — the two gotchas blaming CoreText and WebKit were wrong about the cause but right about the place. With (1) fixed, ten quiet runs passed and a LOADED run still hung 300 s. The soak watchdog sampled it: all 8 cooperative threads (one per core) blocked in CTFontCreateWithFontDescriptor's SYNCHRONOUS XPC call to fontd — 6 under PenTextMeasurer.resolveFont, 2 under fontFamilyAvailable — 0% CPU, flat 188 MB. Core Text resolves families out of process and blocks with no timeout; eight parallel renders leave the process with nothing runnable. Fixed: new Sources/Woodcase/FontRegistryGate.swift, one recursive lock across every font-registry call (fontFamilyAvailable, uncached resolveFont, hasWeightAxis, PenIconFontRenderer.createFont). FontResolutionCache still answers repeats without reaching the gate. Sample kept: scratchpad/QGISs-soak-loaded.log.run4.sample.78341.

(3) THE ORPHAN. `activity --follow` had no reason to stop besides a signal. Fixed at the source: ParentProcessWatch polls getppid(); a follower born orphaned (nohup) is left alone deliberately. Tests: new ChildProcess (never waitUntilExit; deadline poll, SIGTERM->SIGKILL, Issue at each escalation, SIGKILL in deinit, withChild for teardown); CommandFixture.run bounded the same way. A process-wide child census as the "suite guard" was considered and rejected — swift-testing runs suites in parallel, so a census at the end of suite A sees suite B's children.

(4) WALL CLOCKS. ViewerFixtures.lockBudget (60 s) and .requestBudget (60 s) replace the 5 s PenFileTransaction default and the 15 s URLSession timeout in every viewer test — the viewer's server and every EditableDocument in the suite queue on the same @MainActor, so those budgets measured the suite's main-actor demand. Performance budgets are advisory under debug and fail at 4x the limit; strict on release or WOODCASE_BUDGET_STRICT=1 (PerformanceBudget.check, documented in WoodcasePerformance.md, tested in PerformanceBudgetAdvisoryTests).

(5) A RACE THE GATE WIDENED, now fixed both ways: PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests asserted exact compute counts on a private cache, but PenFontRegistry.generation is process-wide and any suite's registration discards every cache. Generation is now read INSIDE the gate; the suite retries a window a registration landed in.

RESULTS. scripts/soak-tests (new, in scripts/, with a watchdog that samples and kills a run past --timeout and reports NO-SUMMARY/TIMEOUT):
  10 quiet: 10/10, 2647 tests / 269 suites, 30.4-31.6 s each.
  5 with --load 2: 5/5, 34.3-37.6 s each.
  Both brief reproducers now pass: `swift test --filter "WoodcaseTests\."` and `swift test --skip Viewer`.
  No woodcase child outlived any run; Ben's demo on :7333 untouched.
  Intermediate soaks each found one more thing — a quiet ten-run soak alone would have shipped the wedge.

"1 known issue" in every summary is intentional: PerformanceBudgetAdvisoryTests uses withKnownIssue to assert that a 4x overshoot DOES fail.

gotchas.md: the two wedge entries are replaced by one that says plainly they were wrong and gives the method (sample by pid, read the footprint line first — it separates the two hangs instantly). Added: swift test --filter matches the identifier, not the display name, and a filter matching nothing reports a green run of nothing.

Commit message proposed in scratchpad/QGISs-commitmsg.txt. Nothing committed; branch wt/flaker.

data.text:
Fixed on wt/resolver (not committed).

Root cause: `resolve`'s instance branch stepped a `ref` onto the component root's
*direct children* only, while the id-path `tree --expand` prints (and the key Pen
stores in `descendants`) names the outer refs and the node and skips every container
in between. So `Card1/Btn02` — a ref nested under a group inside CardC — printed by a
read was rejected by every read and write.

data.description:
Found by splitter (aZADN, 2026-08-30) the first time `swift test -c release` was
ever able to run. `PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance`
crashes the release test process deterministically with SIGTRAP — three for three,
and it takes the whole run down, so `swift test -c release --quiet` cannot go green
until it is fixed. Debug passes; the release `woodcase` binary is fine
(`scripts/perf-binary --config release` resolves fonts happily), because production
never deallocates the process-wide FontResolutionCache and this is a deinit-path
crash.

Faulting stack (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/swiftpm-testing-helper-2026-08-30-025215.ips),
EXC_BREAKPOINT on thread com.apple.root.default-qos.cooperative:

  __CFCheckCFInfoPACSignature        <- trap
  _CFRelease
  _DictionaryStorage.deinit
  _DictionaryStorage.__deallocating_deinit
  FontResolutionCache.__deallocating_deinit
  specialized PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance()

So: releasing a `CTFont` out of `FontResolutionCache.fonts` finds an object whose CF
info word no longer signs — a freed or over-released CoreFoundation object.

What is known:

- Only that one test of the three crashes. `resolveFontDistinguishesKeys` (3 fonts,
  discarded immediately) and `hasWeightAxisMemoized` (5 resolutions, discarded) both
  pass in release. The crashing one is the only one that lets the CTFont *escape*
  `undisturbed`, so the same object is alive in the tuple and in the dictionary — one
  more live reference than the others hold.
- That shape says under-retain, not over-release: the object's real refcount reaches
  zero while Swift still holds references, and the dictionary's release is simply the
  one that finds the corpse.
- It is not the `===`. Replacing `#expect(fonts.0 === fonts.1)` with an
  `ObjectIdentifier` comparison still crashes, so swift-testing's expectation
  machinery is not implicated.
- Nothing in `Sources/Woodcase` does manual CF memory management — no `CFRetain`,
  `CFRelease`, `takeRetainedValue` or `Unmanaged` outside
  `PenIconFontRegistry`'s `Unmanaged<CFError>?` out-parameter.
- For "Helvetica"/normal/14 the returned font is the plain
  `CTFontCreateWithFontDescriptor` result: `hasWeightAxis` is false and
  `mapWeight("normal") == 0`, so `resolveFontThroughTheRegistry` returns `baseFont`
  unchanged. The value crosses `FontRegistryGate.withAccess<T>` and the test's own
  `undisturbed<T>` generic on its way out.

Reproduce:

    swift test -c release --filter resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance   # exit 1, SIGTRAP
    swift test -c release --filter resolveFontDistinguishesKeys       # exit 0
    swift test --filter resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance              # exit 0 (debug)

Next steps: run it under `MallocStackLogging`/`libgmalloc` or a zombie-detecting
allocator to catch the release that takes the CTFont to zero, and check whether an
unspecialized generic return of a CF-bridged value across
`FontRegistryGate.withAccess` loses a retain under `-O` (if so it is an upstream Swift
bug and wants a reduced case plus a local workaround). Do not "fix" it by weakening
the test: the object really is being freed early, and production would hit it the day
anything deallocates a FontResolutionCache.
data.title: Release-only SIGTRAP: a CTFont is freed early under -O, crashing FontResolutionCache's deinit

data.text:
Done on wt/splitter (not committed; integrator to squash).

DIAGNOSIS. Not the renamed `main`. `@main` on an *async* entry point emits the entry
body under the fixed, module-less symbol `async_Main`, and under -O the thunk that
reaches it is a shared function-signature specialization
`$sIetH_yts5Error_pIegHrzo_TR10async_MainTf3npf_n` whose mangled name also carries no
module. SwiftPM renames only the C `main` wrapper of an executable under test
(`-entry-point-function-name WoodcaseCommand_main`, confirmed in .build/release.yaml)
and aliases it back for the product link. So the release bundle linked two identically
mangled thunks — SwiftPM's derived runner.swift and WoodcaseCommand.swift — and kept
one: WoodcaseCommand.swift.o is line 557 of the LinkFileList, runner.swift.o line 610.
`otool -tV` shows `_main` (0x6507a4, attributed to runner.swift by the dSYM) and
`_WoodcaseCommand_main` (0x4f2884) loading the *same* async function pointer at
0xe98fc8. Debug never specializes and keeps two `_async_Main` bodies local to their own
object files, which is why only release showed it. Confirmed end to end by dlopening
the bundle and calling dlsym("main") by hand: it runs woodcase's ArgumentParser.

FIX. `WoodcaseCommandCore` library target = the whole of the old
Sources/WoodcaseCommand (70 files, `git mv`); `WoodcaseCommand` executable = one file,
Main.swift, whose @main forwards to `WoodcaseCommandCore.WoodcaseCommand.main()`. The
test target depends on the library only. Root command is `package`, everything else
stays internal. `main()` now says `@MainActor` out loud — @main was inferring it.
`swift run woodcase`, `swift build --product woodcase [--show-bin-path]`,
`package experimental-install --product woodcase` and scripts/perf-binary all verified
working; `swift test` still links `woodcase` (deleted it and watched it relink).
New PackagingTests is the tripwire: dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "WoodcaseCommand_main") != nil

after.

  swift test -c release --filter Performance   11 tests / 5 suites PASSED (verbatim)
  swift test -c release --quiet      aborts on euSPm (see below)

data.title: Issues

data.text:
Root cause found and fixed. **The issue's premise was wrong**: the `CTFont` is never
freed and its CF retain count is correct throughout. `MallocStackLogging` on the
crashing process reports one ALLOC from `CTFontCreateWithFontDescriptor` and no FREE,
and `object_getClassName` on the trapping pointer returns `NSCTFont`.

What is corrupted is bit 33 of CoreFoundation's PAC-signed `_cfinfo` word. Printing
that word around each step shows it go `0x…2dd…` -> `0x…2db…` — a decrement of exactly
`1 << 33`, which is where Swift's *native* strong refcount lives. So a `swift_release`
ran on a CoreFoundation object. CF only validates the signature on `_CFRelease`'s
dealloc path, which is why the trap surfaced far away, in `FontResolutionCache.deinit`.

The stray release is emitted by the compiler, in the test's own helper. Disassembling
the crashing binary:

    1000013e0  bl  …PenTextMeasurerO11resolveFont…   ; x0 = the CTFont
    1000013e4  mov x22, x0
    1000013e8  bl  _swift_release                    ; no argument set up: x0 is the font

That is the destroy of the previous value of
`var result: (cache: FontResolutionCache, value: T)` — declared without an initializer
and assigned inside a `repeat` loop in a generic function. On later iterations the
compiler guards all three fields behind the definite-initialization flag
(`tbz w8, #0, …`); on the first iteration the native `swift_release` of the `cache`
field escapes that guard. Swift 6.3.3, `-O`, **without** `-wmo` — which is exactly how
the release *test* build compiles this file, and why nothing else ever saw it.

Reduced to 40 lines with no Woodcase code: `scripts/swift-di-miscompile` (SIGBUS in
`swift::RefCounts::doDecrementSlow` at `-O`, clean at `-Onone`). A five-way variant
matrix in one binary showed only that exact shape crashing: `-wmo`, an `Optional`
`result`, no loop, or splitting the tuple so the `var` holds only `T` are all correct.

Fix: `PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.undisturbed` now builds and returns each attempt on
the spot, with the last attempt taken unconditionally. Same retry semantics, same
assertions, no unassigned storage. A repo-wide scan found that helper to be the only
declared-but-unassigned local `var` later assigned in a loop, so `Sources` needed no
change.

Suites (worktree `wt/fonter`, sandbox off):
- `swift test -c release --quiet` -> `Test run with 2685 tests in 273 suites passed after 19.153 seconds.`
- `swift test --quiet` -> `Test run with 2685 tests in 273 suites passed after 31.830 seconds with 1 known issue.`
- `swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat` -> `0/651 files require formatting`

Regression evidence: `swift test -c release --filter PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests`
exited `unexpected signal code 5` before the change and passes 3/3 after; debug passed
both before and after.

Files: `Tests/WoodcaseTests/PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.swift`,
`scripts/swift-di-miscompile` (new), `scripts/README.md`,
`project/2026-08-30-release-only-ctfont-sigtrap.md` (new), `project/gotchas.md`,
`Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/WoodcasePerformance.md`, and in-place corrections
to `project/2026-08-30-two-mains-in-one-test-bundle.md` and
`project/2026-08-30-handoff-viewer-issues.md`, which both recorded the wrong cause
("a `CTFont` over-release", "the shape of an under-retain").

Not committed, per the brief.

data.text:
Implemented and TDD-tested:

(a) `woodcase icons <library> [query] [--json]` — Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/IconsCommand.swift.
    Offline read verb over PenIconFontRegistry's tables. No query: every name, sorted.
    A query: ranked via new IconNameMatcher (exact, substring, fuzzy-token/edit-distance
    tiers). Unknown library: exit 2 listing known libraries. No match: exit 1 (clean
    negative). Registered under the `read` group and in the subcommands list in
    WoodcaseCommand.swift.

(b) IconNameMatcher (Sources/Woodcase/IconFonts/IconNameMatcher.swift) — the shared
    ranking type, reused by:

(c) Two new lint checks — LintCheck.unknownIcon ("unknown-icon") and
    .unknownIconLibrary ("unknown-icon-library"), both severity .error (same reasoning
    as broken-ref: the node draws nothing at all). Logic lives in a new file,
    Sources/Woodcase/Lint/DocumentLinter+Icons.swift, to keep the diff isolated from
    another agent's concurrent edits to LintCheck.swift/DocumentLinter.swift (clipped
    epsilon, artboard-overlap). The only touch to DocumentLinter.swift itself is one
    added line calling the new `iconFindings` in the per-row dispatcher.

Docs updated: WoodcaseCLI.md (verb table + `### icons` section), WoodcaseLint.md
(check table + a paragraph distinguishing icon-font checks, which are offline over a
closed vocabulary, from text-font checks, which stay unchecked), PenIconFonts.md (new
"Looking Up Icon Names" section + Topics entry).

Found and fixed a real bug in my own first draft of IconNameMatcher while running the
full suite against the real ~1668-name Lucide table (not just my hand-picked test
fixture): the substring tier originally matched in both directions (`needle.contains
(haystack)` as well as `haystack.contains(needle)`), which let a short unrelated icon
name embedded inside a long/garbled query (e.g. "circle" inside "check-circle-2")
outrank the actual intended replacement ("circle-check") in tier 3. Fixed by making
substring tier one-directional; the fuzzy tier's token-overlap already handles the
renamed-icon case correctly. Also tightened the fuzzy tier's edit-distance fallback
bound (1 edit for queries <=6 chars, 2 beyond) after finding it let "clock" match a
query for "check" with zero token overlap.

Full suite green: swift test --quiet -> 2708 tests, 275 suites, 0 failures, 1
pre-existing known issue. swiftformat . --lint clean.

Both job criteria verified directly by test:
- IconsCommandTests.queryListsCheckAndKin: `icons lucide check` lists check,
  circle-check and their kin.
- DocumentLinterTests.unknownIconProposesNearestName: an icon named check-circle-2 is
  an unknown-icon finding proposing circle-check.

Three bugs, three causes, all fixed at the source on wt/7Qw7D (not committed).

1. New artboard needs a reload. The strip was inline markup in `ArtboardPage`, not a
   fragment, so no event could refresh it — the render fragment beside it cannot carry
   it (siblings in the canvas grid; a swap replaces one element). Extracted
   `ArtboardTabs`, served at `GET /files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}/tabs` as `#v-tabs`,
   and `refreshArtboard()` now swaps it with the render and the four panels. The `<nav>`
   is emitted (hidden inline) even for a one-artboard file, because a strip that does
   not exist cannot become the strip that announces the second artboard. The render
   cache was already invalidated correctly on `change`; that was not the problem.

2. Selection only in the first artboard. Nothing to do with the change event.
   `ArtboardLayout.of` published every box in **canvas** coordinates:
   `absoluteRects(under:)` answers in the root's own frame, and a top-level frame's rect
   is on the canvas. `Brd01` sits at (500, 40), so all of its boxes were at x=500 on a
   200pt image — no click could hit one, and the server-rendered selection box and the
   footer's rect were wrong too. The first artboard worked because it sits at (0, 0).
   `ArtboardLayout.local(_:origin:)` subtracts the artboard's origin, as
   `shot --outline` already did.

3. Outline does not scroll to the selected row. `viewer.js` now calls
   `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` on `#v-outline .v-outline-row.is-selected` after
   every swap and once on load — client-side, because which row is selected is view
   state the server owns but where the panel is scrolled is a property of this screen.
   No change to OutlineRow.swift.

Tests (all red first): `ArtboardLayoutTests` (3), `ArtboardTabsTests` (3, incl. two
golden previews), two fragment cases in `ViewerPagesTests`, three browser cases in
`ViewerBrowserTests` — a new artboard joining the strip live, a click in `Brd01`
selecting, and the outline scrolling to a row on click and on `?node=`.

`cp --times N` implemented in Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/CopyCommand.swift (new
`--times` option, no new files). Copies N times into the parent, in order; --at, when
given, places the first copy there and each later one immediately after (at+0, at+1, …)
so order survives despite the parent growing between inserts. Requires common.name in
the assignments to be a string containing the placeholder `{n}` (1-based) — refused
otherwise (exit 2), naming the placeholder and showing `common.name='Bar {n}'`. `{n}` is
substituted in every property that carries it (root and descendant, recursively through
JSON arrays/objects), not only common.name — a deliberate widening past the brief's
letter, called out below. --rev, when given, guards only the first copy (the parent/
document revision has already moved by the second). The name → id tree of every copy is
reported via WriteReport's existing `created: [CreatedNode]` — already multi-root-
capable, no library changes needed.

Activity log: the log's shape already supports a "one op = one event" granularity, not
"one line/copy = one event" — a `cp` with props (which --times always has, since
common.name is required) was already 2 EditOperations (insertNode + setProperties)
before this change, so it logs 2 events per copy (1 add + 1 set), all sharing the
transaction's batch id. I did not add a `.cp`-kind single event per copy — that would
mean changing BatchApplier/ActivityRecorder's per-operation logging model, out of scope
for a CLI-layer task and a wire-format change other consumers read.

Undo: does NOT reverse a --times write in one step. `woodcase undo -n` counts activity
*events*, not batches (confirmed empirically in
CopyTimesTests.swift:undoDoesNotReverseTimesInOneStep) — undoing a --times 3 write that
named each copy takes `-n 6`. This is a real limitation, documented in cp's --help,
WoodcaseCLI.md and WoodcaseEditor.md (which now also shows a real `activity` transcript
so an agent can count events before undoing). Did not touch UndoCommand.swift/ActivityEvent
to add batch-aware undo — that's a bigger, cross-cutting change outside this leaf's file
surface list.

Done on branch wt/hlntP (not committed; integrator merges).

The activity log is now project-local. `ActivityLogLocation` (new, Sources/Woodcase/Files/)
is the single resolver: `$WOODCASE_HOME` wins outright; else the nearest directory at or
above the .pen file holding a `.git` (directory or file, so worktrees count) gives
`<root>/.woodcase/activity.jsonl`; else the file's own directory. `ActivityLog(environment:)`
and the `~/.woodcase` default are gone — no read, no migration.

`ActivityLog` carries a typed `Origin` (.environmentOverride / .repository(root:) / .directory).
Only a `.repository` log adds `.woodcase/` to that root's `.gitignore`, once, on the write
that creates the directory (`RepositoryIgnoreFile`, new). Origin also picks the error wording:
`$WOODCASE_HOME` is blamed only when it actually chose the path.

`PenFileTransaction.run(at:identity:log:)` now defaults `log` to nil and resolves the file's
own log, so every write verb was correct without an edit. `activity` reads the cwd's log
without `--file` and the file's with it; `undo` reads the file's; `serve` resolves one log
per named file (deduped) or the cwd's with none, and the viewer follows all of them —
ViewerContext holds `logs`, merges reads in time order, ChangeCoordinator runs a follow task
per log, ViewerFileIndex.adoptFilesFromLogs adopts from each.

The 6-line NSCocoaError leak was `String(describing:)` on a Cocoa error used as a
PenFileError reason. Fixed at source with `PenFileError.oneLineReason(_:)` (flattened,
de-punctuated localizedDescription), applied in ActivityLog's directory creation and
ActivityReader's opens. Verified: one stderr line, exit 5, names the log path, the .pen file,
"the edit is on disk", and `mkdir -p <dir>`. It was already once per process — each verb is
its own process and one transaction appends once; see the report's caveat.

data.text:
`woodcase replace` landed on wt/TuTFD.

Shape: a new first-class `EditOperation.replaceSubtree(ReplaceSubtree)` carrying only
the subtree (its `id` names the node being replaced). Delete + insert was rejected —
`deleteNode` refuses a reusable definition with instances, would change the id, and
would log two events. `replaceSubtree`'s inverse is another `replaceSubtree` carrying
the materialized old subtree, so one activity event (`op: "replace"`) reverses in one
`undo` step and restores the previous bytes, including a `"children": []` that would
otherwise become absent.

Guards live on the document, not the CLI:
- `EditingError.componentTypeChange(componentID:from:to:instanceIDs:)` — new case,
  refusing a root type change on a reusable definition that instances point at. Exit 2
  (usage), matching `componentHasInstances`: it is the "consequential destruction is
  refused, then explained" family, not "the world changed" (3).
- The existing `componentHasInstances` now also fires when the *replaced* subtree
  contains a definition whose instances outlive it.
- `BatchError.replacementIDMismatch(address:supplied:kept:)` — a root id that is not
  the target's is refused rather than ignored.

Batch grammar gained `{"op":"replace","target":ADDR,"node":SUBTREE,"rev":REV}` — it
mirrored `add`'s line shape, so it was a small addition.

CRDT: no whole-subtree primitive exists, so `applyLocal` decomposes a replace into
deletes + updateCommon + updateKind + inserts, the way `detachRef` is already
decomposed. `CRDTDocument.processLocal` gets a defensive empty case.

Viewer: `ActivityRow` prints `event.op.rawValue` and does not switch on op, so it
needed no change. `ActivityRowFormatter.verbColumnWidth` is derived from
`Kind.allCases`; "replace" (7) is shorter than "override" (8), so the column is
unchanged.

data.text:
Implemented and tested. GoogleFontResolver.resolve(family:) already swallowed disk-cache-write
errors before this change (try? cache.cache(...)), so `shot`/`render`/`serve` already never
failed on a bad cache dir — what was missing was the memory fallback and the one-time stderr
notice. Added:

- Sources/Woodcase/GoogleFonts/GoogleFontMemoryFallback.swift (new): a process-wide,
  root-directory-scoped Data store (same shape as PenFontRegistry/FontResolutionCache) that
  GoogleFontResolver.resolveCached(family:) checks before touching disk, and that
  resolve(family:) populates when cache.cache(...) throws.
- GoogleFontResolver.swift: catches the cache-write error explicitly (was `try?`), stores into
  the fallback, and calls a new logCacheFallbackOnce() that writes exactly one
  FileHandle.standardError line naming cache.rootDirectory, gated by a counter
  (cacheFallbackNoticeCount, exposed for tests) so a document with many missing fonts prints
  once, not once per font.
- PenGoogleFonts.md: documents the fallback and the one-line notice under Caching.
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/GoogleFontResolverTests.swift: three new tests — cache-write failure
  still resolves (unwritableCacheStillResolves), logs exactly once across two families
  (unwritableCacheLogsOnce), and a second resolver sharing the same broken cache root reuses
  the fallback instead of re-fetching (memoryFallbackIsReusedAcrossResolvers). The unwritable
  root is a plain file blocking the directory path, not a chmod'd directory — sandbox-portable
  and doesn't depend on process UID.

Criterion XdO ("shot with an unwritable cache location renders and exits 0 with one stderr
line") is covered at the resolver level directly rather than through a `shot` CommandFixture
run, since shot already routes every font call through GoogleFontResolver.shared and never
inspects cache errors — the resolver-level tests are the more direct proof and don't need a
real network fetch through the CLI. Mark XdO done if that's an acceptable reading, or ask if
you want an end-to-end `shot` CommandFixture test added on top.

Full report (deviations, "what's wrong with the brief") went to the dispatching agent in this
session; ask there if you need it repeated. Suite: swift test --quiet, 2698 tests, 1 known
issue (pre-existing, unrelated), run twice for stability. swiftformat . --lint clean.

Implemented and tested. Summary:

- ServeCommand.swift: `--port` is now `UInt16?` (was `UInt16 = 7333`) — unset means "search",
  given means "pin exactly this, fail if taken". Added a hidden `--port-base` test-only option
  (documented reasoning: asserting "next port after 7333" against the real 7333 would be flaky
  under concurrent agents/serves on the same machine, so tests point the search at an
  OS-assigned ephemeral base instead of the real default). `defaultPort` stays 7333;
  `autoIncrementSpan` is 100 (7333...7433). Static `bind(_:files:pinned:searchBase:)` does the
  pin-vs-search branching and `failure(for:port:)` renders the two distinct messages.
- Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/SandboxDenial.swift (new): the shared helper you (or whoever owns
  the activity-log leaf) can call. `SandboxDenial.matches(_ error: Error) -> Bool` checks the
  raw POSIX errno first (POSIXError, CocoaError wrapping one via NSUnderlyingErrorKey), then
  falls back to scanning the error's rendered text for "Operation not permitted"/"Permission
  denied" — needed because both PenFileError (reason: String, from strerror) and the viewer's
  NWListener bind failure carry only rendered text, never a raw errno, once they reach
  CommandCore. `SandboxDenial.sentence(forbidding:)` gives the one sentence ("The environment
  forbids <action> (a sandbox); rerun with the sandbox disabled.").
- CommandFailure.swift: logMessage(_:editing:) (the activity-log branch) now calls
  SandboxDenial.matches first and swaps in the sandbox sentence instead of "Check
  $WOODCASE_HOME" when it matches — I only touched wording there, not the log's location or
  its dedup; that's yours. If you rework where the log lives, the SandboxDenial call is the
  one line to keep or move — the detection/sentence logic doesn't care about the log's path.
- Did NOT touch the font-cache side of "same EPERM treatment" — Woodcase's GoogleFontResolver
  never surfaces a cache-write error to CommandFailure at all (it's swallowed before this
  session even started, and the sibling font-cache leaf makes that explicit with a fallback +
  one stderr line instead), so there is no CommandFailure message there to update.
- Tests: Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/SandboxDenialTests.swift (new, pure unit tests on the
  helper). ServeCommandTests.swift: pinnedBusyPortIsConflict (a pinned, already-occupied port
  is exit 3 "in use", never "sandbox") and autoIncrementsPastABusyPort (no --port, --port-base
  pointed at an occupied port, asserts the next one is reported) — both occupy the port with a
  raw POSIX socket, not NWListener; see the two new project/gotchas.md entries dated 2026-08-30
  for why (NWListener reproducibly threw EINVAL in this exact suite, confirmed outside SwiftPM
  too, and separately a DispatchSemaphore-based version of the same helper starved under Swift
  Testing's scheduling before that). CommandFixture.swift gained runInBackground(_:)/LiveRun
  for driving a verb that never exits without waiting out its whole 120s budget.
- Docs: WoodcaseCLI.md's serve section and WoodcaseViewer.md's port paragraph updated —
  no more "fixed 7333."

data.text:
Plan settled after reading the viewer, the codec vocabulary and the emitters.

- Details reads the **expanded but variable-unresolved** document for what the node was
  authored as, and the resolved one for what it renders as. `PreparedDocument` gains
  `parsed` and `expanded` — both already computed inside `RenderCache.prepare` and
  thrown away today, so it costs nothing.
- `$var` is a string value beginning with `$` (the resolver's own test); override is
  `EditableDocument.resolve` + `expandedID`, compared against the stored definition node
  (`document.node(id:)` of the expanded id's last segment). The instance a row came from
  is `ResolvedNodeAddress.targetID` — the outermost ref, which is where the override is
  actually stored.
- Code targets are the real emitter outputs, not guesses: ReactEmitter's
  `components/{Name}.tsx` / `pages/{Name}.tsx`, ThemeEmitter's `theme.css`,
  StateEmitter's `states.css`, ManifestEmitter's `manifest.json`. `generate` has exactly
  one subcommand (`react`), and `render`/`shot` write png and pdf.
- PDFExporter moves from WoodcaseCommandCore to Woodcase so the viewer can export a PDF
  through the one implementation rather than a twin (WoodcaseCommandCore depends on
  WoodcaseViewer, not the other way round).
- Selection sets `tab=details` in `ViewState.selecting(_:)`, so every link that selects —
  outline row, render click, artboard switch — agrees without a second rule.

Added `woodcase help recipes` — a new topic (`HelpTopic+Recipes.swift`, registered as
`case recipes` in `HelpTopic.swift`) with 7 runnable command sequences: start a file,
build a screen root-down via an `apply` batch with `@tag`s, mark a node reusable and
`cp` an instance of it with `override`, `cp --times 5` with `{n}`, `vars set --theme`
for a themed `$var` fill, the lint/shot/tree loop, and `replace -F -` to rebuild a
subtree in place.

`RecipesTests.swift` extracts every `  woodcase …` line (and heredoc bodies opened
with `<<'TAG'`) straight from the topic's own text and runs them, in order, against
one scratch file via `CommandFixture` — added optional `stdin:` support to
`CommandFixture.run` for the `-F -` heredocs. All 7 recipes pass end to end.

data.text: Ben: on the map page the Outline lists the artboards (one row each, KindMark, rect, id chip; click drills in; up/down move the same focus as the boxes). Sent to the agent mid-flight; recorded in the design doc.

Plan (cartographer), after reading the design, the plan's Landed section, WoodcaseViewer.md and the viewer sources. Shape - `MapPage` is a new page at `GET /files/{file}` when the file has >1 artboard (and no `?node=` that resolves to an artboard). One artboard, or a `?node=` that resolves, lands on `ArtboardPage`. - `ArtboardMap` stops being a band and becomes the map page's canvas content: `#v-map`, one `` per artboard holding an `` from `…/{artboard}.png?max=320` and a label *beneath* the frame (KindMark + name). Boxes keep `data-artboard`, so the unread dots and the follow-drop handler are unchanged. - Left pane on the map page is `ArtboardOutline` — one row per artboard, same KindMark, rect and id chip a node row has, `data-artboard`, drilling in. It reuses `#v-outline` as its element id so it swaps into the same slot. - `#v-tabs`, its route, `ViewerLink.tabs` and `Fragment.tabs` are retired. Two fragments replace them: `GET /files/{file}/map` → `#v-map` and `GET /files/{file}/artboards` → `#v-outline` (the artboard listing). Both are whole-file: nothing is "current" on the map. - The node outline becomes artboard-scoped — `GET /files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}/outline` — because an `OutlineRow`'s href has to name the artboard now. Without that, clicking a row with the script off would navigate to `/files/{file}?node=…`, which is the map. - Breadcrumb: the file-name crumb is `a.v-crumb.v-crumb-map` with a map glyph; the script puts `data-unread="1"` on it when any artboard other than the one on screen is unread. - Footer: `ArtboardSteps` — `‹ n of N ›`, prev/next as real links carrying `data-artboard`. `stepArtboard()` clicks them instead of reading the retired strip. - Task B: the code toggle moves into `.v-tabbar` after Export, styled as a switch (track + knob), never a pill like a tab. `.v-canvas-head` goes. - Keys: a third context, `map` (`#v-map` present). ←/↑ previous box, →/↓ next box, Enter opens the focused one; one focus ring mirrored onto the outline row. Escape's ladder becomes presentation → up to the map → clear the selection, as the design words it. - Follow on the map page: the control stays, its form submits to the map's URL, and a matching write drills into the touched artboard — which is what `goToArtboard` already does. Its fragment gains a whole-file route, `GET /files/{file}/follow`.

data.text:
Findings while building remote image support (remote-images, wt/remote-images).

Two things the brief guessed at, now checked against the code:

1. Child-bearing kinds. Only `frame` and `group` carry `[PenNode]` children —
   grep for `var children` across Sources/Woodcase/Models/ returns exactly
   PenNode+FrameData.swift:73 and PenNode+GroupData.swift:35. So
   GoogleFontResolver.collectFontFamilies recursing only those two is *correct*,
   not an oversight; the brief's suspicion that other kinds carry children is
   wrong. Sources/Woodcase/Tree/SettledTree.swift:80 makes the same two-case
   choice, which is the second witness.

2. Stroke image fills are not collected, deliberately. Strokes are typed
   `PenFills` in the model (rectangle, ellipse, polygon, path, frame, text, line),
   so an image stroke fill can be *authored*, but PenStrokeRenderer.renderStroke
   only ever calls resolveStrokeColor — it has no imageProvider parameter and
   never draws a bitmap. Downloading for a stroke fill would be bytes over the
   wire that cannot reach a pixel. Fills are collected from rectangle, ellipse,
   polygon, path, frame, icon and text.

Consequence of the protocol extraction: `GoogleFontError.httpError(Int)` had
exactly one thrower, URLSessionFontFetcher. Moving that fetcher out to
Sources/Woodcase/Networking/ as URLSessionDataFetcher would have left a public
enum case nothing in the library can raise — a trap for a `catch` that never
fires. It is replaced by `RemoteFetchError.httpError(statusCode:)` in the
Networking directory and the GoogleFonts case is removed. That is a breaking
public-API change (BUILD stage, flagged rather than shimmed); I could not check
Penumbra or RapidPro for uses from inside the worktree.

Done on wt/remote-images: full suite green (3058 tests, 313 suites, 1 pre-existing
known issue), swiftformat clean, DocC builds with no new link warnings.

Shape: Sources/Woodcase/Networking/ (RemoteDataFetching, URLSessionDataFetcher,
RemoteFetchError) + Sources/Woodcase/RemoteImages/ (RemoteImageCache,
RemoteImageMemoryFallback, RemoteImageResolver, +Collection) +
PenRenderer.imageProvider(relativeTo:remote:) in the renamed
Rendering/PenRenderer+ImageProvider.swift. prepareImages wired beside
prepareFonts in RenderCache.prepare, RenderCommand and ShotCommand; all four
provider call sites moved to the combined provider.

Not verified here and worth an integrator check: the two Unsplash fills on
artboard ydnjs of local/viewer-demo/woodcase-app.pen. local/ is gitignored so
it does not exist in the worktree — `woodcase shot` on it from the main
checkout after merge is the real end-to-end proof.

data.text:
Diagnosis (sel-tabs, before any code change). Two independent causes, not one.

1. The outline does not walk into instances. `ViewState.expand` defaults to false and
   `ArtboardPageBuilder.rows` passes it to `TreeView.rows(expandInstances:)`, so the
   outline lists a `ref` as a single row. The render's layout is always built from the
   *expanded* document, so a click inside an instance selects `Card1/Ttl03` and no row
   carries that id. What Ben saw as "the Outline shows the component's whole tree" is
   the reusable *definition* listed at top level (its rows are `Ttl03`, not
   `Card1/Ttl03`).

2. The instance root has two spellings and the layout uses the wrong one.
   `PenRefExpander.prefixIDs` roots the clone at `<refID>/<componentRootID>`
   (`Card1/CardC`), and `ArtboardLayout` copies expanded node ids verbatim. But
   `TreeView` names that row `Card1` (the ref), and `EditableDocument.resolve` has no
   step onto the component root — so `Card1/CardC` matches no outline row *and* throws
   `addressNotFound`, which is the pane's "'224Gu/oqIX' names no node in this file"
   verbatim (ref id / component root id). Descendants (`Card1/Ttl03`,
   `Card1/Btn02/Lbl02`) already agree between the two walks.

Tab bugs are wholly client-side, in the k92mT block of ViewerScript:
- `showTab()` writes `#v-right`'s `data-tab` but never moves `is-current` on the
  `.v-tab` links, so the pane shows Details under a highlighted Activity pill.
- the tab `<a href>` is server-rendered from the state *at page load*; a selection made
  after load only pushState's and swaps the render and outline fragments, so the Details
  tab's href still has no `?node=`. Clicking it navigates to that stale URL and drops
  the selection, while the render region (not re-swapped) keeps the box drawn.
- `syncSelectionTab` is only queued from a click on `.v-outline-row`/`.v-render`, so a
  keyboard selection (Arrow keys, Escape) never moves the tab at all.

## Map hover + glyph polish — done

Both criteria met, TDD red→green, in `Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Styles/ViewerStylesheet.swift`
(map section only, between the `B1sAM` markers) and
`Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/ArtboardMapTests.swift` (3 new tests, no new file).

1. Hover outline: `.v-map-board:hover .v-map-frame` border-color changed from
   `var(--v-muted)` to `var(--v-accent)` — the same token `.v-map-board.is-focused
   .v-map-frame` (the selected state) already uses for its outline/border.
2. Kind glyph bubble: added map-scoped overrides (not touching KindMark.swift or the
   general `.v-kind-mark`/`.v-kind-glyph` rules, so outline rows are pixel-identical):
   `.v-map-label .v-kind-mark { width: 15px; height: 15px; padding: 0;
   justify-content: center; }` and `.v-map-label .v-kind-glyph { font-size: 11px;
   line-height: 1; }`. The general pill's padding (1px 5px) was shaped for the
   word-plus-glyph layout; on the map the word is already hidden
   (`.v-map-label .v-kind-label { display: none; }`), so a fixed circle around the glyph
   alone, with `line-height: 1`, centers it on both axes instead of following the pill's
   text baseline.

Verified fact worth noting: commit 0174914 (today, Ben) shrunk `.v-kind-glyph` globally
10px→8px "closer to the cap height of the 9px label text" for the *outline rows*' sake —
that's why the map read too small right after. Confirms the brief's instinct to scope the

data.text: Session practice (Ben, 2026-08-30): every agent briefing from wave 2 on asks for feedback on Sleepy Hollow (`sleepy` CLI / SleepyHollow package) — what was useful, what caused friction. Collection lives in the session scratchpad (sleepy-feedback.md); compile into a report for the Sleepy Hollow project at session end. Wave-2 agents (client-nav, outline-scope) were asked mid-flight via SendMessage.

Investigation (before any edit), against b70dbd6:

WHAT ACTUALLY RELOADS on the artboard page
- Arrow keys: `stepArtboard()` clicks `a.v-step-previous` / `a.v-step-next`. The main
  click listener intercepts only `.v-copy`, `.v-box-tag`, `.v-outline-row` and
  `.v-render`, so a step link falls through to a real browser navigation. FULL LOAD.
- Outline row clicks: already in place — `select()` -> `go()` -> pushState + two
  fragment swaps. NOT a page load. What Ben saw as "jumps" is the outline's
  `scrollTop` being discarded: `swap()` replaces `#v-outline` (the scroll container)
  outright, so it comes back at 0 and `revealSelection()` then parks the row at the
  bottom edge.
- Escape -> map, map box -> artboard, follow -> artboard: real navigations, and
  mode changes (#v-map <-> #v-stage). Out of scope; the follow one is deliberate
  (documented race).

WHAT AN IN-PLACE ARTBOARD SWITCH MUST COVER
`#v-render-region` (image, layout JSON, `#v-stage[data-artboard]`, selection bar +
steps), `#v-outline` (rows link into the new artboard), `#v-right` (tab hrefs,
Details, Export, Code), `#v-follow` (form action names the artboard), `.v-crumbs`
(last crumb is the artboard name) and `document.title`.

The crumb and the title have no fragment endpoint, and TopBar.swift belongs to Qe32p
this wave. So: one fetch of the destination page + swap those elements by selector,
the way `swapFromPage()` already does for the dashboard. Cheaper than five fragment
fetches, no client-side templating, and the server stays the only thing that renders
a string.

Guard: a `change` event's fragment refresh captures its URLs synchronously for the
artboard then on screen (the reason `goToArtboard` is a plain navigation). Adding a
navigation generation counter to `swap()` makes a late response for the old artboard
drop instead of landing.

Also in scope: clicking the canvas outside the stage clears the selection.

Implemented. Full suite green: 3104 tests / 319 suites, 1 pre-existing known issue
(`swift test --quiet`, sandbox off). Base b70dbd6; branch worktree-agent-ac840f795896ac761.

WHAT BECAME IN-PLACE
- The footer's `‹`/`›` and the ← / → that click them. A `pushState` plus one fetch of
  the destination page; five elements are swapped out of it — `#v-render-region`,
  `#v-outline`, `#v-right`, `#v-follow`, `.v-crumbs` — plus `document.title`. Those are
  every piece that names the artboard; the crumb and the title have no fragment, which
  is why it is a page fetch rather than five fragment fetches. It costs the server the
  same render a reload cost it, minus the document, and the result is byte-identical to
  the reloaded page for those five elements.
- `popstate` for a different artboard runs the same swap; the main block's own popstate
  handler now stands aside for that case so the two never both answer.
