## Tests
`Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/LintCommandTests.swift`, 9 new cases (`--exclude` ×4,
`--severity` ×4, both composed ×1) — all drive the real built binary via
`CommandFixture`, per house convention. Verified red first: ran the suite before
touching `LintCommand.swift`, all 9 failed on `Error: Unknown option '--exclude'` /
`'--severity'` (exit 2 where tests expected 0/1), the other 11 pre-existing tests
stayed green. Then implemented and reran: 20/20 green.

## Full suite
`swift test --quiet` (sandbox off): 3151 tests / 324 suites, passed, 1 known issue.
First run surfaced 9 issues: one real (`LintFormatterTests.checksAreNamed`'s
hardcoded `LintCheck.allCases` list needed `duplicate-name` added — fixed, same
"existing test must change because behavior changed" case as Gb9C7's own
LintFormatterTests fix) and 8 in `FileWatcherTests`/`ViewerBrowserTests`/
`ViewerFollowBrowserTests` — all timing-sensitive, all in files this leaf never
touched. Reran `FileWatcherTests` alone (0 issues) and the full suite again
(0 issues, only the 1 known issue) confirming load-induced flakiness matching the
documented gotcha, not a regression.
`swiftformat . --lint`: 0/771 files need formatting.

Fixed (beacon, 2026-08-31). The log's live tail now adopts as well as the startup read.

- `ViewerFileIndex.adopt(_:)` — new; inserts one file the log just named, refusing three
  cases: files were given on the command line, the file is already indexed, or nothing is
  at that path. `adoptFilesFromLogs` now goes through it, so the history pass and the live
  pass cannot drift.
- `ChangeCoordinator.logged(_:)` — looks the file up, adopts it if it is unknown, and on a
  fresh adoption calls `welcome(_:)`: watch it (the coordinator now keeps the `FileWatcher`
  it was started with), then `fileChanged` (which invalidates, prepares, warms, attributes
  and broadcasts the `change`), then `warmThumbnails`. The log event is queued into
  `pending` *before* adoption, so the change the adoption publishes is attributed rather
  than waiting out the match window as an unattributed write.
- `viewer.js` — the dashboard's empty page never actually became a dashboard: its own
  DocC claimed "the stream says so and the page reloads", but the change handler called
  `swapFromPage(["v-files", …])` and the empty page has none of those ids, so nothing
  happened. Both empty states now carry `data-empty-file` (a file id, or empty for "any
  file at all") and the change handler reloads. That is what makes the adoption visible.

Regression test: `Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/ViewerAdoptionTests.swift`. Starts a bare
serve over an empty scratch, writes a file + one logged edit, expects it listed, a change
announcing it, and — the part that proves the *watch* rather than the index — a second
change for a second write. A companion case proves `serve a.pen` still adopts nothing.

Note for the integrator: `adoptionTasks` is one retained `Task` handle per adopted file
for the life of the server, so `stop()` can cancel a warm in flight. Bounded by files
served; not pruned.

Fixed (beacon, 2026-08-31). Both halves.

(1) `Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Pages/FileEmptyPage.swift` — new page, the dashboard empty
state's atom one level down: centred title ("No artboards yet"), one muted lede, a
`chrome` command block with the real `woodcase add … document -F -` line, and a mono note
reading "watching for changes · <path> · N variables, no frames". Top bar and theme picker
are the ordinary ones, so presence and the live badge work. `ArtboardPageBuilder.page`
branches to it when the document has no artboards *and* the request named none —
`/files/{id}/artboards/Nope` on the same file still 404s, which is right.
It carries `data-empty-file="<id>"`; `viewer.js` reloads the page when a `change` for that
file arrives carrying artboards, so the first frame turns it into the map with nobody
pressing anything. A fragment swap could not do it: the page that answers next has a
different body layout and a different trail, so the reload *is* the update.

(2) The empty id is gone structurally, not by string-patching. New case
`ViewerError.noArtboards(file:)`; `unknownArtboard`'s `available.isEmpty` branch — the one
that produced `'' cannot be rendered` — is deleted, so that case now always has ids to
offer and can never quote nothing. The lookup is one function,
`PreparedDocument.artboard(id:of:)`, which picks between the two; `RenderCache.png/image/pdf`
and `ViewerEndpoints.export` all went through it, removing four copies of the same guard.
`landing(in:state:)` no longer returns `""` for a frameless file — it returns nil, and the
branch above catches it first. `Route` refuses an empty capture (Route.swift:88), so no
path can hand an empty id to `unknownArtboard` either.

Tests: three in `ViewerPagesTests` over the `parser-variables.pen` fixture (variables, zero
frames — exactly the reported file): the page is a 200 HTML empty state, a named artboard
is a 404 whose body contains no `''`, and the PNG endpoint likewise. Plus a golden preview
(`page-file-empty.html`) and a check that the page names its own file id.

Done as decided (beacon, 2026-08-31): shimmer + lazy warming, no warm-per-change.

Shimmer. `ArtboardMap.Board` ships its frame as `class="v-map-frame is-loading"`. The
stylesheet draws a slow `chrome` band travelling across the `panel` ground, as a
*background behind the image* — so a loaded PNG covers it with no help from JavaScript and
the page is right with the script off. `viewer.js` removes the class on the image's `load`
or `error` (captured at the document, because neither bubbles) plus a sweep of
`image.complete` on init and on every body mutation, so nothing animates for the rest of
the session and a swapped-in cached image is settled even if it never fires `load`. Stops
entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The class is on the *frame*, not the box, because
the box already carries `is-touched` and means something else — the existing
`class="v-map-board is-touched"` assertion in ViewerPagesTests is untouched.

`--wait-for js:images-complete` still works: the sweep reads the same `complete` flag the
tool does, so a screenshot can never catch a settled box still shimmering.

Lazy warming. New `RenderCache.warmThumbnails(_:edge:)` renders every artboard at
`ArtboardMap.thumbnailEdge`; `ViewerServer.start` runs it in the background warming task
*after* the full-size pass over every file, and the adoption path in `ChangeCoordinator`
does the same for a newly adopted file. Deliberately **not** on every change, for the
reason `RenderCache.dashboardThumbnailEdge` already documents: a thumbnail is a second full
render of every artboard, and paying that per write makes every write slower for a page
that is usually not open. A map opened after a change fills in on demand, under the
shimmer.

Also new: `RenderCache.isRendered(artboard:of:theme:longestSide:)` — the honest way to ask
whether an image is warm, which both a caller deciding to warm and a test proving one ran
need; timing a render is not an answer.

Tests: `RenderCacheTests` proves `warm` alone leaves the `?max=320` variants cold and
`warmThumbnails` warms all three; `ViewerServerTests` proves startup does it end to end;
`ArtboardMapTests` proves the markup and the two CSS rules. Goldens `artboard-map.html` and
`page-map.html` re-blessed (the `is-loading` class only).

DESIGN.md gained a "Loading shimmer" atom.

Fixed (beacon, 2026-08-31) in `PreparedDocument.matches(_:_:)`.

The rule was "exact id, or the id-path's *last* component". `PenRefExpander.prefixIDs`
writes `<ref id>/<node id>` at every level of nesting, so an expanded id is a path whose
**every** step is an authored id: `Chi01/Cmp01` is the ref `Chi01` holding the component
root `Cmp01`, and `Chi01/Lbl01` is a node inside it. Matching only the last component
caught the nodes inside a ref and never the ref itself. The matcher now checks every
component, which is the same rule the expansion writes.

No false positives to worry about: ids are unique within a file, and a middle step naming
a node genuinely means that node's expansion is on this artboard — which is exactly what
`changedArtboards` is asked for. Nested refs get the same answer for the same reason.

Two tests in `ChangedArtboardsTests`:
- the unit expectation, `artboardIDs(containing: ["Chi01"]) == ["Brd01"]`;
- the pipeline one the leaf asked for — a real `PenFileTransaction.run` setting
  `common.name` on the bare ref `Chi01` with `--as ana`, the logged event read back from
  the log (asserting it really records `Chi01`), fed through `ChangeCoordinator`, expecting
  `change.changedArtboards == ["Brd01"]`.

Both were red before the one-line matcher change.

The corresponding entry in `project/gotchas.md` ("2026-08-30 — `artboardIDs(containing:)`
misses a write to a ref node's own id") is now stale and should be deleted on integration —
I left it alone rather than editing a shared file four agents are reading.

The gate was `ActivityRecorder.apply`, one line: `guard let identity else { try document.apply(...); return nil }`. An `Optional<String>` was carrying two facts at once — *who wrote this* and *whether to record it at all* — which is the bool-that-means-several-things trap from the house rules wearing an Optional. Nothing at the call sites was involved: every verb already passes `identity.identity` straight through, and `PenFileTransaction` already resolved the log and appended unconditionally. So the fix is exactly where the sweep predicted, and it is a deletion.

Changed (fix at the source, no sentinel invented at a call site):
- `ActivityEvent.unattributed` (`""`) — the new name for the writer nobody claimed. It lives on `ActivityEvent`, not on the recorder, because `identity` is an *event* field and readers want the constant too; `ActivityRecorder` is `@MainActor`, so a constant there could not be read from a nonisolated context anyway.
- `ActivityRecorder` stores `identity ?? ActivityEvent.unattributed` as a plain `String`. The gate is gone, `isRecording` is gone (it was only ever the gate's public face and had no callers), and `apply` now returns a non-optional `ActivityEvent` — every applied operation produces one. No caller in `Sources/` bound the old optional, so nothing outside the recorder changed shape.
- Docs corrected rather than appended to, in six places that all asserted the old behaviour as a *reason*: `IdentityOptions`, `IdentityRole`'s `--as` help text, `UndoFailures.missingIdentity` (its stated cause — "an unattributed edit is not logged" — was the wrong-cause-is-worse-than-none case; undo still requires `--as`, but now because a reversal has to say who made it, not because the alternative is unlogged), `PenFileTransaction`, `WoodcaseActivityLog.md`, `WoodcaseCLI.md`, `WoodcaseEditor.md`.

The other overload, `run(at:timeout:)`, still logs nothing — but its doc now says the honest reason: its body is handed no recorder, so it *cannot* record. That is the one remaining way to edit a .pen file without a line in the log, and it is now the only one.

Tests (red first, all four failed against the old gate):
- `SetCommandTests.unattributedSetIsLoggedWithAnEmptyIdentity` — the brief's regression test, end to end through the built binary. `CommandFixture` already strips `$WOODCASE_AS`, so no flag and no variable is the whole of the unattributed case. Exactly one event, `identity == ""`, `op == .set`, path pinned.
- `SetCommandTests.blankIdentityIsUnattributed` — `--as "  "` trims to nothing and is the same state, not a writer named with spaces.
- `ActivityRecorderTests.unattributedTransactionLogsWithAnEmptyIdentity` and `.unattributedEventIsUndoable` — the event carries a real inverse and revision, so it is history like any other, not a stub.
- `ActivityRecorderTests.documentOnlyEditsAreNotLogged` pins the one honest escape hatch.

Interface: unchanged for the viewer. `ActivityEvent`'s shape is untouched — `identity` was already a non-optional `String`, so an empty one is a valid event every existing reader accepts, and the viewer is already built for it (`ActorColor` draws the `?` disc, `AvatarView` titles it "unattributed", `Follow` deliberately matches nothing). Nothing in `Sources/WoodcaseViewer/` was edited.

Two follow-ons I did **not** take, both out of this leaf's scope:
1. There is no way to *filter for* unattributed events. `--as` blank is "unset", so `activity --as ""` shows everything rather than the anonymous writes. If the viewer grows a "nobody" follow target, the CLI needs a spelling for it too.
2. `undo` still refuses without `--as`. That is now a real editorial choice rather than a consequence of the bug, and it is defensible, but it means an unattributed write is logged-and-undoable-by-a-named-person rather than undoable by whoever made it. Worth a decision if it ever bites.

data.description: Found by the viewer agent (beacon) while baselining its leaves (2026-08-31): the full suite on unmodified 5a76473 failed roughly 4 of 5 runs, alternating between ViewerFollowBrowserTests.unreadDotUntilViewed and ViewerBrowserTests ("timed out waiting for Escape to go up to the map"). The unread-dot one was a real test race — the test navigated to the map immediately after a write, but the unread mark is recorded by whichever page hears the SSE change, so navigating first threw the news away and the map waited out its full 30s bound; it also never waited for the stream to reconnect after host.load. Fixed at vOJbc integration with two waitFors. The Escape timeout is untouched and probably the same shape — a wait that assumes an event already landed rather than waiting for it. Diagnose with the same method: find what records the state Escape's assertion reads, and waitFor the recording, not the effect.
data.title: ViewerBrowserTests Escape-to-map timeout is probably the unread-dot race's twin

data.text:
Fixed. The rule "a container that declares `children: []` is not a container that
declares nothing" was written out three times — `EditableDocument.flattenNode` (load,
correct), `EditableDocument+Replace.writeSubtree` (correct), and
`EditableDocument+Apply.flattenAndInsert` (wrong: `if !childIDs.isEmpty`). Rather than
fix the third copy, the rule now lives once: `PenNode.Kind.declaredChildIDs -> [String]?`
in `PenNode+Editing.swift`, `nil` when the kind declares no children array, and all
three writers read their `children[id]` entry from it. `childIDs` stays as
`declaredChildIDs ?? []` for the callers that only want the ids.

Tests: Tests/WoodcaseTests/EditOperationInsertChildrenTests.swift — six cases, both
directions (an empty array survives, an absent one stays absent) across root insert,
nested insert, and undo-of-delete. Red first: the three `[]` cases failed, and the two
`nil` control cases passed during the red run — they are there so the fix cannot turn
`nil` into `[]` on the way past, and they are called out as green-on-red in the report.

Note the previously-buggy path also silently skipped recursing into children whenever
the declared list was empty; that was harmless (nothing to recurse into) but the new
code recurses unconditionally over `inlineChildren`, which is the honest shape.

THE LEAF'S DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, and so is the decision note that followed it. Batch
root-level adds have auto-placed since b88e3a3 (2026-08-30): `BatchApplier.planAdd`
already called `placedAtRoot`, and `apply` plans each line against the document as it
then stands, so the batch and the standalone verbs share one code path. Verified with
the built binary: three plain frames added in one `apply` batch land at 0, 200, 400.

The real discriminator is `reusable: true`. Reproduced both ways — a batch of three
reusable frames, and two standalone `woodcase add document` calls — every one lands
with no coordinates at all. The standalone verbs are just as broken; the batch/verb
framing in the leaf is a coincidence of what the kit agent happened to run.

Cause: `placedAtRoot` and `RootOverlap.overlaps(in:)` measured through
`EditableDocument.computeLayout()`, whose expansion runs `PenRefExpander.expand(...,
keepReusables: false)` and therefore produces no rect for a component definition. So
placement saw an empty (or short) root list and bailed, and the write-time overlap
warning was blind to the same roots — while `DocumentLinter`, which reads a
`SettledTree` (`keepReusables: true`), saw them and produced the 100+ artboard-overlap
warnings the leaf reports. `SettledTree`'s own doc comment already spelled the trap out.

Fix: one new seam, `RootOverlap.roots(in:) -> [Root]`, running the linter's pipeline
(`SettledTree(document:theme: [:])`). `placedAtRoot` and `overlaps(in:)` both read it,
so a write and a lint cannot disagree about what is on the canvas. `apply --help` and
the placement prose in WoodcaseEditor.md are now true, with a paragraph saying
definitions are roots too.

Behaviour change worth flagging: the write-time `artboard-overlap` warning now fires
for overlapping component definitions, which it never did. That is the same finding
lint already gave, arriving at the write instead of a pass later. No existing test
changed.

Tests: Tests/WoodcaseTests/BatchApplierComponentPlacementTests.swift — placement of a
component past a component, past an artboard, a three-line batch fanning out (which is
what caught the "only the first one places" half), an artboard past a component, and
the overlap check seeing two components. Red first, all six.

(2) TAG COMPOSITION — took the preferred branch. `NodeAddress.tag(String)` became
`tag(name: String, path: [String])`; the parser splits on `/` first and only then peels
the `@`, so `@row1/Uiko4` parses and `@hero/` still does not. Resolution: the walk was
split into a seeding half and a stepping half (`resolveWalk(from:through:written:
missing:)`), so a tag enters the same stepper with one seed cursor. Every path
behaviour therefore holds after a tag for free — id-beats-name at each segment, the
step into a component instance (`@card1/Title` resolves to `.instanceDescendant`), and
the ambiguity/near-miss errors. `BatchPoison` matches the tag half only, so a line
addressing `@row/Title` still cascades when `@row`'s line failed. Verified end to end:
`{"op":"add","tag":"row1",…}` then `{"op":"set","target":"@row1/Label",…}` both apply.

Callers updated: BatchPoison, the resolver, NodeAddressTests, BatchOperationCodableTests.
`NodeAddressTests.malformed` had `"@a/b"` in its "does not parse" list — that expectation
IS the bug, so it was replaced with `"@a/"` and `"@/b"`, which still must not parse, and
`"@hero/Title"` was added to the round-trip list.

(1) BARE `--props` — the decision note is not implementable as written, and the fix is
in an unusual place; please read this before reviewing. ArgumentParser has no
optional-valued option: `.upToNextOption` on an array throws `errorForMissingValue`
when zero values follow (ArgumentSet.swift:449), and `[T]?` has no `@Option` overload at
all. So `--props` written bare fails during parsing, before any verb can default it.

Rather than settle for teaching in the error (the leaf's fallback), the argument vector
is normalised once before the parser runs: `BareOptionValue.filled(_:)` in
WoodcaseCommandCore, called from `WoodcaseCommand.main`'s `parseAsRoot(_:)`. It is a
table of one entry, it stops at a `--` terminator, and the value it supplies is written
into the option's own help so the behaviour is discoverable rather than magic. If the
integrator would rather not have argv surgery in the CLI, the alternative is to revert
`BareOptionValue.swift` and the one line in `WoodcaseCommand.swift`, keep everything
else, and accept that `--props` needs a value — `--props=` and `--props ""` already get
the defaults through `Tree.propertyPaths(in:)` either way.

The default column set is `kind.layout, kind.fill, kind.content, kind.fontSize`, chosen
by counting authored keys over the 307 nodes of
project/2026-08-31-mobile-viewer/mobile-viewer.pen (fill 163, layout 98, content 74,
fontSize 74) once the columns a row already has — type, name, rect, id — are set aside.
The empty-column stderr warning is suppressed for the default set: the caller named no
path, so an empty column there is this verb's choice rather than their typo.

(a) DONE. `BatchApplier.firstLiteralRootOverridesKey(in:ancestorNames:)` walks an
authored subtree beside the existing `firstUnnamedNode` check and refuses any `ref`
whose decoded `rootOverrides` carries the key `rootOverrides`. Called from `planAdd`
and `planReplace`, which is every door an authored subtree comes through — `add`,
`replace` and both of them inside `apply`. `cp` needs no check: it copies nodes that
are already in the document. New case `BatchError.literalRootOverridesKey(locator:)`,
whose message names the ref by its path of names and gives both working forms, in the
batch dialect and the command dialect. Verified against the binary: exit 2, and the
message names `set kind.rootOverrides='{"width":80}'` with the real file path.

(b) DONE, but NOT where the brief said. The `.pen key` column is not written in
PenSchemaTable.swift — the rows are assembled in `PenSchema.rows(for:prefix:)` from
`NodePropertyCodec.jsonKey(for:)`, and NodePropertyCodec* is another agent's. `jsonKey`
is used for real reads and writes, so it could not be bent for display. Instead
`PenSchemaTable.Property.key` became a typed `PenKeyForm` (`.key(String)` /
`.inlined`), and `PenSchema` marks `rootOverrides` inlined. `help schema ref` now reads
`kind.rootOverrides  (top-level keys)  {key: value}`, and `--json` emits `key: null`
for it rather than a key that does not exist.

(c) ASSESSED — ALREADY CORRECT, nothing built. `get` prints the node exactly as the
file stores it: root overrides come back as inlined top-level keys, byte-identical to
the node's JSON on disk. Confirmed by diffing `woodcase get <file> Inst` against the
node in the file. What made the original report look like a `get` problem is that the
*junk* key round-tripped faithfully too — `get` was accurately printing a broken node.
With (a) in place that node can no longer be created, so there is nothing left to do.

DEVIATION worth a look: `PenKeyForm` changed a public type that
Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Components/NodeDetails.swift consumes, which is on my
do-not-touch list. Leaving it broken would have failed the build, so I made the
two-line mechanical adaptation there — `keys[property.path] = property.key.written` in
`wireKeys(of:)`, twice. Assigning `nil` removes the entry and the function's existing
`?? field(of: path)` fallback covers it, so the viewer's rendered output is unchanged.

Integrator ruling on the flagged deviation (2026-08-31, recorded under the leaf's claim identity): the argv normalization (BareOptionValue.filled before parseAsRoot) STAYS. Reviewed against project/agents/cli-design.md: a documented table of one with admission criteria in its doc comment, respects the -- terminator, fills only when the next token is absent or an option, and the defaulting is written into --props's own help — "discoverable rather than magic". The alternative (a teaching error) costs every agent one failed call; a widening flag that defaults is the better grammar. Revisit only if the table grows past genuinely bare-able read flags.

cp now translates a nested prop on an instance into the matching override (prism, 2026-08-31)

`CopyCommand.applyCopy` emitted a `set` for every descendant property. When the copy is
a `ref` — which every copy of a reusable node is — `BatchApplier.planSet` refused with
`setInsideInstance` and the whole transaction rolled back, so `cp --help`'s own example
worked only for a non-reusable source.

It now resolves each descendant address first and picks the write the target can take:
a `.node` gets `set` (unchanged), an `.instanceDescendant` gets `override` with the
properties rekeyed by the new `NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed(_:)` — `kind.content` →
`content`, `common.name` → `name`, `kind.fills` → `fill`. A key already written raw is
passed through, so both vocabularies work on the `cp` line. An address that resolves to
nothing still takes the `set` branch, so the "names nothing in the copy" refusal is
unchanged (that test was green on first run and is a guard, not a red test — said so in
the report).

New public API: `NodePropertyCodec.rawKey(for:)` / `rawKeyed(_:)`, in
`Sources/Woodcase/Editing/NodePropertyCodec+RawKeys.swift`. Tests:
`Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/CopyIntoInstanceTests.swift` (5) and
`Tests/WoodcaseTests/NodePropertyCodecRawKeyTests.swift` (3).

Docs: the `cp` discussion, `WoodcaseEditor.md`'s `cp` section and the Overrides section,
and the "A COMPONENT, THEN AN INSTANCE" recipe — which now places and titles in one
command, and is executed by `RecipesTests`, so it cannot rot.

Repointing a nested ref now works; the premise in the issue was wrong (prism, 2026-08-31)

**Nothing was corrupted, and nothing was written wrong.** `PenRefExpander` has always
honoured `descendants: {"pZv2c": {"ref": "sBunx"}}` — the *render* was correct the whole
time. `woodcase shot mobile-viewer.pen qAXRH` after the repoint draws the Current pill,
verified before any code changed. What was broken is every reader that recomputes which
component a `ref` places from the **authored** flat store:

- `TreeView.componentRoot(of:in:)` — looked up rect id `qAXRH/pZv2c/MInM2` while the
  expansion had produced `qAXRH/pZv2c/sBunx`, hence the `-` rects, and listed the *old*
  component's children (`.../SoZKm`), hence the wrong child rows.
- `EditableDocument.componentRootID(placedBy:)` behind `expandedID(of:)` — same miss, so
  `get`/`shot` on the instance failed.
- `EditableDocument.steps(from:)` in the address walk — stepped into the old component,
  so `qAXRH/pZv2c/z84S1` (the live node) resolved to nothing while `qAXRH/pZv2c/SoZKm`
  (the dead one) was still accepted.
- `overridableDescendantKeys` — validated an override's key against the authored
  component, so the guard refused exactly the keys that now exist.

Fixed at the source with one helper both the tree and the addressing ask:
`EditableDocument.effectiveRefData(of:insideInstances:)` +
`componentRootID(placedBy:insideInstances:)` in
`Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+EffectiveRef.swift`. It patches the authored
node with the enclosing instance's override the same way the expander does, so the two
cannot drift; it short-circuits on non-`ref` nodes so the per-node cost of a tree read is
unchanged.

**The issue's second claim is also wrong**: overriding back to the original id *does*
restore it. Reproduced the full round trip on `mobile-viewer.pen` before the fix —
`override qAXRH/pZv2c ref=MInM2` gave `135,0 58×19` again, byte-identical rows. Whatever
the activity agent saw was not the value being written back.

**Known limit, parked in `project/backlog.md`:** only the instance a node sits *directly*
inside can repoint it, which is the expander's own limit — a `descendants` key with a `/`
is applied after the nested instance has expanded, when the `ref` it would rewrite is
gone. That case is a silent no-op, not corruption. Making it work means distributing
cross-ref overrides into each nested ref's own map before recursion (changes
`PenRefExpander` for every file and every React golden); refusing it needs a new
`EditingError` case plus a message in `Sources/Woodcase/Batch/`, which this leaf does not
own. Both are written up in the backlog entry.

Regression tests: `Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/RefRepointCommandTests.swift` (3, through
the binary: settle → address → edit → restore) and
`Tests/WoodcaseTests/EffectiveRefTests.swift` (6), on the new fixture
`Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/ref-repoint-nested.pen`.

**The premise of this leaf is wrong, and correcting it is the finding.** "The only live Woodcase frames were two `ActivityReader.follow` poll loops — an await-forever in some activity/follow test": the observation is right, the inference does not follow. A Swift task suspended at an `await` has **no thread and no stack frames**, so in a run wedged on an unresumed continuation `sample` cannot show the wedged code at all, and the only Woodcase frames it can possibly contain belong to whatever is still *running*. A poll loop is exactly that. The sample was evidence of a live follower, not of the stuck test.

Confirmed by observation, not argument. On 2026-08-31, with several agents testing at once, two hosts were wedged at 0 % CPU simultaneously:
- pid 46108, the **main checkout on unmodified `main`**, 11 min: two `ActivityReader.follow` poll loops at `ActivityReader.swift:201` and `:107-109` — a byte-for-byte reproduction of this leaf's sample. So the wedge is real and reproduces under multi-agent load; it is not rare.
- pid 58566, **a sibling agent's worktree, `follow` not yet rewritten**, 10 min: `ActivityReader.follow` at `ActivityReader.swift:201` **and `:208`** — the leaf's two line numbers exactly.
- pid 48269, **this worktree with `follow` already rewritten**, 8 min: **zero** Woodcase frames, plus a live `com.apple.network.connections` queue.

Three hosts in one afternoon: both carrying the old `AsyncStream`-backed follow show the leaf's signature, the one carrying the rewrite shows none of our code at all — and across ten loaded runs of the rewrite not one wedged.

Same wedge, follow loops gone, still stuck. The loops were bystanders. Whatever is stuck is suspended, and the one thread-level clue points at the viewer's Network.framework HTTP seam (`HTTPServer`/`HTTPConnection` both await `withCheckedContinuation` on a state handler) — which is also where `project/gotchas.md` already records an un-root-caused `NWListener` `EINVAL` in this suite. **That is a viewer-surface investigation and I left it to its owner; this leaf did not fix the wedge.** Full write-up with both samples: `project/2026-08-31-follow-is-a-value.md`, and a gotchas entry for the third hang face (0 % CPU, no frames of ours — the signature is the absence).

**What I did fix, because the bystander deserved it anyway.** `follow` returned an `AsyncStream` whose producer was an unstructured `Task` made inside the stream's builder closure, so its lifetime was governed by object-graph reachability rather than by structured concurrency. Three ordinary situations leave that loop running for the life of the process: a feed made and never iterated; a consumer torn down by fire-and-forget cleanup that has not run yet (this suite uses `defer { Task { await bench.stop() } }` in ~30 places — a *request* to stop, not a stop); and the expensive one, a consumer suspended forever in its own loop body, where the producer neither knows nor cares and keeps polling and buffering (`AsyncStream`'s default policy is `.unbounded`) behind a reader that will never take another event. That last shape is exactly the pairing the sample shows.

`ActivityReader.Follow` is now a **value** (`Sources/Woodcase/Files/ActivityReader+Follow.swift`). It holds no task and starts no work; the polling *is* the consuming task. It lives exactly as long as somebody is asking, ends the moment that task is cancelled, and cannot run ahead of a consumer that stopped consuming — the log file, not memory, holds what a slow reader has not reached. There is nothing left to leak.

**Red test, and it is a real red.** `ActivityReaderTests.followIsAValueNotARunningTask` iterates one feed, takes an event, breaks, then iterates the same feed again. Against the old implementation the second iteration **never returns** — an `AsyncStream` is consumable once and the `break` terminated it — so it hung for the full 30 s `BoundedWait` budget and was reported as an expired job instead of wedging the run. Against a value it is two independent walks from the same offset. Honest disclosure: the companion `cancellingTheConsumerEndsTheFollow` was **green against the old code** — `AsyncStream`'s iterator already cancelled correctly. It is kept as a characterization test guarding the rewrite, not as a red one.

**Every wait on a feed is now bounded.** `Tests/WoodcaseTests/BoundedWait.swift` races a job against a deadline and cancels it. 30 s: a *not hung* guard, deliberately nowhere near the interval under test, because gotchas records a 10 ms sleep taking twelve seconds under this suite. It bounds any job that honours cancellation and cannot bound one that does not — stated in its own doc comment rather than pretended away.

**Interface:** `follow`'s return type changed from `AsyncStream<ActivityEvent>` to `ActivityReader.Follow`. `ChangeCoordinator`'s `for await event in reader.follow(...)` compiled **unchanged** — no viewer file was edited. The only site that named the old type was `ActivityCommand.printFollowing`, which is private.

**One trade-off worth knowing.** The old producer polled during the consumer's loop body; the new one does not, so an event written while `ChangeCoordinator.logged()` is running is picked up on the next `next()` rather than concurrently. At the viewer's 100 ms interval that is a sub-100 ms difference, and it is the correct side of the trade against unbounded buffering behind a stalled reader. I first suspected this of the `unreadDotUntilViewed` flake below; it is not the cause — that test was racing a page navigation with no wait at all — but the shift may have made it lose the race more often, and it is the one seam where a slow `logged()` now costs ingestion latency. If the viewer ever needs read-ahead, the fix belongs in `ChangeCoordinator` (don't do async work inside the `for await` body), not in the feed.

**A second wait that assumed timely scheduling, found by the soak and fixed.** `ViewerFollowBrowserTests.unreadDotUntilViewed` failed 2/5 loaded runs, always at its last step: it wrote a node, navigated straight to the map, then waited 30 s for a dot. The dot lives in the *browser's* `localStorage`, written by `ViewerScript`'s `change` handler when the event arrives over the stream — never in the server's markup. A page that navigates away before the event lands never runs that handler, so the mark is never written and **no amount of waiting afterwards can recover it**; the 30 s bound only decided how long the suite took to report a race it had already lost. The same test's earlier step waits correctly; the last one simply omitted it. Fixed by waiting on the state the later step *consumes* (`localStorage.getItem('woodcase.unread:<file>:Cmp01')`) before navigating. That is a test file, not `Sources/WoodcaseViewer/` — but flag it to the viewer's owner, since the wait it was missing is a shape worth checking elsewhere in that bench. Gotcha filed: "A wait after an irreversible step tests nothing."

**Soak (the standing ruling — loaded, not quiet).** `scripts/soak-tests 5 <log> --load 2 --timeout 600`, on a machine already running several agents' builds and suites on top of the two synthetic busy cores. **4/5 runs passed**, 3139 tests each, every run finishing in 41–53 s. No `TIMEOUT`, no `NO-SUMMARY`, no wedge in any of them — and none in the earlier 5-run soak either, so ten loaded full-suite runs of the rewrite with zero hangs. The one failure is `ViewerBrowserTests.selectionScrollsTheOutlineToItsRow`, the pre-existing load-sensitive flake already recorded in `project/gotchas.md` ("a second `scrollIntoView` in `viewer.js` silently undoes the first"); it is viewer-owned and untouched by this work. Earlier soak, before the dot fix: 3/5, both failures the dot race.

## expVd: `_scroll` annotation implemented, tested, and documented

Implementation, tests, docs all landed on worktree branch
`worktree-agent-a31cd51ce2540f13f`. Full report (summary, deviations, "what's wrong
in the brief") is being sent to the integrator; this note carries the load-bearing
decisions for anyone reading the tracker later.

**Check id: stayed `clipped`, no new id minted.** All three behaviors (suppression,
the frame-level teaching finding, the invalid-value warning) report
`check: .clipped`. This is what makes `--exclude clipped` "exclude all of it" true
with no second id for a caller to remember, per the brief's own requirement.
`DocumentLinterScrollTests.everyFindingIsStillTheClippedCheck` pins it.

**"Total pt past the fold" = the farthest child's excess, not a sum.** N overflowing
children folded into one finding report the *max* distance any one of them continues
past the frame's edge on the stacking axis, not the sum of each child's individual
overflow (which would double- and triple-count a stacked list and produce an
enormous, meaningless number). Documented explicitly in WoodcaseLint.md's new
"Scroll axes" section so this doesn't read as an arbitrary choice later.

**`common.metadata` is a whole-object write.** `NodePropertyCodec`/`SetCommand` have
no sub-key addressing (`common.metadata._scroll=vertical` is not valid syntax today —
confirmed by reading `NodePropertyCodec.commonPaths` and `PenPropertyShape`). The
brief's own suggested wording ("set common.metadata._scroll=<axis>") was shorthand for
intent, not literal syntax. Every finding that proposes a command instead builds the
*real* `woodcase set … common.metadata='{...}'` invocation from the node's current
metadata (so `_role`/`_props` survive), computed fresh per finding.

**A real bug caught before it shipped:** `PenNode.FrameData.layout` is
`PenLayoutDirection?`, and `PenLayoutDirection` itself has a case literally named
`.none`. `switch data.layout { case .none: ... }` over the *optional* matches only the
absent key, not the authored `"layout": "none"` — a classic Swift optional-vs-wrapped-case
shadowing trap that would have silently treated every `layout:"none"` frame as if it
had a vertical/horizontal stacking axis had it shipped. Fixed by unwrapping first (see
`DocumentLinter+Scroll.swift`'s `stackingAxis(of:)` doc comment). Not a gotcha entry —
caught in design/review before any test would have needed to find it, per CLAUDE.md's
own "fix at the source" instruction for gotchas (this is a fix, not a discovered trap).

**TDD note:** implementation and tests were designed together (the flex-layout
arithmetic needed hand-derivation from `PenLayoutEngine.layoutFlexContainer` before
correct assertions could be written blind), but red was verified for real: the
scroll-aware call site was swapped for a stub reproducing the pre-feature behavior,
11 of the 13 new/changed assertions failed exactly as expected, then the stub was
reverted and all 13 passed on the first real run. Full transcript in the session, not
duplicated here.

Plan (merkle, after reading the amendment in project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md §1)

1. `TreeRow` gains `public let rev: String`, required in `init`, placed after `address`.
   `TreeView.walk` fills it: `document.revision(of: prefix.first ?? nodeID)`. For an
   instance-descendant row that is the outermost ref's revision, which is exactly what
   `NodeLookup` already hands `get` for the same address (an override to that target is
   stored on the ref), so tree and get cannot disagree. Human outline keeps its shape.

2. Revision cache. `RevisionCache` (entries: [String: String]) beside `ExpansionCache`,
   backed by `EditableDocument._revisionCache`. `revision(of:)` memoizes.
   `documentRevision` is NOT cached — it is one hash over the root revisions, which are.
   Invalidation follows the house rule: the existing `invalidatingExpansions(touching:_:)`
   is the enumerated set of mutating entry points, so it becomes
   `invalidatingCaches(touching:_:)` and carries both rules — whole-cache for expansions,
   spine-scoped for revisions (walk `parents` up from each subject, before AND after the
   body, deduped by a visited set so an insert of N nodes costs the spine once).
   `reconcileChildrenWithParents()` restructures the store outside any wrapper, so it
   drops the whole revision cache.

3. Docs: WoodcaseEditor.md documents the pin (a row's/get's rev covers the subtree; it is
   the token `--rev` takes). EditingDocuments.md's invalidation paragraph follows the
   rename.

Facts checked: `--rev` is per-node (`RevisionOption`, `BatchApplier`), not the document
revision, though `tree`'s header prints `documentRevision`. `get`'s rev is already
covered by four tests in GetCommandTests, so criterion yD0's get half needs verification
only. Cross-process equality gets a real two-process test (the built binary run twice),
which is the only version of that assertion that could fail.

# Spike: what routing CLI writes through the CRDT layer costs

*Read-only spike, no code changed. Design context: `project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md`
(§1 correction block and "Relation to the CRDT layer"), `project/2026-08-31-woodcase-concurrent-dx.md`.
Line numbers are as of d75a700.*

**Verdict up front: no-go for now.** Ship hashes, `--guard` and the echo as designed —
nothing in them waits on this. Routing is blocked on one correctness bug in the CRDT
layer (concurrent overrides on one instance clobber each other) and one missing
mechanism (no CRDT-side rollback for a half-applied batch line). The seam itself is
cheap — one function — so the option stays open at near-zero interim cost. Revisit when
a second concurrent writer exists that is *not* a CLI process (Penumbra, a live viewer
session): that is the first case where the merge is worth its price.

---

## 1. Do the CLI verbs reach `applyLocal` today? No. Where do they diverge?

### The trace: `set`

| step | file:line |
|---|---|
| `SetCommand.run` opens a transaction | `Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/SetCommand.swift:71` |
| `PenFileTransaction.run(at:identity:log:timeout:_:)` builds the document | `Sources/Woodcase/Files/PenFileTransaction.swift:185` — **`EditableDocument(from: parsed)`** |
| `BatchApplier.applyOne` | `SetCommand.swift:75` → `Sources/Woodcase/Batch/BatchApplier+Single.swift:47` |
| `BatchApplier.perform` — plan, doc-rev guard, per-edit loop | `Sources/Woodcase/Batch/BatchApplier.swift:221`, guard at `:229`, loop at `:238–255` |
| `planSet` → `EditOperation.setProperties` | `Sources/Woodcase/Batch/BatchApplier+Plan.swift:41–57` |
| **the seam**, recorder branch | `BatchApplier.swift:245` → `Sources/Woodcase/Files/ActivityRecorder.swift:92`, whose only mutation is **`:101 try document.apply(operation, expecting: expecting)`** |
| **the seam**, recorder-less branch | `BatchApplier.swift:247` (and the atomic replay at `:287–290`) |
| lands in | `Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+Revision.swift:71` `apply(_:expecting:)` → `checkExpectedRevisions` → `apply(_:)` |

The batch path (`ApplyCommand.swift:78–83` → `BatchApplier.apply`/`retry` → the same
`perform` at `BatchApplier.swift:221`) is the identical seam; `applyOne` is documented
as "the same planning, the same revision guard, the same rollback" and it is
(`BatchApplier+Single.swift:8–41`).

`applyLocal` is never reached, and it is not reachable: `EditableDocument.crdtDocument`
is set only by `init(from:peerID:)` (`EditableDocument.swift:127,143`) and
`init(from:snapshot:peerID:)` (`EditableDocument+StateTransfer.swift:21`). Neither is
called anywhere in `WoodcaseCommandCore` or `WoodcaseViewer` —
`grep -rn "peerID:" Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore Sources/WoodcaseViewer` is empty. Every
CLI document is a non-replica, so even if `applyLocal` were called it would fall through
to `apply` at `EditableDocument+CRDT.swift:26–29`.

### Where `applyLocal` would slot in

`EditableDocument+Revision.swift:86` already declares `applyLocal(_:expecting:)` as the
exact twin of `:71`. So the swap is one line at `ActivityRecorder.swift:101` — the single
choke point for **every** logged CLI write (all 11 write verbs pass a recorder; no write
verb uses the recorder-less `PenFileTransaction.run(at:)` overload) — plus
`BatchApplier.swift:247` and `:290` for the unlogged branch.

### Four divergences from the CRDT path

1. **No peer identity.** `--as` is a `String` (`IdentityOptions`), never a `PeerID`.
   `BatchApplier.apply(_:to:atomic:identity:recorder:)` already takes `identity: PeerID?`
   (`BatchApplier.swift:71`) and `ApplyCommand.swift:79–84` never passes it — it is `nil`
   on every CLI batch. The type is on the seam and unfilled.

2. **Rollback has no CRDT-side inverse — blocking.** `BatchApplier.unwind`
   (`BatchApplier.swift:329–335`) restores a half-applied line with `try? document.apply(edit)`,
   straight to the flat store, and `ActivityRecorder.discardEvents(after:)`
   (`ActivityRecorder.swift:136`) drops the events for the same reason. There is no
   equivalent for CRDT ops: `CRDTDocument` mutates eagerly (stated at
   `EditableDocument+CRDT.swift:15–20`), `OperationLog.operations` is `private(set)`
   (`OperationLog.swift:35`), and the only removal is `truncate(acknowledgedBy:)`
   (`OperationLog.swift:98`) — a consensus operation, not an undo. Under routing, a line
   that fails on its second edit leaves the log holding ops the file never kept, with
   `propertyMaps`, the RGA lists and `tombstones` advanced past the flat store.

3. **Atomic mode stages on a non-replica.** `BatchApplier.run:148` builds the stage as
   `EditableDocument(from: document.materialize())` — `init(from:)`, so no
   `crdtDocument`. An atomic batch would run its whole staged pass outside CRDT mode and
   only the replay (`BatchApplier.swift:274`) would touch it.

4. **`undo` is re-application, not retraction.** `UndoCommand.swift:131` reads the
   activity log and re-applies `event.inverse`. In CRDT mode those are new forward ops,
   so an undo can itself be superseded — correct CRDT behavior, but the echo would have
   to say it.

---

## 2. What persisting the op log and clocks beside a plain .pen costs

### Two states with opposite persistence shapes

`CRDTSnapshot` (`Sources/Woodcase/Sync/CRDTSnapshot.swift:28–54`) is
`operationLog` + `propertyMaps` + `childrenLists` + `treeMove` + `tombstones` +
`variableTimestamps` + `importTimestamps` + `themeTimestamps`. The op log is append-only
and cheap to persist. **Everything else is a random-access map that must be rewritten
whole on every transaction.**

### Bytes

*Method: JSON sizes computed from the Codable synthesis of the types named below —
`Friendly = Codable & Equatable & Hashable & Sendable` (`Sources/Woodcase/Friendly.swift:10`),
so every shape is synthesized; enum-with-payload emits `{"case":{"_0":…}}` and
`[PeerID: UInt64]` emits an alternating unkeyed array. Document figures are measured:*
`python3 -c "import json,os; d=json.load(open('project/2026-08-31-mobile-viewer/mobile-viewer.pen'))"`
*over `project/2026-08-31-mobile-viewer/mobile-viewer.pen` (121,059 B, 307 nodes, 394 B/node)
and `.woodcase/activity.jsonl` (212,285 B, 472 events, 450 B/event).*

- **Op envelope: 214 B** with a 5-peer vector clock, 114 B with one peer. Every op
  carries the full clock (`CRDTOperation.swift:24`, `OperationLog.appendLocal:57–65`), and
  `VectorClock.entries` is `[PeerID: UInt64]` (`VectorClock.swift:19`) over a `PeerID`
  struct (`PeerID.swift:15`) — ~30 B per peer per op.
- `setProperty` with a short string value: **321 B**.
- `createNode` carries the whole stripped node (`CRDTDocument+LocalProcessing.swift:39`):
  **~658 B** at this document's average node.
- `listInsert`: **~410 B**, one per created node *on top of* its `createNode`.
- **Projected op log for the four-writer run: ~580 KB** — against a 121 KB .pen and a
  207 KB activity.jsonl. ~5× the file. (Assumption stated: an `add` line averages 3
  nodes; the run logged 140 add / 211 override / 96 set / 18 var / 3 replace / 2 rm / 1
  theme / 1 mv.)
- **Snapshot excluding the op log, 307-node doc: ~150 KB** — `propertyMaps` ~93 KB at 5
  touched paths/node, `childrenLists` ~52 KB (172 B per RGA entry, tombstones retained),
  `treeMove.parentMap` ~5 KB plus 124 B per move ever made.

### Write amplification

Today one `set` rewrites the .pen whole (`PenFileTransaction.write:279`) and appends
~450 B to `activity.jsonl`: **121 KB + 0.45 KB**. Under routing it becomes 121 KB +
0.45 KB + ~0.3–0.7 KB (op-log append) + **~150 KB (snapshot rewrite)** — roughly a
doubling, and the added part scales with *document size*, not edit size. The append is
free; the snapshot rewrite is the whole cost. Skipping the snapshot and replaying the log
on each open trades bytes for time, which is worse: a CLI's value is that every
invocation is cheap.

### Growth is not bounded the way the docs imply

`EditableDocument.truncateLog(acknowledgedBy:)`
(`Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+Checkpoint.swift:29–31`) calls
`OperationLog.truncate` (`OperationLog.swift:98`) **and nothing else**. `TreeMoveCRDT.moveLog`
(`TreeMoveCRDT.swift:60`), the RGA tombstones (`RGAList.swift:55`; `delete` at `:155`
sets `isDeleted` and never removes) and `propertyMaps` are pruned by nothing. Checkpoints
bound the *replication* log; they do not bound the *convergence metadata* — which is
exactly the part that has to be rewritten each transaction. **`CRDTArchitecture.md`'s
"Checkpoints and Log Truncation" section overstates what truncation reclaims and should
be corrected.**

Worse, consensus needs a peer set. `VectorClock.minimum(of:)` requires every peer's
clock, and a CLI has no membership: every `--as` name that ever wrote is a peer forever.
The run had **8 distinct identities** in 472 events (kit, sheet, activity, nav, core,
claude, x, probe) — 240 B of clock on every operation, never shrinking, and truncation
would never fire because no peer is ever known to be gone.

### Can "no daemon, the file is just a file" survive?

**No daemon: yes, unchanged.** Everything is per-invocation under the existing `flock`
(`PenFileTransaction.swift:179`); nothing needs a live process.

**File is just a file: the .pen yes, the workflow no.** The .pen format is untouched, and
`.woodcase/` already holds a sidecar with a resolution rule to reuse
(`ActivityLogLocation.swift:8–32`). What changes is the sidecar's status: today it is
*advisory* — delete `activity.jsonl` and you lose history, the file still edits
correctly. Under routing it is *load-bearing*: delete it (or copy, rename, `git merge`,
or let Pen.app write the file) and the next writer rebuilds CRDT state from the current
file with genesis timestamps (`CRDTDocument.init(peerID:document:)`,
`CRDTDocument.swift:69–116`), producing different `PositionID`s than any surviving op log
references — silently. Nothing today binds a snapshot to the bytes it describes. The fix
is free and sitting right there: stamp `documentRevision`
(`EditableDocument+Revision.swift:43`) on the snapshot and refuse-or-rebuild on mismatch.

### What checkpoints/snapshots give

`CRDTSnapshot` is exactly the "don't replay from zero" primitive a stateless CLI needs,
and both halves exist: `CRDTDocument.snapshot()`
(`Sources/Woodcase/Sync/CRDTDocument+Snapshot.swift`) to capture and
`EditableDocument(from:snapshot:peerID:)` (`EditableDocument+StateTransfer.swift:21`) to
rehydrate. So the persistence *shape* is already built. What they do not give: pruning
(above), and any binding to the file they describe.

---

## 3. Go/no-go on merge-and-report routing

**No-go now.** Three weighings.

### (a) What a stale-read batch actually gains — less than the design doc claims

The doc says routing "would let a batch composed against a stale read be merged over
intervening history rather than path-resolved against whatever is current." Two things
undercut it:

- **The CLI's addressing is by name path, resolved at line-apply time**
  (`BatchApplier+Plan.swift:46`, `document.resolve(op.target, tags:)`). A CRDT merges ops
  on *ids*. A name-addressed line has no op until after resolution, so it is
  path-resolved against current state either way — routing changes nothing for it. Only
  an id-addressed batch gets the merge, and the run's own §4 finding (the override-path
  grammar) says the traffic is overwhelmingly name-addressed.
- **The population being rescued was three.** 457 operations, four fully interleaved
  writers, **zero** lost writes and zero semantic collisions; the only three failures
  were stale-revision refusals fixed by re-read-and-retry (DX report headline). And the
  report's own conclusion is that loud refusals were the *cheap* outcome — "Nothing that
  refused loudly cost more than a retry."

### (b) The merge would be wrong exactly where the traffic is — blocking

`override` was **211 of 472** logged events, 45% of the run.
`CRDTDocument.processLocalOverrideDescendant`
(`Sources/Woodcase/Sync/CRDTDocument+LocalProcessing.swift`) merges the override into the
ref's `descendants` map and delegates to `processLocalUpdateKind`, which diffs to the
single path `"kind.descendants"` (`Sources/Woodcase/Sync/PropertyDiff.swift:237`) and
emits **one** LWW `setProperty` carrying the whole map. So two agents overriding
*different descendants of the same instance* concurrently do not merge: the later write
wins the entire map and the earlier agent's overrides vanish, silently.
`CRDTOverrideConvergenceTests.concurrentOverridesLWW`
(`Tests/WoodcaseTests/CRDTOverrideConvergenceTests.swift:63–93`) asserts only that the
peers *converge* (`refA.descendants == refB.descendants`), not that both edits survive,
and there is no test for two different descendants.

Routing today would convert the run's zero lost writes into a new silent-loss class —
precisely the failure mode guards-and-echo exists to kill. It is fixable (per-descendant
property paths, `kind.descendants.<id>.<prop>`, so each descendant gets its own register)
but that is a change to the CRDT layer, and it must land before any routing.

### (c) Clock guards vs the hash guards being built — the hashes win, and are not wasted

- The hash guard needs nothing but the file (`revision(of:)`,
  `EditableDocument+Revision.swift:25`), is already computed and already surfaced, and
  answers what the caller asked: *is what I reasoned about still true?* Touched-and-reverted
  passes.
- "No foreign ops concurrent-or-later than my read clock" answers a different question —
  *did anyone write here since?* — and answers it worse for an agent: touched-and-reverted
  fails, a formatting no-op fails, and it needs a **read clock**, which means `get` and
  `tree` must open the CRDT sidecar and print a vector clock. Every read would then carry
  the same persistence cost as a write. The hash costs a read nothing.
- They are not exclusive. The clock guard is what you want between replicas that are not
  both CLI processes. The design doc's §1 claim that the hash "survives the CRDT future
  unchanged" is right, and it means `--guard` needs no revision if routing later happens.

### (d) Two write paths in the interim — the cheapest part of the picture

The seam is one function (`ActivityRecorder.apply`, `ActivityRecorder.swift:92–119`, one
mutation at `:101`), the CRDT twin already exists with an identical signature
(`applyLocal(_:expecting:)`, `EditableDocument+Revision.swift:86`), and `applyLocal`
already degrades to `apply` when `crdtDocument` is nil (`EditableDocument+CRDT.swift:26–29`).
So the swap is behavior-preserving on day one and "two paths" is really one path with a
mode flag. The interim maintenance cost is near zero. What is *not* near zero is the
rollback gap (1.2) and the sidecar-binding gap (§2) — those are new code, not a swap.

### Recommendation

1. **Ship hashes, `--guard`, echo unchanged.** Nothing waits on this spike, and nothing
   in them is discarded by a later go.
2. **Do not route now.**
3. **File two prerequisites** so the option stays open: (i) per-descendant override
   registers in the CRDT layer; (ii) a CRDT-side rollback — either a retract on
   `OperationLog` or plan-then-commit so nothing is logged until a line is known to hold.
4. **Correct `CRDTArchitecture.md`**: truncation reclaims the op log only; `moveLog`, RGA
   tombstones and `propertyMaps` grow forever.
5. **When routing happens, the echo (pjupK) is the right channel and needs no new shape** —
   `applied, then superseded by <peer>'s later set on <property>` is one more divergence
   kind on a report that already carries requested → applied-as → superseded.

### Corrections to the premises this spike was given

- "Checkpoints/snapshots exist in the layer" — **snapshots** exist and are complete;
  **checkpoints** are only a clock accessor plus an op-log truncate, and truncation does
  not prune the metadata that dominates the persisted size (§2).
- The design doc's "merged over intervening history rather than path-resolved against
  whatever is current" is true only for id-addressed batches; the CLI's grammar is
  name-addressed and resolves at line-apply time (§3a). Worth an in-place correction in
  `project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md`.
- Everything else in the brief checked out: `CRDTArchitecture.md` is where it was said to
  be, and `CRDTDocument`, LWW property maps, RGA lists, Kleppmann tree-move, the op log
  and vector clocks all exist under those names.

data.text:
## Mechanism (confirmed by reading SleepyHollow's PageHost)

`ViewerBrowserTests.theBreadcrumbAndEscapeGoBackUp` reuses one `PageHost` across three
navigations: `host.load(Brd01)`, a JS `.click()` on `.v-crumb-map` (a *real*, untracked
navigation — the doc comment in ViewerScript.swift says moving between the map and an
artboard "stays a real navigation: those are two different pages", so it is not
intercepted for an SPA swap), then a second explicit `host.load(Brd01)` right before
dispatching a synthetic Escape keydown.

`PageHostDelegate.webView(_:didFinish:)` (.build/checkouts/sleepyhollow/Sources/
SleepyHollow/Host/PageHostDelegate.swift:42) calls `host?.finishNavigation(.finished)`
unconditionally — it does not compare the `WKNavigation` object to the one the current
`pendingNavigation` continuation is waiting on. `PageHost.finishNavigation` (PageHost.swift:295)
just resumes whatever continuation is currently stored, if any.

The click's own navigation reaches `#v-map` in the DOM (satisfying the test's own
`waitFor("the map to come back", ...)`) well before WebKit fires that navigation's
`didFinish` — DOM content is available at commit/early-parse time, `didFinish` waits for
the full load event (all subresources, including the deferred `/viewer.js`). So the test
can (and under load, does) proceed past that `waitFor` and call the second `host.load()`
— which sets a *new* `pendingNavigation` — before the click navigation's own `didFinish`
has arrived. When that late `didFinish` finally lands, it resolves the *new* continuation
instead of the (already-abandoned) old one, so the second `host.load()` returns claiming
success while the page is, in fact, still showing the map (or mid-navigation away from
it). The test then dispatches Escape's keydown against that stale page: `handleEscape()`
reads `.v-crumb-map`, which only exists on an artboard page, so on the map it is a no-op,
and the wait for "Escape to go up to the map" times out — 30s wasted on a race already
lost.

This is the same general shape as `project/gotchas.md`'s "A wait after an irreversible
step tests nothing" (2026-08-31): a wait bound on the *effect* rather than on the
*precondition*. Here the "precondition" is that this host's own most recent `load()` call
is the one whose completion is actually being observed — which SleepyHollow's `PageHost`
does not guarantee when a prior, untracked (non-`.load()`) navigation is still in flight
against the same host.

## Root cause is in SleepyHollow, not Woodcase

`PageHostDelegate.didFinish` / `PageHost.finishNavigation` don't correlate the `WKNavigation`
object with the pending continuation. That's a real latent bug in the dependency (a
`WKWebView` reused across an untracked native navigation followed by an explicit `load()`
call can resolve early). Out of scope here (external repo, pinned to `main` on GitHub) —
worth filing against SleepyHollow: `finishNavigation` should ignore a `didFinish`/`didFail`
whose `WKNavigation` doesn't match the one issued by the in-flight `navigate(to:)` call.

## Test-only mitigation applied

Woodcase's own test code does not need SleepyHollow fixed to be robust: like
`editUpdatesWithoutAReload` already does ("wait for the event stream to connect" rather
than trusting `host.load()` alone), never trust a `host.load()` return as proof the
*requested* page is showing when an untracked navigation preceded it on the same host.
Added a `waitFor` on a page-content predicate (the artboard's `data-artboard` / `#v-map`'s
presence) right after the second `host.load()` in both affected tests, before the next
step consumes that state:

- `ViewerBrowserTests.theBreadcrumbAndEscapeGoBackUp` (the flake): wait for
  `document.getElementById('v-stage')?.dataset.artboard === 'Brd01'` before dispatching
  Escape.
- `ViewerBrowserTests.clickingTheMapFocusesAnArtboard` (same shape, not yet observed
  flaking, but same untracked-navigation-then-load pattern): wait for `#v-map` before
  clicking the outline row that only exists there.

## ViewerKeyboardBrowserTests — checked, not the same mechanism

`escapeLeavesPresentationBeforeGoingUp` (:304) and
`escapeClearsTheSelectionOnASingleArtboardFile` (:347) each call `host.load()` exactly
**once** per test. The race requires an *earlier, untracked* real navigation on the same
host whose late `didFinish` can be misattributed to a *later* explicit `host.load()` call.
With only one `load()` call and no intervening untracked navigation, there is nothing for
a late callback to be misattributed to. Their later steps that do trigger a real
navigation (the final Escape to the map) are the *last* action in the test — nothing
after them calls `host.load()` again — so they don't share the mechanism. Left unfixed
per the brief ("fix them only if the mechanism is identical").

Probes of the Network.framework seam (bare `swift script.swift`, sandbox off; scripts at
scratchpad/3uBxi-probe.swift and 3uBxi-probe2.swift):

- NWConnection.send's `.contentProcessed` completion DOES fire when the connection is
  cancelled in flight, and DOES fire when send is called on an already-cancelled
  connection. Both `withCheckedContinuation`s in HTTPConnection/NetworkSSEWriter are
  therefore resumable on the cancel path — those two leads are weaker than the brief
  implies.
- The 2026-08-30 EINVAL gotcha reproduces exactly and unconditionally in a bare script:
  every NWListener with `requiredLocalEndpoint = .hostPort(.ipv4(.loopback), .any)`
  reported `.failed(POSIXErrorCode 22)` — 20 in a row, fd-starved or not, and also for a
  non-local address and for a port already bound. So EINVAL there is not load-shaped and
  not a `.waiting` case; it is that parameter set outside the test host. It also cannot be
  the wedge: `.failed` resumes the continuation (it throws).
- The only NWListener states HTTPServer.start's handler does not resume on are `.setup`
  and `.waiting`. A listener that stays in either never resumes the continuation, and the
  await is not cancellation-aware, so BoundedWait/test teardown cannot break it either.

Baseline soak on unmodified HEAD (859b68f), sandbox off:
  scripts/soak-tests 3 <log> --load 2 --timeout 180  ->  3/3 passed, 55/85/82 s,
  3254 tests, 1 known issue. No wedge. No sibling agents were building at the time
  (`ps | grep swift-frontend` = 0), which is the condition the wedge is reported under.

Re-reading the preserved sample local/wedge-samples/2026-08-31-integrator-run-46108.txt:
it contains NO com.apple.network.connections queue at all — the issue text's "live
com.apple.network.connections queue" belongs to the OTHER sample (pid 48269, described in
2026-08-31-follow-is-a-value.md), not to this one. This sample is the row-1 host with the
two ActivityReader.follow poll loops. Worth correcting in the issue.

Done (merkle). Full suite green: 3275 tests, 335 suites, exit 0 (`swift test --quiet`,
sandbox off), `swiftformat . --lint` clean.

What landed
- `TreeRow.rev` (required in `init`), filled by `TreeView.walk` from
  `document.revision(of: prefix.first ?? nodeID)` — the outermost ref for an
  instance-descendant row, which is the same token `NodeLookup` gives `get` for that
  address. The human outline is unchanged (16 hex per row would double the line; the
  header rev and `--json` cover it).
- `RevisionCache` (internal), memoizing `revision(of:)`. `documentRevision` stays
  uncached — it is one fold over the root revisions, which are cached.
- Invalidation piggybacks the house rule: `invalidatingExpansions(touching:)` is now
  `invalidatingCaches(touching:)` (file renamed to `EditableDocument+CacheInvalidation.swift`,
  `expansionSubjects(of:)` -> `subjects(of:)`), carrying two rules over one subject
  list — whole-cache for expansions, spine-scoped for revisions, walked before and
  after the body and deduped by a visited set. `reconcileChildrenWithParents()` is the
  one structural write that names no subjects, so it drops the whole revision cache.

Evidence
- Mutation check: with `forgetRevisions` stubbed to a no-op, 17 issues across
  RevisionCacheTests/TreeViewTests/TreeCommandTests. The tests bite.
- Performance, `swift test --quiet --filter TreeTests`, BUDGET lines, debug, min of
  five: the 5000-node synthetic settled read is 773.8 ms memoized and 1044.4 ms with
  the memoization removed — the unmemoized number is over that budget's own 1000 ms
  debug limit. So every row now carries a rev at no cost.
- Cross-process: `revisionsAgreeAcrossProcesses` runs the built binary twice and
  compares every row's rev (a genuinely two-process assertion, which is the only kind
  that could fail).
- `get`'s rev was already covered by four GetCommandTests; `rowRevMatchesGet` now ties
  the two reads together so they cannot drift.

Findings for the parent
- `tree`'s header rev is `documentRevision`, but `--rev` on a write is checked against
  the *node* the verb acts on. The header and the flag it tells you to quote are two
  different tokens; the doc now says where the narrower one comes from. Worth a look
  when 2NW90 lands `--guard`.
- A ref's revision covers the ref node (its overrides and the component id), not the
  component definition it points at — so an edit to the definition does not move an
  instance's rev. Pre-existing and unchanged here, but it is a real hole in "a rev
  pins what this renders" that `--guard` will inherit.

data.note: Integrated as ede8705 (squash of the merkle agent's branch; full diff read as review; suite 3276 tests green, lint clean). Every tree --json row now carries the node's rev (= revision(of:), the existing Merkle hash per the design amendment — no new hash field); revision(of:) memoizes into RevisionCache with spine-scoped invalidation riding the renamed invalidatingCaches(touching:) choke point; WoodcaseEditor.md and EditingDocuments.md document the pin and its limit. Criteria: rows+get carry the token (yD0); cross-process agreement tested via two CLI processes (EGJ); spine-only movement tested at both TreeView and CLI level (mFB). The agent's brief-is-wrong answer surfaced a real design gap, noted on 2NW90: a ref's rev does not fold in its component definition, so a subtree pin passes over definition edits that change what the subtree renders.

data.text: Design input from DemV8's integration (merkle agent's brief-is-wrong answer, verified): **a subtree rev does NOT cover component definitions.** A ref node stores the component's id and its overrides; the definition is not folded into the ref's revision, so editing a definition moves the definition's rev and documentRevision but no instance's rev and no ancestor of an instance. Consequence for this leaf: a --guard pinned on a frame full of instances passes over exactly the change it was meant to catch — the design doc's "a frame's hash covers everything under it" is false for any frame containing a ref, which in a component-driven file is most frames. Options: (a) fold the resolved definition's rev into a ref's rev through effectiveRefData (the original handoff's hint), making rev a rendered-premise pin — definition edits then move instance revs and their spines; needs instance-closure cache invalidation and a cycle guard; (b) keep rev authored-only and require pinning definitions separately (documented in DemV8's docs as the current contract; --guard could accept multiple pins). Decision pending with Ben before this leaf dispatches. The user-facing docs shipped in ede8705 document the current (b)-shaped reality.

## Fix landed and validated

Confirmed the mechanism empirically (not just by reading source): a diagnostic build that
captured `PageFacts.finalURL`/`httpStatus` from the second `host.load()` in
`theBreadcrumbAndEscapeGoBackUp` caught it in the act — one run returned `finalURL`
pointing at the requested Brd01 URL with `httpStatus 200` (correct), but a separate
isolated run (`--filter theBreadcrumbAndEscapeGoBackUp` alone, nothing else in the suite)
came back from `host.load()` with the page still showing the file's **map** page
(`location.pathname` had no `/artboards/Brd01` suffix, `#v-stage` absent, `#v-map`
present) and it never moved off the map for a full 30s of active polling afterward. A
bare `waitFor` after that `load()` could not out-wait it — the real navigation this host's
own `load()` call issued was evidently not the one whose completion resumed it.

Given a plain wait sometimes timed out for 30s straight with no sign the correct page was
ever coming, I strengthened the fix from "wait for the precondition" to "wait for the
precondition, and re-issue the navigation if it doesn't show up" — `Bench.reload(_:until:_:attempts:)`,
3 attempts of 10s each. This is still the same "wait on what the next step consumes,
not on the effect" shape, plus self-healing against the possibility that the specific
`load()` call whose completion got misattributed doesn't recover within any fixed bound.

## Soak result

`scripts/soak-tests 5 <log> --load 2 --timeout 400`, sandbox off, sibling agents also
building on the shared machine (real load on top of the synthetic 2 busy cores). 3/5 runs
failed — but grepping every run's log for `ViewerBrowserTests`, `ViewerKeyboardBrowserTests`,
"breadcrumb", "Escape to go up" and "reloaded artboard" turned up nothing in any of the 5
run logs. The 3 failures were unrelated, pre-existing, load-shaped flakes elsewhere in the
suite, not previously in `project/gotchas.md`:

- `WebViewTestHarnessTests`, "Surfaces an uncaught JavaScript error rather than timing out"
- `PenFileTransactionTests`, "Two concurrent transactions serialize…" — `... is locked by
  another process; gave up after 10s`
- `FileWatcherTests` / `ViewerFixtures.swift:85` — several file-watcher tests recorded an
  issue there under this same loaded run (heartbeat/watch timing)

None of these are in this leaf's scope (vvxHi is specifically the Escape flake) and I have
not investigated or touched them. Flagging for the coordinator to decide whether they're
worth their own `job` leaves — they were not visible before this soak because the last
"last known baseline flake" characterization predates this run.

## Full suite + lint

`swiftformat . --lint` (sandbox off): clean, 0/790 files need formatting.
`swift test --quiet` (sandbox off), once standalone (not under the soak): 3254 tests,
passed, 129s, 1 known issue (the pre-existing `PerformanceBudgetAdvisoryTests` known-issue
test, unrelated).

# pjupK design: the divergence echo

Seam chosen: **the planner**. Every one of the classes in scope is computable from
`BatchOperation` + pre-state `EditableDocument`, and `BatchApplier+Plan.swift` /
`+Create.swift` are exactly where requested becomes applied (address -> id, authored
subtree -> settled subtree, coordinates chosen, detaches prepended). So `BatchPlan`
grows `divergences: [WriteDivergence]`, filled by a new `BatchApplier+Divergence.swift`,
carried through `LineOutcome` onto `BatchLineResult`. Single verbs (`applyOne`) and
batches (`apply`/`retry`) get it from the one place, as required.

Third term of "requested -> applied-as -> superseded/dropped": `BatchLineStatus`
already is it (`applied`/`failed`/`cascaded`). "Superseded by a later merge" is out of
scope (aPPZS no-go). Divergences are only ever produced for a line that applied.

Classes covered (5):
1. `variableReference` - `$name` written to a string-or-`$variable` property where the
   document defines `name`. Replaces `ContentVariableWarning` (retired: one channel, and
   the batch path's re-derivation loop in ApplyCommand goes away).
2. `coercion` - `NodePropertyCodec.coercing` turned a number into the text it spells.
3. `unsetOverrideProperty` - an override whose descendant key is valid but whose raw
   property key the definition's node does not carry. Two notes: the property is not on
   that node type at all (the override will never be read), or the type has it but the
   definition leaves it unset (the override adds rather than replaces).
4. `rootPlacement` - `placedAtRoot` chose `common.x`/`common.y` for a root-level `add`
   with no coordinates, or for a `cp` that carried the source's.
5. `detachedInstances` - `rm --detach` detached N instances before the delete.

`--json`: `BatchLineResult.id` and `BatchLineResult.node` (the stored flat node, children
stripped - the same shape `get` prints), plus `WriteReport.node` for the single verbs.

The issue's premise was corrected by the agent: the race is not the unread-dot's twin (a JS-side recording race) but a navigation-correlation bug in the SleepyHollow test harness — PageHostDelegate.didFinish discards its WKNavigation argument and resumes whichever load is pending, so a click's late completion can settle a following host.load() while the old page still shows (verified in the checkout by the integrator). Fix: Bench.reload(_:until:_:attempts:) — navigate, wait for the target page's own content, re-issue if it never shows — applied to the flaking test and to clickingTheMapFocusesAnArtboard's identical shape. Loaded soak (5 runs, --load 2): zero occurrences of this flake. UPSTREAM: the real fix belongs in SleepyHollow (correlate the didFinish callback's WKNavigation with the in-flight navigation); surfaced to Ben. The soak also exposed three unrelated load flakes (WebViewTestHarnessTests uncaught-JS-error test, PenFileTransactionTests lock timeout under contention, FileWatcherTests heartbeat) — filed separately.

Not investigated further — out of vvxHi's scope. Diagnose with the same discipline as the other timing gotchas: assert the observable outcome, bound waits at "not hung" scale, and remember wall-clock assertions are unreliable in the parallel suite (gotchas.md). A stability claim needs a loaded soak. Note: (2) may be another instance of the already-recorded PenFileTransaction wall-clock gotcha rather than a new bug — check that entry first.

data.text: DECISION (Ben, 2026-08-31, in session): fold definitions in — option (a). revision(of:) folds the resolved component definition's revision into every ref node's revision, resolved through effectiveRefData(of:insideInstances:) and cycle-guarded (visited set, like appendDescendantKeys). The rev becomes a rendered-premise pin: one token on a frame truly covers what it renders, and a definition edit moves the definition's spine AND every instance's spine. Accepted consequences: --rev on an instance conflicts after a definition edit (honest — the caller's rendered premise moved); cache invalidation must extend to the instance closure (a definition edit forgets the revs of its instances and their ancestors — instanceIDs(ofComponent:) exists in EditableDocument+Guards.swift; mind transitively nested refs and repointed refs); some RevisionCacheTests/TreeViewTests just landed in ede8705 assert the authored-only behavior (aDefinitionEditLeavesInstancesAlone and friends) and must be REWRITTEN to assert the new semantics, with the change explained; DemV8's shipped docs (WoodcaseEditor.md, EditingDocuments.md, TreeRow.rev, tree --help) describe the authored-only limit and must be updated in the same commit that changes the hash. socket — resumes exactly once from the callback, a later callback, or a 30 s dispatch

Six divergence classes ship, all decided in the planner (`BatchApplier+Divergence.swift`,
carried on `BatchPlan.divergences` -> `LineOutcome` -> `BatchLineResult.divergences`), so
a single verb and the same edit as a batch line say the same thing:
`variableReference`, `coercion`, `unsetOverrideProperty`, `overrideReplacesNode`,
`rootPlacement`, `detachedInstances`.

`BatchLineResult` also gained `id` and `node` (the stored flat node, the shape `get`
prints); `WriteReport` gained `node` and `divergences`. Text output is unchanged when
requested == applied; golden tests in `WriteReportTests` and `BatchReportFormatterTests`
pin that.

`ContentVariableWarning` retired: one channel, and `ApplyCommand`'s re-derivation loop
over `operations` went with it. The sentence moved from stderr to stdout, and now fires
for every string-or-`$variable` property (not just `kind.content`) and for `override`
as well as `set`.

Suite: `swift test --quiet` = 3303 tests / 336 suites pass, 1 pre-existing known issue.
`swiftformat . --lint` clean.

## Found and NOT covered (from a survey of the write paths)

Ordered by cost to a caller. Each is a real silent consequence today.

1. `cp` of a reusable node makes a `ref` and rebuilds `common` as `PenNodeCommon(name:)`,
   dropping rotation/opacity/enabled/flip/theme/context/layoutPosition/metadata.
2. `set kind.descendants={...}` / `kind.rootOverrides={...}` REPLACE the whole map,
   while `override` merges; nothing tells the caller which semantics it just got.
   `=null` on either clears every override in one write.
3. Override values are stored unvalidated (no `NodePropertyCodec` pass, unlike `set`),
   and `PenNodePatcher.merge` silently returns the node unchanged when the patched JSON
   will not decode - so `override ... content=42` is stored and then does nothing. The
   `override --help` example literally shows `content=42`.
4. `EditableDocument.applyDelete` / `applyDetachRef` throw the `[DetachResult]` away, so
   the old->new id mapping of a detach is lost on the plain `apply(_:)` path. The echo
   names the detached instances by path but cannot name their new ids for that reason.
5. `planVariable` / `planThemeAxis` silently turn an add into an update when the name
   exists; `variableAlreadyExists` can never be surfaced through the batch grammar.
6. `SubtreeIDPlan.regenerating` (cp) discards supplied ids and never surfaces
   `replacements`, so a caller that published the source's ids gets no mapping.
7. `applySetProperties` early-returns when the patch equals the node: reported applied,
   stored nothing, revision unmoved.
8. `applyReplaceSubtree` silently deregisters a reusable component inside the replaced
   subtree when it has no instances.
9. `applyUpdateKind` drops inline children from the supplied kind while leaving the
   node's existing children attached.
10. `$name` inside an authored `add`/`cp`/`replace` subtree is stored as a reference
    with no echo - the detector only reads `set`/`override`/`cp --props` property maps.
11. Move/delete erase a parent's declared-empty `children: []` key.
12. `prepareInverseOverrideDescendant` merges old properties back, so an undone override
    leaves the keys the forward op introduced behind.
