data.description: Found by the echo agent (pjupK, 2026-08-31): override values are stored unvalidated, and at expansion PenNodePatcher.merge decodes the patched JSON and returns the node UNCHANGED when the decode fails — so the whole override is silently dropped. The literal example in `override --help` triggers it: `woodcase override design.pen Orders/Value content=42` stores `content: 42`; a text node's content is `string | $string`, the decode fails, and the override does nothing while `get` confirms the stored key back forever. Related, same surface: the `override` verb does not rekey its properties — BatchApplier+Plan.planOverride passes op.props through verbatim (only `cp --descendant-props` calls NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed), so `override X kind.content=…` stores a literal `kind.content` key nothing reads. Both are now REPORTED by the divergence echo (db32eed) — the unsetOverrideProperty divergence names the dead key — but reporting a silently-dropped write is the floor, not the fix. Fix direction: run override values through NodePropertyCodec coercion the way `set` does (which also lets the coercion divergence fire on overrides), and rekey property-path keys in planOverride; then a patch that still fails to decode should refuse loudly rather than merge-and-drop. TDD: start red with override --help's own example asserting the override applies (content becomes "42") or refuses — either is honest; silent drop is not.

data.text:
sentry, starting 2NW90. Plan settled after reading the design doc, both leaf notes, the
revision/cache/guard/batch seams and cli-design.md.

HALF 1 — fold-in. `revision(of:)` gains a private recursion carrying the chain of
component ids folded in so far. A `ref` node folds `revision(of: refData.ref)` **and**
the revision of every component a repoint in its own `descendants` map names
(`properties["ref"]`). Cycle rule: a definition already on the chain is skipped, and a
computation that cut a cycle is **not cached** — so every cached value equals the value
an empty-chain computation gives, which is what keeps cached == from-scratch and keeps
two processes agreeing.

Reasoning check on the brief's design note: `revision(of: refData.ref)` recursion does
cover nesting (Nav01 → Btn01 → Bdg01 → Bge01 in addressing.pen). But the note's second
half is only half right. A repoint IS authored on the outer ref's props, so *changing
the repoint* moves the outer ref's rev — covered. What is NOT covered by the props hash
is the **repointed-at component's definition**: authored payload names CompB, the
instance renders CompC, so an edit to CompC would move no instance rev. Hence the extra
fold of repoint targets above. Reporting this.

Invalidation: pragmatic and provable rather than a closure walk. `invalidatingCaches`
already computes "could an expansion depend on this?" — ref, reusable, or inside a
reusable — before and after the mutation. That predicate is exactly the condition under
which a fold-in edge can be involved: a node that is none of those has no reusable
ancestor, so no instance's rev folds it and its parent spine holds no component root.
So: when the expansion cache goes whole-cache, the revision cache goes whole-cache too;
otherwise spine-only, unchanged. One predicate, no second index to keep honest, and no
repoint index needed.

HALF 2 — `--guard`. Grammar: `--guard <rev>` (the operation's own target — target
address, else parent, else the document) and `--guard <node>=<rev>` for an ancestor,
repeatable; the value splits on the last `=`. Batch: `"guard": REV`, `{"node":…,"rev":…}`
or an array of either. `BatchGuard` is one shared struct across the seam. Checked once,
at transaction entry, by `BatchApplier.checkGuards(_:in:log:file:)`, called as the first
statement of each verb's transaction body and of `apply`'s — never inside `perform`, so
a batch's own earlier lines can never trip a later line's guard. A failure is
`BatchError.guardConflict`, rendered by BatchErrorMessage with both revs, the last
writer from the activity log (`""` → "an unattributed write"), and the next command;
CommandFailure maps it to exit 3 like the other conflict rows.

sentry, done on branch worktree-agent-a2ac6ee397e267439. Full suite green (3351 tests,
341 suites, 1 pre-existing known issue), `swiftformat . --lint` clean.

FOLD-IN (half 1). `revision(of:)` folds `revision(of: refData.ref)` into a ref's hash.
Checking the brief's reasoning as asked:

- **Nesting: holds.** The recursion covers it with no extra work — Nav01 → Btn01 →
  Bdg01 → Bge01 in addressing.pen, asserted in `RevisionFoldTests`.
- **Repoints: half right, and the other half was a real hole.** A repoint IS authored on
  the outer ref's own props, so *changing the repoint* moves that ref's rev — the props
  hash covers that, as the brief says. What it does not cover is the **component the
  repoint points at**: the authored payload names CompB, the instance renders CompC, so
  an edit to CompC moved nothing. A ref's hash therefore also folds every component id a
  `ref` key in its own `descendants` map names. `aRepointedInstanceCoversWhatItRenders`
  is the test; the sequence is authored-target edit (no move) → repoint (moves) →
  repointed-target edit (moves).
- **Cycles.** A component already on the fold chain is skipped, and — the part that
  matters — a revision computed with such a cut is **not memoized**. Every cached value
  is one no cut took part in, so it equals the empty-chain value, so cached == scratch
  holds and a node's rev never depends on which node was asked for first. Two tests pin
  that, including mutual recursion between two components.

INVALIDATION: the pragmatic one, and it is provable rather than merely cheap. The
revision cache is dropped wholesale exactly when the expansion cache already is —
`expansionCanDepend(on:)`, read before and after the mutation, true for a ref, a
component, or a node inside one. A subject that is none of those has no reusable
ancestor, so no instance's rev folds it and its parent spine holds no component root:
spine-scoped forgetting is then complete. Everything else keeps the existing spine walk,
so an ordinary edit still leaves the cache warm. No second index, and no repoint index
to keep honest. Extended `RevisionCacheTests`' agree-with-scratch pattern with definition
edit, nested-definition edit, delete inside a component and move into a component; all
four were red between the fold landing and the invalidation change, which is what says
they test something.

GUARDS (half 2). Grammar `--guard <rev>` / `<node>=<rev>` / `document=<rev>`,
repeatable; batch `"guard": REV | {"node":…,"rev":…} | [either,…]`. One `BatchGuard`
type crosses the seam. `BatchApplier.checkGuards` is the single door: called from
`applyOne` (a single verb's one line *is* the transaction) and from `ApplyCommand`
before `BatchApplier.apply`, never from `perform` — which is what makes "a batch never
trips its own guards" true by construction rather than by care. `apply`'s doc says
plainly that it does not check guards and names the call that does.

Three refusals that teach, all exercised: a moved premise (exit 3, both revs, the last
writer from the log over the pinned node's `revisionCoverage`, `unattributed` said
rather than omitted, next command); a guard on a node the document no longer holds
(exit 3 — the world moved; an *ambiguous* guard address still gets the resolver's own
candidate list at exit 2); a guard naming a `@tag` (exit 2 — nothing a line creates
exists at the door).

Two things found while building, both fixed rather than worked around:
- `var`/`theme-axis` lines had no `guards` field, so `"guard"` on one would have been
  silently ignored. They carry guards now, and a *bare* one on them is refused naming
  the verb, since they act on no node.
- `--retry` must check only the lines it re-runs: a line that already applied moved its
  own subtree, so re-asserting its premise would refuse the repair. `Apply.guardedLines`.

DEVIATION worth a second opinion: `woodcase help design` sat at exactly its 60-line
budget, and there is no honest way to teach a second pinning token in zero lines. The
budget is now 70 (67 used), named as a constant in `HelpCommandTests` with the reason.
The alternative was deleting a rule from the primer.

A later line's guard passes when only earlier lines of the same batch changed the subtree
Guards are absent by default and nothing changes for unguarded writes

data.note: Integrated as 33b65e7 (squash of the sentry agent's branch; full 3068-line diff read as review; suite 3351 green, lint clean). Both halves landed. FOLD-IN: revision(of:) folds revision(of: refData.ref) into a ref's hash, PLUS every component a `ref` key in the ref's own descendants map repoints a nested ref at — the agent found the decision note's premise half wrong: the repoint itself is authored on the outer ref's props, but the component it points AT is never named by the authored payload, so without the extra fold an edit to the repointed-at component moved nothing (RevisionFoldTests.aRepointedInstanceCoversWhatItRenders proves all three legs). Cycles: a component already on the fold chain is cut, and a cut computation is NOT memoized, so every cached value is chain-independent — cached == from-scratch holds and is tested, including mutual recursion. Invalidation: whole-cache drop rides expansionCanDepend(on:) (before and after), provably the only condition a fold-in edge can move under; spine-scoped forgetting is kept for component-free edits. GUARDS: --guard <rev> / <node>=<rev> / document=<rev>, repeatable; per-line "guard" (bare, object, or array) in apply; one BatchGuard type crosses the seam; BatchApplier.checkGuards is the single entry gate called from applyOne and from ApplyCommand before apply — never inside perform, so a batch structurally cannot trip its own guards (uBq). A stale guard refuses the whole transaction, exit 3, naming node, both revs, the writer from the activity log over revisionCoverage (unattributed writes named as such), and the next command (yNV — including the fold-in case: a definition edit trips a frame guard). Unguarded writes byte-identical (2Zo, golden). Holes found and fixed: var/theme-axis lines silently ignored "guard" (now carried; bare ones refused naming the verb); --retry now checks only re-run lines. help design budget deliberately 60→70 (named constant with reason). Follow-up filed: duplicated instance query (EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:) vs BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:)).

data.description: Noticed by the sentry agent during 2NW90 (2026-08-31): the "every ref pointing at this component" query exists twice — EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:) (EditableDocument+Guards.swift, sorted by name path) and BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:) (sorted by id). Two implementations of one question drift; fold them into one (the EditableDocument one is the natural home; BatchApplier's caller decides its own ordering). Small, mechanical, Sonnet-sized; touches EditableDocument+Guards.swift and the BatchApplier plan path plus their tests.

data.text: Design ruling (integrator, 2026-08-31): the wrinkle — refuse property-path keys in `override`, or rekey them — resolves to **rekey**. The house ruling is already written in NodePropertyCodec+RawKeys.swift's doc comment: "anything that can tell which side of the seam a target is on translates rather than refuse", and planOverride provably knows the target is an instance descendant (it guards on `.instanceDescendant` before planning). Refusing would make `override` the one verb that speaks only the raw vocabulary while `cp --descendant-props` translates; that asymmetry is exactly what the doc comment exists to prevent. So: planOverride runs op.props through NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed (same as CopyCommand.swift:371), values coerce through the codec the way `set` does, and a patch that still fails to decode refuses loudly.

data.text:
Diagnosed all three from vvxHi's own soak run logs (same HEAD 33b65e7), not from guesswork —
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-Woodcase/972be628-.../scratchpad/vvxHi-soak.log.run{1,2,3}`:

1. run1 — `WebViewTestHarnessTests.swift:212` is the `Issue.record("Expected .javaScriptError, got \(error)")`
   line, so the harness threw a `HarnessError` that was **not** `.javaScriptError`: a `.timeout`. The test
   passes `timeout: 5.0`, which is both the `PageHost` load budget *and* the ready-signal budget
   (`remaining = timeout - elapsed`). Under load the trivial page's load alone eats the 5 s, so the harness
   reports a timeout instead of the page error it would have surfaced. A budget near the interval under
   test, exactly the shape gotchas.md warns about.

2. run2 + run3 — `PenFileTransactionTests.swift:310` `concurrentTransactionsSerialize`, with the *typed*
   error: "…layout-vertical.pen is locked by another process; gave up after 10s". Not the recorded
   wall-clock-assertion gotcha (that one is `heldLockTimesOut`, already bounded at 120 s and it passed).
   This is a real `timeout:` budget of 10 s that load exceeds: transaction A holds the exclusive lock
   across `MainActor.run { EditableDocument(from:) … materialize() }`, and `FileLock.acquire` polls with a
   10 ms `Task.sleep` that resumes tens of seconds late under the parallel suite — so B gets ~1 attempt in
   its whole 10 s window.

3. run3 — four `ViewerFixtures.swift:85` timeouts in one run: three FileWatcherTests plus
   `SSEHubTests` "An idle stream gets a heartbeat comment". Common factor is `waitUntil`'s 30 s default
   bound, which is *below* this suite's observed starvation scale, and a second, worse hole: the loop
   checks the deadline before the condition and never evaluates the condition again after the deadline —
   so with poll sleeps resuming ~12 s late, a condition that came true at 25 s of a 30 s bound is reported
   as a timeout it did not earn. (FileWatcherTests.swift:49 is a cascade of the same failure.)

All three are test-shape, not product bugs. FileWatcher, FileLock and PenFileTransaction all behave
correctly in every log line; what failed is three budgets set near the machine's load and one wait that
gives up without looking.

Done on branch worktree-agent-a7f82e7425af3cb87 (not committed; integrator merges).

Three changes, in the order the ruling asked for.

1. REKEY. `planOverride` now runs `op.props` through `NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed`, so
   `override X kind.content=…` stores `content` and applies at expansion. The duplicate
   call in `CopyCommand.assignment(to:props:in:)` is gone — the planner owns the
   translation for every `override`, however it was written.

2. COERCE. Values run through the same number-to-string rule `set` applies, via a new
   `NodePropertyCodec.coercingOverrides(_:on:)` keyed by raw .pen name
   (`fieldName(forRawKey:)` in +JSON.swift is the inverse of `jsonKey(for:)`, derived
   from the same two-entry table). `overrideDivergences` gained a `requested:` argument
   and now emits the `.coercion` divergence, so the echo from db32eed fires on overrides.
   The help's own example, `override design.pen Orders/Value content=42`, now stores
   "42" and says so.

3. REFUSE. New `EditingError.overrideValueRejected(refID:descendantKey:key:expected:actual:)`,
   raised by `EditableDocument.validateOverrideValues(_:)` from both `validate(_:)` and
   `applyOverrideDescendant(_:)`. It judges each key on its own with a new throwing
   `PenNodePatcher.patched(_:with:)` — the same merge the expander runs — so the message
   carries the shape table's `expected` and the DecodingError's own `actual` clause.
   Exempt: an override carrying a `type` key (a replacement, not a patch) and a ref whose
   component is not in the registry.

DESIGN CALL worth reviewing. The brief said "a patch that still fails to decode at
expansion refuses loudly". The refusal is at the WRITE, not at expansion:
`PenNodePatcher.patchNode` still returns the unpatched node. Reason: expansion is what
renders files Woodcase did not write, Pen.app itself accepts these overrides, and
`validateOverrideTarget` — the exact analogue for a dead descendant *key* — already
refuses at the write and leaves expansion tolerant. So a hand-made file still draws,
while nothing Woodcase writes can be silently dropped. Said so in
`PenNodePatcher.patchNode`'s doc comment and in EditingDocuments.md.

Follow-up worth a leaf: `lint` has no rule for an override already in a file that the
merge will drop. The write path can no longer create one, but an imported or
Pen.app-written file can, and only the linter is positioned to say so.

Suite: 3365 tests green (`swift test --quiet`, sandbox off), up from 3351.

Done on branch worktree-agent-a7f82e7425af3cb87 (not committed).

`BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:)` is deleted; its one caller, `planRemove`'s
`--detach`, now calls `EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:)`. No other caller
existed and no test named the deleted method, so no test had to change.

The visible difference is ordering: the deleted copy sorted by node id, the survivor
sorts by full name path (then id, to stay total). `planRemove` uses the list for two
things — the `detachRef` operations, whose order does not matter, and the
`detachedInstances` divergence, which lists the paths; those now read in the same
order as every other list this document prints. The full suite is green either way,
which is the evidence that nothing depended on the id order.

Fixed, all three, on branch `worktree-agent-abf60da809efae460` (worktree
`/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/.claude/worktrees/agent-abf60da809efae460`). No product bug in any
of them — `FileLock`, `PenFileTransaction` and `FileWatcher` behaved correctly in every log
line; three budgets were set near the scale of the machine's load, and one wait gave up
without looking.

- `WebViewTestHarness.defaultBudget` (60 s) replaces the harness's 5 s default and the test's
  own 5 s / 10 s arguments. Side benefit: the host pool goes from four budget-keyed buckets to
  two, so hosts are reused more.
- `PenFileTransactionTests.lockBudget` (60 s) replaces the 10 s and 5 s `timeout:` arguments on
  the two contention tests. `FileLockTests`' short budgets are deliberately untouched: every
  one acquires an uncontended lock, and `acquire` attempts before it checks the deadline.
- `waitUntil` now evaluates the condition once more after the deadline, defaults to
  `ViewerFixtures.waitBudget` (60 s), and returns whether it held so a caller can skip the
  assertions that would only restate the same failure. New `WaitUntilTests` pins it; the

data.note: Fixed in d893dd0 (agent quill, Opus; integrated and suite-verified at 3365 green). `override` now translates property-path keys through NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed (per the rekey ruling noted on this leaf), coerces values the way `set` does (the coercion divergence fires on overrides), and refuses a value the patched node cannot decode with the new EditingError.overrideValueRejected — judged with the expander's own merge via the new throwing PenNodePatcher.patched(_:with:). The refusal is at the WRITE, not at expansion: expansion stays tolerant because Woodcase renders files it did not write (house precedent: validateOverrideTarget). The help example (`content=42`) now stores "42" and echoes the coercion. Docs updated in WoodcaseEditor.md, WoodcaseCLI.md, WoodcaseBatches.md, EditingDocuments.md. Follow-up filed: lint has no rule for an override already in a file that the merge will drop (import or Pen.app-written); the write path can no longer create one.

Fixed in d893dd0 (agent quill, same commit as hTeBC — same file surface). BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:) deleted; its one caller (planRemove's --detach) now uses EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:). No test named the deleted method. Visible difference: the survivor sorts by full name path rather than id, so the detachedInstances divergence now reads in document order — an improvement, matching every other list the document prints. Bonus dedup in the same commit: CopyCommand's rawKeyed call removed since the planner now rekeys every override.

Fixed in 4007571 (agent fenwick, Opus). All three diagnosed from vvxHi's own soak logs at the same HEAD; none was a product bug — all were budgets set at machine-load scale, plus one real helper hole. (1) WebView harness test's 5 s render budget spent by load before the typed error could be judged → named WebViewTestHarness.defaultBudget (60 s). (2) PenFileTransaction contention tests' 10 s lock timeout gave the waiter ~one flock attempt under late-resuming sleeps → 60 s lockBudget; NOT the recorded wall-clock gotcha (that one is heldLockTimesOut, which passed) — the gotchas entry now covers budgets as well as assertions. (3) waitUntil checked the deadline before the condition and never looked again after the loop, so a late-resuming poll reported timeouts nothing earned (this also covered the SSEHubTests heartbeat failure — the leaf title's "FileWatcher heartbeat" conflated two suites); it now evaluates once more past the deadline, defaults to a 60 s waitBudget, and returns whether the condition held. data.description: Found by the quill agent during hTeBC (2026-08-31): since d893dd0 the write path refuses an override value the patched node cannot decode, but an override *already in a file* that the merge will drop — from an import, or a Pen.app-written file — is still silent: PenNodePatcher.patchNode falls back to the unpatched node by design (expansion stays tolerant), and nothing tells the user the override in their file never draws. The linter is the only thing positioned to say so. Fix direction: a DocumentLinter rule that walks every ref's descendants map, runs each non-replacement entry through PenNodePatcher.patched (the throwing variant added in d893dd0) against patchedDefinitionNode, and reports the key, the node path, and the shape mismatch using the same expected/actual wording as EditingError.overrideValueRejected. Skip refs whose component is not in the registry, and entries carrying a type key, matching validateOverrideValues' exemptions.

data.text:
Implemented three lint checks, TDD red-first, in worktree
/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa75a10c745c9adfd (branch: whatever
the worktree's own branch is — see `git branch --show-current` there).

What shipped:
- override-value-rejected: a ref's descendants entry carries a value the descendant
  it patches cannot decode. Judged one property key at a time with the throwing
  PenNodePatcher.patched(_:with:) against EditableDocument.patchedDefinitionNode
  (same primitives EditableDocument+Guards.validateOverrideValues uses at write time,
  but not that function itself, since it stops at the first bad key within one
  override's properties and the brief wants every bad key named).
- override-target-not-found: a descendants key naming no descendant the ref's
  component defines. Reuses EditableDocument.validateOverrideTarget(_:) directly by
  constructing a throwaway EditOperation.OverrideDescendant per key and catching
  EditingError.overrideTargetNotFound — this one already existed as a write-time
  guard, unrelated to d893dd0, and no lint check covered it (checked: grepped
  Sources/Woodcase/Lint for descendantKey/overridableDescendantKeys/patchedDefinitionNode
  before adding, all misses).
- override-key-unread: a descendants entry's property is stored under a dotted path
  ("kind.content") instead of the raw .pen key ("content") a merge reads. This is
  NOT a write-time EditingError case and PenNodePatcher.patched never throws for it —
  an unrecognised JSON key just decodes as a no-op, so the merge "succeeds" and the
  override still never draws. Caught by checking the key itself for the
  NodePropertyCodec.commonPrefix/kindPrefix prefix, not by any merge/decode.

All three share the per-row walk DocumentLinter.unresolvedVariables already uses for
ref override maps (context.resolved(row), unexpanded-but-variable-substituted), and
are guarded by DocumentLinter+Overrides.swift, wired into
DocumentLinter.findings(for:parent:in:) right after unresolvedVariables.

New files:
- Sources/Woodcase/Lint/DocumentLinter+Overrides.swift
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/DocumentLinterOverrideValueTests.swift
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/lint/override-value-rejected.pen
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/lint/override-target-not-found.pen
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/lint/override-key-unread.pen

Modified: Sources/Woodcase/Lint/{DocumentLinter,LintCheck}.swift,
Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/LintCommand.swift,
Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/{WoodcaseLint,WoodcaseEditor}.md,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/LintFormatterTests.swift (the LintCheck.allCases inventory test
needed its expected id list extended — a documented, intentional change, not a
regression fix).

Gotcha found and fixed before it cost the reviewer time: my first WoodcaseLint.md
draft wrote "Pen.app" in prose. VendorWordsTests.docCIsClean scans every
Documentation.docc/*.md file for "pen.app"/"pencil"/"pen.dev"/"mcp"
case-insensitively and failed the full suite on it — the same word is fine inside a
Swift doc comment (DocumentLinter+Scroll.swift and PenIconFontRegistry.swift both use
it) because that test only reads the .md files directly, not generated DocC. Renamed
to "the editor" to match existing doc-file convention (see PenInteroperability.md).
Not adding to gotchas.md since the rule (test scans docc .md for vendor words) is
already legible from VendorWordsTests.swift itself and cost only one red run to find.

Verification: swiftformat . --lint clean (0/811 need formatting); swift test --quiet
full suite: 3377 tests, 2 known issues (unchanged baseline), 0 failures, ~38s.

DEVIATIONS from brief:
- Added override-target-not-found as a genuinely separate check from
  override-value-rejected rather than folding it into one "override problems" check,
  since it has its own EditingError precedent, its own exemption logic (does NOT
  exempt object replacements, unlike value-rejected), and the brief's own wording
  ("Also report a descendants key that names nothing...") reads as a distinct fact
  to report, not a variant message on the same check id.
- Did not add a fourth check for "an unresolved $variable inside an override that
  also fails to decode" (double-counting risk raised in my own reasoning) — confirmed
  by reading PenValue's decoder that a literal "$name" string always decodes fine for
  every field PenValue<T>/PenSizing wrap, so it can never collide with
  override-value-rejected; no extra guard was needed.

WHAT IN THIS BRIEF IS WRONG (or needed judgment calls):
- The brief says "use EditableDocument.patchedDefinitionNode(ofInstance:descendantKey:)
  or the equivalent walk if the linter works on a different model." It does not
  differ: TreeView.rows(of:) with DocumentLinter's default expandInstances:false never
  descends past a ref row, so every ref row's own id is always the raw flat-store id
  (never a compound "outer/inner" path) — refID == row.id everywhere in this check,
  no chain-walking needed. Worth confirming explicitly since the brief left it open.
- The brief's phrase "runs the same judgment as validateOverrideValues" is only
  partly reusable: that function throws on the FIRST bad key within one override's
  properties dict, so calling it directly would silently hide every key after the
  first. I reused its two underlying primitives (patchedDefinitionNode +
  PenNodePatcher.patched) in a per-key loop instead, per the brief's own later
  instruction ("one key at a time so the finding can name the key") — the two
  instructions are in tension and I followed the more specific one.
- One real gap the brief didn't flag: a stale dotted key ("kind.content") does NOT
  throw from PenNodePatcher.patched at all (an unrecognised JSON key decodes as a
  no-op), so it could never have been caught by "the same judgment as
  validateOverrideValues" however it's reused — it needed its own, non-throwing check
  on the key text. The brief's example ("kind.content") already anticipated the
  fixture but not that the detection mechanism has to be structurally different from
  the other two checks.

data.note: Fixed in f18fe15 (agent marlin, Sonnet; integrated, suite 3377 green, pushed). Three new lint checks read the write path's own guards back over a ref's stored descendants map, without expanding the instance (same seam as unresolved-variable): override-value-rejected (per-key judgment via the throwing PenNodePatcher.patched, so one bad key doesn't hide the rest — deliberately not validateOverrideValues, which short-circuits), override-target-not-found (reuses validateOverrideTarget verbatim), and override-key-unread (a dotted `kind.content` key decodes as a harmless unknown field, so no merge judgment can catch it; the check reads the key prefix directly — a case the original issue's fix direction missed). Object replacements and unresolved-import refs are exempt, matching the write guard; unresolved refs still report as broken-ref. Docs: WoodcaseLint.md gained an "Overrides a file already carries" section; LintCommand help and WoodcaseEditor.md updated. All three are errors, same reasoning as the write-time refusal.

tasks.title: Woodcase Viewer & Editor
tasks.description: Agent-first CLI editing of .pen files and a read-only live viewer. Decisions and the verb set are in project/2026-08-29-viewer-editor-plan.md; the agent-experience evidence is in project/2026-08-29-pen-mcp-tire-kick.md. Read both before claiming. Strict TDD on every leaf.

tasks.title: Editing core
tasks.description: Library-level pieces the CLI is a thin consumer of. All in Sources/Woodcase/Editing (or a new Editing/Agent-facing folder, one type per file), Foundation-only, DocC at 100%.

tasks.title: Path-based property patch operation
tasks.description: EditOperation.updateKind replaces a node's whole kind; agents want to set one property. Add a `setProperties` operation carrying a [String: AnyCodable] keyed by the same property paths LWWPropertyMap already uses ("kind.width", "common.name"), applied through PenNodePatcher-style merging, with an inverse, dirty-tracking classification via ChangeCategory, and CRDT emission as per-path LWW writes. Unknown keys and type mismatches are typed EditingErrors naming the key.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a32472027d8c7b81e (agent "patcher", Opus). New: Editing/NodePropertyCodec{,+Write,+JSON,+Shapes}.swift and three test suites (59 tests). Accepted deviations: synthesized Codable for SetProperties; four codec files; PropertyDiff untouched with commonPaths pinned by test. Agent corrections to the brief accepted: unified "$x" variable wire form in the CRDT codec; unknown kinds keep an open vocabulary for convergence. Watch for the perf leaf: each path write is a full payload encode/decode round trip through JSONEncoder, on both the local and the remote CRDT path. The +Shapes table is the ingredient for propertyTypeMismatch messages ("expected: number, \"fit_content\", ..."), which the help-that-teaches leaf should surface verbatim.

tasks.title: Node addressing
tasks.description: A resolver from an address string to a node id: id, name path from any ancestor ("Dashboard/Header/Title"), instance path into a ref's expanded tree ("Orders/Value", resolved to the component child id for storage in descendants), and a within-batch tag ("@hero"). Ambiguity is a typed error carrying every candidate as an id plus its full name path; no match is a typed error that lists near misses (same leaf name elsewhere). Also a name-path formatter for the reverse direction, used by every error message and by tree output.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-aa72bf9b9362ad785 (agent "addresser", Opus) plus one integrator change: an id match beats a name match at every segment (the agent flagged the gap; ruled so tree --expand paths are guaranteed unambiguous), with a test. Agent's deviations accepted: NodeAddress has two cases (path/tag) with a single-string Codable form for the JSONL grammar; "#<id>" is a general id-escape; the ref stands in for the component root (Nav/Label, not Nav/Button/Label); NodeAddressCandidate.id is "<refID>/<key>" for instance descendants (doc comment updated). Harness note from the agent: local/ is gitignored so briefs must cite it by absolute main-checkout path.

tasks.title: Revision tokens
tasks.description: A stable hash per node subtree (properties, children order, descendant hashes) and one for the document, computed from the flat store and exposed on EditableDocument. A mutating operation may carry an expected revision for each node it touches; a mismatch is a typed conflict error naming the node and both revisions. Document-level revision is what the activity log records.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a265a3d84fbad0c11 (agent "reviser", Sonnet). New: Editing/FNV1a.swift, Editing/EditableDocument+Revision.swift, RevisionTests (14). Design: FNV-1a 64 over canonical JSON + child revisions; expected revisions travel beside the op (apply(_:expecting:)), not inside EditOperation. Note for the perf leaf: revision(of:) is recursive and uncached, so documentRevision is O(n) per call.

tasks.title: Batch applier
tasks.description: Applies an ordered list of operations (the JSONL grammar in the plan) to an EditableDocument in memory: each op resolves its addresses (including @tags created earlier in the batch), applies, and records a per-op result; a failure skips the op and marks every later op that references its tag or target as cascaded; independent ops continue. The result is a report (line, status, error, created name→id tree). Atomic mode discards everything on the first failure. Also the retry: given a prior report, re-run only its failed and cascaded lines.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a30b843450baa2985 (agent "batcher", Opus). Sources/Woodcase/Batch/ (20 files, ≤288 lines each), DocC WoodcaseBatches.md, five suites, fixture batch.pen. For the CLI leaves: BatchApplier.identity is a PeerID? but the activity log's identity is a String — the apply verb should build ActivityEvents from BatchLineResult.inverse via the recorder (or the applier should gain a recorder hook); decodeJSONL throws on a malformed file → usage exit 2, not a line failure; `override` takes props only, keyed by raw .pen names (not NodePropertyCodec paths) because that is what Pen stores in descendants; var/theme-axis removal is deliberately not in the grammar; a root-level add's rev checks documentRevision. Pre-existing exposure the agent found: detachRef's remapIDs never consults the document for id collisions (applyInsert makes a collision loud, not silent).

tasks.title: File transactions
tasks.description: PenFileTransaction: open a .pen under an exclusive advisory lock (flock on the file), parse, hand an EditableDocument to a closure, write the result atomically (temp file + rename, same directory) in the canonical form migrate already writes (sorted keys, two-space indent), release. A held lock is waited on with a bounded timeout, then a typed error. Unchanged documents do not rewrite the file (mtime stays).
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a9b2bc6b1b01dee89 (agent "filer", Opus). New: Files/{PenFileTransaction,FileLock,PenFileError}.swift, two test suites (23 tests). The agent found the brief's recipe (flock + rename-over) unsafe as stated and added inode revalidation; accepted. Body is @MainActor @Sendable (must return its result, cannot capture mutable locals). For the activity-log leaf (qoTVa): the commit point is the private write(_:replacing:) and Outcome.didWrite — plan a signature change (a recorder parameter on run, or a second body argument), the agent deliberately built no hook. FileLockTests were written after the implementation (green first run) and mutation-checked instead.

tasks.title: Consequence guards
tasks.description: Operations whose consequence exceeds their target refuse without an explicit flag and explain: deleting a reusable node that has instances (lists them; `detach` applies detachRef to each first), an override or descendant patch that matches no node in the component (error, never a silent no-op, with candidates), moving a node into its own subtree. Each guard is a typed EditingError with the information the CLI needs to print the remedy.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-aee440f96059a620d (agent "guard", Opus). New Editing/EditableDocument+Guards.swift and three suites; DeleteNode gains Instances (.refuse/.detach) with a custom Codable defaulting to refuse; two gotchas appended. Known holes, deliberate: a ref whose component is not in componentRegistry skips override validation (needs a componentNotFound case to refuse); the component root is a valid descendant key that the name-path resolver cannot address (only the id-path). Filed a leaf for applyLocal to fail closed.

tasks.title: Settled tree view
tasks.description: A TreeRow model and formatter: for a document (or subtree), one row per node with id, type, name (or an unnamed marker), resolved layout rect in the parent's space, and a clip flag (partially/fully outside its parent), computed from PenLayoutEngine after variable resolution for a chosen theme; optional expansion of refs with path addresses ("SAjDU/B0M8B8/uKX6O") that resolve back through the addresser; optional property columns; depth limit; and a JSON form. This is the read that replaces most screenshots.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-aa55ce1955742cc74 (agent "treeview", Opus). New folder Sources/Woodcase/Tree/ (TreeRow, TreeReport, SettledTree, TreeView, TreeFormatter), two suites (24 tests), fixture tree-overflow.pen. Findings for later leaves: computeLayout() takes no theme and strips reusables — SettledTree runs its own pipeline (consider giving computeLayout theme:/keepReusables: when the perf leaf measures); the expanded instance root is keyed "<ref>/<component root id>" while its address is just "<ref>" (TreeView.componentRoot bridges it); a property path no node has renders "-" rather than erroring — a candidate EditingError case for the help leaf. Agent noted one unattributed flaky full run (2 issues, then 3 clean runs).

tasks.title: Activity log
tasks.description: An append-only JSONL event log at ~/.woodcase/activity.jsonl ($WOODCASE_HOME overrides the directory), one event per applied operation: timestamp, identity (PeerID name), absolute file path, op kind, node ids and name paths touched, the inverse EditOperation (from EditableDocument+Inverse), document revision after. Written by the file transaction on commit. A reader that tails it (with an offset) and filters by file and identity, for the CLI and the viewer. Rotation at a size threshold.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a1bf166672627a006 (agent "logger", Opus). Files/Activity{Event,Event+Codable,Log,Reader,Recorder}.swift, four suites, DocC article WoodcaseActivityLog.md. Rulings from the report for the CLI leaves: a failed log append throws PenFileError naming the *log* after the .pen is already written — needs its own exit-code mapping; the log append happens while the .pen lock is still held; `cp`/`undo` kinds are caller-supplied via `as:`; rotation renames the locked file with a bounded retry (a sidecar lock would be stricter — backlog if it ever bites). Gotcha to file: ISO8601FormatStyle truncates fractional seconds rather than rounding; ActivityEvent rounds milliseconds itself.

tasks.title: CLI verbs
tasks.description: Sources/WoodcaseCommand grows one command file per verb, each a thin adapter over the core: no decisions in the adapter. Conventions from the plan: --json on every read, the sleepy-style exit codes, name→id tree on every mutation, errors that name the path and the remedy, --as/$WOODCASE_AS. Tests in WoodcaseCommandTests drive the commands against fixture copies in a temp directory.

tasks.title: tree and get
tasks.description: `woodcase tree <file> [<node>]` prints the settled tree view; --depth, --props, --json, --expand, --theme. `woodcase get <file> <node>` prints one node as .pen JSON (or expanded), with its revision. Output must be the outline of what an agent should read first; the default is rows, not JSON.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a2acadae3da948f19 (agent "treeget", Opus). Doc sections for tree and get are in the agent's report (per-verb ### sections, before render). Findings: EditableDocument.expandRef builds a single-entry registry so a nested ref inside the component stays a raw ref (expandSubtree/expandedDocument inherit it) — filed as an issue; tree's header is the document revision (document-wide --rev), get's is the node revision (per-node --rev); NodePropertyCodec paths are prefixed (kind.fill), the plan doc's bare `--props fill` is wrong; `swift test --filter "<display name>"` matches zero tests and exits 0 — filter by type name.

tasks.title: add, cp, set, mv, rm, override
tasks.description: The single-op verbs. `add <parent|document> -F subtree.json` inserts a .pen subtree (generated ids, names required — an unnamed node in the subtree is a usage error that suggests naming; a root-level add without x/y is auto-placed in empty space to the right of existing roots); `set <node> key=value…` with typed value parsing (numbers, colors, $variables, fill_container, JSON for objects) and --rev; `cp <node> <parent> [key=value…]` duplicates a subtree with fresh ids (copying a reusable node makes an instance, as Pen does) and applies overrides to the copy — descendant overrides by name path resolve against the copy, never silently; `mv`, `rm --detach`, `override <instance>/<path>` with flags or a subtree. Each prints the name→id tree of what it created and appends to the activity log.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-ae18586077795e1e9 (agent "mutator", Opus). Verb type names carry the Command suffix (struct Set would shadow Swift.Set). Value rules are in PropertyAssignment.valueRules. No --tag on add (no later lines to use it); override -F is a props object, not a subtree (the grammar has no subtree override). Follow-ups: BatchErrorMessage wants a dialect parameter so CommandRemedy's three rephrasings exist once; root-level cp lands on its source (filed as an issue). Doc rows/paragraphs are in the agent's report for RXaYR.

tasks.title: apply
tasks.description: `woodcase apply <file> -F ops.jsonl [--atomic] [--retry report.json]` over the batch applier. The report goes to stdout as one line per op; --json emits the full report. Exit 0 if every op applied, 1 if any failed or cascaded, 3 on conflict.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-aeafbe7eadd4ba118 (agent "applier", Sonnet). Seams changes: BatchLineResult.isRevisionConflict (typed, additive); BatchErrorMessage.describe(_ BatchError) needs no document and the outside-body mapper now uses it. Doc section for apply is in the agent's report for RXaYR.

tasks.title: vars
tasks.description: `woodcase vars <file>` lists variables and theme axes; `vars set name=value [--theme mode=dark]` adds or updates (typed by value: color, number, string; themed values per axis, registering a new axis value on the fly as Pen does); `vars rm name` refuses while any node references it unless --force; `vars axis add mode=light,dark`. Over the existing variable and theme EditOperations.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a10fcc4e6d608a164 (agent "varser", Opus). tasks.title: undo
tasks.description: `woodcase undo <file> [-n N] [--as name]` replays the inverse operations of the last N activity-log events for this file (by this identity, or any with --all) through a file transaction, appending undo events of its own. Refuses with a conflict if the file revision no longer matches the event's recorded revision — undo never guesses.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-a397bab83545fa28a (agent "undoer", Opus). Semantics in UndoStep.decide. Follow-ups noted, not filed: an `undoes` link on undo events would remove the one heuristic (a mismatch after a passed undo = already undone; an outside-log edit then reads as "nothing to undo", exit 1); IdentityOptions' shared --as help says an unattributed edit is applied unlogged, which undo contradicts (it refuses). Doc paragraph is in the agent's report for RXaYR.

tasks.title: lint
tasks.description: `woodcase lint <file> [<node>]` runs the pipeline's PenDiagnosticCollector (missing fonts, broken refs, unresolved variables) plus layout checks from settled layout: text without fill, fill_container inside a fit_content parent on the same axis, fit_content with no children, a child clipped by its parent. One line per finding naming the node path; exit 1 when findings exist; --json.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-acf4b04f1c4c74659 (agent "linter", Opus). Brief corrections: PenDiagnosticCollector carries no font/ref/variable diagnostics — broken refs and unresolved variables became real library checks, fonts are unchecked; the clip flag is TreeView's, not SettledTree's. Follow-ups: lint --json is a bare array with no revision (a LintReport would fix it); the read verbs (lint, shot, tree) have no --library, so a library-based document reports every import as broken-ref — a leaf for the docs/install pass or a small verbs leaf.

tasks.title: Viewer
tasks.description: `woodcase serve [--port N] [<file>…]` — a local, read-only web viewer. Apple-only like render; a minimal HTTP/1.1 + SSE server on Network.framework with no dependency. Watches the given files (or every file seen in the activity log) with a DispatchSource/FSEvents watcher, re-renders changed artboards through a warm pipeline (fonts, layout cache), and pushes updates over SSE. One page: a file/artboard list (the dashboard: last change, by whom, from the activity log), the artboard image, an outline side panel from the tree view, and an activity feed. Selecting a row in the outline or clicking the image outlines that node in the render via the shared helper and shows its name path and id for handing to an agent. The JSON and SSE endpoints the page uses are the API other dashboards consume; document them.

tasks.title: Viewer design prototype

tasks.title: Server and file watching
tasks.description: The HTTP/SSE server, the file watcher, the warm render cache, and the JSON endpoints (/files, /files/{id}/tree, /files/{id}/artboards/{id}.png, /events). Tests drive it in-process with URLSession.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-afd2476a3d0e0804b (agent "server", Opus). API: ViewerServer(pages:) actor with start(files:port:log:)/stop(); ViewerRoutes seam (add(method, pattern, handler); patterns literal | {name} | {name}.png; first registration wins, pages first); ViewerContext {files, renders: RenderCache, log, events: SSEHub}; RenderCache.png(artboard:of:theme:longestSide:); FileWatcher; SSEHub; ChangeCoordinator; ViewerJSON.encoder/decoder (ISO-8601 dates). Events: `change` {file, artboards, identity, op, nodes, paths, revision, time, name, path} and `presence` {identities:[{name, lastSeen, events, files}]}. File id = 12 hex FNV-1a of the canonical path. Traps for the page leaf: SSE frames end with an empty line, and AsyncLineSequence drops empty lines — EventSource in the browser handles it; a hand-rolled reader must split on "\n\n". ?theme= accepts both `axis:value` and `axis=value`. One @unchecked Sendable (ResumeOnce in HTTPServer.swift, NSLock-guarded) — flagged for Ben. The `serve` verb is not wired yet (the page leaf wires it).

tasks.title: Speed up the WebView regression suite
tasks.description: The full suite is ~95 s and WebViewRegression alone is ~78 s of it (11 serialized tests, ~7 s each; measured 2026-08-29 with `swift test --filter WebViewRegression`), while PenSnapshotTests is 14 s and everything else is seconds. Profile where each test's seconds go (PageHost/WKWebView spin-up per render, loadDocuments() re-parsing the banking fixture, the ReactEmitter run, the 2x screen renders, font loading) with timestamps, then take the low-hanging fruit: reuse one PageHost across the suite if WebKit allows it safely, parse and emit the fixture once per suite, and drop `.serialized` if the harness's ready-signal makes parallel safe. Keep MAE results identical (performance/mae-baseline.csv must not change). Record the before/after numbers and the reproducing command in the leaf's done note and in project/2026-08-29-test-suite-speed.md.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-af502ff6b545944d2 (agent "speeder", Opus). The premise was load-inflated 4×; real before 18.7 s, after 8.0 s for WebViewRegression, ~16 s full suite. SleepyHollow is not the cost (host 14 ms, shot 22 ms); four PageHost improvements are written up in project/2026-08-29-test-suite-speed.md for Ben to carry to ../SleepyHollow. Profiler stays behind WOODCASE_TEST_PROFILE; WOODCASE_TEST_NO_HOST_POOL reproduces the A/B.

tasks.title: applyLocal fails closed
tasks.description: Found by the guards agent (zF7AK): EditableDocument.applyLocal runs crdtDocument.processLocal first, then swallows a throw from apply(_:) and reconciles, so any validation added to apply() is invisible in CRDT mode — the edit replicates while the local call "refuses". The consequence guards work around it with a pre-flight in applyLocal. Make applyLocal fail closed: validate every operation up front (a validate(_:) pass mirroring apply's guards, or a dry run on a copy), or roll CRDT state back on a throw; then remove the pre-flight special case. A test per EditOperation case: an invalid op leaves the operation log and tombstones untouched.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the squash of worktree-agent-aab1f2b7ba44a6f71 (agent "failclosed", Opus). Guards factored once into EditableDocument+Validate.swift; applyLocal validates before processLocal; override pre-flight removed. Two applyMove bugs fixed en route (negative index trapped; out-of-range index checked after unlinking). Agent's finding: the leak was narrower than the leaf said — node-missing cases already failed closed via CRDTDocument's bail-out; the real leak was guards that fire when the node exists and every document-level LWW op. Trap for future briefs: a red pass over out-of-range indices can hit a hard trap that kills the in-process run — isolate with --skip.

tasks.title: Full-suite flake under load (2 issues, passes on rerun)
tasks.description: The full suite intermittently reports 2 issues under load (seen 2026-08-29 by four separate runs across agents and the integrator; two immediate reruns pass). Reports name PenFileTransactionTests' lock-timeout test ("locked by another process; gave up after 10s") and the Task.sleep-resumes-late effect in project/gotchas.md. Capture the failing run's output to a file (`swift test 2>&1 | tee $TMPDIR/run.log`, sandbox off) until it reproduces, identify the test(s), and make them load-proof: no wall-clock assertions near the interval under test, or serialize the file-lock suites, or give the lock tests their own timeout budget. Done when ten consecutive full runs pass with the suite-speed changes (VY4EA) in.

tasks.title: expandRef leaves nested refs unexpanded
tasks.description: Found by the tree/get agent (xXuLn): EditableDocument.expandRef(nodeID:) builds `[refData.ref: materializedComponent]` as its whole registry, so a ref nested inside that component does not expand — on addressing.pen, expanding Nav01 leaves Nav01/Bdg01 as a raw ref. expandSubtree and expandedDocument route through it and inherit the hole. `get --expand` avoids it by using PenRefExpander.expand over the whole document. Fix: build the registry from every reusable in the document (or delegate to PenRefExpander), with a regression test on addressing.pen.

tasks.title: shot cannot render a reusable-component top-level frame and exits 5
tasks.description: Found by the docs agent (RXaYR, 2026-08-29) verifying WoodcaseEditor.md against the binary. Regression test first, on banking.pen. shot works on batch.pen.

tasks.title: Most-specific-first route matching in the viewer
tasks.description: ViewerRoutes.match is first-registered-wins, so a page route `/files/{file}/artboards/{artboard}` also matches `Cnv01.png` and would shadow the PNG endpoint; ViewerPages.routes() works around it by claiming the `.png` pattern first for ViewerEndpoints.artboard. Replace precedence-by-order with most-specific-first: a literal segment beats a `{name}.png` suffix pattern beats a bare `{name}` capture, ties broken by registration order (so a page still shadows a built-in at equal specificity). Then remove the workaround from ViewerPages and keep ViewerPagesTests.pngStillWins as the regression test. Found by the page agent (ExnBl).
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main as e154128 (pushed), 2550 green. Route.Specificity (public, Friendly & Comparable; literal > suffixed capture > capture, lexicographic, length as the total-order fallback); ViewerRoutes.match keeps the most specific method-matching entry with strict > so equal shapes fall through to registration order; ViewerPages holds page routes only. Decision (integrator): Specificity stays public — precedence is part of the contract a route registrant reasons about.

tasks.title: set kind.fills rejects an array while saying it accepts one
tasks.description: Seen 2026-08-29 while demoing the viewer. `woodcase set batch.pen Canvas/Cards kind.fills='[{"type":"solid","color":"#FFD166"}]' --as claude-a` is refused with: "kind.fills on Canvas/Cards (Crd01) takes a color string, a fill object, or an array of fills, but the value given is array". The message contradicts itself — it lists arrays as accepted and then rejects one — so either NodePropertyCodec's fills decoding does not accept the documented array form (or requires a different fill shape than {"type":"solid","color":…}; check PenFill's wire form in the 2.17 schema) or the accepted-forms text is wrong. Regression test first with the exact value above; fix whichever side is wrong, and make the mismatch message name the shape it actually wanted (an example literal). `kind.fills="#FFD166"` works.
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main as d7bdce2 (pushed), 2610 green. The refusal was right ("solid" is not a fill type; it is "color"); three faults fixed: PenFills/PenEffects swallowed the array's own error, the shapes table was hand-typed and had drifted (padding order was reversed), and valueRules taught {"type":"solid"}. PenPropertyShape generates shapes from the decoders; PenDecodingFailure renders DecodingError in file vocabulary. Loose end noted: PenSizing's decode message leaks a Swift type name (unreachable from a caller today).

tasks.title: One absolute-rect walk and one expanded-id mapping, shared by shot, the viewer and NodeLookup
tasks.description: Found integrating wlAte (2026-08-29). PenLayoutEngine settles rects relative to the parent; anything that needs canvas coordinates walks the subtree composing origins — and that walk now exists twice: ShotFrame.rects(under:in:layoutRects:) in WoodcaseCommand and ArtboardLayout in WoodcaseViewer (which also computes TreeRow.Clip). Lift ONE walk into the library (e.g. PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects(under:in:layoutRects:) or a SettledTree accessor, whichever the layout cache already has the pieces for — check LayoutCache/SettledTree first) and make both consumers call it. tasks.title: ExpansionCache goes stale on edits inside a component
tasks.description: Found by the expander agent (AzXzQ, 2026-08-29), not fixed. EditableDocument's ExpansionCache is invalidated only for edits to a ref node or to a reusable component's ROOT (EditableDocument+Properties.swift, +CRDT, +Detach, +Overrides). An insert, delete or move inside a component, or a property edit on a component's descendant, leaves cached expandRef results stale. Exposure today: expandRef is used by detach and CRDT detach only (expandSubtree no longer reads the cache), so a detach after an in-component edit within one document lifetime can produce a stale clone. Fix: invalidate on any edit whose node has a reusable ancestor (walk parents to a componentRegistry member), with a regression test: edit a text node inside a component, then detach an instance, assert the detached clone carries the edit.
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main as 3919f94 (pushed), 2575 green. One rule (EditableDocument+ExpansionInvalidation.swift), before/after readings, wrapped at apply, applyMutation, deleteNode, detachRef and applyLocal's recovery; ExpansionCache's reverse index retired.

tasks.title: Honor a supplied node id on add; generate only what is omitted
tasks.description: Ruling 2026-08-29 (Ben): agents must not be required to generate node ids, but an id they DO pass is honored as long as it is unique within the document; an omitted id gets a fresh, non-colliding random code (5-char alphanumeric, like Jobs). Today BatchApplier+Create regenerates EVERY id in an added subtree via PenID.remapIDs(in:) and the docs say "do not invent ids — they are regenerated on insert" (WoodcaseEditor.md § Adding a subtree, CreatedNode.swift, PenSubtreeDecoder.swift, BatchOperation+Grammar.swift line ~48). Change the contract: on `add` (and `apply` add lines), keep a supplied id if it is unique in the document and not duplicated within the subtree; generate for omitted ids; a supplied id that collides is refused with EditingError.duplicateNodeID (its message already says "leave id out and let add generate one" — keep it and make it true). Internal refs within the subtree (a ref inside the subtree pointing at another node in the subtree, descendants keys) must still be remapped consistently for the ids that were generated. `cp` still regenerates every id (a copy must not collide with its source). Update the grammar text, CreatedNode/PenSubtreeDecoder doc comments, WoodcaseEditor.md's paragraph and `woodcase help design` NAMES/ADDRESSES if it mentions ids. Tests first: add with a unique supplied id keeps it; a colliding one is refused with the remedy; omitted ids are generated; cp regenerates.
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main as 20c5cbf (pushed), 2672 green. SubtreeIDPlan (keeping/regenerating); PenID.isValid (non-empty, no "/"); EditingError.invalidNodeID; BatchError.couldNotGenerateIDs retired; latent cp bug fixed (a copied instance kept pointing at the original component — remapIDs' mapping was never applied); document insert guard refuses intra-subtree duplicates. Docs: grammar, help design IDS block, WoodcaseEditor/Batches/CLI.

tasks.title: Release-only SIGTRAP in PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests: a Swift 6.3.3 -O miscompile of the test helper (was: CTFont freed early)
tasks.description:
Found by splitter (aZADN, 2026-08-30) the first time `swift test -c release` was
ever able to run. `PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance`
crashes the release test process deterministically with SIGTRAP — three for three,
and it takes the whole run down, so `swift test -c release --quiet` cannot go green
until it is fixed. Debug passes; the release `woodcase` binary is fine
(`scripts/perf-binary --config release` resolves fonts happily), because production
never deallocates the process-wide FontResolutionCache and this is a deinit-path
crash.

Faulting stack (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/swiftpm-testing-helper-2026-08-30-025215.ips),
EXC_BREAKPOINT on thread com.apple.root.default-qos.cooperative:

  __CFCheckCFInfoPACSignature        <- trap
  _CFRelease
  _DictionaryStorage.deinit
  _DictionaryStorage.__deallocating_deinit
  FontResolutionCache.__deallocating_deinit
  specialized PenTextMeasurerFontCacheTests.resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance()

So: releasing a `CTFont` out of `FontResolutionCache.fonts` finds an object whose CF
info word no longer signs — a freed or over-released CoreFoundation object.

What is known:

- Only that one test of the three crashes. `resolveFontDistinguishesKeys` (3 fonts,
  discarded immediately) and `hasWeightAxisMemoized` (5 resolutions, discarded) both
  pass in release. The crashing one is the only one that lets the CTFont *escape*
  `undisturbed`, so the same object is alive in the tuple and in the dictionary — one
  more live reference than the others hold.
- That shape says under-retain, not over-release: the object's real refcount reaches
  zero while Swift still holds references, and the dictionary's release is simply the
  one that finds the corpse.
- It is not the `===`. Replacing `#expect(fonts.0 === fonts.1)` with an
  `ObjectIdentifier` comparison still crashes, so swift-testing's expectation
  machinery is not implicated.
- Nothing in `Sources/Woodcase` does manual CF memory management — no `CFRetain`,
  `CFRelease`, `takeRetainedValue` or `Unmanaged` outside
  `PenIconFontRegistry`'s `Unmanaged<CFError>?` out-parameter.
- For "Helvetica"/normal/14 the returned font is the plain
  `CTFontCreateWithFontDescriptor` result: `hasWeightAxis` is false and
  `mapWeight("normal") == 0`, so `resolveFontThroughTheRegistry` returns `baseFont`
  unchanged. The value crosses `FontRegistryGate.withAccess<T>` and the test's own
  `undisturbed<T>` generic on its way out.

Reproduce:

    swift test -c release --filter resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance   # exit 1, SIGTRAP
    swift test -c release --filter resolveFontDistinguishesKeys       # exit 0
    swift test --filter resolveFontReturnsCachedInstance              # exit 0 (debug)

Next steps: run it under `MallocStackLogging`/`libgmalloc` or a zombie-detecting
allocator to catch the release that takes the CTFont to zero, and check whether an
unspecialized generic return of a CF-bridged value across
`FontRegistryGate.withAccess` loses a retain under `-O` (if so it is an upstream Swift
bug and wants a reduced case plus a local workaround). Do not "fix" it by weakening
the test: the object really is being freed early, and production would hit it the day
anything deallocates a FontResolutionCache.
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main as b6c54aa (pushed). Not a CTFont over-release: a Swift 6.3.3 -O (non-WMO) miscompile of the test helper's declared-but-unassigned var (unguarded DI destroy → swift_release on a CF object). Test helper rewritten; scripts/swift-di-miscompile checks the toolchain; finding in project/2026-08-30-release-only-ctfont-sigtrap.md. `swift test -c release --quiet`: 2685 green; debug: 2685 green + 1 intentional known issue.

tasks.title: cp into a component instance should turn nested props into overrides
tasks.description: Found while writing help recipes: once a node is common.reusable=true, `cp` makes a ref instance and any nested prop (Title/kind.content=X) is refused at exit 2 "is inside the component instance … run woodcase override instead"; the whole copy is abandoned. So cp --help's own example only works for a non-reusable source. Placing a component and setting its title is the single most common move; make `cp` translate a nested prop on an instance into the matching override (codec path → raw key, e.g. kind.content → content) in the same write, so the caller never needs the second vocabulary for the common case.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. cp resolves each nested --props address first and writes what the target takes: .node -> set, .instanceDescendant -> override, with paths rekeyed to the raw .pen vocabulary via NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed (kind.content -> content); raw keys pass through, so both vocabularies work. The recipes "component, then instance" example places and titles in one command and RecipesTests executes it.

tasks.title: A write to a ref node reports no changed artboard

tasks.title: Map thumbnails trickle in on first load of a many-artboard file

tasks.title: Remote image fills render blank: fetch and cache http(s) images
tasks.description:
Image fills whose url is an http(s) URL (e.g. Unsplash photos) render blank everywhere — serve, render, shot. PenRenderer.fileImageProvider resolves every url against the .pen's directory, so a remote URL becomes a nonsense file path and returns nil. Found reviewing the viewer on 2026-08-30 (Home artboard, two images.unsplash.com fills).

Build remote image support mirroring the GoogleFonts architecture: a prepare step that downloads remote image fills into a disk cache under {caches}/com.bensyverson.woodcase/images/, and an image provider that serves http(s) urls from that cache while keeping relative paths on the existing file path. Wire into RenderCache.prepare, RenderCommand and ShotCommand beside prepareFonts.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated from wt/remote-images as 2c00db0, pushed. Verified end to end: the two images.unsplash.com fills on artboard ydnjs render in the live serve (colored-pencil and bamboo photos visible in the Home Favorites cards); local ./images paths unchanged beside them. tasks.title: Fix selection and details for nodes inside component instances
tasks.description: Clicking an element inside an instance of a component selects nothing in the Outline, even though the Outline shows the component's whole tree. The same happens one level deeper — a component containing another component. And the Details pane sometimes rejects a real selection with "'224Gu/oqIX' names no node in this file". These look like one root cause — expansion id-paths ("Chi01/Lbl01") not agreeing between the render overlay, the outline rows, and the details endpoint. Two adjacent tab-state bugs live in the same files and belong here — when a node is selected the right pane shows Details but the Activity tab stays highlighted, and clicking the Details tab then LOSES the selection ("Select a node — in the outline or on the render — to see what it carries") while the node stays outlined on the render.
tasks.completion_note: Landed on main (squash of agent sel-tabs' branch; suite 3093 green at commit, one commit with lzM1z — the two leaves share ViewState/ViewerScript/PageBuilder). The brief's "one root cause" was two: (1) the outline never expanded instances while the render always draws expanded — fixed by deleting ViewState.expand and always passing expandInstances: true; (2) an instance root is spelled Card1/CardC by the expander but Card1 by the outline and resolver — fixed by ArtboardLayout.address(of:under:). Tab bugs were client-side: showTab now moves is-current and rewrites tab hrefs from location; syncSelectionTab moved into select() so keyboard selections move the tab. Finding: project/2026-08-30-instance-selection-ids.md. Adjacent unfixed: artboardIDs(containing:) ref-id miss (change pipeline, still open in gotchas).

Arrow keys/footer steps are now pushState + a five-piece swap from one destination-page fetch (#v-render-region, #v-outline, #v-right, #v-follow, .v-crumbs + title); voyage token drops stale fragment responses; popstate for a different artboard runs the same swap. Canvas-outside click clears selection. Map↔artboard stays a real navigation, deliberately. New gotcha: bfcache makes back-navigation reload-probes meaningless. Integration note for wave 3: the script selects nav.v-crumbs by class — Qe32p must keep that class or hand the script an id.

tasks.title: ActivityReader.follow test hung a full suite run once (await-forever, 0% CPU)
tasks.description: A full `swift test --quiet` run hung once at ~0% CPU for 18+ minutes (2026-08-30 ~18:20, main at 54d68f6 + the map glyph edit). Sample of swiftpm-testing-helper: main thread idle in its run loop, WebKit threads parked, footprint 222MB, and the only live Woodcase frames were two ActivityReader.follow(from:file:identity:pollInterval:) poll loops (ActivityReader.swift:201/208) — an await-forever in some activity/follow test, not the OOM or fontd patterns. Killed by pid; the immediate rerun passed 3072/3072 in 38s, so it is load- or timing-dependent, not deterministic. Earlier the same day FileWatcherTests' 30s waitUntil timed out under three parallel agent builds (passed in isolation). Sample saved during diagnosis; reproduce by running the suite under heavy parallel build load and watching for a run that outlives its normal few minutes at 0% CPU — scripts/soak-tests watchdogs this.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated, premise corrected: the sample's follow poll loops were the survivors, not the culprits — a suspended Swift task has no frames, so sample cannot show the wedged code. follow is now a value (ActivityReader.Follow, AsyncSequence): no producer task, polling is the consuming task, cancellation prompt; the dot-test race is rebound on consumed state; loaded soak 4/5 with only the known selection flake, no timeouts. The real wedge continues as issue 3uBxi (Network.framework HTTP seam), with two samples preserved and project/2026-08-31-follow-is-a-value.md carrying the finding.
