tasks.title: A bare serve never adopts a file first seen after startup
tasks.description: Found while starting the mobile-viewer dogfood run (2026-08-31): a bare `woodcase serve` adopts files from the activity log exactly once, at startup (ViewerServer.start -> ViewerFileIndex.adoptFilesFromLogs, documented "Called once at startup"), and FileWatcher.watch is handed that snapshot. ChangeCoordinator follows the log live for presence and re-renders, but no path inserts a new file into the index or the watch set — so a .pen file created after the server starts never appears on the dashboard and is never watched, even though the log names it. The dashboard's own doc says it serves "whatever the agents in this session have been editing"; an agent creating a file mid-session is that case exactly. Fix: when the followed log yields an event for a file the index does not know (and no files were named explicitly), insert it, watch it, warm it, and push the dashboard fragment over SSE. Regression test: start a bare serve, write a new file with `woodcase new` + one edit, expect it listed and its change events flowing.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. ViewerFileIndex.adopt(_:) is the live counterpart to the startup pass (refuses when files were named explicitly, already indexed, or missing on disk); ChangeCoordinator.logged adopts and welcomes — watch, fileChanged (invalidate/prepare/warm/attribute/broadcast), thumbnail warm — queueing the event before adoption so the announcing change is attributed. Both empty states carry data-empty-file so viewer.js reloads them; the dashboard's claimed-but-never-working reload on new files was found and fixed in the same pass.

tasks.title: A zero-artboard file page 404s as JSON instead of an empty state
tasks.description: Found during the mobile-viewer dogfood run (2026-08-31), seconds after `woodcase new`: navigating to a served file that has variables but zero top-level frames returns a raw JSON 404 — {"error": "File '1167717f1223' has no artboards; '' cannot be rendered.", "remedy": "GET /files/<id> lists this file's artboards"} — because the file page picks the first artboard to showcase and, with none, asks the render endpoint for the empty id. Two fixes: (1) the file page should render a real empty-state HTML page for a zero-artboard file — "No artboards yet — watching for changes", styled like the dashboard's empty state, and live-update in place when the first frame arrives over SSE; (2) the error text should never interpolate an empty id as '' — if the message can quote nothing, the branch above it chose the wrong response. This state is not exotic: every `woodcase new` passes through it, and an agent registering variables before frames sits in it for minutes.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. FileEmptyPage renders for a zero-artboard file (styled per DESIGN.md's empty atom, live-replaces itself when the first frame lands); ViewerError.noArtboards is its own case, unknownArtboard always has ids to offer, Route refuses an empty capture, and the four artboard lookups are one PreparedDocument.artboard(id:of:).

tasks.title: lint reports unresolved-variable for every $var in a ref override
tasks.description: Found by the kit agent in the mobile-viewer dogfood run (2026-08-31, leaf NrsX4): any $variable in a ref node's kind.rootOverrides or kind.descendants is reported by `woodcase lint` as unresolved-variable, though it resolves and renders correctly in both themes. Cause per the agent's read: DocumentLinter.Context.resolved falls back to the *authored* ref node for a ref row (Sources/Woodcase/Lint/DocumentLinter.swift:126), and variableReferences(in:) then walks the un-resolved override maps. Consequence: "instanced with overrides" and "every color rides theme variables" cannot both be lint-clean, which forced the kit into literal-hex identity overrides and blocks every design leaf whose criterion is lint-clean. Fix in the linter (resolve the ref's override maps, or check overrides against the document's variable table directly) with a regression test: a ref carrying a known $variable in an override lints clean; an unknown $typo in the same position is still a finding.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed by the lintfix agent, integrated as bec675d: DocumentLinter.Context now holds a second, unexpanded resolve of the document (shared indexer SettledTree.indexed) and reads a ref row settled -> unexpanded -> authored. Five regression tests (three genuinely red first; two true-positive guards green by design, said so honestly). Suite 3132 green on the merged result. Known remainder, deliberately out of scope: TreeView.walk has the identical authored fallback (TreeView.swift:161), so `tree --props fill` still prints $name unresolved on an instance — file separately if it bites.

tasks.title: Root-level add in an apply batch skips auto-placement despite the help
tasks.description: Found by the kit agent (2026-08-31, leaf NrsX4): root-level `add` operations inside an `apply` batch do not auto-place — all 16 kit atoms landed at 0,0 and lint returned 100+ artboard-overlap warnings — while the standalone `add`/`cp` verbs do auto-place with a margin. `apply --help` claims batch adds place like the verbs. Either make batch root adds run the same placement (probably right: nothing re-settles between lines today, so place at insert) or correct the help text; the mismatch costs a full re-layout pass on any generated batch.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated, with the premise corrected: batch and standalone adds share one path and both have auto-placed since b88e3a3. The real bug was reusable:true — placement and the write-time overlap warning measured through computeLayout(), which strips definitions, so components never placed and their collisions were invisible to the write while lint saw them. Both now read RootOverlap.roots(in:), the linter's own pipeline. Overlapping definitions now warn at write time — new behavior, intended.

tasks.title: shot cannot enlarge a small component for review
tasks.description: Found by the kit agent (2026-08-31, leaf NrsX4): `shot` has no --scale and --max never enlarges, so a 6-22pt component renders as a 6-22px PNG that no reviewer (human or vision model) can read. The agent's workaround was copying the file to scratch, instancing every atom into a contact-sheet frame, and upscaling outside woodcase. A --scale N flag (or letting --max upscale) makes atom review a one-command loop; the renderer already takes a scale internally for the map thumbnails' cap.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated in 9394777. shot --scale <multiplier> renders at an exact pixels-per-point ratio and enlarges; --max stays a cap and is overridden entirely by --scale. Validation rejects non-positive values at exit 2 with a message naming the fix. Docs: WoodcaseCLI.md option table, WoodcaseEditor.md example.

tasks.title: A literal rootOverrides key in a ref subtree is silently swallowed
tasks.description: Found by the core agent (2026-08-31, leaf SwMzf): writing a literal "rootOverrides" key in a ref subtree handed to add/apply is silently swallowed — PenNode+RefData's decoder sweeps every non-reserved top-level key into rootOverrides, so the key becomes an override NAMED rootOverrides patching a property no node has. It applies cleanly, `get` prints it back verbatim (confirming the mistake), and the node renders with the definition's values. Worse, `help schema ref` prints "kind.rootOverrides | rootOverrides | {key: value}" — the middle column claims a .pen key that does not exist. Fixes in priority order: (a) add/replace/apply REJECT a ref subtree containing a literal rootOverrides key, error naming the two working forms (inline top-level keys, or set kind.rootOverrides={...}); (b) fix the schema row to say the .pen form is inlined top-level keys; (c) consider get printing root overrides the way the file stores them so a read can be pasted back.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. (a) add/apply/replace refuse a ref subtree with a literal rootOverrides key, naming both working forms; (b) the schema's .pen-key column is typed (PenKeyForm) and prints "(top-level keys)" for root overrides, with --json emitting key: null; (c) needed no work — get already prints the node byte-identically to disk; the report of a get bug was get faithfully printing a node that (a) now prevents.

tasks.title: Duplicate node names are silent; lint should report them
tasks.description: Found by the nav agent (2026-08-31, leaf jts5k) in the four-writer session: two agents independently created nodes named FL-TopBar (Files vs Following prefixes). No write warned, no lint fired; the file silently gained an ambiguous address, discovered only by hand-scanning the tree. In a CLI whose contract is "names are addresses", a duplicate name is address-space corruption: make it a lint finding (name + both ids + both paths), and consider a warning on the write that creates the duplicate. The nav agent fixed theirs by renaming via #id (which is also the documented escape once ambiguity exists).
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. duplicate-name lint check (warning): one finding per node after the first occurrence, naming the shared name, both ids, both paths, and the #id escape; judged within the linted scope, matching artboard-overlap's choice. The write-time warning half was assessed by the lint agent as belonging to the write pipeline; no trivial hook surfaced, so it stays unbuilt — refile if duplicates keep arriving faster than lint catches them.

tasks.title: No way to put a literal $-prefixed string in text content
tasks.description: Found by the sheet agent (2026-08-31, leaf z5bOc): setting a text node's kind.content to the literal string "$v-muted" silently resolves it as a variable reference and renders the color's hex — there is no way to display a string that starts with $, and no warning that resolution happened. help schema text's "kind.content string | $string" is the only hint. Wanted: a documented escape (e.g. \$) honored by the resolver, and/or a diagnostic on set/apply: "content resolved $v-muted to a color — write \$v-muted for the literal". Bit an agent building a Details mock that wanted to SHOW a token name.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. PenValue<String> Codable honors \$name as the literal $name (decode strips, encode restores — inverses; the one lossy edge, a pre-existing literal \$ prefix, is pinned as an expected-value test). set warns on stderr without refusing when an unescaped $name resolves to a defined variable. Documented in PenValue's doc comment, the schema legend, and WoodcaseEditor.md. Pen.app compatibility gap (it renders the backslash literally) stated in the docs. The apply-side diagnostic ships separately with the write-pipeline merge via the agent's integration note: ContentVariableWarning.lines(properties:in:) folded into apply's warnings.

tasks.title: Readers disagree with the expander about a repointed nested ref (was: corrupts to 0x0)
tasks.description: Found by the activity agent (2026-08-31, leaf 0oHow), reproduced twice (qAXRH/fIyg4 and qAXRH/pZv2c in mobile-viewer.pen): using `override` to repoint a NESTED ref descendant's own `ref` property (e.g. flipping a Sheet's tab from TabPill to TabPill-Current) corrupts that descendant to 0x0 with `-` rects — and overriding it BACK to the original value does not recover it; only `override <node> ref=null` (clearing the key) does. Either repointing a nested instance's target should work (it is the natural way to express component variants), or the override should be rejected with an error naming the limitation; silently corrupting layout and not round-tripping is the worst of both. Regression test: override a nested ref's ref to a sibling component, expect either a settled render of the new target or a typed refusal; then restore and expect the original render.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated, with the premise corrected (title updated to match): nothing was corrupted — PenRefExpander always honoured the repoint and the render was right the whole time; four READERS recomputed the component from the authored store and disagreed (tree rects/children, expandedID, the address walk, the override guard). All now ask effectiveRefData(of:insideInstances:), which patches the authored ref with the enclosing instance's override the way the expander does. "Override back does not restore" did not reproduce. The deeper-than-one-level repoint is a silent no-op, parked in project/backlog.md with the honest fix sketched.

tasks.title: lint cannot express scroll intent; clipped findings force design changes
tasks.description: Reported independently by the nav agent (jts5k) and foreshadowed in the Jobs mobile-dashboard report (suggestion 5): lint's `clipped` warning cannot distinguish "cut off by mistake" from "this list scrolls past the fold", so a correct phone screen fails a lint-clean criterion and the agent redesigns to satisfy the linter (nav shrank thumbs 144->112 and dropped a scrolling-grid concept for it — the linter made a design decision). Wanted, one of: honor an explicit scroll intent on a frame (kind.scroll: "vertical" or similar), treat clip:true + content overflowing on exactly the scroll axis as intended, or at minimum lint severity/exclude filters (--exclude clipped, --severity error) so a gate can be expressed. The intentional-truncation idea from the Jobs report is the same family; solving scroll intent likely solves both.

tasks.title: lint takes no node scope; concurrent agents cannot ask if their frame is clean
tasks.description: Asked for independently by three of four design agents in the fan-out (jts5k, z5bOc, SwMzf implicitly via grepping frames out of shared output): lint is whole-file only, so under concurrent multi-agent editing each agent greps the shared findings list, gets false hits on name substrings (SwMzf matched MP-Cell-Immersive), and must justify other agents' findings in reports. `lint <file> <node>` matching every other read verb's signature (the library's findings(in:root:) already exists — the sheet agent nearly named it) makes "is MY frame clean" one command. The nav agent also wants duplicate-name reporting scoped the same way.
tasks.completion_note: Verified already implemented: `lint <file> <node>` matches the other read verbs (help shows the positional; `woodcase lint Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/banking.pen 'banking-home/status-bar'` exits 0 while the whole file has findings). The nav agent's wish — duplicate-name reporting scoped the same way — is folded into Gb9C7's brief for the issue sweep.

tasks.title: Premise guards and the divergence echo (was: subtree revision guards)
tasks.description: RESHAPED 2026-08-31 after design discussion with Ben: the original ask ("subtree revision guards") is superseded by project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md — read it before claiming any child. Two complementary mechanisms replace the subtree-rev idea: Merkle content hashes on every read with an opt-in --guard evaluated at transaction entry ("unchanged by anyone else since my read" — state-based, so touched-and-reverted passes, and a batch's own lines are exempt), and a divergence echo on every write (requested -> applied-as -> superseded, interpreted semantics, quiet on agreement) that also becomes the report channel if writes later route through the CRDT layer (see the spike child). The original finding text is preserved in this issue's history and in the DX report (project/2026-08-31-woodcase-concurrent-dx.md).

tasks.title: apply paper cuts: bare --props errors unhelpfully; @tag does not compose with a sub-path
tasks.description: Two apply paper cuts from the fan-out (2026-08-31): (1) nav agent — `tree <file> <node> --props` with no value dies with "Error: Missing value for '--props <props>'"; every other read defaults sensibly, so default to a useful column set or teach the fix in the error. (2) activity agent — a batch tag does not compose with a sub-path: {"target":"@row1/Uiko4"} is refused as "not a node address" while the identical suffix on the tag's resolved id works, forcing a two-pass batch (create, read ids back, then override) for any batch that creates an instance and dresses its descendants. Name paths created in the same batch DO resolve (nav used that heavily) — so either make @tag/child resolve the same way, or say in apply --help that tags are whole addresses and name paths are the composition mechanism.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. (1) tree --props bare defaults to kind.layout, kind.fill, kind.content, kind.fontSize via BareOptionValue argv fill-in (ruling on the leaf: it stays). (2) @tag/child composes: the tag seeds the same segment walk a path uses, instances included; NodeAddress.tag now carries a path.

tasks.title: An unattributed write skips the activity log entirely
tasks.description: Found by the integrator during the mobile-viewer run (2026-08-31): a woodcase write with no --as and no WOODCASE_AS mutates the document but appends NOTHING to .woodcase/activity.jsonl — verified by paired probes on mobile-viewer.pen (a set --as probe logs; the identical set without an identity bumps the revision and the log's tail is unchanged). Every unattributed write is therefore invisible to serve, follow mode, unread dots and history — ~22 integrator edits happened on a watched file while a live dashboard showed nothing. The design's own position is the opposite: ActorColor's `?` initial exists because "an unattributed write is a real state" that must render, not vanish. Log the event with an empty identity (the viewer already draws the ? disc), or refuse the write and demand an identity; silently forking history is the one wrong option. Regression test: a set with no identity produces exactly one activity event with identity "".
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. The gate was one line in ActivityRecorder.apply — an Optional<String> carrying both "who" and "whether to record". Unattributed writes now log under ActivityEvent.unattributed (""), apply returns non-optional, and the six doc sites that stated the old behavior as a reason were corrected. Regression test: a set with no identity produces exactly one event with identity "".

tasks.title: Merkle content hashes on every read
tasks.description: hash(node) = H(canonical props encoding, ordered child hashes), cached on the prepared document, recomputed along a write's spine. Surfaced as `hash` on every `tree --json` row and on `get`'s answer, beside the revision. Two processes reading identical state print identical hashes. WoodcaseEditor.md documents the pin. Design: project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as ede8705 (squash of the merkle agent's branch; full diff read as review; suite 3276 tests green, lint clean). Every tree --json row now carries the node's rev (= revision(of:), the existing Merkle hash per the design amendment — no new hash field); revision(of:) memoizes into RevisionCache with spine-scoped invalidation riding the renamed invalidatingCaches(touching:) choke point; WoodcaseEditor.md and EditingDocuments.md document the pin and its limit. Criteria: rows+get carry the token (yD0); cross-process agreement tested via two CLI processes (EGJ); spine-only movement tested at both TreeView and CLI level (mFB). The agent's brief-is-wrong answer surfaced a real design gap, noted on 2NW90: a ref's rev does not fold in its component definition, so a subtree pin passes over definition edits that change what the subtree renders.

tasks.title: --guard on writes, evaluated at transaction entry
tasks.description: Opt-in premise assertion: --guard <hash> on single write verbs, "guard" per apply line, scoped to the target or a named ancestor. Evaluated at file-lock entry so a batch's own earlier lines never trip a later line's guard. A failed guard names the node, both hashes, the intervening writers when the activity log knows them, and the next command. Unguarded behavior unchanged. Design: project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as 33b65e7 (squash of the sentry agent's branch; full 3068-line diff read as review; suite 3351 green, lint clean). Both halves landed. FOLD-IN: revision(of:) folds revision(of: refData.ref) into a ref's hash, PLUS every component a `ref` key in the ref's own descendants map repoints a nested ref at — the agent found the decision note's premise half wrong: the repoint itself is authored on the outer ref's props, but the component it points AT is never named by the authored payload, so without the extra fold an edit to the repointed-at component moved nothing (RevisionFoldTests.aRepointedInstanceCoversWhatItRenders proves all three legs). Cycles: a component already on the fold chain is cut, and a cut computation is NOT memoized, so every cached value is chain-independent — cached == from-scratch holds and is tested, including mutual recursion. Invalidation: whole-cache drop rides expansionCanDepend(on:) (before and after), provably the only condition a fold-in edge can move under; spine-scoped forgetting is kept for component-free edits. GUARDS: --guard <rev> / <node>=<rev> / document=<rev>, repeatable; per-line "guard" (bare, object, or array) in apply; one BatchGuard type crosses the seam; BatchApplier.checkGuards is the single entry gate called from applyOne and from ApplyCommand before apply — never inside perform, so a batch structurally cannot trip its own guards (uBq). A stale guard refuses the whole transaction, exit 3, naming node, both revs, the writer from the activity log over revisionCoverage (unattributed writes named as such), and the next command (yNV — including the fold-in case: a definition edit trips a frame guard). Unguarded writes byte-identical (2Zo, golden). Holes found and fixed: var/theme-axis lines silently ignored "guard" (now carried; bare ones refused naming the verb); --retry now checks only re-run lines. help design budget deliberately 60→70 (named constant with reason). Follow-up filed: duplicated instance query (EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:) vs BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:)).

tasks.title: The divergence echo on every write
tasks.description: Every write line reports requested -> applied-as -> superseded/dropped; agreement prints today's line, divergence prints the interpreted meaning (coercion, variable resolution, override of an unset property, structural consequence). --json carries the post-state node per line. Covers the silent-acceptance classes IAZIe and o8ahR's warning half (o8ahR's rejection half stays its own issue). Design: project/2026-08-31-guards-and-echo.md.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as db32eed (squash of the echo agent's branch; full diff read as review; suite 3316 green, lint clean). Every write line reports three-way (requested → applied-as → status); agreement prints byte-identical output, pinned by goldens (5Q2). Six divergence classes decided at the planner so single verbs and batch lines report identically: variableReference (widened from kind.content/set to every string-or-$variable property on set/override/cp), coercion, unsetOverrideProperty (both halves: unset-in-definition and no-room-in-type), overrideReplacesNode, rootPlacement, detachedInstances (tEm). --json carries the post-state node and divergences per applied line (MSt). ContentVariableWarning retired — one channel, stdout, one detector. TDD deviation honestly reported by the agent: divergence tests were first-run green; a sabotage run (divergences: [] at the seam) showed 9 issues with goldens staying green, so the tests bite. The agent's survey of uncovered silent consequences is in its worktree notes on this leaf; the sharpest finding (override values stored unvalidated → PenNodePatcher.merge silently drops the whole override on decode failure, including override --help's own example) is filed as its own issue.

tasks.title: Spike: what routing CLI writes through the CRDT layer costs

tasks.title: lint gains --exclude <check> and --severity <level> filters
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. lint --exclude <check-id> (repeatable) and --severity <level> filter findings before both the printed report and the exit-code decision; unknown values are rejected with the valid list (exit 2). Help carries the scrolling-screen worked example. This was the mechanical half of dN6XF; the scroll-intent design half is expVd.

tasks.title: metadata._scroll declares a designed scroll axis; lint honors and teaches it
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. common.metadata._scroll ("vertical"|"horizontal") declares the designed scroll axis; clipped honors it (same-axis silent, cross-axis trips), an unannotated stacking clip frame collapses same-axis overflow into one teaching finding whose set command merges existing metadata, and an invalid value warns. tasks.title: ViewerBrowserTests Escape-to-map timeout is probably the unread-dot race's twin
tasks.description: Found by the viewer agent (beacon) while baselining its leaves (2026-08-31): the full suite on unmodified 5a76473 failed roughly 4 of 5 runs, alternating between ViewerFollowBrowserTests.unreadDotUntilViewed and ViewerBrowserTests ("timed out waiting for Escape to go up to the map"). The unread-dot one was a real test race — the test navigated to the map immediately after a write, but the unread mark is recorded by whichever page hears the SSE change, so navigating first threw the news away and the map waited out its full 30s bound; it also never waited for the stream to reconnect after host.load. Fixed at vOJbc integration with two waitFors. The Escape timeout is untouched and probably the same shape — a wait that assumes an event already landed rather than waiting for it. Diagnose with the same method: find what records the state Escape's assertion reads, and waitFor the recording, not the effect.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as 0a08ea8 (squash of the sable agent's branch; diff read as review; suite 3276 green). The issue's premise was corrected by the agent: the race is not the unread-dot's twin (a JS-side recording race) but a navigation-correlation bug in the SleepyHollow test harness — PageHostDelegate.didFinish discards its WKNavigation argument and resumes whichever load is pending, so a click's late completion can settle a following host.load() while the old page still shows (verified in the checkout by the integrator). Fix: Bench.reload(_:until:_:attempts:) — navigate, wait for the target page's own content, re-issue if it never shows — applied to the flaking test and to clickingTheMapFocusesAnArtboard's identical shape. Loaded soak (5 runs, --load 2): zero occurrences of this flake. UPSTREAM: the real fix belongs in SleepyHollow (correlate the didFinish callback's WKNavigation with the in-flight navigation); surfaced to Ben. The soak also exposed three unrelated load flakes (WebViewTestHarnessTests uncaught-JS-error test, PenFileTransactionTests lock timeout under contention, FileWatcherTests heartbeat) — filed separately.

tasks.title: Full-suite 0%-CPU wedge with no live Woodcase frames: the Network.framework HTTP seam
tasks.description: The ActivityReader.follow rewrite (8kAHL) did NOT fix the intermittent full-suite wedge — it corrected the diagnosis. A Swift task suspended at an await has no thread and no stack frames, so `sample` cannot show the wedged code; the follow poll loops in the original sample were the survivors, not the culprits. Two further observations pin the new signature: (1) the activity agent's run on the REWRITTEN follow wedged with zero Woodcase frames and a live com.apple.network.connections queue; (2) the integrator's suite run on the main checkout (token's staged merge, no viewer changes at all) wedged the same way — 27 min elapsed, 86MB footprint, ~0% CPU, sample showing live Network.framework/CFNetwork and no live Woodcase frames (sample: scratchpad/wedge-46108-sample.txt, session 1319dbb0). Lead: HTTPServer/HTTPConnection both await a withCheckedContinuation on a Network.framework state handler; gotchas.md already records an un-root-caused NWListener EINVAL on the same seam. Diagnose there; the signature is the ABSENCE of our frames plus a live network queue. Reproduce by running the full suite under multi-agent build load.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as cc7b4f3 (squash of the wedge agent's branch; full diff read as review; suite 3289 green; loaded soak on the MERGED tree 2/2 at --load 6 --timeout 280, zero wedges — plus the agent's own 8/8). Root cause (best-supported; the finding project/2026-08-31-the-await-that-cannot-resume.md marks proven vs not): the viewer's three socket awaits were unbounded and uncancellable; the listener handler swallowed .waiting (retried forever, unreachable by stop()); and SSEHub's in-actor sends meant one non-reading peer held the hub and every stop(). All three now go through ResumeOnce (callback or 30 s deadline, exactly once, expiry released on answer); HTTPServer.outcome(of:) classifies every listener state with no default; an abandoned write drops the client and says so on stderr. Reproduction is now on demand: scripts/soak-tests 2 <log> --load 6 --timeout 280 — CONTENTION, not multi-agent load. Bonus: the 2026-08-30 NWListener EINVAL gotcha was root-caused and was mis-documented — a listener with no newConnectionHandler fails EINVAL; scripts/probe-network-seam.swift reproduces it. CORRECTIONS to this issue's own text, recorded in the finding: the 46108 sample has NO network queue (it is the follow-poll-loop host); the network queue belonged to the other sample (pid 48269). The fresh sample is preserved at local/wedge-samples/2026-08-31-wedge-load6-run1-55807.txt. Not proven: that the observed wedge was one of these three awaits — but they were the only unbounded awaits in the process, and if it returns, the typed errors and stderr line give the next reader a name instead of an empty sample.

tasks.title: Concurrent overrides of different descendants on one instance clobber each other (kind.descendants is one LWW register)
tasks.description: Found by spike aPPZS (2026-08-31, note on that leaf) and verified in source by the integrator: `CRDTDocument.processLocalOverrideDescendant` (Sources/Woodcase/Sync/CRDTDocument+LocalProcessing.swift:269-276) merges an override into the ref's `descendants` map and delegates to `processLocalUpdateKind`, which diffs the whole map to the single path "kind.descendants" (PropertyDiff.swift:237) — one LWW register. Two peers concurrently overriding *different descendants of the same instance* therefore do not merge: the later timestamp wins the entire map and the earlier peer's overrides vanish silently. That was 45% of the four-writer run's traffic (211 of 472 events were overrides), and Penumbra's day-one multiplayer hits it regardless of whether CLI writes ever route through the CRDT layer. The existing test only asserts convergence, not survival: CRDTOverrideConvergenceTests.concurrentOverridesLWW checks refA.descendants == refB.descendants, and no test covers two different descendants. Fix direction (from the spike): per-descendant property paths — kind.descendants.<id>.<prop> — so each descendant override gets its own register; concurrent writes to the same descendant+property stay LWW. TDD: start with a red test where peer A overrides Tab01 and peer B overrides Tab02 on the same instance concurrently, exchange ops, and assert BOTH survive on both peers.

tasks.title: Three load-shaped flakes outside the browser suites, found by vvxHi's soak
tasks.description: Found by the sable agent's loaded soak while fixing vvxHi (scripts/soak-tests 5 <log> --load 2 --timeout 400, 2026-08-31, sibling agents building): 3 of 5 runs failed, none on the browser suites — three previously unrecorded load-shaped flakes elsewhere: (1) WebViewTestHarnessTests "Surfaces an uncaught JavaScript error rather than timing out"; (2) PenFileTransactionTests lock timeout under contention; (3) FileWatcherTests heartbeat/watch timing via ViewerFixtures.swift:85. Not investigated further — out of vvxHi's scope. Diagnose with the same discipline as the other timing gotchas: assert the observable outcome, bound waits at "not hung" scale, and remember wall-clock assertions are unreliable in the parallel suite (gotchas.md). A stability claim needs a loaded soak. Note: (2) may be another instance of the already-recorded PenFileTransaction wall-clock gotcha rather than a new bug — check that entry first.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed in 4007571 (agent fenwick, Opus). All three diagnosed from vvxHi's own soak logs at the same HEAD; none was a product bug — all were budgets set at machine-load scale, plus one real helper hole. (1) WebView harness test's 5 s render budget spent by load before the typed error could be judged → named WebViewTestHarness.defaultBudget (60 s). (2) PenFileTransaction contention tests' 10 s lock timeout gave the waiter ~one flock attempt under late-resuming sleeps → 60 s lockBudget; NOT the recorded wall-clock gotcha (that one is heldLockTimesOut, which passed) — the gotchas entry now covers budgets as well as assertions. (3) waitUntil checked the deadline before the condition and never looked again after the loop, so a late-resuming poll reported timeouts nothing earned (this also covered the SSEHubTests heartbeat failure — the leaf title's "FileWatcher heartbeat" conflated two suites); it now evaluates once more past the deadline, defaults to a 60 s waitBudget, and returns whether the condition held. Red-first unit test: WaitUntilTests.alreadyTrueHoldsAtASpentBound. Verified: full suite 3368 green post-merge; loaded soak `scripts/soak-tests 5 <log> --load 2 --timeout 400` 5/5 (machine loaded, load avg 13–15) vs 2/5 on base 33b65e7. Finding: project/2026-08-31-load-shaped-budgets.md.

tasks.title: Override values are stored unvalidated; a failing patch decode silently drops the whole override
tasks.description: Found by the echo agent (pjupK, 2026-08-31): override values are stored unvalidated, and at expansion PenNodePatcher.merge decodes the patched JSON and returns the node UNCHANGED when the decode fails — so the whole override is silently dropped. The literal example in `override --help` triggers it: `woodcase override design.pen Orders/Value content=42` stores `content: 42`; a text node's content is `string | $string`, the decode fails, and the override does nothing while `get` confirms the stored key back forever. Related, same surface: the `override` verb does not rekey its properties — BatchApplier+Plan.planOverride passes op.props through verbatim (only `cp --descendant-props` calls NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed), so `override X kind.content=…` stores a literal `kind.content` key nothing reads. Both are now REPORTED by the divergence echo (db32eed) — the unsetOverrideProperty divergence names the dead key — but reporting a silently-dropped write is the floor, not the fix. Fix direction: run override values through NodePropertyCodec coercion the way `set` does (which also lets the coercion divergence fire on overrides), and rekey property-path keys in planOverride; then a patch that still fails to decode should refuse loudly rather than merge-and-drop. TDD: start red with override --help's own example asserting the override applies (content becomes "42") or refuses — either is honest; silent drop is not.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed in d893dd0 (agent quill, Opus; integrated and suite-verified at 3365 green). `override` now translates property-path keys through NodePropertyCodec.rawKeyed (per the rekey ruling noted on this leaf), coerces values the way `set` does (the coercion divergence fires on overrides), and refuses a value the patched node cannot decode with the new EditingError.overrideValueRejected — judged with the expander's own merge via the new throwing PenNodePatcher.patched(_:with:). The refusal is at the WRITE, not at expansion: expansion stays tolerant because Woodcase renders files it did not write (house precedent: validateOverrideTarget). The help example (`content=42`) now stores "42" and echoes the coercion. Docs updated in WoodcaseEditor.md, WoodcaseCLI.md, WoodcaseBatches.md, EditingDocuments.md. Follow-up filed: lint has no rule for an override already in a file that the merge will drop (import or Pen.app-written); the write path can no longer create one.

tasks.title: One instance-of-component query exists twice (EditableDocument and BatchApplier)
tasks.description: Noticed by the sentry agent during 2NW90 (2026-08-31): the "every ref pointing at this component" query exists twice — EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:) (EditableDocument+Guards.swift, sorted by name path) and BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:) (sorted by id). Two implementations of one question drift; fold them into one (the EditableDocument one is the natural home; BatchApplier's caller decides its own ordering). Small, mechanical, Sonnet-sized; touches EditableDocument+Guards.swift and the BatchApplier plan path plus their tests.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed in d893dd0 (agent quill, same commit as hTeBC — same file surface). BatchApplier.instanceIDs(of:in:) deleted; its one caller (planRemove's --detach) now uses EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:). No test named the deleted method. Visible difference: the survivor sorts by full name path rather than id, so the detachedInstances divergence now reads in document order — an improvement, matching every other list the document prints. Bonus dedup in the same commit: CopyCommand's rawKeyed call removed since the planner now rekeys every override.

tasks.title: lint: an override already in a file that the merge will drop is reported by nothing
tasks.description: Found by the quill agent during hTeBC (2026-08-31): since d893dd0 the write path refuses an override value the patched node cannot decode, but an override *already in a file* that the merge will drop — from an import, or a Pen.app-written file — is still silent: PenNodePatcher.patchNode falls back to the unpatched node by design (expansion stays tolerant), and nothing tells the user the override in their file never draws. The linter is the only thing positioned to say so. Fix direction: a DocumentLinter rule that walks every ref's descendants map, runs each non-replacement entry through PenNodePatcher.patched (the throwing variant added in d893dd0) against patchedDefinitionNode, and reports the key, the node path, and the shape mismatch using the same expected/actual wording as EditingError.overrideValueRejected. Skip refs whose component is not in the registry, and entries carrying a type key, matching validateOverrideValues' exemptions.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed in f18fe15 (agent marlin, Sonnet; integrated, suite 3377 green, pushed). Three new lint checks read the write path's own guards back over a ref's stored descendants map, without expanding the instance (same seam as unresolved-variable): override-value-rejected (per-key judgment via the throwing PenNodePatcher.patched, so one bad key doesn't hide the rest — deliberately not validateOverrideValues, which short-circuits), override-target-not-found (reuses validateOverrideTarget verbatim), and override-key-unread (a dotted `kind.content` key decodes as a harmless unknown field, so no merge judgment can catch it; the check reads the key prefix directly — a case the original issue's fix direction missed). Object replacements and unresolved-import refs are exempt, matching the write guard; unresolved refs still report as broken-ref. Docs: WoodcaseLint.md gained an "Overrides a file already carries" section; LintCommand help and WoodcaseEditor.md updated. All three are errors, same reasoning as the write-time refusal.

data.title: Teach the CLI what it already does (Quill DX follow-up)
data.description: The Quill mobile run (project/2026-09-01-quill-mobile-agents-dx.md) built a 1,850-node design system and four Python generators. An audit found the costliest problems were teaching failures: a false divergence message denied slot filling that works, and the answers agents needed were in DocC where agents never look. This tree fixes the real bugs, adds the few features that delete agent code, and moves the curriculum to the CLI surface. Design: project/2026-09-02-teach-the-cli-what-it-does.md. Strict TDD on every leaf; a doc leaf carries help-text snapshot tests where they exist.

data.title: Slot filling honoured end to end
data.description: The divergence check (BatchApplier+Divergence.swift:186) reports "the override is stored but nothing will read it" for a `children` override on a slot frame, because its accepted-key list omits `children` while PenNodePatcher.swift:90 honours it. Make the check agree with the patcher. Demote the "does not set X in Component — the override adds the property" divergence to an informational line: adding `enabled`/`opacity` is the sanctioned variant idiom. `tree --expand` must render the children an instance injects into a slot frame; `lint` must not report `empty-fit-content` on a definition's `kind.slot` frame. Regression tests first for all four. Design: project/2026-09-02-teach-the-cli-what-it-does.md §A1.

criteria.label: A children override on a slot frame prints no divergence and the patched tree renders the injected children
An override that adds enabled or opacity to a descendant prints an informational line, not a divergence
tree --expand prints the injected slot children under the instance
lint reports no empty-fit-content on a definition's slot frame

data.title: One font path for every verb
data.description: Only shot, render and the viewer call GoogleFontResolver.prepareFonts, so tree and lint measure text in SF Pro even when the font is cached on disk (D1: tree and shot disagree on text metrics). The resolver already emits "Font 'X' could not be resolved; will fall back" (GoogleFontResolver.swift:107) but ShotCommand.swift:272 passes no collector (D2). Prepare fonts on tree and lint before measuring, pass the collector on every verb so the warning reaches stderr, and if a read is offline say so on stderr rather than report a measurement in a face the render will not use. Test with a fixture whose font is disk-cached and one whose font cannot resolve. Design §A2.

criteria.label: tree and shot report the same text width for a Google-font fixture with the font cached
Every verb prints the fallback warning on stderr when a font cannot resolve
A measurement taken in a fallback face is labelled as such

data.title: Batch parity with the single-node verbs
data.description: The apply `cp` op puts op.props straight into setProperties (BatchApplier+Create.swift:117) and so refuses path-keyed overrides the cp verb splits (CopyCommand.swift:102, 332) — D3. A batch `add` rejects "parent":"document" (BatchOperation+Codable.swift:75) although AddressArgument maps it to nil and help design teaches it — D4. apply takes no --guard on argv though every other write does (§9.4). -F /dev/null fails because FileManager.contents returns nil for a char device (ApplyCommand.swift:188) — D19. Fix all four so the op and the verb share one assignment path. Design §A3.

data.title: Override messages and --unset
data.description: `override x=null` writes a null instead of removing the override, and valueRules says "clears the property" generically (PropertyAssignment.swift:56) — §9.3. Add `override --unset <key>` and invert the warning: warn when the definition sets the key (destructive), stay quiet when it does not (no-op). The near miss for a step-skipping name path into an instance offers the definition's own copy; say instead that a path into an instance names every frame of the definition's tree and suggest the instance path — D7. Design §A4.

data.title: Small CLI fixes
data.description: --version on the root command (CommandConfiguration sets none, D18). Flush stdout before TreeCommand.warnAboutEmptyColumns writes its stderr advisory so the two streams do not interleave inside a table (D17; the report misdiagnosed this as a wrong stream). data.title: Lint calibration — sibling duplicates and text overflow
data.description: duplicate-name (DocumentLinter+DuplicateNames.swift) flags every same-named pair in scope, but the resolver lets an address start at any node, so only same-named siblings defeat every name path. Scope the check to siblings; the finding's advice stays. Add a `text-overflow` check: a text node with fixed width/height whose measured content does not fit renders nothing silently (D8; PenLayoutEngine.swift:675 skips measurement, PenTextRenderer.swift:62 drops lines that do not fit). Design §A6 and the duplicate-name decision.

data.title: tree --absolute
data.description: tree rects are parent-relative (gotchas.md "PenLayoutEngine rects are parent-relative") while shot uses PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects (ShotCommand.swift:283); three agents re-derived absolute coordinates by walking parents (D13). Add --absolute to the text form and an absRect key to --json rows, from the same function shot uses. Document the convention in tree --help. Design §B1.

data.title: shot --json rects and --crop
data.description: shot --json carries only the root rect; --outline targets and the drawn rects are not reported, so an agent cannot locate what it sees (D9's real ask). Return every rect drawn, outline targets included, in the node's own coordinate space with the existing point = (pixel − gutter)/scale + origin contract. Add --crop x,y,w,h in that same space so a tall board can be tiled for a vision model. Add one help sentence: pass the model's edge limit as --max and use the printed pixels= to decide whether to tile. Default scale is unchanged. Design §B2 and the shot decision.

data.title: cp --each
data.description: cp --times N substitutes {n} into root and descendant path props (CopyCommand.swift:73, 254) but cannot vary content per copy, so all four agents wrote generators for rows with per-item payloads (~300 lines; report §1.2 #1). Add --each <rows.jsonl>: one copy per row, keys are exactly the argv keys cp takes (common.name, Chip/kind.fills, Name/kind.content), {n} still substituted, --at placement as today. No --bind or template syntax. The batch cp op gains the same field. Design §B3 and the --each decision.

data.title: Metadata deep keys and _props in the editing verbs
data.description: common.metadata is a whole-object property, so `set … common.metadata='{"_role":"button"}'` drops _props and every other key (WoodcaseLint.md warns about this). Add common.metadata.<key>=<value> as a merge of one key, and --unset for one key. Codegen already reads common.metadata._props as prop name → descendant name path (ComponentAnalyzer.swift:236); make override and cp --each accept a declared prop name as a key, resolved through the component's _props, and make `get <definition>` print the _props as its parameter list. This is the named-parameter concept the detail A agent asked for; nothing new enters the format. Design: the _props decision and §B4.

data.title: --dry-run on the write verbs
data.description: Asked in both DX runs (2026-08-31 #2, D15). On add, apply, cp, rm, set and override: run the transaction to the point of settling, print what the real write would print including divergences and the post-state tree, run lint on the result, and roll back without touching the file or the activity log. Last in the tree because every earlier leaf changes what it prints. Design §B7.

data.title: help design and the verb help
data.description: The curriculum, at the surface agents actually read. help design gains: naming (short names unique among siblings; an address may start at any unique ancestor; the ambiguity error names the fix); components (overrides are keyed by the definition's child ids, so renaming children is free and replace on a live definition drops overrides it does not carry forward; enabled=false on an instance descendant is the variant mechanism; a ref may be written inline in an add subtree; a slot frame's children are replaced from the instance); values (kind.lineHeight is a multiple of fontSize; \$ escapes a literal $); reads (get --expand is the bulk content read; --props takes a comma list; rects are parent-relative unless --absolute); the loop (activity is step four; undo is per writer; a guard suits a short structural batch, not a session-long gate); and a "see also <verb> --help" foot. replace --help stops promising overrides survive; override --help and add --help carry the examples; schema's lineHeight row says multiplier. help recipes gains a slot-filling and a cp --each recipe. WoodcaseEditor.md moves in step. Every claim here must already be true in the code, which is why this leaf is blocked on the others. Design §C1.

criteria.label: help design covers naming, id-keyed overrides, variants, inline refs, slot filling, lineHeight, the $ escape, get --expand, coordinates and the loop
replace --help states that id-keyed overrides the new definition does not carry are dropped
help recipes has a worked slot-filling example that runs clean against a fixture
WoodcaseEditor.md matches help design on every point above

data.text:
Done on wt/shot. All three criteria met.

aU2 — `shot --json` gains `rects`: the rendered node first (its OWN rect, not the crop),
then one entry per --outline in flag order. Each is {role, id, address, name, rect} in
the rendered node's own coordinate space. New type ShotRect.

HNC — `--crop x,y,w,h` (ShotCrop) renders exactly that sub-rectangle, in the node's own
space, and becomes the printed `rect=`, so point = (pixel − gutter)/scale + origin needs
no second form. --max/--scale size the crop. --outline is judged against the crop. A crop
that runs off the node is refused (exit 2) naming the node's rect and the largest crop
that fits at the same origin.

tOu — help + DocC: pass the vision model's edge limit as --max, read pixels= to decide
whether to tile, tile with --crop. Default scale unchanged.

Rendering: the crop needed an origin the library's sizing entry point does not take, so
ShotRegionRenderer drives PenRenderer.render(_:layoutRects:into:rootNodeID:…) — the
documented "caller manages positioning" seam — with the same transform and the region's
origin substituted. Uncropped runs go through the same path and are byte-identical
(ShotOverlaySnapshotTests unchanged and green). No library change was needed.

NHPFAN's one-liner is included: ShotCommand now builds a PenDiagnosticCollector, passes
it to prepareFonts AND prepareImages, and writes it to stderr. Verified end to end:
a copy of banking.pen with fontFamily "Zzz Not A Font" now prints
  warning: [fontResolution] Font 'Zzz Not A Font' could not be resolved; will fall back to SF Pro
on stderr, exit 0, stdout unchanged.

Design point for the integrator: crop coordinates are in the node's OWN space, so a
top-level artboard at (3053, -10) is cropped as `--crop 3053,-10,402,300`, not
`--crop 0,0,402,300`. That is what "the same space rect= uses" means and it keeps one
mapping formula, but it is a real surprise; the refusal names the node's rect and the
help says which space, and there is a test pinning it. Flagging in case a
node-relative crop is preferred.

swift test --quiet: 3392 tests, 346 suites, passed. swiftformat . --lint --config
.swiftformat: 0/817 need formatting. (Sandbox off for both; the worktree lives under a
dot-directory so --config must be passed explicitly or zero files are checked.)

Done on wt/lint (not committed).

duplicate-name is now sibling-scoped. `duplicateNames(rows:)` keys the first-seen map by
(parent id, name), reading the parent off the listing's own depth stack, so document roots are
siblings of one another. The finding says "sibling", and closes by teaching that a same-named
cousin is fine because an address may start one segment higher. The file's doc comment now says
plainly that the old document-wide argument was wrong (not merely wider) and why it cost work,
with the same correction as a blockquote in WoodcaseLint.md's Names section.

New check `text-overflow` (warning) in Sources/Woodcase/Lint/DocumentLinter+TextOverflow.swift.
A text node whose box cannot grow — `fixed-width-height` growth, or any height that is not
fit_content — is re-measured at its settled width with PenLayoutEngine.defaultTextMeasurer; an
overflow past TreeRow.clipTolerance is a finding naming the height needed, the box, the overflow
in points, and both remedies (`kind.height=<n>`, or `kind.height=fit_content` plus
`kind.textGrowth=fixed-width` when the growth is what blocks measurement). Only height is asked:
the renderer wraps at the box width, so width alone cannot overflow. Zero-width boxes are
skipped.

Verified the premise by rendering: a 16pt text in a 12pt-tall box draws NOTHING (the whole line
is dropped), so D8 is real and the check is a true positive, not a cosmetic one.

The check immediately found the same latent bug in 8 of the repo's own lint fixtures
(Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/lint/*.pen): a label `width 40, height 12` with the default 16pt
font, which needs 19pt. Four "…-clean.pen" tests were asserting an empty finding list over a file
that renders no text at all. Raised those labels to height 20 (and the one enclosing frame in
ref-nested-instance-clean.pen). That is the honest fix — the fixtures meant to be clean.

`swift test --quiet` and `swiftformat . --config .swiftformat --lint` both pass, sandbox off.

Done on wt/lint (not committed).

`get <definition> --instances` lists every ref whose target is the definition.

  $ woodcase get instances.pen Chip --instances
  Cmp01  Chip  rev 87128dd18c3403ad  3 instances
  Board/Zeta     Zta01  rev f9da102d4b4ff4e1
  Board/Alpha    Alp01  rev a7161c4cca9b6ff9
  Second/Middle  Mid01  rev 3817955ae95ea769

Header line is byte-identical in shape to a plain `get`'s, with the count appended; rows are the
aligned two-space style `tree` uses. `--json` is
{"definition":{id,address,rev},"instances":[{id,address,rev}]}. Zero instances prints the header
alone ending "no instances" at exit 0 — never a blank answer. A non-reusable node is refused at
exit 2, naming `woodcase tree` as the next command; `--instances --expand` is refused rather than
silently ignoring one flag.

Seams touched beyond GetCommand.swift:
- EditableDocument.instanceIDs(ofComponent:) made public (it was internal, so CommandCore could
  not call it). One word plus a doc line saying why.
- Document order: instanceIDs sorts by name path, which is not document order. Promoted the
  private documentOrderNodeIDs() from EditableDocument+VariableReferences.swift to a public
  EditableDocument.nodeIDsInDocumentOrder() in its own file, and pointed the old caller at it, so
  "document order over the flat store" has one definition instead of a copy in a CLI adapter.

New fixture Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/instances.pen, deliberately shaped so document order
(Zeta, Alpha, Middle) differs from instanceIDs' name-path order (Alpha, Zeta, Middle), and with a
second component and an uninstanced one.

`swift test --quiet` and `swiftformat . --config .swiftformat --lint` both pass, sandbox off.

One font path for every verb — done on wt/reads.

The seam: `SettledTree` is the one place a read settles a document (TreeView.rows,
DocumentLinter.findings and RootOverlap all go through it, and every write verb that
prints a settled tree afterwards goes through TreeView). It now calls a new
`GoogleFontResolver.prepareCachedFonts(for:diagnostics:)` before `PenLayoutEngine.layout`,
so `tree`, `lint`, `get`, `set`, `add`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `override` and `apply` all
measure in the faces `shot` and `render` draw with.

`prepareCachedFonts` is the resolver's chain with step 3 (the GitHub download) removed:
system faces and the on-disk cache, synchronous, never a network call. That keeps
`lint`'s documented "stays offline" promise and stops a read hanging behind a captive
portal, which is what §A2 asked for ("if a read must stay offline, it says so").

DEVIATION from the brief: the warning does **not** go through a `PenDiagnosticCollector`
plumbed from the verbs. One rule instead, on the resolver: the warning goes to the
collector when the caller passes one, and to standard error when it does not — never
both. Reasons: (1) the collector would have to be threaded through
`SettledTree` → `TreeView.rows` → `DocumentLinter.findings` and every verb, for a
message whose only destination is stderr; (2) lint already holds a collector, and
feeding font warnings into it would turn "not installed on this machine" into a lint
*finding*, which `lint --help` explicitly disclaims; (3) it gives `shot` the warning
today without touching ShotCommand.swift. The library already writes to stderr this way
in two places (GoogleFontResolver's cache-fallback notice, RemoteImageResolver's) —
those now share the new `StandardErrorLine` helper.

Criteria:
- l5w: `GoogleFontResolverTests.cachedFontRegistersWithCoreText` now measures the same
  document before and after the cached TTF registers and asserts the width *changes* —
  that is the whole of D1. It had to go there rather than in a new suite: CoreText
  registration is process-global and irreversible, so exactly one test per run may watch
  a family go from absent to present, and a second one racing it is what turned that
  test red the first time I tried.
- rnV: `FontFallbackWarningTests` drives the binary — `tree`, `lint` and `set` each print
  one line for `font-missing.pen`, stdout untouched, exit 0.
- rLo: the line names the family *and* the face: `font "X" is not installed and not in
  the font cache; text in it is measured in SF Pro. Run \`woodcase render\` or
  \`woodcase shot\` once to download it.`

Two things worth knowing:
- A cache miss on the read path is deliberately not recorded in `resolvedFamilies`, so a
  `render` later in the same process can still fetch the font. Pinned by a test.
- `placedFamilies` memoises the confirmed-available answer, because
  `PenTextMeasurer.fontFamilyAvailable` is a blocking XPC round trip to `fontd` and a
  settle happens on every CLI invocation and every viewer edit. Misses are not
  memoised — a render may place the family at any moment.

Integration note for the shot leaf: ShotCommand.swift:272 can now pass a collector or
not. If it stays `await GoogleFontResolver.shared.prepareFonts(for: document)`, `shot`
already gets the fallback line on stderr. If the shot agent wants it collected instead,
the line is:

    await GoogleFontResolver.shared.prepareFonts(for: document, diagnostics: diagnostics)

and it must then print the collector itself, because passing one suppresses the stderr
line.

Docs: PenGoogleFonts.md gained "Reads take the offline half"; WoodcaseEditor.md gained
"Fonts, and a width you should not trust".

tree --absolute — done on wt/reads.

`SettledTree` now carries `absoluteRects` beside `rects`, composed by
`PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects(under:in:layoutRects:)` — the walk `shot --outline` and
the viewer's overlay already share — run once per root node and merged. `TreeRow` gained
`absRect`, `TreeView` fills it from the same key it uses for `rect` (so an expanded
instance descendant gets one too), and `TreeFormatter.text(_:properties:absolute:)`
swaps the rect column.

CLI: `tree --absolute`. Two teaching details beyond the brief:
- the header line gains `  absolute` (`rev X  9 rows  absolute`), because a saved outline
  outlives the command line that produced it and the two forms are indistinguishable on
  a top-level node;
- with `--props`, the column header reads `absRect` rather than `rect`.
Say so if either is unwanted; both are one line to remove.

`--json` carries both on every row with no flag, as asked.

Criteria:
- hYm: `TreeAbsoluteCommandTests.absRectAgreesWithShot` parses `shot`'s own
  `rect=x,y,w,h` for a top-level node and compares it to that row's `absRect`;
  `TreeAbsoluteRectTests.absRectMatchesShotsOwnWalk` does the library-level comparison
  against `PenLayoutEngine.absoluteRects` for every row of `layout-deep-nesting.pen`.
- FUD: `--absolute` prints `209,24 30×20` for the leaf whose parent-relative rect is
  `0,0 30×20`.

TreeView.swift was touched, but only the two lines that add the rect field — the expand
path is untouched, as the brief asked.

Docs: `tree --help` gains a COORDINATES paragraph; WoodcaseEditor.md's "Read" section
gains "Coordinates are parent-relative" with a worked `--absolute` example.

One cost worth naming: `absoluteRects` finds its root with a pre-order search of the
whole forest, so composing N roots is O(N × nodes). woodcase-app.pen is 37 roots over 392
nodes and it does not show up in the profile (tree total 449.8 ms, unchanged), but a
document with hundreds of roots would want an overload that takes the root node rather
than its id.

Small CLI fixes — done on wt/reads.

(a) e7r — `woodcase --version`. New `Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/WoodcaseVersion.swift`:
    `current = "0.1.0"` plus `line`, which appends the .pen format read from
    `PenFormatVersion.current` — so the format half cannot drift from what the writer
    emits, and `woodcase --version | cut -d' ' -f1` is the bare version.

        $ woodcase --version
        0.1.0 (.pen 2.17)

    HOW IT STAYS CURRENT: by hand, in the commit that tags a release — the doc comment
    says so in one sentence. SwiftPM does not hand a package its own version at build
    time (a tag is a property of the repository, not the source), and this repo has no
    tags at all yet, so there is nothing to derive it from. Deriving it from `git
    describe` at build time would make the number depend on whether the consumer built
    from a checkout, which is worse than a constant somebody has to move. If a release
    script appears later, that script is the right place to bump it.

    Note for whoever writes CommandConfiguration next: `version:` must be passed *after*
    `discussion:` — ArgumentParser's initialiser is order-sensitive and the compiler's
    message ("argument 'discussion' must precede argument 'version'") does not say why.

(b) Gzy — the flush. `StandardError.write` now delegates to a new library helper
    `Woodcase.StandardErrorLine.write`, which `fflush(stdout)`s first. One
    implementation for both halves of the package: `GoogleFontResolver` and
    `RemoteImageResolver` already wrote to fd 2 directly and now go through it too, so
    the ordering rule cannot hold on one side and not the other.
    `StreamOrderingTests` runs the binary with both streams pointed at one file — the
    only arrangement where the bug is visible — and asserts the `--props` advisory is
    the last line, after a whole 11-line report.

(c) 8jx — the `.gitignore` line. `ActivityLog.ignoreInRepository` now checks
    `addIfMissing`'s return value and, when it changed the file, writes:

        woodcase: added ".woodcase/" to /path/.gitignore — the activity log is local state, not history.

    Silent when it changed nothing, so a second write says nothing (pinned by a test).

Nothing here changed stdout for any verb.

slots: A1 done on wt/slots. All four criteria met; full suite (3400 tests) and swiftformat --lint pass.

What landed
- `PenNodePatcher.structuralKeys(of:)` + `childrenKey` is the single source of truth for
  "a patch may name `children` on a container". `NodePropertyCodec.rawKeys(acceptedBy:)`
  unions it, so the divergence check now reads the patcher's contract rather than a
  second list. A `children` override on any frame (slot or not) is silent.
- `WriteDivergence.Severity` (`divergence` | `note`) + `reportLine`. The "adds a
  property the definition does not set" branch is now a `note`, rendered `note  <sentence>`
  by both WriteReport.text and BatchReportFormatter, and carried as `severity` in --json.
  New wording: "<path> adds <key> rather than replacing it — <Component> does not set
  <key>, which is how an instance varies from its component".
- `tree --expand` walks injected slot children. TreeView.walk now takes a `Source`
  (`.stored(id)` | `.injected(node)`); TreeView+Slots.swift holds the child sourcing.
  A `ref` among the injected children stays a `ref` row and expands in turn, with its
  own descendant overrides applied. Needed one small refactor:
  `EditableDocument.componentRootID(of: PenNode.RefData)` split out of
  `componentRootID(placedBy:insideInstances:)`.
- `empty-fit-content` skips a row where `TreeRow.isSlot`. Lint does not expand
  instances, so this is exactly the definition's slot frame.

Verified pre-existing (green on first run, deliberately): the patcher already applies a
`children` override and the settled tree renders it — the brief's premise holds; only
the message lied.

OPEN GAP for whoever owns addressing (A4 / a later leaf): `tree --expand` now prints
`Inst0/Note0` for an injected child, and no verb resolves it — `get` exits 2 with
"matches no node in this document — run `woodcase tree ...`", i.e. it points at the
command that produced the address. `resolve` walks the flat store and injected children
are not in it. Making them addressable is real (the expander's applyOverrides recursion
already applies a simple override keyed by an injected node's id, so a write would
work), but it touches EditableDocument+Addressing.swift, +Guards.swift
(validateOverrideTarget / overrideKeys) and namePath — out of this leaf's surface.
Documented as a stated limit in WoodcaseEditor.md and TreeView's doc comment for now.

Behaviour change to existing tests: OverrideCommandTests.overrideOfAnUnsetPropertyEchoes
and WriteDivergenceTests.overrideOfAnUnsetProperty pinned the old divergence sentence;
both updated to the note form. No other golden moved.

Files added: Sources/Woodcase/Tree/TreeView+Slots.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/slot-fill.pen, Tests/WoodcaseTests/SlotFillDivergenceTests.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/SlotFillTreeTests.swift, Tests/WoodcaseTests/DocumentLinterSlotTests.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/DivergenceNoteRenderingTests.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/TreeSlotExpandTests.swift.

shot --crop renders exactly the requested sub-rectangle and reports its origin
shot --help names --max as the vision-model edge limit

data.note: Integrated from wt/shot as a squash. Reviewed the full diff; adjusted the help's tiling example to start from the printed rect= origin (a board's own space is canvas space, which the agent flagged). Kept node-own-space crops for the one-formula property. Suite 3392/346 green, swiftformat clean.

data.text:
Done on wt/batch (not committed). All four defects fixed, red-first.

(a) One assignment path. New Woodcase/Batch/CopyAssignment.swift owns every decision
    about where a cp key lands: destination(of:) is THE SEAM the _props leaf (Nk8RX9)
    extends — one function, key -> (.root | .descendant(path), property). split(),
    the {n} substitution and decodeRows() moved there from CopyCommand. planCopy now
    plans the insert only (root props); the assignments inside the copy are applied by
    the new BatchApplier+CopyLine.performCopy, which reuses document.resolve exactly
    as the verb used to. CopyCommand is a thin adapter: it types argv, decides how
    many copies, and makes one applyOne(.cp(...)).

(b) "parent":"document" accepted for add, cp and mv. The word now lives once, on
    NodeAddress.documentRoot; BatchGuard.documentScope and AddressArgument.documentRoot
    point at it. Decoded in BatchOperation+Codable.parent(in:).

(c) apply --guard, via the shared GuardOption. New library entry
    BatchApplier.checkGuards(_:pinning:of:in:log:file:) so a bare pin's meaning is
    expressed as GuardTarget.document rather than decided in the CLI. Argv pins are
    asserted first, then each line's.

(d) InputFile.data(at:) now reads through FileHandle. Data(contentsOf:) — what the
    brief prescribed — ALSO fails on /dev/null ("you don't have permission to view
    it"): it refuses anything that is not a regular file. FileHandle also makes
    -F <(jq ...) work. ApplyCommand's private readData is gone in favour of InputFile,
    which fixes its "no such file" message for a directory too.

BREAKING (BUILD stage, all call sites updated): BatchLineResult.created and
LineOutcome.created are now [CreatedNode]. A cp line with `each` creates several nodes
and reporting one of them would be a lie; id/path/node stay nil for such a line,
matching what cp --times already did on argv.

Done on wt/batch (not committed).

cp --each <rows.jsonl>: one copy per JSONL row; blank lines skipped; row keys are
exactly the argv keys cp takes; {n} is the 1-based row number, substituted into values
only (a key names a node in the source, which does not vary). An argv assignment is the
default for every row and a row key wins over it. --at places the copies in row order
from the index. --rev guards the first copy only.

--times is now sugar for N empty rows, so there is ONE loop: BatchApplier.copyRows(of:)
turns a CopyOp into one property map per copy. The activity log for --times 3 is
byte-identical to before (add,set x3), so WoodcaseEditor.md's "undo -n 6" still holds.

All-or-nothing before any write: refuseUnknownPaths resolves every row's name-path key
against the SOURCE before the first insert (a copy is name-for-name its source, and an
instance's descendants are the definition's), so row 39's typo is named with nothing
created. New BatchError.copyPathNotInSource(row:key:source:) — "row 3 writes
Nowhere/kind.content, but Component has no Nowhere inside it ... run `woodcase tree
<file> Component`". This also improves the single-copy message, which used to name the
opaque anchored id (#M7DAQ/Nowhere).

--each and --times together: exit 2 naming both and saying which to use when.
Empty rows file: BatchError.emptyCopyRows rather than a silent no-op.
Malformed row: BatchError.malformedRow(row:reason:), naming the 1-based row.

Batch op: CopyOp gains `each: [[String: AnyCodable]]?`, same semantics, rows inline.
`tag` with `each` is refused (BatchError.copyTagWithRows) — one tag cannot name several
copies; the report lists every copy's name and id instead.

DECISIONS made unattended (both fail-closed, both easy to relax):
  - tag + each refused rather than tagging the first or last copy.
  - an empty each/rows file refused rather than copying nothing.

Seam for Nk8RX9 (_props): CopyAssignment.destination(of:) is the single function that
maps a row key to where it lands. A declared prop name is a third case there; it will
need the source node passed in, which is a one-line signature change at its two callers
(CopyAssignment.split and BatchApplier.refuseUnknownPaths). Nothing else needs to know.

Docs: cp --help, apply --help (BatchOperation+Grammar), WoodcaseEditor.md ("A list of
nodes", and the guard section for apply --guard), WoodcaseBatches.md ("One cp line, many
copies", and the parent/"document" note).

Done on wt/overrides (not committed).

`override --unset <key>` (repeatable, either vocabulary) removes an override; the
entry goes away when its last key does, and so does an empty `descendants` map.
Modelled as `unset: [String]` on `EditOperation.OverrideDescendant` and on the batch
`override` op (`"unset":[…]`); a line with neither `props` nor `unset` is refused
(`BatchError.overrideWithoutProperties`) rather than silently doing nothing. The same
key assigned and unset on one command is refused.

Null warning inverted: a new `WriteDivergence.Kind.nullOverride` fires only when the
definition *does* set the key ("… sets content in Button — the null override clears it
rather than removing the override; unset content instead …"). A null over a property
the definition leaves unset is a no-op and now says nothing.

Near miss: `resolveWalk` remembers the cursors the failing step started from. When that
step was a step *into* an instance, `addressNotFound` carries the instance's own
addresses for the name (`Dashboard/Body/Nav/Badge/Count`, `Nav01/Bdg01/Cnt01`) instead
of the definition's copy, and the message ends "a name path into an instance names
every frame of the component's tree, and only an id may skip one".

Found and fixed alongside: the inverse of `overrideDescendant` only restored old
values, so undoing an override that *added* a key left the key behind
(`override fontSize=18` then `undo` kept the 18). The inverse now unsets what the write
added. Regression test: OverrideUnsetTests.undoRemovesAnAddedOverride.

Red observed for all three behaviours by neutering the three implementing hunks and
re-running (11 failures), then restoring.

Done on wt/overrides (not committed).

`override <instance> <prop>=<value>` with no descendant path writes `kind.rootOverrides`
(the ref node's own non-reserved top-level keys, as the format writes them). New
`EditOperation.overrideRoot(OverrideRoot)` — refNodeID, properties, unset — so the
activity log still reads `override`, the inverse is exact, and the CRDT records it as
the `kind.rootOverrides` change the wire already carries. `set <instance>` still writes
the ref node. `--unset` works on root overrides too. Batch: same `override` op, same
address.

Key surface: a root override may be any raw .pen / `kind.*` key the component root
accepts. Every key `PenNode.RefData` reserves is refused with a typed reason
(`RootOverrideRefusal`: identity / refStructure / instanceCommon) naming the command
that works — `opacity` → `woodcase set … common.opacity=…`, `descendants` → override a
descendant, `id`/`type` → nothing sets those. `set <instance> kind.width=…` now answers
with `woodcase override … width=…` instead of just listing the ref's three properties.

Candidate list: `addressableDescendantKeys(ofInstance:)` drops every component-root key
(`Nav01/Btn01`, `Nav01/Bdg01/Bge01`), so `overrideTargetNotFound` never prints an
address `resolve` refuses. `overridableDescendantKeys` is unchanged and still *accepts*
a root-keyed entry already in a file, so lint does not start failing old documents.
New test: every candidate a refusal lists resolves both by id and by name path.
Two existing expectations in OverrideTargetGuardTests changed because the candidate
list changed on purpose.

CAVEAT on criterion 5aX: `override Card1 opacity=0.5` cannot write a root override —
`opacity` is one of `RefData.reservedKeys`, so stored there it would be the *instance's*
own opacity. The criterion's spirit is met with a kind key (`width=200`, tested through
`get --expand` to prove the render path applies it); `opacity` is now the tested
refusal that names `set`.

`get <instance>` already showed root overrides (a ref's canonical JSON carries them as
top-level keys), so GetCommand was not touched.

data.text:
Done on wt/props. swift test --quiet: 3572 tests pass (3540 on main + 32 new). swiftformat . --lint --config .swiftformat clean.

New library seams:
- NodePropertyCodec+DeepKeys.swift — deepKeyedPaths = ["common.metadata"], deepKey(of:), folding(_:onto:). The fold runs in planSet, before the EditOperation exists, so the recorded/replicated/undone edit is the ordinary whole-object write. Arbitrary depth: common.metadata._props.label=Body/Title works; null removes one entry, and an object a null empties goes with it.
- ComponentParameter.swift + EditableDocument+Parameters.swift — parameters(ofComponent:) reads _props off the flat store by the same rule ComponentAnalyzer uses, and reuses ComponentAnalyzer.inferPropType (made internal) so `get` prints the type codegen will emit. property(of:) maps kind -> kind.content / kind.fills, the only two codegen reads.
- BatchApplier+Parameters.swift — routing(_:at:of:in:) sorts an override's keys into groups by target node; planOverride now emits one edit per group.
- CopyAssignment.destination(of:parameters:) / split(_:parameters:) — the one seam, so cp argv, batch cp and --each rows all learn it.

Decisions worth flagging to the integrator:
1. `set --unset` was NOT added. The house form for removing a property on `set` is `=null` (its help has always said "Setting a key to null clears it"), so `set X common.metadata._role=null` removes one entry. --unset stays override's, where it means something different (remove the override, not store a null).
2. `_props` values stay pure name paths — no `Name/Path.kind.prop` form. ComponentAnalyzer.resolveDescendantPath splits on "/" and matches names exactly, so a value carrying a property would resolve to nothing there. The property is inferred from the target node's kind instead, which is what inferPropType already assumes.
3. The collision rule is judged against NodePropertyCodec.rawKeys(acceptedBy:) on the addressed node, so `width` on a frame instance is the frame's width and carries a note; `label` is not a frame property and routes.
4. The schema "row" for metadata is its signature, not a new row: PenSchemaTests pins Set(PenSchema.common.properties.map(\.path)) == commonPaths, so a second row would have broken that invariant. `woodcase schema` now prints
   common.metadata  metadata  {type: string, …}, or one entry at common.metadata.<key>

Left for others (did not touch):
- WoodcaseLint.md 104-111 and the `clipped` remedy string in Sources/Woodcase/Lint/* still teach the whole-object form: `woodcase set … common.metadata='{"type":"unknown","_scroll":"vertical"}'`. It should become `common.metadata._scroll=vertical`. Lint files belong to YYiFP0.
- WoodcaseEditor.md line ~1191 carries the same stale one-liner, inside the lint section.

Agent corrections: no `set --unset` (null clears, house form); _props values stay pure name paths since codegen splits on "/". Integration notes for the lint agent: the `clipped` remedy and WoodcaseLint.md should use the deep-key form. Suite 3572/369 green.

data.text:
Findings from the teaching pass (leaf ojoBLn), all verified against the binary at e34877b.

1. The brief's `\$` claim is half wrong, and the Quill report's D10 is stale.
   `PenVariableResolver.resolveTextContent` restores an unresolved *text content*
   `$name` as a literal when the document defines no variable of that name, so
   `kind.content=$120,000` draws "$120,000" and `lint` reports nothing — verified on
   two files, with and without a variable table. The escape still matters: a name the
   document DOES define substitutes, and outside text content a bare `$name` naming
   nothing stays a dangling reference and lints as `unresolved-variable` (verified with
   `kind.fills=$--nope`). `help design` and WoodcaseEditor.md now say exactly that.
   The `errata` leaf should correct D10 in the report the same way.

2. Filling a slot through the CLI requires an explicit `"id"` on every injected child.
   `override Inst/Slot children=[{"type":"text",...}]` with no id is refused
   ("[0]: the required key \"id\" is missing"). Nothing in the docs said so; both the
   topic and WoodcaseEditor.md do now, and the example JSON in "Filling a slot" gained
   ids (it would have been refused as written).

3. `replace` on a live definition leaves the dropped overrides *in the file*, keyed to
   ids that no longer exist — not removed, just unreachable. No warning, no lint.

4. `override <instance> opacity=0.5` — the design doc's own §B6 acceptance criterion —
   is REFUSED, because every `common.*` key is one the ref reserves for itself. Root
   overrides work on component-root properties (`gap`, `padding`, `width`, `fills`).
   The criterion as written in the plan does not describe what shipped.

5. `--props` is a `tree` flag; `get` has no `--props` at all. The brief and report §4
   both put it under "reads" without naming the verb.

6. Root overrides are stored as top-level keys on the ref node, not under a
   `rootOverrides` object — WoodcaseEditor.md already had this right.
