data.text:
help codegen is written and green (worktree wt/codegenhelp, not committed).

New: Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore/HelpTopic+Codegen.swift (`codegenTopic`, 115 lines,
<=100 cols). Tests appended to Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/HelpCommandTests.swift: the
topic prints, every ComponentRole case is named in it (iterating the enum — I added
CaseIterable to ComponentRole), every key/rule is taught, every bare `  woodcase …`
line runs in order against one scratch file, and the worked example's output really
contains `interface ButtonProps` and `<Button label="Send" tint="#FFD166" />`.

Five findings from verifying against the code and the fixtures:

1. `_bind` IS NOT READ. No version of ComponentAnalyzer has ever looked at it; it
   survives only in a comment, a doc comment and PenCodeGen.md. Bindings come from
   `_role` alone (textInput/toggle/select), named after the node. The design doc, the
   leaf description and PenCodeGen.md all claim `_role` + `_bind`. Code wins; I have
   corrected PenCodeGen.md in place with a dated block quote, and the doc comments on
   ComponentDefinition.actions/bindings/role.

2. `_action` and bindings reach ComponentDefinition and stop there — no emitter reads
   `.actions` or `.bindings`, and neither appears in the manifest. `_action` changes no
   output today. The topic says so rather than promising an onSubmit prop.

3. CRASH: `woodcase generate react` dies with `Fatal error: Duplicate values for key`
   (signal, exit 133) when two `_props` entries name the same descendant.
   ComponentDefinition.propByNodeID builds `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)`.
   Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/component-props.pen is exactly such a document —
   `label` and `width` both point at `Body/Title` — so `generate react` on that fixture
   crashes today. I did not fix it: which of two names wins is a decision, not wiring.
   Relevant to YYiFP0 (a lint check could catch it before the emitter does).

4. `generate react` constructs no PenDiagnosticCollector, so the "Inlined component …
   due to unmapped descendant overrides" diagnostic never reaches stdout or stderr.
   The only evidence a consumer gets is the `{/* Customized from: X */}` comment in the
   emitted .tsx. The topic says that plainly, and points at lint. YYiFP0's
   `codegen-unmapped-override` is the fix for the silence.

5. Emitted pages do not compile: `pages/*.tsx` renders `className={cn(…, className)}`
   and `...style` inside `export function Home() {` — neither identifier is declared or
   destructured. Reproduce: the topic's own worked example, then read ui/pages/Home.tsx.
   Separate bug, no leaf; not mine to fix.

Minor: `set <node> common.metadata._role=button` on a node that had no metadata writes
`"type": "unknown"` into the object alongside it. Harmless for codegen (nothing reads
`type`), but it is noise the writer did not ask for.

data.text:
`--dry-run` landed on all eight write verbs (add, apply, cp, mv, override, replace, rm,
set — mv and replace do share the transaction path, so they are in). Branch wt/dryrun,
not committed. Suite green: 3595 tests, exit 0; `swiftformat . --lint --config
.swiftformat` clean.

Mechanism (library, not CLI):
- `Sources/Woodcase/Files/WriteEffect.swift` — `.commit` / `.dryRun`, a defaulted
  parameter on both `PenFileTransaction.run` overloads. Consulted at the one point a
  transaction commits: the rename and `log.append` are skipped, everything before them
  happens, so no log file, no `.woodcase/` directory and no `.gitignore` line.
- `Outcome.didWrite` became a typed `PenFileTransaction.Commit` (`wrote` / `unchanged` /
  `previewed`) with `didWrite` and `wouldWrite` computed. BREAKING for
  `Outcome(value:didWrite:url:)`; nothing outside the package used it.
- `Sources/Woodcase/Files/LintPreview.swift` — snapshot before, diff after, plus
  `WriteEffect.preview(of:)` so a verb adds one line before its edit and one after.

Two rulings worth reviewing:
1. **Only the findings the write introduces are printed**, not the whole lint of the
   result. Same shape as RootOverlapWarnings. Sameness is (check, node), not the
   sentence — without that, `set Canvas/Title kind.content=Hello` shifted a sibling
   three points and re-announced a `clipped` the file already had, and `mv` re-announced
   the moved node's own `text-without-fill` under its new path. Measured on batch.pen.
2. **No revision line at all**, text or JSON — not the literal `dry-run`. cli-design's
   "never a plausible wrong answer", and `rm` already declines to print a node revision
   for the node it deleted. `BatchReport.documentRevision` and `WriteReport`'s two
   revisions are now optional.

Out of scope, deliberately: `undo`, `vars set/remove/axis add` and `new` also write but
do not go through `BatchApplier`, and their reports have no revision/lint seam to reuse.
Worth a follow-up leaf if "the write verbs" is meant to include them.

data.text: Premise checked 2026-09-02 on HEAD 01d3df2: `generate react` on the bare fixture exits 0 — propByNodeID is only reached when an instance carries descendant overrides. `woodcase override cp.pen Page/Card label=Hello` then `generate react` reproduces exit 133 exactly. Ruling (main thread, unattended): one descendant may carry several props — `label` (content) and `tint` (fill) on one text node is legitimate — so the lookup becomes node id → [props] and the mapper emits one value per prop whose type finds a field in the override. Two props of the same type on one node read the same field and are ambiguous: lint reports that under codegen-prop-path, the emitter keeps the first by name so it never crashes. Dispatched to agent quince with vfNhzi (same files).

Ruling (main thread, unattended): pages take the same optional `className` and `style` a component root takes, so a page dropped into a router layout can be styled from outside and the root-element emission stays one code path. The page signature gains a `<Name>Props` interface with those two optional members and a default `= {}`. Dispatched to agent quince with SZCjUL.

Ruling (main thread, unattended): keep `type`. local/Pen-Schema-2.17.md line 105 declares `metadata?: { type: string; … }` with `type` required, so a deep-key write that creates the object must give it one; "unknown" is the model's default (PenMetadata). The fix is to say so where the deep-key form is taught (help codegen, WoodcaseEditor.md) and to let the caller pick a better one in the same write: `common.metadata.type=component common.metadata._role=button`. Docs only. Dispatched to agent sable with 47zOYP.

Ruling (main thread, unattended): the same contract as DryRunOption on the eight verbs — marker line first in text, `"dryRun": true` in JSON, no revision line, then the lint findings the result would introduce (LintPreview). vars set/remove/axis add and undo pass `effect:` to PenFileTransaction. `new` does not go through the transaction: its dry run runs both refusals and prints the marker and the path, no revision. Dispatched to agent sable with d5owef.

Premise checked 2026-09-02 on slot-fill.pen: tree --expand prints Inst0/Note0 and Inst0/Tag00/BTxt0; get and set on Inst0/Note0 exit 2. Ruling (main thread, unattended): the address of an injected child is what tree --expand already prints — by id `Inst0/Note0`, by name `Page/Filled/Body/Note` — and every verb resolves it. A write to one lands as an override on the instance keyed the way the expander's applyOverrides already applies it (the injected node's own id per the slots agent; the expander is the authority if that is wrong). Dispatched to agent rowan.

Fixed on wt/emitter-props. ComponentDefinition.propByNodeID -> propsByNodeID:
[String: [PropDefinition]], grouped and sorted by prop name, so a descendant several
props name no longer traps Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:). PropMapper.map emits one
MappedProp per prop whose type finds a field in the override, and claims each PropType
once per node so two props of the same type keep the first by name. hasUnmapped and
unmappedOverrideIDs in ReactEmitter+Ref read the same multi-map (a shared descendant
still counts as mapped, so the instance is not inlined). DocumentLinter+CodegenPropPath
gained a second finding shape for the ambiguity, naming both props, the descendant they
share and `woodcase set <file> <id> common.metadata._props.<name>=<path>` for the ones
the emitter drops.

Verified end-to-end: copy of component-props.pen + `override Page/Card label=Hello` +
`generate react` now exits 0 and writes `<StatCard label="Hello" />`; `lint` on the same
file reports the label/width ambiguity as a codegen-prop-path error.

FINDING worth the tracker: the ruling's "legitimate" case — one node carrying a `label`
(content) and a `tint` (fill) — is unreachable through ComponentAnalyzer today.
inferPropType(from:) is a pure function of the *node*, so every prop resolving to one
node gets the same PropType. The one-to-many lookup is still right (PropMapper handles
it, and it is what a per-prop type inference would need), but in every real document two
props on one node are ambiguous by construction and always produce the lint finding. If
per-field props are wanted, the change is in inferPropType / the _props declaration
shape, not here.

The fixture's `width` prop is deliberate — ComponentParameterCommandTests
aCollidingNameIsTheRawProperty uses it for the raw-property shadowing message — so the
ambiguous case was built in a new fixture (Fixtures/lint/codegen-prop-path-ambiguous.pen)
rather than by editing component-props.pen.

Fixed on wt/emitter-props. ReactEmitter.emitPage now runs the page's props-less
definition through the same emitInterface used for a component — no second copy — so a
page carries `interface <Name>Props { className?: string; style?: React.CSSProperties; }`
and the signature `export function Home({ className, style }: HomeProps = {})`. The
default keeps `<Home />` renderable from the viewer's router, which calls it with no
attributes.

No React import was added, matching component files: `React.CSSProperties` is a *type*
position, and TypeScript allows a UMD global there inside a module (the emitted
tsconfig.json is jsx: "react-jsx"). Adding one to pages alone would have made them
inconsistent with every component file.

BRIEF WAS WRONG on the goldens: no golden fixture covers a page. All ten
Fixtures/golden/*.golden are components emitted through the components-only
`ReactEmitter.emit(document:components:theme:)` overload — ScreenLab and ScreenSettings
look like screens but are `reusable: true` in woodcase-app.pen, so PageAnalyzer returns
nothing for it (recorded in project/2026-03-28-codegen-design.md). `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 swift
test --filter ReactEmitterTests` rewrote two goldens byte-identically; `git status` on
Fixtures/golden is clean. The page format is therefore covered only by unit tests, which
is what the new ReactEmitterPageSignatureTests file is for.

The existing ReactEmitterTests test "Page has no props interface" asserted
`!content.contains("interface")` and `export function Home()`. It was rewritten to the
new expectation rather than deleted; the behaviour it guarded is exactly the bug.

data.text:
Done on wt/injected-address (not committed). Injected slot children now resolve
everywhere: `Inst0/Note0`, `Page/Filled/Body/Note`, `Inst0/Tag00/BTxt0`.

Expander key form VERIFIED, not assumed: PenNodePatcher.applyOverrides applies
overrides[node.id] and *then* recurses into the result's children, so a simple key
"Note0" on Inst0 reaches the injected node the CSlt0 fill just put there. A node
inside an injected ref is the cross-ref key "Tag00/BTxt0", prefixed to
"Inst0/Tag00/BTxt0" post-expansion. Both are exactly ResolvedNodeAddress.address,
so no new address form was needed.

New shared primitive EditableDocument+Injected.swift: injectedChildren /
injectedNodes / componentRoot(ofInstanceChain:) / node(ofInstance:descendantKey:) /
injectionPoint. TreeView+Slots, the resolver's cursor walk, the override guard and
namePath all read it, so they cannot disagree about what an instance put in a slot.

Two bugs fixed on the way, both pre-existing:
- expandedID(of:) returned "Inst0/Tag00" for an injected ref instead of
  "Inst0/Tag00/Badg0", so `get` on an injected ref found nothing in the expansion.
- TreeView.starts() could not root a walk at an injected node; `tree Inst0/Tag00
  --expand` printed one row.
- TreeView.injectedChildren could not see a slot fill written by an *injected* ref's
  own descendants map (effectiveRefData has no store entry for it); the shared
  primitive falls back to the injected payload.

DEVIATION: `set` on an injected child still refuses and points at `override` — the
existing contract for every instance descendant; a write is an OverrideDescendant,
which only `override` produces. rm/mv/cp now refuse with a new BatchError case
`structureInsideSlot`, naming the slot and the `children=` rewrite.

INTEGRATION NOTE: HelpTopic.swift (help design, SLOTS) still says injected ids "are
names and not addresses any verb resolves yet" — now false. Not edited per brief.

data.note: Landed in 0e917b6 (agent rowan, squash of wt/injected-address). Injected ids resolve for get/override/tree; set keeps refusing instance descendants; rm/mv/cp get a slot-aware refusal. Three adjacent bugs fixed (expandedID of an injected ref, TreeView start at an injected node, fills written by an injected ref). Left at parity: steps(from:) follows refData.ref directly, not componentRootID, so a component that is itself a ref is not followed when stepping in.

data.title: Address walk does not follow a ref chain into an instance
data.description: The address resolver does not follow a ref chain when stepping into an instance. `steps(from:)` in Sources/Woodcase/Editing/EditableDocument+Addressing.swift takes `refData.ref` directly, while PenRefExpander and `expandedID(of:)` follow `componentRootID` through a reusable component that is itself a ref to another component. So an instance of an aliased component expands, prints rows in `tree --expand`, and then refuses every address inside it — the same dead end kVs5oC closed for slot children. Fix: step through the chain-following lookup, with a regression test on a ref-to-ref fixture (TDD; if the red test is green because Pen never writes that shape, record that on this leaf instead). Also fold in one sentence for `set --help` (SetCommand.swift, off limits to leaf 47zOYP at the time): a deep key that creates common.metadata puts `type: "unknown"` beside it because the schema requires the key; choose it in the same write with `common.metadata.type=component`. Found by the addressing agent (leaf kVs5oC) and the dry-run agent (leaf 47zOYP), 2026-09-02.

data.text:
Fixed on wt/ref-chain (tamsin).

The shape is real: the expander DOES follow a reusable-to-reusable ref chain and
clones its far end. New fixture Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/addressing-ref-chain.pen
(`Page2 > ref Inst2 -> IconC (reusable ref, with overrides) -> BtnB0 > Lbl04, Grp04 >
Ico04`). `PenRefExpander.expand` yields Inst2/BtnB0, Inst2/Lbl04, Inst2/Grp04,
Inst2/Ico04 — no `IconC` step. `tree --expand` printed exactly those rows before the
fix, and `get`/`override`/`resolve` refused every one of them.

Two seams disagreed with the expander, both fixed:

1. `steps(from:)` (EditableDocument+Addressing.swift) took `effectiveRefData(...)?.ref`
   and required `nodes[target] != nil`. For an alias that target is the alias node
   itself, which has no children, so the step returned []. Now it uses
   `componentRoot(ofInstanceChain: cursor.refChain + [cursor.nodeID])`, which covers
   all three cases at once: repointed nested refs, injected refs, and alias chains.
   Side effect, deliberate: a `ref` at a node that is NOT in `componentRegistry` no
   longer steps. The expander leaves such a ref standing, so the old `nodes[target]
   != nil` test was the disagreeing one. Whole suite still passes.

2. `descendantKeys(ofInstance:)` / `appendDescendantKeys` / `appendInjectedKeys`
   (EditableDocument+Guards.swift) built keys through the alias, producing
   `IconC/Lbl04` — a key with a step the expander never applies, so an override
   written under it would never land. Now they resolve through
   `componentRoot(ofInstanceChain:)` / `componentRootID(placedBy:...)` /
   `componentRootID(of:)`.

One seam did NOT have the gap: `namePath(ofDescendant:in:)` / `componentSegments`
(EditableDocument+NamePath.swift). `componentSegments(to:insideInstances:)` walks
ancestors and stops at the nearest reusable one, which is correct whatever the alias
chain looks like, and its injected branch already goes through
`injectedNodes(insideInstances:)` -> `componentRoot(ofInstanceChain:)`. Its two tests
were green on first run — as was `expandedID(of:)`, which already followed the chain.

Also: added the `type: "unknown"` sentence to `set --help`'s metadata paragraph, with
one assertion (`common.metadata.type=component`, a single token so line wrapping
cannot split it) in MetadataDeepKeyTests.theHelpSaysBoth — verified red first.

Docs: new "Through an alias" paragraph in Documentation.docc/EditingDocuments.md,
Addressing Nodes.

data.text:
Catalog gaps closed: 20 components / 34 states -> 35 components / 84 states. All 15 HTML components under Components/ that had no entry now have one; four states added to existing entries (top-bar/unread, top-bar/dashboard, presence-stack/unattributed, avatar/unattributed). No existing golden changed by the three additive initialisers (IdChip.copied, TopBar.Crumb.unread, ArtboardRow.unread), which is the proof they are additive. Full suite passed (3714 tests); swiftformat --lint clean. FINDINGS — states whose golden disagrees with DESIGN.md. Not fixed here (this leaf is additive only); the goldens record the truth and the review leaf should file them. 1. An unattributed writer is a `?` avatar but a *blank* text column. DESIGN.md § Components, Avatar: "An empty identity renders `?` — an unattributed write is a real state, not a rendering bug." AvatarView honours it; nothing else does. - Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/presence-stack/unattributed.html — the summary reads `2 active · editing` (two spaces, no name) and `` is empty. - Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/activity-row/cross-file.html — `` leaves a hole in the five-column grid. Suggested fix: one shared display name for `ActivityEvent.unattributed` ("nobody" / "unattributed") used everywhere the name is written as text, not just in the avatar's `title`. 2. A theme picker with no axes renders an empty wrapper, not nothing. Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/theme-picker/none.html and the new top-bar/dashboard.html both hold `
`. The existing theme-picker/none note claims "Renders nothing at all"; an empty flex child still takes the control row's gap. Either the note is wrong or the component is. 3. `ViewerScript` writes words, which DESIGN.md forbids. DESIGN.md § Do's and Don'ts: "script never writes a word of text." The id-chip copy handler does `chip.textContent = "copied"` (Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Client/ViewerScript.swift:511, and the selection footer's copy button at :356). The server-rendered alternative is the same shape as the live badge's: render both words and let a class choose. `IdChip(id:copied:)` now renders exactly what the script writes, so the fix is a swap of which side owns the text, not new markup. 4. The unread dot has no rule for a file card. The brief asked for "a file card with the unread dot". The stylesheet hangs the dot on `[data-artboard][data-unread="1"]` and `.v-crumb-map[data-unread="1"]` only; a `FileCard` carries `data-file`. So the state does not exist today — declared instead on the two surfaces that do have it (artboard-row/unread, top-bar/unread). Whether the dashboard should mark a changed *file* is a design question, not a bug.

data.title: Unattributed writers render as a blank name outside the avatar
data.description: DESIGN.md says an empty identity renders `?` — "an unattributed write is a real state, not a rendering bug". AvatarView honours it; everywhere the name is written as text does not. Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/presence-stack/unattributed.html summarises as `2 active · editing` (two spaces, no name) with an empty .v-presence-name, and golden/activity-row/cross-file.html leaves ``, a hole in the five-column grid. Wants one shared display name for ActivityEvent.unattributed wherever the name is written as text. Preview: /preview/presence-stack/unattributed and /preview/activity-row/cross-file. Found by the preview-states agent (leaf RFfrBV) reading the goldens.

data.description:
A theme picker with no axes renders an empty wrapper, not nothing. golden/theme-picker/none.html and golden/top-bar/dashboard.html both hold `
`, while the `none` state's own note says "Renders nothing at all". An empty flex child still eats the control row's gap. Either the note is wrong or the component is; decide and fix the other. Preview: /preview/theme-picker/none. Found by the preview-states agent (leaf RFfrBV).

data.title: ViewerScript writes the word copied instead of toggling a class
data.description: ViewerScript writes words, which DESIGN.md's Do's and Don'ts and the fragments rule forbid: Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Client/ViewerScript.swift ~line 511 does `chip.textContent = "copied"` on an id chip, and ~line 356 the same for the footer's copy button. The live badge's recipe is the fix: server-render every label, let the script own only a class or data attribute, and let the stylesheet show the one that matches. IdChip(id:copied:) now emits exactly the markup the script produces, so the swap is which side owns the text, not new markup. Preview: /preview/id-chip/copied. # Activity rows truncate the path from the end, so every row reads `Dashboard/…` and the node it is about is lost

## States
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/activity-row/default
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/activity-row/many-nodes
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/activity-row/cross-file
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/activity-feed/default
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/right-pane/map
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/dashboard-page/default
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/map-page/default

Shots: `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/activity-feed--default--light.png` (four rows, all reading `Dashboard/…`),
`/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/activity-row--many-nodes--light.png`, `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/activity-row--cross-file--light.png`.

## What should be seen
DESIGN.md, *Layout*: "Paths truncate from the *front* (an RTL box around a `<bdi>`
isolate), so the tail that names the node is what survives." Do's and Don'ts: "Don't clip
or wrap chrome text as an overflow strategy; shedding and front-truncation are the two
affordances." The `many-nodes` note asks the reviewer to check that the column "names the
*first* path and says `+3`"; the `cross-file` note that "the file name and the path share
one column separated by a middot".

## What is seen
Back-truncation. `sleepy query` on `/preview/activity-row/many-nodes` gives the text
`Dashboard/Cards/Revenue +3` in a 75.86 px column, rendered as `Dashboard/…`. The `+3`, the
node name and the middot the notes ask about are exactly what is thrown away, and in the
feed all four rows collapse to the identical string.

## Cause
`ViewerStylesheet.swift:395` — `.v-activity-path { overflow: hidden; text-overflow:
ellipsis; }` with no `direction: rtl` and no `<bdi>`, unlike `.v-selection-path` (536) and
`.v-box-path` (504) which both do it correctly. The grid's last track is
`minmax(0, 1fr)` at a 320 px pane, so there is never enough room.

data.title: Twelve token pairs in the chrome fall below WCAG AA, the worst being the live badge's own word at 1.98:1
data.description:
# Twelve token pairs in the chrome fall below WCAG AA, the worst being the live badge's own word at 1.98:1

`sleepy contrast --min wcag-aa` over all 88 states in both schemes (full log:
`Iw1PsY-contrast.txt` in the leaf's scratch). Every state fails, because the failures are in
the palette, not in any one component. Distinct pairs, by how many states carry them:

| element | ratio | ink on ground | scheme |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.v-live-label` (`live`) | 1.98:1 | `#2fbf6f` on `#eceae3` | light |
| `.v-id-chip.v-mono` (faint id) | 1.95:1 / 2.24:1 | `#a5a096` on `#e2dfd6` / `#6a665e` on `#33322f` | both |
| `.v-crumb-sep` | 2.16:1 / 2.76:1 | faint on chrome | both |
| `.v-section-note` (source path) | 2.39:1 / 3.17:1 | faint on bg | both |
| `.v-panel-note`, `.v-activity-time`, `.v-outline-rect`, `.v-variant-axis`, `.v-glyph`, `.v-empty-note`, `.v-step-count` | 2.60:1 / 2.95:1 | faint on panel | both |
| `.v-avatar` white initial | 1.72:1 / 2.26:1 | `#ffffff` on a hashed hue | both |
| `.v-id-chip` | 3.55:1 / 3.88:1 | muted on line | both |
| `.v-crumb`, `.v-presence-note`, `.v-key-hint` | 3.92:1 | muted on chrome | light |
| `.v-kind-label` (instance) | 4.08:1 | `#2f7de1` on `#ffffff` | light |
| `.v-preview-note` | 4.33:1 | muted on bg | light |

Two of these DESIGN.md already owns: white ink on a hashed avatar is the standing exception
to the colour rule, and `faint` is defined as "scaffolding (glyphs, unnamed nodes, dimmed
counts)" — deliberately quiet. The rest are not obviously intentional, and one is load-
bearing: `live` is the word DESIGN says the badge must carry so "the badge can never go
amber while still reading 'live'", and at 1.98:1 in light it is the least readable text on
the strip.

Filed as a fact, not a verdict — DESIGN.md sets no contrast bar, so whether AA is the bar
is Ben's call. The measurement is here so the decision is made once rather than re-argued
per component.

data.title: Eleven state pages carry duplicate DOM ids, so the script and popovertarget drive the chrome's copy, not the previewed one
data.description:
# Eleven state pages carry duplicate DOM ids, so the script and popovertarget drive the chrome's copy, not the previewed one

## States (11)
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/live-badge/connecting, /live, /lost — `v-live` twice
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/presence-stack/empty, /pair, /overflow, /unattributed — `v-presence` twice
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/top-bar/artboard, /unread, /dashboard — `v-presence`, `v-live`, `v-keys` twice
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/keyboard-hint/default — `v-keys` twice

Measured with `sleepy eval --file` counting `[id]` across each of the 88 states; the scan
is `Iw1PsY-dupids.txt` in the leaf's scratch.

## What should be seen
One id per document. `ViewerScript` reaches these by `getElementById`, and the keyboard
hint's `<button popovertarget="v-keys">` resolves by id.

## What is seen
The preview document's own chrome already renders a `PresenceStack`, a `LiveBadge` and a
`KeyboardHint` with those ids, and the framed state renders a second set. `getElementById`
and `popovertarget` both take the *first* match, which is the page's chrome — so clicking
the previewed `?` opens the chrome's panel, and a live `presence`/`change` event repaints
the chrome's badge while the state under review stays put.

## Cause
`PreviewStatePage`/`PreviewCanvas` nest a component that hard-codes an id inside a
`ViewerDocument` whose top bar renders the same component. Either the preview layout drops
the chrome's copies of these three controls, or the ids stop being literals.

`/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/artboard-overlay--default--dark.png` (" mv 12s" floating outside the pill).

## What should be seen
DESIGN.md, *Render stage and overlay*: "Box tags cap their width at the artboard's edge and
front-truncate like the footer." So an over-long tag should end in an ellipsis inside its
own coloured ground.

## What is seen
The tag's background stops after `claude-b`; the `mv 12s` span keeps going for another
40 px on the page ground. In dark that white text lands on a dark page and is readable but
plainly outside the pill; in light it is white on `#F6F5F1` and disappears entirely. A
light/dark mismatch and a clipped fact at once.

Measured: `.v-box-tag.v-edit-tag` is 76 px wide (x 373→449) while its child `.v-edit-op`
runs from x 452 to 489.

## Cause
`ViewerStylesheet.swift:489-500` gives `.v-box-tag` a `max-width` but no `overflow: hidden`,
and only `.v-box-path` (the *selection* tag's child, 504-508) carries the
`min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; direction: rtl` treatment. The
edit tag's `.v-edit-who` / `.v-edit-op` have none, so they overflow the capped box.

## What should be seen
The state's note: "In the canvas the panel sits inert beneath the badge — that *is* the
closed state, drawn honestly. Read the key table against ``ViewerScript``'s: this component
only restates what the script dispatches, and the two drifting apart is the failure it
exists to make visible."

## What is seen
A full-width strip with a 16 px `?` at its right end and nothing else. The panel is not
"inert beneath the badge": `sleepy query` reports `.v-key-hint-popover` at 0x0,
`visible: false`. `[popover]` is `display: none` until the popover is shown, so the six
shortcut rows never render, and the one thing the note tells a reviewer to do cannot be
done from the picture.

## Cause
The note describes pre-`popover` behaviour. Either the state has to open the popover (it
cannot: a closed `[popover]` needs `showPopover()`), or the component needs a way to render
the panel in place for the preview, or the note is wrong. This also makes the state the
only one on the strip whose whole content is off-screen.

## What should be seen
The state's note: "One state: the fade is a CSS animation on the same markup… Check that it
names *both* keys — `f` and Escape — since a screen with nothing on it makes neither
guessable, and that the text is server-rendered."

## What is seen
An empty frame, zero visible height, in both schemes. Nothing to check.

## Cause
`ViewerStylesheet.swift:833` — `.v-present-hint { display: none; }`, lifted only by
`body.is-presenting .v-present-hint` (834). The preview document's body has no
`is-presenting`, so the pill is never laid out. `sleepy query` reports the element at
0x0, `visible: false`, with the text `Press f or Escape to exit` present in the markup.

The state is declared as the mode's markup but the mode's body class is not, so the
preview shows the component in the one condition where it is hidden.

data.description: # The live stream wipes the server-rendered presence and live badge on page previews, so two shots of one state disagree ## States Every `page` state, most visibly: - http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/artboard-page/default - http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/map-page/default Shots: `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/artboard-page--default--light.png` vs `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/artboard-page--default--dark.png`; `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/map-page--default--light.png` vs `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/map-page--default--dark.png`. ## What should be seen The server renders the fixture's presence. `Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/artboard-page/default.html` contains `2 active · claude-a editing`, and the map page's the same. ## What is seen The light shot of artboard-page reads `no identities yet` with an empty stack; the dark shot of the *same state*, taken seconds apart, reads `2 active · claude-a editing`. The live badge flips the same way (`live` in one, `connecting` in the other). Three consecutive `sleepy query --selector '.v-presence-note'` runs now all answer `no identities yet`, so the script wins once its `/events` connection lands — the dark shot simply beat it. ## Cause `woodcase preview` serves the real `viewer.js`, which opens `/events` and repaints presence and the live badge from the (empty) live stream, discarding what the state declared. Same family as the unread-dot issue. It also makes the review loop non-deterministic: the picture depends on the race, which is exactly what a preview must not do.

## What should be seen
The `long-path` note: "The truncation case. The path is cut from its *front* —
`…/Fav Card 2/Cover Image`, never `Home — Colle…`". DESIGN.md, *Selection footer*: "the
rect and revision are shed first when the pane narrows" (the `@container (max-width: 560px)`
rule at `ViewerStylesheet.swift:527`).

## What is seen
The full path, untruncated: `Home — Collection (Light)/Content/Favorites/Fav Card 2/Cover
Image`, with the rect and the revision both present. Neither affordance fires.

## Cause
The four states declare `frame: .topBar`, and `.v-preview-frame[data-frame="top-bar"]` is
`width: 100%` — 1216 px at the 1280 reference window. In production `SelectionBar` is
rendered inside `RenderRegion` (`Sources/WoodcaseViewer/Components/RenderRegion.swift:85`),
i.e. the canvas column, which the same stylesheet computes as
`1280 - 340 - 320 - 2*grip` = about 608 px. At that width it works: the same footer inside
`/preview/render-region/default` reads `…board/Header/Title` and truncates correctly.

The frame is simply the wrong surface. `canvas` is the one it lives on. A narrower state
(or a second one) would also be needed to reach the 560 px shed.

data.title: The unread dot never renders, because the script deletes the attribute the server wrote
data.description:
# The unread dot never renders, because the script deletes the attribute the server wrote

## States
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/top-bar/unread
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/artboard-row/unread

Shots: `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/top-bar--unread--light.png`, `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/top-bar--unread--dark.png`,
`/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/artboard-row--unread--light.png`, `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/artboard-row--unread--dark.png`.

## What should be seen
DESIGN.md, *Unread dot*: "A 6px warn dot with a panel ring, hung on `data-unread="1"` — an
attribute, not a class". The top-bar state's own note: "The file-wide unread dot, hung on
the map crumb by setting the attribute the script sets — `data-unread="1"` on
`.v-crumb-map`. The crumb gains 10 px of right padding to make room."

## What is seen
No dot, in either scheme, on either state. The crumb also does not gain its 10 px, so the
padding half of the note cannot be checked either.

## Cause
Not a shot artefact and not a stylesheet bug. The server *does* write the attribute — the
golden `Tests/WoodcaseViewerTests/Fixtures/golden/top-bar/unread.html` has
`class="v-crumb v-crumb-map" href="…" title="…" data-unread="1"` — and the rule
`.v-crumb-map[data-unread="1"]::after` in `ViewerStylesheet.swift:876,881-882` is correct.
`viewer.js` removes it. `ViewerScript.swift`, `applyUnread()` (around line 1116) runs on
every page, reads this browser's `localStorage`, finds nothing marked unread for a file id
that does not exist on a preview page, and ends with:

    for (const box of document.querySelectorAll("[data-artboard]")) { … else { delete box.dataset.unread; } }
    const up = document.querySelector(".v-crumb-map");
    …
    if (elsewhere) { up.dataset.unread = "1"; } else { delete up.dataset.unread; }

Confirmed live: `sleepy dom /preview/top-bar/unread` shows the anchor with no
`data-unread`, and `sleepy query /preview/artboard-row/unread --selector '[data-artboard]'`
shows only `class`, `data-artboard`, `href`.

This is the general shape of the problem — the live script overwrites server-rendered
preview state — and it also destroys the presence stack (filed separately). Any fix should
decide once whether the preview pages run the live half of `viewer.js` at all.

data.title: Variable numbers are not right-aligned, because the summary row shrink-wraps to 206px inside a 340px pane
data.description:
# Variable numbers are not right-aligned, because the summary row shrink-wraps to 206px inside a 340px pane

## States
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/variables-panel/default
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/artboard-page/default
- http://127.0.0.1:7419/preview/map-page/default

Shots: `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/variables-panel--default--light.png`, `/Users/ben/git/Woodcase/local/viewer-shots/preview/variables-panel--default--dark.png`.

## What should be seen
DESIGN.md, *Variables pane*: "Swatches for colors, **right-aligned mono for numbers**".
The state's note calls it "Every variable type", so the alignment is part of what it shows.

## What is seen
`16` sits at x 167.36 and `8` at x 174.78 — each immediately after its own name, so the two
numbers do not even line up with each other, let alone with the pane's right edge at 372.

## Cause
`.v-variable-value` has `flex: 1` and `.v-variable-number` adds `text-align: right`
(`ViewerStylesheet.swift:352-356`), and the computed `flex-grow` is indeed 1 — but the flex
container never spans the panel. Measured: `.v-variable-row` (`<details>`) is 338 px wide
while `.v-variable-summary` inside it is 205.69 px. The `<summary>` with `display: flex`
(337) shrink-wraps rather than filling its `<details>`, so `flex: 1` has nothing to grow
into. A `width: 100%` (or `display: flex` on a wrapper that is a block) is the shape of the
fix.

data.label: Every state in `preview --list` has a shot in both schemes
Every visual defect found is an issue naming the state URL

data.text:
First review pass done. 38 components, 88 states, both colour schemes, 176 shots in
`local/viewer-shots/preview/` (`<component>--<state>--<light|dark>.png`), plus full-page
shots of the nine `page` states. Dark was forced with `sleepy shot --theme dark`; the flag
repeats and sweeps, so one call per state rendered both.

Verdicts: 26 ok, 56 carrying at least one defect, 6 questions. Table in
`local/viewer-shots/preview/REVIEW.md`; contact sheets `contact-sheet-1.png` …
`contact-sheet-4.png` (ten components each, light and dark side by side).

23 issues filed, and three existing ones appended to (`JFazoq`, `MqMUlS`, `ymsE0s`) rather
than duplicated. Nothing was fixed and no file under `Sources/` or `Tests/` was touched.

The specific check the brief asked for: the unread dot on the map crumb is **not** a
stylesheet bug or a shot artefact. The server writes `data-unread="1"` (it is in the
golden), the CSS rule is correct, and `viewer.js`'s `applyUnread()` deletes the attribute on
load because this browser has nothing marked unread for a file id that does not exist on a
preview page. Filed as `wNhNQp`. It is one instance of a larger shape — the live half of
`viewer.js` overwriting server-rendered preview state — which also wipes the presence stack
and the live badge on every `page` state (`GqUQys`) and makes two shots of one state
disagree. Whoever fixes either should decide once whether the preview routes run the live
script at all.

The three biggest findings by blast radius, if the tree wants an order:

1. `4FmPKE` — the artboard render 404s on every preview that draws one (12 states), so the
   render box shows a broken-image glyph and its alt text under the overlay boxes.
2. `eJcZJU` — activity rows back-truncate their path, against DESIGN.md's front-truncation
   rule, so all four rows of the feed read `Dashboard/…`.
3. `gtuww7` + `4GVELx` + `KKPpCv` — three frame choices put components on the wrong surface
   (`top-bar` paints no ground for eleven non-TopBar controls; the selection bar is
   full-window so neither of its two affordances fires; the file cards are on `canvas`, the
   one surface the file list's own note says they do not sit on). These are catalog-side, not
   component-side, and are the cheapest to fix.

Reproduce anything here with `woodcase preview --port 7419` and the URL in the issue.

Headline: ViewerScript applyUnread() deletes the server-written data-unread on load (wNhNQp) and the stream wipes presence/live badge on page states (GqUQys), so several declared states can never be seen through the script.

data.title: Ink pivot, AA tokens, command-block fade, two catalog drops, mono handles, list paths
data.description:
Six rulings from Ben (2026-09-02), one leaf:

1. Avatar ink pivots between white and black by the disc's relative luminance (WCAG two-way threshold ≈ 0.179), so every hashed identity colour reaches AA. Hue, saturation and the fixed 48% lightness stay exactly as they are (the Go dashboard shares the formula). The ink is a second custom property beside the colour; the edit tags over the render, which also draw white on the hue, take the same pivot. Closes the avatar rows of bQ5vIa.
2. AA is the bar for text that carries meaning; `faint` stays exempt as scaffolding. Bring the live badge's `live` word (1.98:1 light) and the crumbs / presence note / key hint (3.92:1 light) to AA by adjusting those tokens, not by restyling components. Note what moved in DESIGN.md's colour section. Closes the rest of bQ5vIa that is not `faint`.
3. The empty page's command block gets a right-edge fade as a scroll affordance; the block still scrolls sideways and never wraps (DESIGN.md's rule stands).
4. Drop the catalog states id-chip/outline and pane-grip/rows with their goldens (same rule as the empty states: not gradeable in isolation).
5. DESIGN.md typography: one sentence that an identity is an `--as` handle and is set in mono as an address, not sans as a name.
6. `woodcase preview --list` and `--list --json` print bare paths, not URLs; the running verb's `--json` already reports the real base. Update PreviewCommand's help, PreviewCommandTests, WoodcaseCLI.md and WoodcaseViewer.md § The review loop.

criteria.label: Every avatar and edit tag reaches 4.5:1 in both schemes, measured with sleepy contrast over the catalog
The live badge word and the crumbs reach AA in both schemes
id-chip/outline and pane-grip/rows are gone; the catalog test passes
preview --list prints paths and its tests say so

data.text:
All six rulings implemented on wt/review-round-one. Full suite green (3746 tests, 2
pre-existing known issues); `swiftformat . --lint --config <worktree>/.swiftformat` clean.

Measurement (before → after), `woodcase preview --port 7423 &` then
`woodcase preview --list | scripts/viewer-contrast --base http://127.0.0.1:7423`
(a new script wrapping `sleepy contrast --min wcag-aa`, both schemes, every state):

  85 states / 140 distinct failing pairs  →  83 states / 65 pairs.

Every remaining failure is one of two families, both deliberate:
  - `faint` (#a5a096 / #6a665e) as text — exempt by Ben's ruling, scaffolding.
  - white ink on the *fixed* accent fill (copied id chip, true bool pill, selection box
    tag): 2.39:1 light, 1.92:1 dark. DESIGN's standing exception, untouched — a fixed
    fill has no hash to pivot on. Not in bQ5vIa, not in the brief; flagged, not fixed.

Named pairs:

data.title: A JavaScript host for the editing loop
data.description:
Vision, contract and rationale in project/2026-09-07-scripting-host.md; read it first.
A `woodcase js` verb runs a JavaScript program inside one file transaction against a
`doc` object whose members mirror the editing verbs one for one, returning the same
typed reports the verbs print. JavaScriptCore is the engine; the host is a new
library target so Penumbra can consume it. Out-of-band write detection ships
alongside because it is the same premise from the other side: every byte the file
changes by is accounted for in the activity log.

Strict TDD throughout: every leaf begins with failing tests. CLI tests spawn the real
binary through CommandFixture (Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/CommandFixture.swift), which
isolates the activity log with WOODCASE_HOME; library tests get their own target.
The Swift toolchain fails inside the Bash sandbox; see project/agents/harness.md.

data.title: Group the command core into folders
data.description:
Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore is a hundred files in one folder and
Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests ninety, against the rule that sources and tests are grouped
in folders at most one level deep. A pure `git mv`, no content change, done first so
no fan-out branch has to merge across renames:

- Verbs/ — every *Command.swift, WoodcaseCommand.swift, WoodcaseVersion.swift
- Options/ — AddressArgument, BareOptionValue, DryRunOption, GuardOption,
  IdentityOptions, IdentityRole, InputFile, LintCheck+Argument, OutputFormat,
  OutputOptions, PenDiagnosticSeverity+Argument, PenFilePath, PenInputPath,
  PenVariableType+Argument, PositionOption, PropertyAssignment, RevisionOption,
  ThemeOption, ThemePinParser, ThemeCombination, VariableAssignment, VariableTyping
- Reports/ — WriteReport, NodeReport, NewFileReport, UndoReport, InstanceReport and
  every *Formatter, RootOverlapWarnings, CanonicalJSON, Schema*JSON
- Failures/ — CommandFailure, ExitCode+House, ParsableCommand+Failures,
  ParserFailureMessage, SandboxDenial, StandardError, UndoFailures
- Help/ — HelpTopic and its extensions, SchemaHelp
- Shot/ — Shot*, ImageExporter, OutputNamer
- Lookup/ — NodeLookup, InstanceLookup, LibraryResolver, UndoStep, VariableValueEditor
- Hosting/ — ViewerHosting, ParentProcessWatch

Tests mirror the same folders by the type they test. SwiftPM needs no manifest change
for subfolders. Any file that resists a group is a sign it wants splitting; note it
rather than forcing it. A Sonnet leaf; the integrator can also do it directly.

criteria.label: No Swift file sits directly in Sources/WoodcaseCommandCore or Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests, and every folder is one level deep
git shows every move as a rename with no content change, and the full suite passes unchanged

data.title: Move the report vocabulary into the library
data.description:
WriteReport, NodeReport and CreatedTreeFormatter's Report are internal to
WoodcaseCommandCore, so a library caller cannot get a write's echo or a `get` result
as a value and the host could not return them without a twin. Move them into
Sources/Woodcase/Batch/ as public Friendly types beside BatchReport; the command
core's Reports/ keeps only the text formatting, as pure functions of those values.
Name the write echo once — WriteReport is the name; the plan doc's `WriteResult` is
it. Touches the command core's formatters and none of the un-pin's files, so it runs
in parallel with unpin.

criteria.label: WriteReport, NodeReport and the created-tree report are public library types with DocC, and the CLI's text and JSON for them are byte-for-byte unchanged under the existing tests

data.title: Un-pin the editing layer from the main actor
data.description:
Remove `@MainActor` from EditableDocument and everything pinned by contagion —
nineteen files in Sources/Woodcase: BatchApplier and its helpers (BatchErrorMessage,
BatchPoison, CopyAssignment), the three caches (Expansion, Layout, Revision),
RootOverlap, EditableDocument+StateTransfer, ActivityRecorder, LintPreview,
PenFileTransaction, DocumentLinter, PenRenderer, CRDTDocument, CRDTSnapshot,
SettledTree, TreeView. The types become non-isolated and non-Sendable: whoever creates
a document owns it on the actor of their choosing, and the compiler still refuses to
let it cross a boundary. PenFileTransaction's bodies take
`isolation: isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation` and run on the caller's isolation
instead of `MainActor.run`; the CLI still lands on main because its entry point is.
Two spots need thought rather than deletion: `onRemoteChange` and the CRDT peers, whose
operations are Sendable values crossing to wherever the peer lives, and the caches,
which stay owned by the document. Keep `@Observable`. `nonisolated(unsafe)` is not an
answer anywhere in the library. Rationale and the superseded April reasoning:
project/2026-09-07-scripting-host.md, "Un-pinning the editing layer".

This is fail-closed concurrency work: an Opus leaf. Penumbra
(/Users/ben/git/Penumbra, 26 app files hold the document) consumes Woodcase by local
path (`../../Woodcase`), so this breaks its build the moment it lands on main: land
the Penumbra changes in the same sitting, with its `nonisolated(unsafe) var
_editableDocument` workaround in PenumbraDocument.swift deleted, not kept, and name
the Penumbra commit in the report. RapidPro imports none of these types.
Run the loaded soak afterwards (scripts/soak-tests, --load 6) — the suite's
main-actor saturation should ease, and any new flake is this leaf's.

criteria.label: No @MainActor remains in Sources/Woodcase, proven by a grep test, and the package builds under Swift 6 strict concurrency with no warnings
A transaction body runs on the caller's isolation, proven by a test that runs one from a non-main actor
Penumbra builds and its tests pass against the un-pinned library with the nonisolated(unsafe) holder removed
The full suite passes and a loaded soak run shows no new flake

data.title: WoodcaseScripting target and the read-only host
data.description:
Add the `WoodcaseScripting` library target (Package.swift; depends on Woodcase;
`#if canImport(JavaScriptCore)` around every file, the WoodcaseViewer posture) and
its test target. Build `ScriptHost`: one synchronous run that creates a JSContext,
evaluates the prelude, installs `doc` and `console`, evaluates an ordered list of
`ScriptSource` values — `.file(URL)` or `.text(String, name:)`, in one context — and
returns a typed `ScriptRun`: one ordered timeline of events (write, log with level,
warning), the completion value of the last source as JSON (null plus a warning event
when it cannot cross), the document revision, the commit outcome, and an error carrying
the source's name, line, column and quoted line. An optional sink closure receives each
event as it happens. Library consumers pass strings they already hold; the CLI's
repeated -F maps onto the list and holds no decision of its own. The host is written
isolation-agnostic — no global-actor annotation anywhere — and its only runaway
protection is a deadline that bridged calls check and throw on (`code: 'timeout'`);
the process-ending watchdog is the CLI's, in the verb leaf. Each source is evaluated
on its own with its own source URL, so an error reports that source's line, not a
line in a concatenation. The report types are already public library types (reports
leaf); the host returns them. This leaf ships the read side only: `doc.rev`,
`doc.tree(address?, options)`, `doc.get`, `doc.lint`, `doc.schema`, over an
`EditableDocument` the caller hands in. Tree rows come from `TreeView.rows(of:settled:…)`
over one lazily built `SettledTree`, held by the host and dropped by any write (the
write side lands in the next leaf; this leaf ships the cache and its invalidation hook).

Bridging shape, spiked 2026-09-07: `@convention(block)` closures via
`setObject(_:forKeyedSubscript:)`; throw into JS by assigning
`JSValue(newErrorFromMessage:in:)` to `context.exception`; marshal node subtrees and
reports through JSON (JS `JSON.stringify` on the way in, the library's Codable on the
way out) rather than `toDictionary()`. Every error crossing into JS is a
`WoodcaseError` with `code` (the EditingError case name), the remedy sentence from
BatchErrorMessage+Editing.swift, and `candidates` where the error carries them.

The prelude is a Swift string constant (ViewerScript.swift is the precedent). It makes
`doc` a Proxy whose unknown-member access throws the teaching sentence listing the
real members, and validates option-object keys per member, naming the keys that
member takes. `console.log/warn/error` join arguments with spaces and render objects
as JSON. There is no event loop: the prelude defines setTimeout, setInterval, fetch,
require and a top-level `import` guard to throw a sentence saying scripts are
synchronous and why, and a Promise as the completion value yields the null-plus-warning
result. The public JavaScriptCore headers have no time-limit API (checked 2026-09-07);
document that in the host's DocC.

criteria.label: The target builds under Swift 6 strict concurrency with no warnings, JavaScriptCore never appears in the Woodcase target, and no global-actor annotation appears in the host
A run over a file source and a text source in order shares one context, and an error in either is reported with that source's name
A run from a non-main actor works, and the sink receives events in the order the timeline records them
A script whose completion value is a function, a Promise or a cycle yields a null result and a warning event, never an unreadable string
setTimeout, fetch and require each throw the synchronous-scripts sentence, and an error in the second of two sources reports that source's name and line
doc.tree, doc.get, doc.lint and doc.schema return the same values the corresponding verbs print with --json, proven by a parity test over the batch.pen fixture
An ambiguous or missing address thrown into the script carries code, the verb's own sentence and a candidates array the script can read
Accessing an unknown member of doc throws a sentence naming every real member, and an unknown option key names the keys that member takes
A script past its deadline receives a catchable timeout error on its next doc call, asserted on outcome and not on elapsed time
An uncaught error is reported with its line, column and quoted source line

data.title: The write API over BatchApplier
data.description:
Add set, add, replace, cp, mv, rm, override, vars.set/rm and themes.set/rm to `doc`,
each translating its arguments into the matching `BatchOperation` and running
`BatchApplier.applyOne(_:to:recorder:log:file:)` with the transaction's
ActivityRecorder — the host adds no editing semantics of its own. Options are the
verb's flags camel-cased (`at`, `name`, `props`, `detach`, `unset`, `rev`); `rev`
becomes the line's revision pin and a conflict throws `code: 'revisionConflict'`.
The return value is the WriteReport (id, path, rev, created with ids, divergences,
node). No @tag support: the return value carries the id. Every write drops the
settled-tree cache so the next read settles. Values arrive typed, as JSONL values do:
the argv coercion rules do not apply, `$name` strings stay strings, and marshalling
goes through JSON text so an integer from JavaScript is stored as an integer. The
recorder is optional, so a library caller runs a script over an in-memory document
with no activity log.

Prove the per-call atomicity invariant: a write that throws has changed nothing
(materialize before and after are equal; documentRevision unchanged), so a script
that catches and continues works from a consistent document. Measure the
write-then-read cost on local/ design-system file (1,850 nodes): a script that
alternates 100 sets and 100 tree reads; record the figure and the command in
WoodcasePerformance.md, and if it is over budget note the incremental-settle
optimization in the doc rather than building it here.

criteria.label: Every member of doc that writes routes through BatchApplier.applyOne and appears in the activity log as the same event the verb would record, proven by a parity test against the verb
A write that throws leaves the document and its revision unchanged, and a script that catches the error continues and commits the rest
A read after a write returns settled rects that reflect the write
The write-then-read figure on the 1,850-node file is recorded in WoodcasePerformance.md with the command that reproduces it
An uncaught error after several successful writes commits nothing, and the activity log gains no events
An integer written from a script is stored as an integer and the node's revision equals the one the verb produces for the same edit
A run over an in-memory document with no recorder and no log succeeds and returns the same reports

data.title: The js verb
data.description:
`woodcase js <file> -F <script> [-F <more>…] [--as] [--guard…] [--dry-run] [--json] [--timeout]`
in WoodcaseCommandCore, sitting exactly where ApplyCommand sits: one
`PenFileTransaction.run(at:identity:log:effect:)`, entry guards via
`BatchApplier.checkGuards`, then the host. stdout: one row per write as it happens
(verb, path, id, (+N) created, divergences indented under the row), console.log
lines interleaved, `result  <value>` and `document  <rev>` last. stderr: warnings
and refusals only. `--json` is one object built from the same typed ScriptRun.
Exit codes: uncaught script error 1 (file untouched), parse error 2 with line and
message, stale guard or timeout 3, unreadable file 4. Register the verb in
WoodcaseCLI.md's table with its exit codes, and read project/agents/cli-design.md
before writing a single message. Tests spawn the binary through CommandFixture.

`-F` repeats: the files are concatenated in order and evaluated in one context, so
`-F helpers.js -F run.js` is the durable-code pattern the doc describes; an error's
reported location names which file. Nothing persists between runs and nothing is
auto-loaded — the plan doc's "No session" section says why; put that sentence in
the verb's help.

The verb is the host's sink: write rows and console.log lines go to stdout as they
happen, console.warn/error to stderr, all of them in order under --json. The verb
installs the process-ending watchdog on top of the host's deadline: a thread that at
--timeout plus grace prints "script ran past N s; nothing was written" on stderr and
exits 3 — safe because the transaction writes nothing before the body returns and the
flock is the kernel's to release. This watchdog lives only in the verb.

criteria.label: The transcript in the plan doc runs as written against a fixture and prints the rows, result and document lines shown
A function defined in a first -F file is callable from a second, and an error in the second is reported with that file's name and line
A script that loops without calling doc exits 3 with the stderr sentence and leaves the file untouched, asserted on outcome and not on elapsed time
console.log lines appear on stdout between the write rows they were printed between, and console.error lines on stderr
Each exit code in the verb's row of WoodcaseCLI.md has a test that produces it
The text and --json forms are built from one ScriptRun value and a test proves every field printed in text appears in the JSON
--dry-run runs the script, writes nothing, and reports lint findings on the would-be document
--guard with a stale document pin refuses before the script runs, naming the writer as apply does

data.title: The find verb
data.description:
`woodcase find <file> [<address>] <predicate> [--expand] [--props…] [--absolute] [--json]`
in WoodcaseCommandCore: a read verb over the host's read side. Open the file with
`PenFileTransaction.read`, settle once, build the same rows `tree` prints (with
`--props` columns under `r.props`), evaluate the predicate — a JavaScript arrow
function receiving one row — against each, and print the truthy rows in tree's text
format and its --json shape, so `find` output pipes into everything `tree` output
does. The predicate is a positional argument or `-F` for a longer one; it sees no
`doc` and cannot write. Exit 0 with matches, 1 for none, 2 when the predicate does
not parse or throws — the sentence names the row it threw on and lists the
property names a row carries, since `r.fontSize` for `r.props['kind.fontSize']` is
the mistake to expect. Register the verb and its exit codes in WoodcaseCLI.md and
un-park `find` in project/backlog.md with a pointer here. Tests through CommandFixture.

criteria.label: The find transcript in the plan doc runs as written against a fixture
find output on a matching set equals the corresponding tree rows byte for byte in both text and JSON
A predicate that references a property outside r.props gets a sentence listing the row's members, exit 2
No matches exits 1 with nothing on stdout, and a predicate cannot reach doc

data.title: help js and the executable primer
data.description:
A `js` HelpTopic whose body is a short primer followed by the `.d.ts` declaration of
`doc`, `WriteResult`, `TreeRow`, `WoodcaseError` and the option types. The primer
teaches the three rules (one transaction, atomic calls, reads see settled layout),
the no-session rule, that scripts are synchronous (no timers, no fetch, no await),
that top-level const is shared across -F files, the `-F helpers.js -F run.js`
pattern, and shows a fan-out,
a measurement, a caught conflict and the one-line read-only query from stdin, each
snippet ending in the read that verifies it. It also teaches the two routes: when a
verb is enough (`cp --each`, `apply`, `find`) and when control flow makes it `js`.
Two tests keep it honest: a RecipesTests-style extraction runs every snippet against
a fixture; a reflection test evaluates the prelude, lists the members the Proxy
exposes and their option keys, and checks them against the `.d.ts` in both
directions. Add `js` and `find` to the design primer within its 140-line budget,
and a `help js` pointer to the sentences the host throws.

criteria.label: Every snippet in help js runs green under the extraction test
Every runtime member and option key appears in the .d.ts and every declared one exists at runtime
help design still fits its line budget and names find for a query and js for a loop-shaped task
The primer states that nothing persists between runs and shows the repeated -F pattern

data.title: Out-of-band write detection and undo by transaction
data.description:
Extract the revision-lineage comparison from UndoStep.decide into a library type in
Sources/Woodcase/Files/ that both undo and the transaction use. Add
`ActivityEvent.Kind.external` (no inverse, unattributed identity, the revision the
file was found at). In `PenFileTransaction.run(at:identity:log:…)`, after the parse
and before the body, compare the parsed documentRevision with the newest logged
event for the file; on mismatch append an external event as the batch's first event
and surface a note the verb prints on stdout: `note  <file> was rewritten outside
woodcase since rev <short> (<identity>, <time>); the log has no record of that change`.
A file with no log history is not a mismatch. undo reaching an external event refuses
with the sentence naming the time; remove the stepOverUndone heuristic if the external
row makes it unnecessary and say so in UndoStep's doc comment. `activity` renders the
row. Update WoodcaseActivityLog.md and the undo section of WoodcaseEditor.md.

Move undo itself into the library with the lineage type: UndoStep and the replay
(UndoCommand's body) become public library API in Sources/Woodcase/Files/, so a
library caller with the log can reverse an edit; UndoCommand keeps only argv and
formatting.

Undo by transaction (ruled 2026-09-07): every event carries the transaction's batch id
and nothing reads it, so a forty-write script run is forty undos. `undo` now reverses
the most recent transaction as one step — every event sharing the newest batch id, in
reverse order, under one new undo event — and `-n` counts transactions; `--event`
keeps the per-event form. The stale and blocked-by-other checks apply to the
transaction's last event. Update the undo section of WoodcaseEditor.md and the
activity-log article; the existing undo tests change expectation and the leaf's note
says why. Independent of the host; runs in parallel with unpin and host-core, but
touches PenFileTransaction, which unpin also edits — take the transaction's isolation
change from main before starting, or coordinate the seam with the unpin agent.

criteria.label: Undo's step and replay are public library API, and the CLI's undo output for a single-event transaction is unchanged
undo after a batch or a script run reverses every write of that transaction as one step, and -n 2 reverses two transactions
undo --event reverses one event, as before
Rewriting the fixture with python3 json.dump between two set calls makes the second print the note once, and a third set prints no note
The activity log gains one external event carrying the revision the file was found at, and activity renders it
undo refuses to step past an external event with a sentence naming its time
A file edited only by woodcase never produces the note, proven over the full CLI suite

data.title: Imports on every route
data.description:
The typed edits addImport/updateImport/removeImport exist in EditOperation, but there
is no BatchOperation, no verb and so no script member: a CLI caller cannot add, change
or remove a library import by any route. Add a `BatchOperation.importOp` shaped like
`variable` (alias, path; remove), a `woodcase imports set/rm` verb pair beside `vars`,
and `doc.imports.set(alias, path)` / `doc.imports.rm(alias)` on the host. Same
transaction, same log event kind (`import` already exists in ActivityEvent.Kind), same
three-line echo. Read the import-namespaces article (PenImportNamespaces.md) first: an
alias in use by a ref refuses removal the way vars rm refuses a referenced variable.

criteria.label: An import can be added, changed and removed from the CLI, from a batch and from a script, each logged as an import event
Removing an alias a ref still uses is refused with a sentence naming the instances, in every route

data.title: Agent trial of the host
data.description:
Run a Sonnet-class agent in a worktree against a task of the Quill shape on a copy of
a real file: build a list from a template, fan out twelve rows, measure for overflow
after layout, fix what overflows, and lint clean. Its only teaching is `woodcase help
design` and `woodcase help js`; every route is available (cp --each, apply, find, js)
and it may use any tool it likes. Record which route it reached for at each step and
why, every sentence the host threw and whether the sentence was enough, and whether
the activity log accounts for every byte the file changed by (walk the file's
revision lineage and check for external events). Findings land as
project/2026-MM-DD-scripting-host-trial.md; each sentence that was not enough
becomes an issue-tree entry.

criteria.label: The finding doc records, step by step, which route the agent used and whether anything left the tool, with transcript excerpts
Every out-of-band write during the trial appears as an external event in the log
Each host sentence the agent could not act on is filed as an issue with the sentence quoted

data.title: Decide what the batch surface keeps
data.description:
Decision, informed by the trial's finding: does any verb-side loop surface — apply
and its JSONL wire form, cp --each — go unused with js and find available, and is the
primer simpler without it? The default is to keep everything; a retirement needs the
trial's evidence as its note. If a surface is retired: BatchApplier, BatchOperation,
BatchReport and the guard machinery stay as the planner the host and verbs share;
WoodcaseBatches.md is rewritten as the library-level article; the recipes that used
the surface become scripts under the extraction test; a grep test in the style of
VendorWordsTests proves no caller-facing text still names it. Record the ruling here
and in project/backlog.md whichever way it goes.

criteria.label: The ruling is recorded as a note on this leaf citing the trial doc
If anything is retired, no caller-facing text names it and the recipes that used it run as scripts
The full suite and swiftformat lint pass

git shows every move as a rename with no content change, and the full suite passes unchanged

Done directly by the integrator at 0dc0372. 100 sources into Verbs/ (32), Options/ (22), Reports/ (19), Failures/ (7), Help/ (4), Shot/ (9), Lookup/ (5), Hosting/ (2); 90 tests mirror them, with the process-driving harness (CommandFixture, ChildProcess, CommandRun, PenFileProbe, CommandFixtureTests) in Support/ — the plan named no home for files that test no type. Fixtures/ stays where it was.

Deviation from criterion 2: not a pure content-free move. Six tests locate fixtures relative to #filePath (ShotOverlaySnapshotTests, CommandFixture, CommandFailureTests, ThemesCommandTests, VendorWordsTests, EditingErrorRemedyTests) and each gained one deletingLastPathComponent(); git still records all 190 as renames. Two docs naming old paths were updated (WoodcasePerformance.md, the plan doc). Nothing resisted grouping. Suite: 3748 tests passed in 44.9 s (swift test --quiet); swiftformat lint clean.

data.text: Sequencing ruling (integrator, 2026-09-07): this leaf waits for the un-pin (111nTf) to land on main rather than running in parallel with it. Both rewrite the body of PenFileTransaction.run (unpin: isolation parameter replacing MainActor.run at lines 233 and 288; this leaf: the lineage check after the parse) and both edit UndoCommand.swift (unpin strips a @MainActor at line 132; this leaf moves its body into the library). Same functions, so a genuine conflict, not a distant-region merge. It runs in parallel with host-core instead.

Two phases: (A) the agent un-pins Woodcase in its worktree; the integrator merges to main; (B) the same agent then fixes Penumbra in place against main and runs its tests. data.text:
Un-pin landed in the worktree. Decisions, in the order they had to be made.

**The caches stay owned by the document.** ExpansionCache, LayoutCache and RevisionCache
lose `@MainActor` *and* their `@unchecked Sendable` extensions. The two went together:
the conformance was only safe because the pin made it so, and asserting it without the
pin would be the lie `nonisolated(unsafe)` is. Non-Sendable is the honest answer — a
cache belongs to the one EditableDocument that made it, and the compiler now enforces
that rather than trusting a comment. Each cache's doc comment says so.

**onRemoteChange stays a plain closure.** No `@Sendable`, no global actor. It is called
synchronously from inside `applyRemote`, in the domain that owns the document, so a view
model may touch its own state from it — the whole point of a change hook. The isolation
boundary sits one step earlier, where a peer's `CRDTOperation` arrives; that is a
Sendable value and always was. Same for CRDTDocument: it is the shadow of a document
that does not travel, so it does not travel either, and `CRDTSnapshot` + `CRDTOperation`
remain the only two things that cross. Both facts are now written into the DocC
(EditingDocuments "Who owns a document", CRDTArchitecture "Snapshots and State
Transfer") rather than living in a `@MainActor` attribute.

**PenFileTransaction.** All three entry points take
`isolation: isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation` and a plain, non-`@Sendable` body; both
`MainActor.run` hops are gone. The CLI still lands on main because
`WoodcaseCommand.main()` is `@MainActor` — that annotation is now the *only* thing
putting a verb on the main actor, and its doc comment says so.

**The tests' isolation stance.** Main-actor test suites stay main-actor: main-actor code
may own a non-isolated, non-Sendable object, so the 210 `@MainActor` marks in Tests are
mostly fine as they are. I removed exactly four, all of them helpers taking an
`EditableDocument` that were pinned only because the library was, and that a nonisolated
async caller could no longer reach: ActivityCommandTests.renameOperation,
ActivityRecorderTests.renameOperation, PenFileTransactionTests.rename,
PenFileTransactionDryRunTests.rename.

**One test's expectation genuinely changed.** EditableDocumentSnapshotTests' "Concurrent
materializeSnapshot calls do not crash" fired 100 concurrent calls at one document from
a task group. That no longer compiles, by design — it is precisely the thing the missing
Sendable conformance refuses. It is replaced by "repeated materializeSnapshot calls
agree", and the compile-time answer it used to hope for at runtime now lives in
EditingIsolationTests. The other four cases in that file lost their `MainActor.run`
wrappers, which had become boundary crossings.

**Two things `nonisolated(unsafe)` would have bought, and what I did instead.**
CommandFailure's `private static let noDocument = EditableDocument(...)` became a
computed property returning a fresh empty document — a shared instance of a non-Sendable
class is exactly the global mutable state the un-pin is meant to make visible, and an
empty document is a handful of empty dictionaries. `EditableDocument.materializeSnapshot`
kept its "do the tree walk off the owner's isolation" promise by taking the snapshot on
the caller's isolation and handing the Sendable `FlatStoreSnapshot` to a detached task.

**Toolchain bug worth knowing.** Swift 6.3.3 refuses `Task.detached` written inside a
function that takes an `isolated (any Actor)?` parameter: *"pattern that the
region-based isolation checker does not understand how to check. Please file a bug"*.
Hoisting the detach into a `nonisolated static` helper one call out compiles and changes
nothing about what runs where. Recorded in project/gotchas.md.

**A real bug the un-pin uncovered, fixed here.** ViewerCopyChipBrowserTests failed 3/3
full runs on this branch and 0/2 on main. Not a flake and not scheduling luck: with the
library off the main actor, the browser suites stop being serialized by main-actor
saturation, and the copy-chip test's two ambient dependencies both broke. (1)
`navigator.clipboard.writeText` does not reject on an unfocused document — it returns a
promise that never settles — so `ViewerScript`'s unguarded `await` swallowed the copy
and never reached its own execCommand fallback. Fixed at the source with a
`document.hasFocus()` guard and a 500 ms deadline on the race, with a regression test
that stubs a hung promise. (2) The test polled for a 1.2 s flash through an `evaluate`
round trip whose latency it does not own. It now has the page record the flash with a
MutationObserver, and stubs the clipboard seam rather than asserting the state of the
machine's front window — which also lets it assert, for the first time, *what* was
copied.

Soak result, and the twenty minutes it took to believe it.

`scripts/soak-tests 3 --load 6 --timeout 280` gave **1/3** on the branch and **3/3** on
main run minutes later in the same worktree, and the sample of a timed-out test host had
no Woodcase frames at all — the 2026-08-31 "third face", which reads as an unresumable
await. It is not one. At `--timeout 600` the branch is **3/3** (199.5 s, 586.0 s,
76.1 s). The browser tests' `waitFor` polls with `Task.sleep`; a sleeping task has no
thread, so a slow phase and a wedged one look identical in a sample.

With every WebKit-dependent test skipped (`--skip Browser --skip WebView --skip Viewer`),
three loaded runs each: branch 56.3 / 56.8 / 57.6 s, main 58.4 / 57.7 / 56.7 s. Our own
code costs nothing. The whole difference is a tail in the WebKit tests — full-suite wall
clock under `--load 6`: main 75, 77, 223, 66, 68, 68 s; branch 73, 81, 199, 268, 278,
586 s plus two runs cut at the 280 s watchdog. One WebView regression case took 228 s in
a slow run against about 30 s in a fast one.

Best-supported reading, stated as such in the finding: the pin was an accidental
*throttle*. Page building used to take turns with WebKit's main-thread work on one actor;
un-pinned it runs on the pool in parallel, and on a machine already saturated by six
spinners it takes CPU the WebKit main thread had to itself. In production that is the
change working — page building no longer blocks the main thread. Nothing was changed for
it. Full numbers, method and what is *not* proven:
project/2026-09-07-unpinning-and-the-loaded-soak.md.

Two things for whoever runs the next soak: `--timeout 280` sits inside that tail on this
machine, so use 600; and a sample with no frames of ours does not prove a hang. Both are
in project/gotchas.md. Raising the script's default watchdog is a candidate, unowned.

Done in the worktree; not committed, not closed (per the brief). Final state: build with
no new warnings (the 85 SendableMetatypes lines in WoodcaseViewer/Previews/PreviewState.swift
are pre-existing — verified by touching that file and building unmodified main, same 85),
`swiftformat . --lint --config <worktree>/.swiftformat` clean, `swift test --quiet` green
at 3753 tests in 389 suites.

Also fixed while here: the three ``PenFileTransaction/run(...)`` and ``read(...)`` DocC
symbol links, which the added `isolation:` label would have broken and which two of them
were already broken by a missing `effect:`.
