data.title: Font and image downloads honor the proxy environment
data.description: URLSessionDataFetcher uses URLSession.shared, which on macOS ignores HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY. Inside the Claude Code sandbox the only egress is an authenticated HTTP proxy given in those variables (http://user:pass@localhost:<port>), so every Google Font download (and remote image fetch) fails and text falls back to the system face. Also: GoogleFontResolver.fetchMetadataWithLicense swallows every error, so a blocked network reads as "family not found". Fix: honor the proxy environment (including basic auth credentials and NO_PROXY) in the production fetcher, and make the fallback diagnostic distinguish a network failure from an unknown family.

criteria.label: The production fetcher routes through HTTPS_PROXY with credentials, respecting NO_PROXY
A network failure is reported differently from an unknown family
woodcase render fetches an uncached Google family inside the Claude Code sandbox

data.text:
Root cause established (2026-09-26), three stacked failures inside the Claude Code Bash sandbox, probed with a standalone swiftc binary run sandboxed:

1. URLSession.shared ignores HTTPS_PROXY and goes direct: fails NSURLErrorDomain -1003 (cannot find host) — the sandbox has no DNS (com.apple.dnssd.service is not in the Seatbelt mach-lookup allowlist).
2. A proxy host of "localhost" cannot be resolved for the same reason (connectionProxyDictionary -> kCFErrorDomainCFNetwork 310; Network ProxyConfiguration -> -1003). curl works only because it hard-codes localhost. With 127.0.0.1 the proxy is reached; ProxyConfiguration.applyCredential (or a delegate answering the isProxy 407 Basic challenge) authenticates and CONNECT succeeds.
3. TLS server-trust evaluation then fails: NSURLErrorDomain -1202, SecTrustEvaluateWithError -> errSecInternalComponent (-26276), even offline with a basic X509 policy on github's real chain. Cause: the Claude Code Seatbelt profile only allows mach-lookup "com.apple.trustd.agent" when settings `sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation: true`. Proven with sandbox-exec outside the session sandbox: `(allow default)(deny mach-lookup (global-name "com.apple.trustd.agent"))` reproduces -26276; `(allow default)` evaluates ok. curl works because it verifies with LibreSSL against /etc/ssl/cert.pem, no trustd.

So criterion 3 cannot be met in-process with Apple TLS under the default sandbox; it needs the user setting (or a non-Apple TLS stack / curl subprocess). Plan: env proxy support (loopback-literal host, credentials, NO_PROXY) + typed network failure reasons, including a distinct "certificate trust service unavailable" reason.

## Fix: unthemed artboards render in every theme combination

Root cause: `ThemeCombination.frameMatches` treated an unthemed frame (`theme` nil/empty)
as matching only a *default* combination (first option of each axis) whenever a
`defaultCombination` was supplied — and `RenderCommand` supplied one whenever there was
more than one combination. So a document with a two-option `mode` axis and an unthemed
top-level frame rendered light only; the dark pass found zero matching frames and hit
`guard !frames.isEmpty else { continue }`.

Fix: an unthemed frame now matches *every* combination unconditionally. A themed frame
still matches only combinations whose values agree with every entry in `theme`. Removed
`defaultCombination` entirely — both the parameter on `frameMatches` and the
`ThemeCombination.defaultCombination(from:)` function, plus `RenderCommand`'s
`defaultCombo` computation — since nothing needs "the default combination" as a concept
once "unthemed = matches all" no longer has an exception.

### Tests (Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/Verbs/RenderCommandTests.swift)
- "An unthemed artboard renders once per combination of a two-option axis" — new fixture
  `render-theme-unthemed-only.pen` (one unthemed frame, `mode: [light, dark]`). Watched it
  fail against the pre-fix code: only 1 file total, `dark/` never created (the exact bug
  shape). Passes after the fix (2 files, one per combo).
- "A themed artboard renders only in matching combinations" — new fixture
  `render-theme-axis.pen` (unthemed `Screen` + `Special` pinned to `mode: dark`). Pre-fix:
  `dark/` held one un-suffixed file (only `Special` matched, `Screen` was excluded because
  `dark != defaultCombo`). Post-fix: `light/` holds exactly `Screen`'s render, `dark/`
  holds both `Screen`'s and `Special`'s.

### Existing tests changed (Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/Options/ThemeCombinationTests.swift)
Removed because they exercised the API being deleted (`defaultCombination:` parameter /
`ThemeCombination.defaultCombination(from:)`), not because their expectations were
loosened:
- `nilThemeMatchesDefault`, `emptyThemeMatchesDefault` — asserted the *old*, buggy
  contract ("unthemed matches only the default combo when one is given"). That contract
  is exactly what this leaf removes.
- `defaultCombination()`, `defaultCombinationNil()`, `defaultCombinationEmpty()` — tested
  the now-deleted `defaultCombination(from:)` function directly.

Reworded (same expectation, updated docstring/wording since "when no default specified"
no longer parses — there is no default parameter any more):
- `nilThemeMatchesAll` → "Frame with nil theme matches every combination"
- `emptyThemeMatchesAll` → "Frame with empty theme matches every combination"

Added:
- `nilThemeMatchesEveryMultiAxisCombination` — unit-level check that an unthemed frame
  matches all 4 combinations of a two-axis document. (This one was already green under
  the pre-fix code in isolation, because the pre-fix bug only bites when `RenderCommand`
  passes a non-nil `defaultCombination`; a bare `frameMatches` call with no default was
  never buggy. Said so rather than passing it off as a red test — the real red coverage
  for this leaf is the two `RenderCommandTests` above.)

## Fix: render keeps reusable definitions visible, and keepReusables becomes a typed enum

Root cause: `RenderCommand.swift` called `PenRefExpander.expand(document)` with the
default `keepReusables: false`, stripping reusable definitions before layout. Every
other design-canvas reader (`shot`, `tree`/`SettledTree`, `NodeLookup`, the viewer's
`RenderCache`) passes `keepReusables: true` explicitly. A definition placed directly in
visible flow — the pilot's actual failure — got no rect and never drew, while `shot` and
`tree` showed it fine.

Fix, two parts:

1. `RenderCommand` now expands with the new `.canvas` purpose (see below), matching the
   other design-canvas verbs.
2. Replaced the `keepReusables: Bool` parameter on `PenRefExpander.expand(_:keepReusables:)`
   with `PenRefExpander.expand(_:for:)`, nesting a new `PenRefExpander.Purpose` enum:
   - `.canvas` — design-canvas reading/rendering (`shot`, `tree`, `render`, the viewer).
     Definitions stay in the tree and get a rect like any artboard.
   - `.export` — code generation or export. Definitions are stripped: only their `ref`
     instances belong in generated output. **This is the default**, unchanged from the
     old `keepReusables: false` default — chosen deliberately because most callers
     (every test in `PenRefExpanderTests.swift` that calls the bare `expand(doc)`, plus
     `EditableDocument.expandedDocument()` via `EditableDocument+Layout.swift`'s
     `computeLayout(textMeasurer:)`) rely on stripping as the *implicit* default and are
     out of scope here — the brief says not to change what non-render callers do, and
     `computeLayout`'s strip-by-default is itself a documented, separate known issue
     (`Sources/Woodcase/Editing/RootOverlap.swift`'s doc comment), not something to fix
     as a side effect of a rename.

All non-render callers that previously passed `keepReusables: true` now pass
`for: .canvas` with identical behavior — nothing changed for them but the spelling.

- "A reusable definition in visible flow appears in render output" — new fixture
  `render-reusable-visible.pen`: one plain frame (`Screen`) plus a top-level
  `reusable: true` frame (`Component`) with its own children, sitting directly in
  visible flow (no `ref` anywhere — this is the pilot's exact shape: the first visible
  instance of a component *was* the definition). Watched it fail pre-fix: `Component`
  never appeared, `Rendered 1 file(s)` instead of 2. Passes after the fix.

Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-26): build the curl fallback. On macOS only (#if os(macOS)), when a fetch fails with NetworkFailure.Reason.certificateTrustUnavailable, retry the same URL with /usr/bin/curl, which reads the proxy variables itself and verifies with its own CA bundle. data.text:
Split GoogleFontResolver.swift (616 lines) into five files along its real seams, all in
Sources/Woodcase/GoogleFonts/:

- GoogleFontResolver.swift (282 lines): class decl, shared/init, State, resolve(family:),
  prepareFonts (x2), prepareCachedFonts, fallbackNoticeCount. Left `public static let
  shared = GoogleFontResolver(cache: GoogleFontCache(), fetcher: URLSessionDataFetcher())`
  untouched per the brief's concurrency constraint.
- GoogleFontResolver+Registration.swift (170 lines): resolveFromCache, markPlaced,
  CachedFont, resolveCached, cacheFallbackNoticeCount, logCacheFallbackOnce,
  registerFont(at:)/registerFont(data:).
- GoogleFontResolver+Fallback.swift (104 lines): fallbackMessage, cacheIsUnreadable,
  reportFallback, downloadFailureMessage.
- GoogleFontResolver+Metadata.swift (61 lines): fetchMetadata, fetchMetadataWithLicense,
  notFoundStatus, fetchFailure.
- GoogleFontResolver+FamilyCollection.swift (42 lines): the two collectFontFamilies
  overloads (document-tree walk).

Loosened private -> internal (no modifier) on: cache, fetcher, state (stored properties
used from every extension file); resolveCached, CachedFont, registerFont(at:),
registerFont(data:), logCacheFallbackOnce, resolveFromCache (each called from the main
file's resolve()/prepareCachedFonts()); fallbackMessage, reportFallback,
downloadFailureMessage (called from prepareFonts()/prepareCachedFonts()); fetchMetadataWithLicense,
fetchFailure (called from resolve()). Kept private where the only caller stayed in the
same file: markPlaced, cacheIsUnreadable, notFoundStatus, the inner collectFontFamilies
overload. The `State` struct itself stayed private — callers only ever touch `$0.field`
through closures, never name the type.

Pure move: behaviour unchanged, no test edits. Verified with the existing suite
(GoogleFontResolverTests, FontDownloadFailureTests) plus the full `swift test --quiet`
(2648+161+947 tests, 1 pre-existing known issue, all green) and `swiftformat . --lint`
clean. No new tests for this leaf, as the brief said.

One deliberate follow-on from leaf hjzTDr's work touches GoogleFontResolver+Fallback.swift
a second time: downloadFailureMessage's inline `unreachable/httpError` switch was
replaced with the new shared `RemoteFetchError.reasonPhrase` (defined in
Sources/Woodcase/RemoteImages/RemoteFetchError+Explanation.swift) so the two resolvers'
"why the download failed" wording lives in one place. Output text is identical;
GoogleFontResolverTests and FontDownloadFailureTests confirm it.

Made RemoteImageResolver's download warning say why, matching GoogleFontResolver's
phrasing for fonts.

TDD: added Tests/WoodcaseTests/ImageDownloadFailureTests.swift with three tests (mirroring
FontDownloadFailureTests.swift's shape) before touching resolver code:
- unreachable(NetworkFailure) -> warning contains the NetworkFailure.Reason's explanation
- httpError(statusCode: 404) -> warning contains "HTTP 404"
- an arbitrary Error from a custom fetcher -> warning contains NetworkFailure.Reason.other's
  explanation (reads as unreachable, same fallback GoogleFontResolver.fetchFailure uses)
All three failed red on first run (message.contains(...) false against the old
"could not be fetched" text) before the implementation; none was green on arrival.

Implementation, Sources/Woodcase/RemoteImages/RemoteImageResolver.swift:
- State gained `downloadFailures: [String: RemoteFetchError]`.
- resolve(urlString:)'s catch now records `Self.fetchFailure(error)` (new private static
  func, same shape as GoogleFontResolver's: casts to RemoteFetchError or wraps as
  .unreachable(NetworkFailure(classifying:...))) alongside the existing failedURLs insert.
- New private downloadFailureMessage(for:) builds "Image '<url>' could not be downloaded:
  <reason>; the fill will not be drawn", falling back to the old generic sentence only
  when there is no recorded failure (e.g. an unparseable URL that never reached the
  fetcher). prepareImages(for:diagnostics:) now calls it instead of a hardcoded string.
- Left `fetcher: URLSessionDataFetcher()` on `public static let shared` untouched.

Shared the "why" phrasing rather than duplicating it: new
Sources/Woodcase/RemoteImages/RemoteFetchError+Explanation.swift adds
`RemoteFetchError.reasonPhrase` (the unreachable/httpError switch, one clause). Placed
beside RemoteImageResolver (RemoteImages/, not Networking/, per the brief) because the
wording is a decision the two callers make together, not one RemoteFetchError itself
should own. GoogleFontResolver+Fallback.swift's downloadFailureMessage now calls
`failure.reasonPhrase` instead of repeating the switch — same output, confirmed by

Updated Sources/Woodcase/Documentation.docc/PenRemoteImages.md's Failures section to

data.title: Font staging honours $TMPDIR inside the sandbox
data.description: GoogleFontResolver.registerFont(data:) (now in GoogleFontResolver+Registration.swift) stages font bytes in FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory before registering them by URL. Found by the curl-fallback agent, which hit the same trap. Check every FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory use in Sources/ for the same issue.

Findings so far (pen-report):
- 1.2.14 writes version "2.19" (app.asar index.js c8="2.19"; shipped skill pen-schema.md). Schema delta vs 2.17: shadow `spread` removed; new `browser` node. Validator-only root keys `fonts` and top-level `connection` nodes predate 2.19 (present in CLI 0.3.5's 2.17 engine).

Bugs: bg blur composites a vertically mirrored backdrop (PenEffectRenderer.swift:354-367), sigma=radius (Pen sigma=radius/2), blurs in linear light, ignores Pen's "no fill -> no blur" and "opacity<1 -> no blur". Layer blur sigma is radius px regardless of scale (right only @2x). Inner shadow order differs (Pen: fills, inner shadow, stroke, children).
- CoreImage blur silently no-ops inside the Bash sandbox.
- Woodcase write downgrades version 2.19->2.17 (PenParser.swift:86) so 1.2.14 re-migrates inner->outer: real data corruption. Unknown keys on known nodes, root `fonts`, dropped. Unknown effect type -> hard decode failure. browser node -> 0x0 inert layout box. lint exits 1 on every 2.19 file.

data.text:
Fixed: `GoogleFontResolver.registerFont(data:)` staged font bytes via
`FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`, which ignores `$TMPDIR` on macOS and resolves
to `/var/folders/.../T` — a directory the Claude Code Bash sandbox denies writing to
while it allows `$TMPDIR` (`/tmp/claude-501`) itself.

Added `Sources/Woodcase/Files/ScratchDirectory.swift`: a small enum, modeled on
`WoodcaseHome`, that answers "this process's scratch directory" by reading `$TMPDIR`
from an injectable environment and falling back to `FileManager`'s own answer when it
is unset or empty. `registerFont(data:environment:)` now routes through it; the
`environment` parameter defaults to `ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment` and exists so
a test can prove the redirection without mutating the real process environment.

Audited every other `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` use under `Sources/`:
`registerFont(data:)` was the only production one. (One doc-comment example in
WoodcaseActivityLog.md uses a placeholder variable named `temporaryDirectory`, unrelated.)

Red-first tests, both failing before the fix with `cannot find 'ScratchDirectory' in
scope` / `extra argument 'environment' in call`, green after:
- `Tests/WoodcaseTests/ScratchDirectoryTests.swift` (new suite) — set/empty/unset $TMPDIR.
- `GoogleFontResolverTests.registerFromDataHonoursTMPDIR` — stages bogus TTF bytes under
  an injected $TMPDIR and confirms the file lands there. Deliberately does not use a
  real font family, so it doesn't collide with the "one test may watch a family go
  absent→present" constraint the JetBrains Mono test already owns.

Real-world proof (criterion "Font registration from data works when only $TMPDIR is
writable"), run from a SANDBOXED Bash call after a sandbox-off `swift build`:

    WOODCASE_HOME=<fresh 555 dir> .build/debug/woodcase render tmpdir-proof.pen \
      --output-dir out

Printed `woodcase: cannot write the font cache at .../fonts; caching downloaded fonts
in memory for this process instead.`, exited 0, and wrote a PNG that is visibly set in
Lobster's cursive face (not the SF Pro fallback) — proving the memory-fallback
registration reached CoreText even though the disk cache directory was read-only.

Sources/Woodcase/GoogleFonts/GoogleFontResolver+Registration.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/ScratchDirectoryTests.swift (new),

data.text:
Diagnosed from pen-oracle renders (probe fixtures in scratch, red→blue ramps fitted per pixel): Pen lays out every gradient type in the node's normalised box. Local gradient space → scale(size.w, size.h) → rotate CCW-on-screen by `rotation` → translate to `center` (fraction) → stretch to the box. Linear: stop 0 at (0, .5), stop 1 at (0, -.5); size.width ignored. Radial: radius 0.5 (rotation matters with non-uniform size — Woodcase ignored it). Angular: t = (atan2(q) + 90°)/360, start up, clockwise; stops outside [first,last] pad. Woodcase was computing linear length/angle and angular angle in pixel space. Fix: PenFill.PenGradientFill.frameTransform(in:) (new file Rendering/PenFill+GradientFrame.swift) + PenFillRenderer draws in that frame; angular bitmap now at device resolution. New fixture render-gradient-geometry.pen (36 boards) with Pen 1x/2x refs: all MAE ≤ 0.45 after.
Green on first run (red phase): lin-*-r0 and lin-*-r90 on all three boxes, ang-sq-r0/r45/r90/r210 (square boxes don't expose the stretch); the frame unit tests and all other cases were red.

Pen's per-side stroke (measured on 2x renders; Pen's re-save drops strokeAlignment "center" → centre is the default): band runs k·w outside to (1−k)·w inside, k = 0/.5/1. Square corners stay square (ring corners filled). Rounded corner r: inner edge elliptical radii max(0, r − (1−k)·w_axis); outer edge circular r + k·min(adjacent widths), except centred when r < ½·min → ½·min (Pen's uniform centred strokes do the same: r6 w16 → outer radius 8). Implemented as an even-odd ring in PenStrokeRenderer+PerSide.swift for frame/rectangle/browser (roundedBox passed from PenRenderer). Ellipse/path per-side is NOT modelled — Pen draws an ellipse with per-side widths as a uniform thin stroke, Woodcase keeps its inner bands fallback (documented). New fixture render-per-side-strokes.pen (26 boards) with Pen 2x refs; test compares band edges along 19 rows × 18 columns within 0.5 pt, plus MAE < 1.
Green on first run: the square inner cases (mixed/sides/top/even/rect-inner) — old code already drew inner bands correctly; radius-inner and corners-inner were red (inner corners).

Typed mesh model done in worktree meshmodel (wt/meshmodel), uncommitted. PenMeshPoint (.bare/.object, Vector/Object/Handles, defaults(columns:rows:), canonicalized(defaults:)), PenFill.PenMeshGradientFill split to PenFill+MeshGradientFill.swift, PenValueForm.arrayOf for the schema row, mesh point nested table. Fixtures: render-mesh-gradients.pen (+ .pen-saved.pen), mesh-point-elision.pen (+ .pen-saved.pen) from pen-oracle / pen 0.3.9. Measured elision rule: handle dropped when |written - default| < 1e-4 per component, judged before rounding; values round to 4 dp. Golden round-trip compares modulo key order and `version` (PenParser stamps 2.17). Full suite green (swift test --quiet), swiftformat lint clean. Criteria POC and ZBu met (not marked; integrator's call).

data.text:
Cause established (linter, 2026-09-26). The premise "tree/render/shot resolve imports" is wrong: NOTHING in Woodcase resolves a document's declared `imports` from the file. SettledTree (tree, lint, scripting, overlap), ShotCommand, NodeLookup, EditableDocument+Expansion and the viewer's RenderCache all go materialize -> PenRefExpander.expand with no import stage. `tree banking.pen banking-home/header` shows `ref bellBtn 378,46 0x0 E97qI` - the instance of V:u4Spp settles to nothing, exactly what lint says.

Only `render --library` and `generate --library` call PenImportResolver, through WoodcaseCommandCore/Lookup/LibraryResolver.swift - and that is broken too: it keys each library by `lastPathComponent` minus extension ("kit.lib"), while PenImportResolver looks libraries up by the import path as written ("kit.lib.pen"), so the lookup misses and the import is silently skipped. Proof: `woodcase render banking.pen --library kit.lib.pen` and `woodcase render banking.pen` write byte-identical banking-home PNGs (md5 49fc67e1a70945ad76387810eb64e216 both). No test covers --library.

So lint is not wrong relative to the renderer today: every renderer draws those 5 instances as nothing. The fix belongs to the shared read path, which is exactly backlog.md "2026-08-29 - --library on the read verbs" (parked; its un-park condition - someone lints a real library-based document and has to be told the errors are not real - has now fired).

Findings breakdown (24 errors): 5 broken-ref, all V: (V:u4Spp, V:DFkNc, V:IbYvu, V:Vo8Mo, V:ynZzl); 11 override-target-not-found keyed through V: (M7RGT/V:Xxvji x4, Qh9Dq/q9NGq/V:EpasF x2, q9NGq/V:EpasF, sXaY2/V:exTZA x2, sXaY2/V:XAn1t x2) - import-caused; 8 override-target-not-found on the two theme instances #YGJ0d/#8ruxp keyed bare kit ids (2592p, G6llC, T2IOh, WKey6) with no V: prefix - these name nodes that live only in kit.lib.pen, unprefixed, so they are probably real stale overrides even after resolution (unverified until resolution exists).

Not implemented: the fix is an architectural choice across the read path (where libraries load, where they attach - EditableDocument read-time context vs a parameter on SettledTree/findings/TreeView - and every expansion site incl. WoodcaseViewer, which this brief puts off limits). Stopped for a ruling per CLAUDE.md "architectural -> ask".

CONFIRMED in Pen.app 1.2.14 (linter, 2026-09-26): Pen strips text stroke, underline and strikethrough on load and draws none of them.

Probe: one 400x300 frame (layout none) with four Inter 40pt text nodes - control; "stroked" (fill #FFFFFF, stroke #FF0000, strokeWidth 4, strokeAlignment outer); "underlined" (underline: true); "struck" (strikethrough: true). File kept at <worktree>/local/rjt7to/probe.pen (gitignored; not committed - Pen output is not vendored).

1. Pen.app 1.2.14 (/Applications/Pen.app, CFBundleShortVersionString 1.2.14, running), sandbox off:
   open -a Pen local/rjt7to/probe-app.pen
   pen interactive --app desktop --in local/rjt7to/probe-app.pen < app.txt
   where app.txt = get_app_state(); execute Get(n => text nodes -> Print(JSON)); execute Export(['board'],'png',<dir>,{scale:1}); save(); exit()
   - Get printed tStk as {type,id,x,y,name,fill:"#FFFFFF",content,fontFamily,fontSize,fontWeight:"normal"} - no stroke, strokeWidth or strokeAlignment. tUnd has no underline key, tStr no strikethrough key.
   - The exported PNG shows "Control", an empty band where "Stroked" sits (white text on white, no red outline), "Underlined" with no underline, "Struck" with no strike line.
   - save() wrote version "2.19"; grep for underline|strikethrough|stroke in the saved file matches only the two node *names*.
2. Headless engine (pen CLI, /opt/homebrew/bin/pen): printf ... | pen interactive --in probe.pen --out headless-saved.pen with save() -> the saved 2.19 file carries none of the three keys either (same shape as above).

So all three cases are real; none is exempted from the lint.

Pen evidence for the mesh cases (linter, 2026-09-26). Headless pen CLI, sandbox off:
  pen interactive --in local/JXbZb2/mesh-probe.pen --out local/JXbZb2/mesh-saved.pen < mesh.txt
  (Get -> Print each frame's fill after load; Export all to PNG at 1x; save()). Probe files under <worktree>/local/JXbZb2/ (gitignored).

After load, as Pen's Get reports it, and what the export draws:
- 2x2 control                                  -> kept; draws the 4-colour mesh.
- colours #F00F-style (#RGBA)                  -> kept verbatim; draws NOTHING (transparent). Ruling confirmed.
- colours #F00-style (#RGB)                    -> kept; draws identically to the 6-digit control.
- 3 points for a 2x2 grid                      -> the whole fill is REMOVED on load (fill undefined; save() writes no fill).
- 3 colours for a 2x2 grid                     -> the whole fill is REMOVED on load.
- rows: 1 (2 points, 2 colours)                -> kept; draws nothing.
- a point written [1] (one number)             -> kept as [1, null]; the whole mesh draws nothing.
- a point written "oops" (not an array/object) -> replaced by its default grid position [1, 1]; draws like the control.
- the report's folded 2x2 (mfold)              -> kept; draws the folded, partly uncovered shape.

Decision 9 (a malformed mesh point fails Woodcase's whole-file decode): Pen never refuses the file - it repairs or keeps the point, and at worst the one fill draws nothing. So failing the decode is stricter than Pen and makes a file Pen opens unreadable to every Woodcase verb, lint included. Recommendation: decode a malformed point as a preserved raw value (a PenMeshPoint case carrying the JSON as written, round-tripped verbatim per ruling 4 "preserve only"), have the tessellator treat it the way Pen does (non-array -> default grid position; wrong-length array -> draw nothing), and report it as a mesh-gradient-dropped lint finding. NOT implemented here: it adds a case to the public PenMeshPoint enum (and makes `position` partial), which the in-flight tessellator leaf OHdROl consumes, so it wants the same coordination CIcquU's .unknown cases get.

Leaf 6 (Pen oracle scripts + Core Image sandbox gotcha): built and verified.

New files:
- scripts/pen-validate — round-trips a .pen through `pen interactive` (save()), reports
  PASS/FAIL with the validator's own messages, and on PASS diffs the re-saved JSON against
  the input (generic structural diff, ignoring fileToken). Tested against
  Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/blur1.pen (PASS) and parser-unknown-properties.pen (FAIL).
- scripts/blur-sigma-fit — Swift script, fits Gaussian sigma of a blurred edge in a PNG by
  grid-search least squares against the erf edge model, in sRGB and linear light, with a
  --radius/--scale check against Pen's radius/2 convention (the Gusv9b criterion). Verified
  against a synthetic CIGaussianBlur ground truth (recovers a known radius=10 to 10.055px,
  and the true edge center, when fit in the colorspace the blur actually ran in) and against
  Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/blur1.png.
- scripts/README.md — both documented with worked examples (real invocations, real output).

Significant finding, outside this leaf's scope, flagged for the integrator: the installed
`pen` CLI is now 0.3.9 (was 0.3.5 when the compat report was written), and it already
serialises `"version": "2.19"` on a plain save() and reproduces the 2.17->2.19 migration
(inner shadow -> outer, spread dropped) on parser-effect-variants.pen — i.e. checks 1-2 of
the report's "What a 0.3.9 CLI upgrade has to show" list already hold. Worth a dedicated
pass to run checks 3-4 (spread refusal on Insert, export match) and update the report's
"which engine produced which evidence" section if they hold too — CLI 0.3.9 may already be
a valid headless oracle for leaves 4-6, not just the app.

Gotcha entry drafted (not written — gotchas.md is integrator-owned per the brief) and
reported to the caller: "Core Image fails silently inside the Claude Code Bash sandbox."
Verified directly: `~/.swiftpm/bin/woodcase render Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/blur1.pen
--scale 1` exits 0 both in and out of the sandbox, but in the sandbox the red/blue seam at
row 100 is a hard, unblurred step (RGBA 255,128,128 -> 128,128,255, blur-sigma-fit fits
sigma ~0.05px) while sandbox-off the same command produces a real blurred edge (sigma
~12px in sRGB, matching a gradual transition over x~90-140).

Full report (verification commands/output, deviations, brief critique) delivered via
SubagentHandback to the dispatching agent.

test in question (`fontCacheIsUnderWoodcaseHome`) runs `tree`, not `shot` — it must have
been rewritten sometime after the issue was filed. `tree` goes through `SettledTree`,
which calls `GoogleFontResolver.prepareCachedFonts` (the offline half: system + disk
cache only, no GitHub fetch) rather than `shot`'s `prepareFonts`. Manually confirmed:
`tree` over font-missing.pen produces the exact fallback message the test asserts, with
zero files ever written under $WOODCASE_HOME/fonts — no METADATA.pb probes, no 404s.

`Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/shot-component-addressing.pen`, purpose-built for
addressing (a reusable definition + two named refs, one nested text child), with no
`fontFamily` at all — falls back to `PenTextMeasurer.defaultFontFamily` ("SF Pro"),
resolved from CoreText's system list and never handed to GoogleFontResolver. Repointed
all 6 tests in ShotComponentTests.swift at it, preserving the original test intent
(definition addressing, ref-expansion addressing, descendant addressing, --outline,
the "no node given" listing). Verified each of the 6 scenarios by hand against the
binary with a single shared scratch $WOODCASE_HOME before touching the Swift test file,
then again through the full `swift test --filter WoodcaseCommandTests` run — zero files

scans every `@Test` in Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests that runs `shot` or `render`, and for
every fixture it loads (via CommandFixture(fixture:) or .copy(fixture:)), asserts the
.pen file names no fontFamily at all. This is the CLI-test analogue of
HermeticNetworkTests (which scans test *sources* for forbidden network types) — it
exists because a CommandFixture test never names GoogleFontResolver itself; the
subprocess it launches does. Verified TDD-red first by temporarily restoring the
pre-fix ShotComponentTests.swift (git show HEAD:...) and confirming the guard flagged
exactly the 6 known offending call sites (banking.pen×3 Inter, woodcase-app.pen×3
$font-primary), then green after restoring the fix.

data.text:
mesher: tessellator + rasterizer built in Sources/Woodcase/Rendering/Mesh/ (pure Swift, no CG), tests in Tests/WoodcaseTests/Mesh/ (6 suites, 43 tests).

Design: PenMeshGrid(fill) validates (Invalidity enum = Pen's drop rules) -> PenMeshTessellator.tessellate(grid, width:, height:) in device px -> PenMeshRasterizer.rasterize -> PenMeshRaster (premultiplied RGBA8 sRGB).

Adaptive subdivision: Filip-Magedson-Markot bound, error <= 1/8 (Muu hu^2 + 2 Muv hu hv + Mvv hv^2). Geometry tolerance 0.25 device px (control-net second differences, scaled to px); premultiplied colour tolerance 0.5/255 (smoothstep |S'|<=1.5, |S''|<=6, product rule c*alpha). Per patch-column / patch-row max so the lattice is shared: no T-junctions. Colour alone caps near 62 cells; flat single-colour patch = 1 cell.

Seams: fixed-point 1/256 px, exact Int64 edge functions, top-left rule. Mutation check: forcing one edge bias to inclusive makes PenMeshSeamTests fail (8 issues). Found and fixed on the way: a 4-weight bilinear colour blend gave 0.49999 for a uniform alpha 0.5 mesh (127 vs 128 at some pixels); nested lerp keeps uniform colours exact.

Red run: every test failed or crashed on stubs except "A grid without patches tessellates to nothing" (stub returned .empty, so it was green during red).

Perf (swiftc -O standalone harness, load average ~235-290, so inflated): 4x4 mesh 400x400: tessellate 7 ms, total 17 ms, 17k triangles; 2000x2000: tessellate 26 ms, total ~500 ms wall, ~250 ms CPU, 55k triangles. Unmeasured on a quiet machine.

Red/green so far (keeper):
- Red: 48 new tests (PenExtrasDecodingTests, PenExtrasEditingTests, PenLayoutUnknownNodeTests, PreservedExtrasCommandTests). 38 failed red. Green on first run, by design: PenExtras encode/keys (implemented before the run), root-authoring refusal (PenDocument Codable written with the skeleton), and regression guards for pre-existing behaviour (unknown fill/effect type refused in authoring, ref keys stay rootOverrides, unknown node keeps properties, unsized unknown node is 0x0, modelled-only node has no extras). Two CLI refusal tests first passed for the wrong reason (the fixture failed to decode, and stderr contained "fil"e / "preserved"-extras.pen); tightened, re-run red.
- Brief premise wrong: authoring input was NOT refused before this leaf. `add` with {"fil":…} silently dropped the key (checked on main's build). Strict authoring is new behaviour here.
- Stroke is five sibling keys in 2.17, not a payload struct: "stroke-level extras" = extras on the stroke's paint (a PenFill), covered by fill extras.
- Default mode is FILE (no userInfo = capture). Authoring is opt-in at PenSubtreeDecoder and NodePropertyCodec.checkAuthored (set + cp props). Reason: undo log, CRDT ops, codec round trips and override merges all re-decode Woodcase's own output and must keep extras.

clipper: seam built, even-odd fixed. PenFillRenderer.renderFills(_:clip:fillRule:domain:in:imageProvider:) — clip = CGPath + CGPathFillRule, domain = node box CGRect. Old renderFills(_:path:) removed; PenRenderer's solid-only renderFillsEvenOdd deleted; PenShapeBuilder.fillRule(for:) names the rule.
Pen probe (render-fill-domains.pen, pen-oracle 2x): Pen puts linear stops on the node box edges for donut, even-odd path, hexagon, triangle, quarter arc, overshooting curve, viewBox path. Woodcase before: donut/even-odd drew nothing (MAE 23-30), polygons/arcs/viewBox domain too narrow, curve domain too wide (boundingBox includes control points; stop 0 at -20 vs 20). After: all 10 boards MAE <= 0.13, fitted stops within 0.5 pt.
Criterion 3Ol: 139 existing MAE ids from a full swift test before (155eef2) and after — every one identical to 4 decimals.
Criterion MWw: PenFillDomainTests (donut/even-odd gradient + image + fixture) red before, green after.
Found, not fixed: ellipse with partial sweepAngle AND innerRadius is pie + full inner ellipse, so even-odd fills the inner ellipse outside the pie (PenShapeBuilder).
Doc: project/2026-09-26-fill-clip-and-domain.md.

data.title: An arc donut fills the inner ellipse outside its sweep
data.description: PenShapeBuilder builds an ellipse with both a partial sweepAngle and an innerRadius as a pie plus a FULL inner ellipse; under the even-odd rule the inner ellipse's part outside the pie gets filled. Found by EL9llT (see project/2026-09-26-fill-clip-and-domain.md). Probe Pen's render of an arc-donut (pen-oracle) first, then build the inner arc with the same sweep. Red test first.

data.note: Landed on main (mesh core). 43 new tests, including seam tests (seen red with an inclusive edge rule). Error bound: position 1/4 device px, premultiplied colour 1/2 8-bit step (Filip-Magedson-Markot). Brief corrections: the patches are tensor-product, not Coons; a 2x2 is bilinear only with third-length handles on a parallelogram. Choices to confirm: #RGBA -> opaque black (Pen: transparent black; lint JXbZb2 flags it); columns/rows of 1 = no patches, not invalid. API for NxjNuS/2JchRX is in the agent report: PenMeshGrid(fill) -> PenMeshRasterizer.rasterize(grid,width:height:) -> premultipliedLast sRGB CGImage clipped to path over the node box.

data.title: Two hex colour parsers: PenColorParser and PenMeshColor
data.description: PenMeshColor(hex:) (Rendering/Mesh) re-implements the #RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA grammar of PenColorParser, because PenColorParser returns a CGColor and the mesh core must build on Linux. Two parsers of one grammar drift. Move the grammar into a Foundation-only RGBA value both use (PenColorParser wraps it into a CGColor).

data.text:
Green (keeper): all 48 new tests pass; full `swift test --quiet` green (WoodcaseTests 2806, CommandTests 976, Scripting 446, Viewer 161); `swiftformat . --lint --config <wt>/.swiftformat` clean. DocC: no new warnings in touched pages.
Existing tests changed, with reason:
- StructuredPropertyShapeTests: helper now runs NodePropertyCodec.checkAuthored before setting. `setting` is the replay funnel (undo inverses, CRDT peer writes, codec round trips) so it decodes in file mode and keeps an unknown fill/effect type; the "solid is not a spelling" refusal moved to the authoring check the batch planner runs for set.
- PenSchemaTests.storedKeys: skips the `extras` stored property (it is the bag of unclaimed keys, not a key).
- GoldenParity normalizer: Pen writes width/height on note/prompt/context; unmodelled, so now kept as extras (they were silently dropped before this leaf). Normalizer strips them, documented in its list.
Found: Pen's width/height on note/prompt/context nodes were being lost on every Woodcase write until now.
Not covered (reported): unknown keys inside nested objects below the payload level (gradient stops, shadow offset, per-side strokeWidth object, variable definitions, theme/import maps) are still dropped; cp's path-keyed descendant props skip the authoring check.
Criteria 53b / sXT / 9Va: tests PreservedExtrasCommandTests, PenExtrasEditingTests, PenLayoutUnknownNodeTests — left for the integrator to mark.

Probed with scripts/pen-oracle on Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-arc-donut.pen (5 boards: quarter 0/90/0.5, three-quarter 45/270/0.6, negative 90/-120/0.4, half-thin 200/180/0.85, stroked 0/90/0.5 with a 4pt centre stroke). Pen draws an arc donut as ONE closed ring: outer arc over the sweep, straight cut along the end angle to the inner ellipse, inner arc back, straight cut home. Cuts lie on lines through the centre at the parametric (unit-circle) angle, which is the convention PenShapeBuilder already used. The stroked board shows the four-edge outline directly.
Fix: PenShapeBuilder.ellipsePath builds that ring (full-sweep donut unchanged: two ellipses, even-odd). Red before: MAE 17.6/8.6/10.1/34.0/5.3, inner-outside-sweep pixel filled, 2 subpaths. After: MAE 0.049/0.127/0.051/0.097/0.072 (swift test --filter PenArcDonutTests).

The two parsers were NOT identical: PenColorParser accepted a signed digit string ("#+12345", "#+1234567") because UInt64(_:radix:) takes a leading sign; PenMeshColor refused it (explicit isHexDigit check). Red: the new agreement test failed on exactly those two inputs.
Fix: new Foundation-only PenHexColor (Friendly; four UInt8 channels, init?(_ hex:), unitComponents) is the one grammar. PenColorParser.parse wraps it into a CGColor; PenMeshColor(hex:) maps its unit components. Behaviour change: PenColorParser now refuses signed strings (a bug fix, not a regression). #RGBA still refused by both. Bytes rather than Doubles because the grammar spells bytes; each consumer picks its own float type.

Woodcase side done: PenBrowserPlaceholder is now public, with a public Friendly PenBrowserPlaceholder.Style (fillHex, borderHex, borderWidth, borderAlignment, labelHex, labelSize, labelInset, emptyLabel; static standard; label(for:) for the URL-or-fallback rule) in PenBrowserPlaceholder+Style.swift. render(...) takes style: Style = .standard (stays internal). The old internal statics are gone.
RapidPro side NOT applied (brief: integration note only): RenderNodeProducer+BrowserPlaceholder.swift should read PenBrowserPlaceholder.Style.standard and build its default border as PenNode.BrowserData(...).toRenderStroke(), exactly as Woodcase builds its default border. Exact code is in the tidy agent's report.

meshdraw: renderer integration done in worktree agent-ad3f37a0023a01bd9 (uncommitted). New PenFillRenderer+Mesh.swift; Pen 1x/2x PNGs for render-mesh-gradients.pen committed as fixtures (pen-oracle, pen 0.3.9). Measured MAE vs Pen 0.23-0.38 on every board and scale (pinned per board, +0.02). Finding: the MAE is NOT the adaptive tessellation — it is the mesh core rounding colours where Pen truncates: ~half of RGB samples read +1 step, signed error +0.5/channel, alpha 0, so 3*0.5/4 = 0.37 on every opaque board. PDF: 2x floor, image XObject 240x160 for a 120x80 box. Criterion AJy (MAE <= 0.5) is met by every case; zIJ (XObject) met by PenMeshPDFTests.

data.text: Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-26): no CLI flag. Every read loads the libraries the document's own imports declare, relative to the file, once, as read context (PenFileTransaction load -> EditableDocument non-persisted context -> SettledTree and every expansion site incl. the viewer); retire --library and LibraryResolver. A bare file name (banking.pen's 'kit.lib.pen') is a relative path = sibling; establish with the pen CLI whether Pen falls back anywhere else when the sibling is missing, and mirror it. A missing library is a lint finding, not a failure. The same seam carries the font resolver (ukfIU2) and consumes the typed root fonts from lebBvI.

Pen's import resolution, established with pen 0.3.9 headless (pen interactive --in <host> --out <x>, get_app_state() + a Get visitor), sandbox off, fixtures under the session scratchpad (koyac9-pen/):

1. A bare name is a path relative to the importing file's directory, and only that. host.pen importing {"V":"kit.lib.pen"} with kit.lib.pen beside it: get_app_state lists every V: reusable. The same host in a directory without the sibling, run with the working directory holding kit.lib.pen: "[ERROR] Cannot import 'kit.lib.pen'! Error: ENOENT ... open '<host dir>/kit.lib.pen'", "[ERROR] Invalid ref 'V:b32gU'", "Reusable components: No reusable components found". One path tried; no working-directory or other fallback.
2. Absolute paths and file:// URIs resolve (ABS:Bcmp1 and U:Bcmp1 both listed).
3. A file that is not JSON: "Cannot import 'bad.lib.pen'! ... DocumentParseError" and the refs are invalid. The document still opens.
4. Pen does NOT follow a library's own imports. libs/a.lib.pen imports {"B":"b.lib.pen"} (b present beside a AND beside the host): Pen reports "Invalid ref 'A:B:Bcmp1'" and never attempts to load b (no Cannot-import line). One level only.
5. A document importing itself ({"S":"host.pen"}) loads itself once as a library (S:Cmp01 resolves); the copy's own imports are not followed (S:S:Cmp01, S:ABS:Bcmp1 invalid). So there is no cycle to detect: Pen's one-level rule makes cycles impossible.

Consequence for the design: mirror Pen - load the host's direct imports only, relative to the host file; a library's own imports are not followed (a lint finding says so), and "cycles" reduce to that same rule. This deviates from brief point 7 (nested + cyclic handling), on purpose.

Progress + two more Pen facts (readctx, 2026-09-26).

1. `pencil:<name>` is a real form: Pen resolves it to a library bundled with Pen itself (pen CLI: `<install>/dist/out/data/<name>`, which holds halo/lunaris/nitro/shadcn .lib.pen; the desktop app keeps them inside app.asar). `pencil:kit.lib.pen` with kit.lib.pen beside the file -> "Cannot import ... ENOENT .../out/data/kit.lib.pen", i.e. the document's folder is NOT tried. `pencil:shadcn.lib.pen` resolves. Woodcase cannot ship Pen's libraries, so a pencil: import is a lint finding (import-not-found, "bundled with Pen") - never read from beside the file. NOTE: Penumbra's DocumentPipeline.resolveImports strips "pencil:" and reads the name from the document's own directory, which is not what Pen does.

2. The 8 bare-id override findings on banking #YGJ0d/#8ruxp are NOT stale and NOT import-related. 2592p/G6llC/T2IOh/WKey6 are icons that nSNTs' own transaction rows (ALu8G etc.) inject into their URnQO slot (children override). Woodcase honours the key ALu8G/2592p; the bare key applies nothing in Woodcase's render, so lint is consistent with the render (criterion t39 holds). But Pen DOES apply the bare key: probe inj.pen (Slot1 with slot Hole1; Scr01 containing Ins0A ref Slot1 injecting rectangle Inj01 red; Top01 ref Scr01 descendants {"Inj01":{fill blue}}, Top02 {"Ins0A/Inj01":{fill green}}) -> Pen export draws blue AND green; woodcase shot draws red and green, and lint flags Top01. This is a PenRefExpander fidelity bug (bare key reaching a node injected into a nested instance's slot) - out of this leaf's scope; recommend filing it.

- A stroke that is one enabled solid of normal blend keeps box-shadow/outline/borders/SVG stroke attr (byte-identical; every existing golden unchanged). Anything else:
  - rect / frame / CSS ellipse: an aria-hidden absolutely positioned overlay CHILD (inline React styles cannot do pseudo-elements). Transparent border = stroke's outer reach (0, w/2, w per side; per-side widths honour alignment, default centre) so the padding box IS the node box (images/mesh origin padding-box: decal, as Pen); padding = rest of width so the content box is the inner edge, cut out by mask `linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box exclude, linear-gradient(#000 0 0)` (+ -webkit-mask xor). Radii grow by the outset. Gradient layers span border-box with geometry pulled back onto the node box (linear stops moved by the line's growth at each end in calc(); radial sized/centred on the node box) so they pad like Pen. Host gets position: relative; a frame with children gets isolation: isolate and the overlay zIndex -1 (Pen draws a container's stroke before its children).
  - path / polygon / arc+donut ellipse / SVG line: userSpaceOnUse paint servers. Linear/radial use Pen's exact unit gradient through a gradientTransform matrix (same map as frameTransform), image/mesh as a pattern drawing the image once with a tile big enough that the overhang shows nothing. Stacks = one stroked copy per layer; inner = 2w clipped to the shape, outer = 2w masked by it; svg gets overflow=visible. Ids = FNV hash of node id + definition (stable).

data.text:
ukfIU2 done on the read-context seam (readctx, 2026-09-26), per Ben's ruling that the imports seam carries the font resolver.

Design: the resolver is read context, not a parameter threaded through lint/tree/overlap/batch placement. PenReadContext.fonts (GoogleFontResolver?) rides on EditableDocument.readContext; PenFileTransaction.read/run take `fonts:` (default nil) and set it; SettledTree has NO fontResolver parameter and no default any more - it asks the document (EditableDocument.registerFonts(forSettling:)). nil = measure in the faces the process already has, no cache consulted. So a library test can only reach GoogleFontResolver.shared by naming it, which HermeticNetworkTests already forbids.

Why not the brief's "thread an explicit resolver through DocumentLinter.findings(in:) and TreeView": the settle sites also include RootOverlap (reached from BatchApplier placement, 126 test call sites), LintPreview (every write verb), SettledTreeCache/ScriptRunner and the viewer endpoints. A parameter with a .shared default is the leak; one without a default is a ~250-site plumbing change. The document already carries the libraries it was read with; its fonts belong beside them (and lebBvI's declared fonts need the same sourceURL).

Proof:
- HermeticNetworkTests gains "No library code settles through the shared font resolver unless a caller names it": scans Sources/Woodcase and Sources/WoodcaseScripting for any `= .shared` / `GoogleFontResolver.shared` besides the declaration. Red before (SettledTree's default), green after.
- ProductionFontWiringTests (WoodcaseCommandTests) is the other half: every PenFileTransaction the CLI and the viewer open must name fonts: (CLI passes .shared, viewer passes RenderCache.fonts). Red before, green after.
- Full suite run with WOODCASE_HOME pointed at an empty directory while ~/.woodcase/fonts holds Inter: see final report.

Declared-fonts hook for lebBvI (not landed on main when checked): EditableDocument+Fonts.swift `registerFonts(forSettling:)` - the one place every settled read registers fonts; documented as where the typed root `fonts` register ahead of Google Fonts, URLs resolved against PenReadContext.sourceURL.

- Model: PenMeshPoint gains `.malformed(AnyCodable)`, produced only by a file decode and written back verbatim. Authoring (PenDecodingMode.authoring: set via checkAuthored, add via PenSubtreeDecoder) still refuses it. `position` is now `Vector?` and `handles(defaults:)` is now `Handles?`, both nil for malformed. That is a breaking change to the public API. canonicalized() leaves a malformed point as written.
- Pen's rule, measured with the pen CLI 0.3.9 over about 30 spellings (2 scratch probes plus the committed fixture render-mesh-malformed-points.pen, which has Pen's @1x/@2x exports and its re-save). It is JavaScript semantics:
  - A non-array point reads position and handles with `??`, so absent or null gives the grid position or the default handle, and a string or number has no position.
  - An array reads its first two entries; longer arrays are truncated.
  - Each entry goes through arithmetic: null is 0, a boolean is 0 or 1, and anything else is NaN, which paints NOTHING for the whole fill.
  - So "oops", null, 42, true, {} and {"position":null} draw at the grid position. [0.3,0.2,9] draws at [0.3,0.2]. [1], [], ["0.3","0.2"], {"position":"oops"} and a handle of [1], "oops" or {} draw nothing.
  - The brief's "non-array vs wrong-length" was the right shape but too coarse.
  - Gotcha: Pen's save uses Number(), so ["0.3","0.2"] saves as clean numbers but draws nothing.
- Placement: `PenMeshPoint.placement(gridPosition:defaults:)` and `PenMeshPoint.gridPosition(...)` implement the rule. PenMeshGrid builds vertices from placements and throws the new `Invalidity.unplaceablePoint(index:)`. MeshFoldDetector now tests `try? PenMeshGrid(fill)`, which also removes its duplicated vertex building. The React emitter needed no change.
- Lint: an unplaceable point is `mesh-gradient-dropped` (error). A point Pen places anyway is `mesh-gradient-distorted` (warning): Pen paints the mesh from its own repair, and the finding quotes the canonical value Pen draws as the fix. See DocumentLinter+MeshPoint.swift.
- Tests: new suites PenMeshPointMalformedTests, PenMeshPointAuthoringTests, PenMeshGridMalformedPointTests, PenMeshMalformedPointSnapshotTests and DocumentLinterMeshPointTests.
  - MAE of painted boards against Pen is 0.30-0.35. `booleans` is 0.60-0.62 because its vertex lands on its neighbour and the overlap is rasterised differently. Pen's export of that board equals its export of a literal [1,0] at MAE 0, so the placement itself is right.
  - The painted boards' placements equal those of Pen's own re-save.
  - Green on the red run, by design: the authoring-refusal tests (authoring was already strict), the count-mismatch-first ordering guard, and the well-formed controls. The re-save test was written after green and proven to bite by sabotaging placement.
  - Existing PenMeshPointTests changed: malformedIsRefused/malformedHandleIsRefused now decode in authoring mode, because file mode preserves by ruling. objectFillsMissingHandles unwraps the now-optional handles.

data.text:
Pen's 2.19 validator on root `fonts` and the `connection` node — established black-box (format219, 2026-09-26)

Method: hand-written probe .pen files round-tripped through headless `pen` CLI 0.3.9 (`printf 'save()\nexit()\n' | pen interactive --in X --out Y`, sandbox off), reading the validator's "Document is not valid" list and the re-saved JSON. Note: scripts/pen-validate reports PASS on these probes — the validator logs errors but the engine still loads and saves, silently dropping what it cannot use. The error list, not PASS/FAIL, is the evidence; pen-validate should grow a check for "[ERROR] Document is not valid" (follow-up, not done).

ROOT `fonts` (array of objects):
- `name`: string (validator: "expected string, got 5"). `url`: string. Neither is flagged when missing, but the engine DROPS any entry without a non-empty name and url on load.
- `style`: one of "normal" | "italic" ("expected one of: \"normal\", \"italic\", got \"oblique\"").
- `weight`: "expected either number or number[2]" — a number, or a two-number array [min, max]. No range check on values (-5, 0, 1200, 450.5 all accepted). [100], [100,200,300], "100 900", {"min":..} refused.
- Any other key: "unexpected property" (e.g. `family`).
- Save quirks (engine, not validator): weight 400 and 0 are omitted; style "normal" omitted; a [min,max] range is written back as its FIRST element only ([100,900] -> 100, [900,100] -> 900) — Pen loses the range on save. Woodcase keeps the range as written.
- Woodcase model: PenFontDeclaration {name, url, style?, weight? (.single | .range(from:to:)), extras}; PenDocument.fonts / EditableDocument.fonts: [PenFontDeclaration]?.

`connection` node:
- Top level only. Inside a frame the validator lists allowed child types WITHOUT connection and the engine drops it ("Node of 'f' has missing child").
- `source`, `target`: required objects ("missing required property"; "expected object, got \"a\""). Each takes exactly `path` (required; "expected slash-separated path of IDs") and `anchor` (required; one of "center", "top", "left", "bottom", "right"); any other key is "unexpected property".
- Accepted without complaint: every Entity key (name, context, reusable, theme, enabled, opacity, flipX, flipY, layoutPosition, metadata, x, y, rotation) and the CanHaveStroke keys (stroke as Fills — an object needs `type`; strokeWidth incl. per-side; strokeLinecap; strokeLinejoin; strokeAlignment).
- Refused as unexpected: fill, effect, width, height, cornerRadius, blendMode, children, and every guess at arrows/curves/labels/points/dash.
- NEITHER engine loads a connection: headless 0.3.9 `Insert` says "Unknown node type: connection", and a valid top-level connection is silently dropped on open and save. Pen.app 1.2.14 (driven via `pen interactive --app desktop` after `open -a Pen local/lebBvI-connection/conn-app.pen`) also drops it: get_app_state lists only the two rectangles and Get("cAB") fails. So there is NO Pen reference render of a connection. Woodcase draws a straight stroked segment between the anchors (line semantics: no stroke, nothing drawn); RapidPro matches CG.
- Pen.app still has local/lebBvI-connection/conn-app.pen open (unsaved, unchanged).

Probe files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-Woodcase/40c1db86-1dc8-4906-ace3-df843d161e9b/scratchpad/lebBvI-probe/ (fonts1/2, conn1/2/3, edge) and local/lebBvI-connection/conn-app.pen.

Also confirmed: gArj6O's stated symptom does not reproduce — a migrate (even --force over hand-reformatted bytes) of a logged file does NOT make the next write print the outside-write note, because LogLineage compares model revisions and the parse already migrates. The real defects were: no lock (lost-update race with a concurrent write) and no log row. Both fixed.

Correction to the done note's "open curiosity": the cause is established, not probable. RapidPro's fixture MAE comes from PixelPeeper's ImageComparator, which reports on a 0-100 scale (divides by 2.55); Woodcase's PenSnapshotTestHelpers reports 0-255. RapidPro's 0.07-0.15 is 0.18-0.38 in Woodcase units - the same as Woodcase's 0.23-0.38. RapidPro's FixtureTestHelper.maeAgainstReference doc comment says "0-255", which is wrong. Standardising on PixelPeeper across repos is proposed to Ben (2026-09-26).

data.text:
Report written: project/2026-09-26-swiftui-codegen-feasibility.md (worktree swiftui-research, branch wt/swiftui-research, uncommitted). Probes: scripts/swiftui-api, scripts/swiftui-fixture-probe.swift (+2 README rows).

Verdict: feasible, and the right second target. About 14 leaves, roughly the React emitter's size (React 5,415 lines/36 files plus shared 2,242/19; tests ~11k/40). Riskiest part: flexbox vs SwiftUI stack negotiation around wrapping text in fill/fit siblings. The fallback, a support Layout porting PenLayoutEngine, is exact by construction but less idiomatic.

Measured (ImageRenderer against Pen PNGs, PenSnapshotTestHelpers MAE arithmetic, loaded machine):
- layout-nested and space-between: 0.000 (CG 0.000).
- render-gradients: 0.135 with Gradient.colorSpace(.device) (CG 0.133). SwiftUI's default interpolation gives 10.69, so March's "exact" was wrong without .device.
- render-transforms-and-effects: 0.59 whole board (CG 1.12). The shadow/blur mapping is radius = Pen blur/2; radius = blur gives 3.4 and 5.0.
- render-text: 3.17 with Inter's automatic optical sizing pinned off (3.61 as written; CG 2.57). The remaining error is vertical metrics.

March mapping corrections:
- Inner shadow is built in (ShadowStyle.inner, iOS 16).
- linearBurn and linearDodge are exact as plusDarker and plusLighter.
- Outer strokes are exact via inset(by:-w).strokeBorder.
- UnevenRoundedRectangle is iOS 16, not 17.
- lineHeight(.exact) exists since iOS/macOS 26.
- justify is impossible in Text.
- Background blur is approximate only (Material).

Generalization gaps:
- There is no IR; Pen decisions live inside ReactEmitter extensions: PaintRoute, gradient geometry, mesh themes, stroke outsets.
- StateTrigger carries CSS pseudo-classes.
- PropMapper returns jsValue.
- PenSVGPathParser and PenShapeBuilder are CoreGraphics, so the Linux-safe emitter cannot reuse them without a split.

Loop timings (minimum of 3 runs, loaded machine):
- Interpreter (xcrun swift file.swift): 0.65-1.0 s per view.
- Batch of 20 views, one module: 5.5 s compile + 0.5 s run.
- Resident dlopen host: compile still ~1 s per view; not worth it.
- Cold module cache: 4.9 s once.
- typecheck-only is slower than a compile (8.7 s).
Recommendation: the suite runs one batch swiftc child that writes PNGs, and compares in-process under #if os(macOS). An agent iterating uses the interpreter.

API churn: floor iOS 18 / macOS 15. #available branches live only in the generated PenSupport.swift. Goldens compile at -target macos15 (verified to catch lineHeight). Soft deprecations (deprecated-in-100000, e.g. foregroundColor) never warn, so audit the vocabulary with scripts/swiftui-api.

Docs: the symbol graph (10,952 declarations, 8,072 with doc comments, SDK-exact, 4 s) is primary via scripts/swiftui-api. sosumi.ai works (clean Markdown) and is the second source. Apple's DocC JSON under /tutorials/data works with curl. The .swiftinterface has zero doc comments. Xcode's AdditionalDocumentation is 20 thin notes. The Xcode MCP is disabled and needs sudo.

Plan: 14 leaves in §6, after Ben's rulings (floor, native vs baked mesh, output package shape, layout policy).
Agent finished; integrator closes.

data.title: Per-side strokeWidth object drops unknown keys
data.description: A per-side strokeWidth object ({"top":1,"right":2,"bottom":3,"left":4,"future":5}) still drops unknown keys on write. PenStrokeWidth.perSide(top:right:bottom:left:) has no room for PenExtras without changing the case's public shape (add an `extras:` associated value, or wrap the sides in a struct), and every exhaustive pattern breaks: Sources/Woodcase/Rendering/PenStrokeRenderer.swift, CodeGen (NodeDiffer, ReactEmitter+Stroke, ReactEmitter+StrokeRing), PenStrokable, PenVariableResolver, ~9 test files, and RapidPro's PenStrokable+RenderStroke.swift. VaJSI3 left it out because Rendering/ and CodeGen/ were owned by other agents and RapidPro is a cross-repo change. Test: PenNestedExtrasTests.perSideStrokeWidth runs under withKnownIssue; remove the wrapper when this lands. data.text:
Done in the Penumbra worktree .claude/worktrees/9xn91l/Penumbra (branch wt/9xn91l), not committed.

I deleted Penumbra's resolveImports, in both DocumentPipeline and CanvasViewController. The replacement is EditableDocument.readLibraries(importedBy:) in Canvas/EditableDocument+Imports.swift. It runs once per document, after folder access is granted. It calls PenLibraries.load(importedBy:at:) on a detached task and stores the result in the document's readContext. The full pipeline input now carries importedDefinitions, and processDocument expands with PenImportedDefinitions.expand(_:for: .canvas). Imported definitions no longer become roots.

The problems go to EditorState.importProblems. A new ImportProblemsBanner shows them under the BreadcrumbBar and can be dismissed. Before this there was no on-screen idiom for document warnings, only MigrationDiagnosticsLog (os.Logger).

The old incremental path also had a second bug. EditableDocument.expandedDocument() never had the libraries, so after any colour or property edit, every instance of an imported component expanded to nothing. The 2026-04-10 pipeline doc called this "safe". It now has a marked correction. A regression test covers it.

Tests: ImportResolutionTests (4) and ImportProblemsBannerTests (4). All 8 failed at the assertion level against stubs, then passed. The full PenumbraTests run passed: 508 passed, 0 failed.

No Woodcase API was missing.

data.note: Landed as Penumbra 921aea3 (pushed). data.text:
Fixed scripts/pen-validate's classification bug and added `--allow-unknowns`; scripts/test-pen-validate (new, stub-`pen`-based, red-first) and scripts/README.md updated. Full detail in the handback to the dispatcher; headline finding for the tracker:

The bug reproduces at fixture-suite scale, not just on format219's synthetic probes. Swept all 149 `Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/*.pen` through the real `pen` CLI (0.3.9) both before and after the fix:

- Before (unmodified script): 147 PASS / 2 FAIL. Of those 147 "PASS", 11 secretly carried a non-empty validator error list the old script never looked at (only exit code + output-file presence gated FAIL) — `imports.pen`, five `lint/*-trips`/`override-*` fixtures, `parser-imports.pen`, `render-mesh-malformed-points.pen` (+ its `-saved` twin), and `v2.9/parser-text-content.pen`.
- After (fixed script, no flag): 136 PASS / 13 FAIL — the original 2 plus those 11.
- After (fixed script, `--allow-unknowns`): 139 PASS / 10 FAIL. The flag (pattern-matched, not filename-keyed) forgives exactly 3 files whose *every* violation is an unrecognized property/enum/node-type: the two named in the leaf (`parser-unknown-properties.pen`, `preserved-extras.pen`) plus `v2.9/parser-text-content.pen` (one legacy `fill` property the current validator no longer recognizes) — a good sign the pattern-based design generalizes correctly rather than needing a filename allowlist. The other 10 FAIL for a different reason (broken refs, missing imports, malformed mesh points) that `--allow-unknowns` deliberately does not cover.

The handoff's recorded "142/144 validate clean" figure is stale/wrong under honest detection: it was produced by a narrower grep (`Document is not valid|Fatal error|Error loading`) that misses "Invalid ref"/"Cannot import" messages entirely. Recommend whoever owns that handoff doc corrects the figure in place (dated doc convention) rather than let it stand as the premise for the next reader. I did not edit it myself — out of this leaf's scope — flagging it here instead.
Work complete: pen-validate fixed + --allow-unknowns + test-pen-validate + README. Handed back to dispatcher for review/commit.

data.text:
Pen's rule measured (pen CLI 0.3.9) and implemented; handed back uncommitted in wt/ILYyZi (slots).

Rule: a descendants key's FIRST step names any node the component itself wrote, however deep - its tree plus slot content it writes for nested instances (descendants children, or children on the nested ref), at any depth. LATER steps name a node below the previous one written by an already-entered component, or a node of the previous instance's own component tree (entering it). Pen re-saves resolved keys canonically (bare id for component-written nodes, instance path otherwise) and drops the rest. Two keys on one node: the last written applies, whole (no merge) - Woodcase uses last-sorted since descendants order is lost. Finding: project/2026-09-26-slot-override-keys.md.

Code: PenOverrideKeyResolver (+Builder), PenRefExpander+OverridePlan / +Instance, PenNodePatcher+SlotContent, EditableDocument+PenKeyRule (guard/lint accepts resolver-placed keys). banking.pen: 0 override-target-not-found (BankingImportsLintTests flipped). Fixture slot-override-keys.pen + 22 Pen PNGs + pen-saved; pen-oracle gained --no-layout and waives "Invalid override path" under --accept-invalid.

Found, not fixed: (1) debug build overflows 512 KiB cooperative stack at ~4 nested instances (woodcase tree exits 138) - expandRef frame slimmed, root cause open; (2) guard accepts keys for content an instance injected itself (Pen drops them); (3) structural key naming a nested instance root (Ins0A/Ins0B) is lint-valid but not applied by the expander.

Background blur: flip fixed (drawn in device space, no extra scaleBy -1); sigma = radius*scale/2 px for background and layer blur; blur is a CPU Gaussian (PenGaussianBlur, Accelerate vImageSepConvolve) on encoded sRGB bytes; capture cropped to node device bounds + 3 sigma; fill gate via public PenFills.hasVisiblePaint; opacity gate NOT copied (ruling), documented in PenRendering.md.
Core Image root cause: CI renders through Metal even with useSoftwareRenderer; the sandbox has no Metal device (MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice nil), so createCGImage returns nil. Core Image is gone from Sources; renders now blur inside the sandbox (verified: sandboxed woodcase render fits sigma 9.98 px at r20 @1x).
Fitted sigma (scripts/blur-sigma-fit, sRGB) after: bg r20 9.98/19.97 px @1x/@2x, bg r8 3.96/7.93, layer r8 3.97/7.96 (before 21.8/44.0, 8.38/17.3, 8.00/8.00). Edge profile vs Pen 1.2.14 export: r20 3/255 at 1x and 2x; r8 @2x 3/255; r8 and layer r8 @1x 5/255 because Pen's own sigma-4px blur fits 4.24 px (Woodcase keeps the exact Gaussian; documented).
Fixture: Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-background-blur.pen (+ @1x/@2x PNGs via scripts/pen-oracle --scale 1,2, pen CLI 0.3.9).
RapidPro would need: call PenFills.hasVisiblePaint for the fill gate; keep drawing blur under opacity < 1; blur in encoded sRGB (MPS works in the texture's space - check it is not an _srgb texture view that linearizes); sigma already radius/2.

Done in wt/Gusv9b (uncommitted). Paint order now outer shadows -> fills -> inner shadows -> stroke -> children (PenRenderer+OwnContent.swift); own content is drawn before a clipping frame's clip, so a clip frame keeps its shadow and outer stroke. Every outer shadow in the array is drawn, each in its own layer with its blendMode; inner shadows honour blendMode too.
Pen 1.2.14 facts established from exports (render-shadows.pen, and a scratch probe): an outer shadow is cast by the node's opaque silhouette (shape + outside part of the stroke; glyphs for text), full strength regardless of fill alpha, and knocked out under the node (a translucent fill does not show the shadow); a fill-less frame casts its box shadow and its children cast none. Woodcase now does all of that (PenShadowSilhouette + PenEffectRenderer.renderOuterShadows: silhouette drawn off-clip with a compensating CG shadow offset, then destinationOut knockout). Groups: shadow cast from the children's painted content (approximation; Pen draws a translucent child's shadow full strength).
MAE vs 1.2.14 exports (PenShadowSnapshotTests): all 7 artboards < 0.47 at 1x and 2x; before: two-outer 9.26, outer-translucent 15.0, outer-frame-children 20.6, inner-under-stroke 2.97, inner-under-child 2.59.
RapidPro would need: same paint order (inner shadows before stroke/children), all outer shadows, silhouette-based opaque shadow with knockout under the node, frame children not casting, shadow blendMode.

References: Woodcase Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-background-blur.pen and render-shadows.pen (Pen 1.2.14 exports at 1x/2x).

data.text: Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-26, session after wave four): neutral smart state defaults are TYPED EFFECTS. RoleStateMapping's smart defaults stop being CSS-shaped PropertyChange values (opacity 0.95, transform "scale(0.98)", shadow "outline") and become a named, target-neutral effect per state — e.g. dim(0.95) for hover, scale(0.98) for pressed/active, a focus ring for focused, dim(0.5) for disabled — which each emitter spells: React as its CSS, SwiftUI as .opacity / .scaleEffect / a focus overlay. One definition, two spellings. Options rejected: native per-platform behaviour (targets diverge on purpose), dropping the defaults.

Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-26): the wedge leaf runs FIRST in priority but in parallel with the other file-disjoint leaves of this wave, not alone; every agent's suite run keeps the 10-minute watchdog (perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' swift test ...).

data.title: Typed smart state effects: one neutral definition for React and SwiftUI
data.description: Ben's ruling (2026-09-26): neutral smart state defaults are typed effects. RoleStateMapping.smartDeltas today holds CSS-shaped PropertyChange values nothing but React reads (opacity 0.95, transform "scale(0.98)", shadow "outline", opacity 0.5). Replace them with a named, target-neutral effect per state (dim, scale, focus ring, ...) that React spells as its current CSS and that the SwiftUI states leaf (wXirUH) will spell as .opacity / .scaleEffect / a focus overlay. React goldens stay byte-identical unless a difference is argued.

wedge agent, 2026-09-26 18:45, worktree wt/wedge. Findings so far:
1. PageHost.evaluate (WKWebView.callAsyncJavaScript), PageHost.load's trailing console-count evaluate, and ShotOperation's WKWebView.takeSnapshot are completion handlers with no deadline. Built one: `await (window.__never = new Promise(() => {}))` hangs a test forever, and its sample (scratchpad DpQmXu-red3-sample.txt) has exactly the wedge's thread shape — idle main run loop, NSEventThread, WebCore: Scrolling, Log work queue, no frame of ours. (A promise that becomes garbage does NOT hang: WebKit fails it with "Completion handler for function call is no longer reachable".)
2. BoundedWait's old task-group form could not bound such a job (a group waits for every child); rewritten to abandon it. Red was a hang, green passes.
3. First full run with deadlines (load ~460): FIVE takeSnapshot calls in the WoodcaseTests WebView suites never answered within 120 s — all issued at the same moment after the main actor was starved — and later snapshots in the same host worked. Under the old code each of those is a wedge. They now fail by name ("snapshot did not finish within 120.0 seconds"). Same suites pass alone at load ~110 (17.9 s).
4. Side fact: when the perl alarm kills `swift test`, the swiftpm-testing-helper survives with ppid 1 at 0 % CPU — the watchdog leaves an orphan host; kill it by pid.

Eight layout-text-* fixtures authored (IBM Plex Sans, one board per file) and run through scripts/pen-oracle. Found pen-oracle's layout.json racy against Pen's web-font load: the Get ran before the export and sometimes measured in a fallback face (19 pt lines vs 18), while the PNG always had the settled layout. data.title: Decision: rewrite own-slot-content overrides into the slot's children, or keep refusing?
data.description: Since 223122a, `woodcase override <instance>/<content the instance wrote into its own slot> …` is refused (EditingError.overrideOnOwnSlotContent, naming the slot to rewrite), because Pen drops such keys. data.title: Rewrite own-slot-content overrides into the slot's children
data.description: Ben's ruling on caIi4g (2026-09-26): an override addressed to content an instance wrote into its own slot (e.g. `woodcase override Inst0/Note0 content=Hi` on slot-fill.pen, where Inst0 fills Body with Note0) is rewritten into that slot fill's `children` instead of refused with EditingError.overrideOnOwnSlotContent. Pen drops such descendants keys (project/2026-09-26-slot-override-keys.md, rule 5 and the follow-up table), so the rewrite is what makes the file honoured by Pen. The command's output says where the change landed. Lint's report of such keys in hand- or Pen-written files stays (Woodcase never writes them); consider whether lint should offer the rewrite as its fix. Batches and the JS host go through the same editing path and must agree.

Root cause found and fixed at the source in wt/sleepy (uncommitted). It was not the macOS 12 floor. Swift Build (SwiftPM 6.4's default backend) links via swiftc -sdk, which passes clang --sysroot; Apple clang takes the SDK version for ld -platform_version only from -isysroot/$SDKROOT, and Swift Build runs the link without $SDKROOT, so sleepy recorded `sdk 12.0` (otool -l, LC_BUILD_VERSION). WebKit then treats the get-task-allow debug binary as old-SDK: inspectable by default, and it prints the notice. The --build-system native path and xcrun swiftc both record sdk 27.0.
Fix: Package.swift reads Context.environment["SDKROOT"] (the swift shim exports it) and gives the sleepy executable -Xclang-linker -isysroot -Xclang-linker <sdk>. The floor stays .macOS(.v12) (minos 12.0). Flag on the executable only; a scratch consumer resolved it as branch and version dependency.
Tried and failed: SDKROOT=... swift build (Swift Build drops it); unsafeFlags with $(SDKROOT) (manifest refuses $(...)).
Evidence: LoadGoldenTests|DoctorGoldenTests red before (2 issues, the notice), green after; no "Inspection" line in 3 full-suite runs.
Findings: project/2026-09-26-old-sdk-inspection-notice.md; gotcha corrected in place.
The hook still did not pass on this machine (load 110-250): remaining failures are not the notice. A PDF print timeout in CapturePDFOperationTests, and SessionIntegrationGoldenTests' shot/pdf/archive --session. Separate bug, reproduced on an untouched HEAD build as well: `sleepy open <url> --name x; sleepy eval --session x ...; sleep 2; sleepy shot --session x` stalls until the budget, with both SDK stamps, and every later call to that page stalls too. An eval right before the shot avoids it. Worth its own leaf.

Done in wt/sleepy (uncommitted). ArchiveOperation goes through PageHost.answer at host.callBudget. CookieStoreBridge takes its owner through an internal DeadlineKeeper protocol: PageHost (its answer, which records abandonedCall) or HostGroup (same race, no record, internal callBudget = LoadOptions.defaultCallBudget). data.title: SwiftUI fill_container has no zero minimum, so content grows the frame
data.description: Found by comps (FPHQQ5): the SwiftUI frame emitter writes fill_container as .frame(maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity) with no zero minimum, so SwiftUI takes the child's ideal size as the minimum and content larger than its room grows the frame. Pen's flex item shrinks and lets content overflow (React writes flex: 1; minHeight: 0 for this). It carries most of the woodcase-app screen gap: Home's favourites row widens the screen, Ratings pushes the tab bar below. Likely fix: minWidth: 0 / minHeight: 0 beside the .infinity maxima in frameModifiers; every layout golden moves, so read them. Then re-measure SwiftUIScreenRenderTests' baselines (wishlist 3.02, usage-log 3.21, home-collection 3.42, lab 3.83, settings 5.16, ratings 5.42) and the layout boards, and tighten. See project/2026-09-26-swiftui-components.md.

data.title: SwiftUI slots: components take @ViewBuilder content for their slot frames

Today an instance that fills a slot draws correctly as an inlined copy (PenRefExpander.prepareInstance applies slot content), but a component takes no generic Content: View parameters. Needs: one generic parameter per slot frame (<Slot>Content, since Body is taken); default content when the slot frame has children (a nested <Slot>Default view and a constrained extension init); a filled slot on a call as the trailing closure. Cause: ~1 s after the last JS call WebKit throttles the windowless view's WebContent process to the background band (task priority 31 -> 4; ps -M, proc_pidinfo). evaluateJavaScript takes a foreground activity (logged: 'WebPageProxy::runJavaScriptInFrameInScriptWorld'); takeSnapshot, printing, createWebArchiveData take none. data.title: Mutating verbs settle the whole document twice for root-overlap warnings (set 402 ms vs 110 ms budgeted)
data.description:
Measured 2026-09-27 on a quiet machine (project/2026-09-27-quiet-machine-measurements.md): `scripts/perf-binary --config release --reps 7` puts `woodcase set woodcase-app.pen` at 401.9 ms release (694.3 debug), against the in-process `set` budget's 110.5 ms (limit 200 ms). It was 123.6 ms on 2026-08-30 and already 357.8 ms at 936a89d.

Cause (read from the code, consistent with the numbers): SetCommand.run calls RootOverlapWarnings.pairs(in:) before the edit and RootOverlapWarnings.lines(since:in:file:) after it, and each builds a whole SettledTree (RootOverlap.roots(in:) -> SettledTree(document:theme:[:])). So every set settles the document twice to answer whether two roots now overlap. add, move, copy and apply do the same. The same shape in ScriptRunner (settle at run start + at end) is why a writes-only js run of 100 set calls costs 828 ms debug on a 956-row document.

The PerformanceSetBudgetTests budget times PenFileTransaction + BatchApplier only, so it cannot see this: the budgeted number and the number a caller waits for have drifted 4x apart.

Options, not decided: (a) compute root rects without a full settle (roots' own frames only — only the roots' x/y/size matter, and a fixed-size root needs no layout of its descendants); (b) skip the before/after pass when the edit cannot move or resize a root (the edited node is not a root and no ancestor sizes to content); (c) budget the verb as a caller sees it. Decide the approach before building.

data.title: Text measurement typesets every text twice since natural line height (+7 ms layout on woodcase-app.pen)
data.description:
Measured 2026-09-27 (project/2026-09-27-quiet-machine-measurements.md, xrqqge): e578829 (natural line height as Pen rounds it) added 7-8 ms to layout of woodcase-app.pen in release (24.9 -> 32.8 ms, and 53.5 -> 60.3 ms on the synthetic 5000-node document; `tree` +5.7 % / +2.5 %), interleaved A/B of 89e43e8 vs e578829, `WOODCASE_TEST_PROFILE=1 swift test -c release --filter PerformanceBudgets.TreeTests`, minimum of 5 runs.

Cause: PenTextMeasurer.measureCFAttributedString now typesets every text twice — CTFramesetterSuggestFrameSizeWithConstraints for the width, and CTFramesetterCreateFrame in lineCount(of:width:) for the line count.

Possible fix: take both from the one CTFrame (width = max line typographic width, height = line count x pitch) and drop the Suggest call. Not built because whether the lines' typographic widths equal the suggested frame width (trailing whitespace, rounding, ceil) must be proven against the MAE gates and the pen-oracle layouts; it is a correctness-sensitive change, not a mechanical one. Worth it because together with the iterative rewrite the `tree` budgets now have only 8-10 % headroom (271.7 / 300 ms, 370.0 / 400 ms release).

data.title: CG draws unfilled text and icons black; Pen draws them as nothing
data.description:
Pen draws a text or icon node with no fill as NOTHING, not black. Measured 2026-09-27 (leaf PlHnG2) with scripts/pen-oracle on Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/swiftui-color-scheme.pen (artboard "unfilled": Inter 44 bold "Ink" and a lucide square, both unfilled, over #808080 — Pen's export is plain grey) and a control probe where the same text and icon with fill #000000 draw black beside unfilled twins that draw nothing (also true with no fontFamily).

The SwiftUI emitter now matches Pen (.foregroundStyle(.clear) on unfilled text; unfilled icons were already Color.clear), and SwiftUIRenderTests holds swiftui-color-scheme-unfilled under a ceiling because CG + 1.0 would pass black text.
