The React emitter should be checked too (a CSS text with no color inherits, usually black). Owner of PenTextRenderer at the time: agent "cgtext". Also revisit lint's text-without-fill message ("whose colour is left to the renderer"): Pen draws it invisible, so the warning can say so.

data.title: Mesh colours parse as Pen parses them (length-keyed, NaN channels 0, other lengths transparent)
data.description:
Pen's mesh colour parser is not "#RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA, else opaque black", which is what PenMeshColor(hex:) + PenMeshGrid+Fill, the SwiftUI emitter (SwiftUIMeshGradient) and PenMeshGradients.md assume. Measured 2026-09-27 (leaf ifNKJL) with scripts/pen-oracle --scale 1 --accept-invalid --no-layout on 2x2 meshes of one repeated colour over a #00FF00 fill layer (pen CLI, Pen re-saves as version 2.19):

  "#GGGGGG"  -> opaque black (0,0,0)          renderer: black  (agrees)
  "red"      -> (0,238,221) opaque            renderer: black  (WRONG)
  "#F00F"    -> nothing (green shows through) renderer: black  (WRONG; lint's mesh-gradient-distorted is right)
  "#F008"    -> nothing                       renderer: black  (WRONG)
  "#FF000"   -> nothing (5 digits)            renderer: black  (WRONG)
  ""         -> nothing                       renderer: black  (WRONG)

The model that fits every row: strip an optional leading '#'; by the remaining length, 3 = RGB (each digit doubled), 6 = RRGGBB, 8 = RRGGBBAA, any other length = transparent (paints nothing, colour and alpha 0). Each channel is JavaScript parseInt(pair, 16) with NaN -> 0, so an unreadable pair is 0 ("rr" -> 0, "ee" -> 238, "dd" -> 221; a 6-digit non-hex string is black, alpha 1). Note parseInt reads a leading valid prefix ("eG" -> 14), so check a partial pair with a probe before relying on it.

Fix: a Pen-mesh parse on PenMeshColor (e.g. init(penMesh:)) used by PenMeshGrid+Fill.init and SwiftUIMeshGradient.content; update PenMeshGradients.md and the "unreadable colour is black" test in SwiftUIEmitterMeshTests (it pins "red" -> black and "#12345" -> black, both wrong); extend lint's mesh-gradient-distorted from 4-digit to every length Pen reads as nothing, and to non-hex digits. Check render-mesh-* fixtures hold no such colour so no snapshot moves, and pin the table above with a pen-oracle fixture. Probe files: scratchpad swiftfix-probe/probe3.pen (recreate from the table).

criteria.label: CG and SwiftUI paint the measured colour table as Pen does, pinned by an oracle fixture
Lint's mesh-gradient-distorted covers every length Pen reads as nothing

data.text:
The leaf's title is wrong: Pen does NOT draw unfilled text black. Measured 2026-09-27 with scripts/pen-oracle on Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/swiftui-color-scheme.pen (artboard "unfilled": Inter 44 bold "Ink" and a lucide square, both with no fill, over #808080): Pen's export is plain grey, and a control probe drew filled (#000000) twins black beside unfilled ones that drew nothing, with and without a fontFamily. So Pen draws a text or icon with no enabled paint as nothing. Integrator ruling: match Pen.

Done (branch wt/swiftfix, uncommitted at hand-off):
- SwiftUINodeEmitter+Text: a text with no enabled fill (no fill, an empty list, every fill disabled) gets .foregroundStyle(.clear) before its growth frame. A fill that exists but cannot be written (an undeclared $variable) is still left to SwiftUI with its warning, not hidden. Unfilled icons were already Color.clear.
- SwiftUIEmitterUnfilledPaintTests (new): no fill, disabled fills, empty list, unwritable fill, unfilled icon. Red first (the three .clear tests failed; the unwritable-fill and icon tests pinned existing behaviour and were green on first run).
- SwiftUIRenderTests renders the "unfilled" board under light and under dark (new SwiftUIRenderBoard.colorScheme/darkBoards; the batch wraps a dark board in .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)); both measure MAE 0.000 against Pen's export. They sit under a 0.0 ceiling because the CG renderer draws the text black (CG 8.77), so CG + 1.0 would pass black text.
- Goldens moved: pages/Components/Card, pages/Pages/About, pages/Pages/Home, theme/parser-themed-variables (each an unfilled Text now .foregroundStyle(.clear)); new swiftui-color-scheme golden. The layout goldens did not move: their texts are all filled, so "every layout golden moves" in the description was wrong too.
- PenCodeGen.md says so.

Not done here: the CG side (PenTextRenderer / PenIconFontRenderer drawing nothing) is PRFPX5, blocked behind agent cgtext. When it lands, the swiftui-color-scheme-unfilled ceilings can come out. Note for review: a text field's prompt inherits the text's style, so an unfilled text input's prompt is clear too — which is what Pen draws.

Mesh colour variables are read through the theme (branch wt/swiftfix, uncommitted at hand-off).

- SwiftUIMeshGradient.content now takes the node emitter's colorCode (same ColorCode closure SwiftUIGradient takes): a $variable becomes the token read (theme.brand), noting the theme read so the view gets @Environment(\.penTheme), and PenMeshGradient resolves the Color in the view's environment at draw time. A variable the document does not declare is still reported and drops the mesh. Literal colours go through Pen's own mesh parse (x3UuVF).
- Fixture: Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/swiftui-color-scheme.pen, with a "themed-mesh" artboard (3x2 mesh of $mesh-warm / $mesh-cool light-dark variables, a single-value $mesh-ink and a literal) and its twin "themed-mesh-dark" (theme {mode: dark}); Pen exports of both by scripts/pen-oracle. Added to SwiftUIFixtures.paintFixtures, so it has a golden (swiftui-color-scheme.swift.golden: ThemedMesh reads theme.meshWarm etc.; ThemedMeshDark wraps them in PenThemeReader under .penTheme(mode: .dark)).
- SwiftUIRenderTests pins the mesh in light (themed-mesh, MAE 0.455, CG 0.378) and in dark: themed-mesh rendered under .colorScheme(.dark) and measured against Pen's themed-mesh-dark export (board id swiftui-color-scheme-themed-mesh-in-dark, MAE 0.457, CG 0.368), plus the themed-mesh-dark board itself (0.457). The harness learned referenceArtboard + colorScheme on SwiftUIRenderBoard and writes each themed fixture's Theme files into the batch module (refusing two fixtures whose theme files differ).
- Tests: SwiftUIEmitterMeshTests.themedColour (red first), undeclaredColourVariable (was the old "themes are a later slice" test; its expectations held).
- The "settle #RGBA with a Pen export" part of the description turned into x3UuVF: lint was right (Pen paints #RGBA as nothing), and Pen's mesh parse differs from ours in more than that.

Correction to this leaf's own description: the per-pair model ("each channel is parseInt(pair, 16)") is wrong for 6 and 8 digits. Two more pen-oracle probes (2026-09-27, pen CLI 0.3.9) settled it; "#eGeGeG" is #00000E, not #0E0E0E. The model that fits all 30 measured strings:

- drop ONE leading '#' (UTF-16 code unit); "##F00" and "F00#" are transparent;
- 3 units: each digit doubled, one channel each, opaque; a unit that is not an ASCII hex digit reads 0 ("red" -> #00EEDD, "#F0G" -> #FF0000, "#-0F" -> #0000FF);
- 6 or 8 units: ONE JavaScript parseInt(digits, 16) over the whole string (skip JS whitespace, optional sign, optional 0x, then the longest hex prefix; none -> NaN -> 0), low 32 bits split into bytes: RRGGBB opaque, or RRGGBBAA ("#-f-f-f" -> #FFFFF1, "# f f f" -> #00000F, "#FFGG00" -> #0000FF, "#FF0000FG" -> #0FF0000F, "#GGGGGGGG" -> transparent, "#-0000001" -> opaque white);
- any other length transparent (colour and alpha 0).

Done (branch wt/swiftfix, uncommitted at hand-off):
- PenMeshColor+PenMesh.swift (new): PenMeshColor.transparent, init(penMesh:), static hexColor(penMesh:) -> PenHexColor (the one parse), internal penMeshDigits(_:) (shared with lint). PenMeshColor.init?(hex:) is removed — nothing used it but PenMeshGrid (BUILD stage; RapidPro/Penumbra do not reference PenMeshColor).
- PenMeshGrid+Fill and SwiftUIMeshGradient both read literal colours through it. An unresolved $variable in PenMeshGrid is still opaque black (unmeasured).
- Oracle fixture: Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-mesh-colors.pen (30 frames, one colour string each over #00FF00) + Pen's 30 exports + .pen-saved.pen (`scripts/pen-oracle Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-mesh-colors.pen --scale 1 --accept-invalid --no-layout`). PenMeshColorSnapshotTests: CG MAE 0.00 on every frame (pinned at 0.05). The fixture is also a SwiftUI paint fixture: every frame renders within CG + 1.0 (0.000–0.198), golden render-mesh-colors.swift.golden.
- PenMeshColorTests rewritten as the table; PenMeshGridTests.unreadableColors and PenHexColorTests.entryPointsAgree (now accepted forms only) updated; SwiftUIEmitterMeshTests.unreadableColourIsBlack replaced by malformedColourIsReadAsPenReadsIt — the old test pinned "#12345" and "red" as black, which Pen does not draw.
- Lint mesh-gradient-distorted: every colour of a length Pen reads as nothing (not just 4-digit #RGBA; #RGBA keeps its "write #RRGGBBAA" fix), and every readable-length colour with a non-hex digit, naming the colour Pen reads ("vertex 4 `red` as `#00EEDD`"). LintCheck, LintCommand help, WoodcaseLint.md updated.
- PenMeshGradients.md has a new "Colours" section and a marked correction; PenRendering.md and PenCodeGen.md updated. No render-mesh-* fixture held a malformed colour; no existing snapshot moved.

data.text:
React transform deltas now draw, and they match Pen (worktree reactxf, branch wt/reactxf, uncommitted).

Pen's convention, from Pen's own export of Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/react-transform-states.pen (scripts/pen-oracle, pen CLI, 2x):
- rotation turns counter-clockwise on screen, so CSS gets rotate(-θdeg);
- the node turns AND flips about its x/y (top-left corner of its unturned box): the layout of a 50x50 child at (35,35) turned 25° is bbox (35, 13.87, 66.45x66.45), and a flipX child at x=70 lands at x=20;
- the flip applies before the turn (the turned-and-flipped bbox is x 24.68, y 35), so CSS is `rotate(-25deg) scaleX(-1)` (rightmost applies first).

What changed:
- DeltaTransform+CSS: cssFunctions (nil when identity; 0° is none) / cssValue (`none` when identity); the fraction is kept (was Int-truncated on the base path).
- The node's own transform (emitCommonStyles) and the state's share that one spelling via DeltaTransform(of: PenNodeCommon). The base path had the same wrong sign.
- TransformPivot: `anchor` (transformOrigin "0 0") for nodes placed by their own x/y — layout:none children, group children, layoutPosition absolute, a group itself; `center` (CSS default) in flex flow, where Pen grows the slot to the turned bounds and CSS cannot.
- StateEmitter: a transform var's base value is the node's own transform (it used to fall back to the STATE's value, so the rest state would have drawn turned once the spelling was valid).
- substituteStateVars inserts `transform: var(...)` (+ origin) when the node has no base transform.
- ReactHarnessBuilder now inlines states.css — before, no designer state could draw in a WebKit harness test at all.

MAE, WebKit (SleepyHollow) vs Pen's 2x export, reproduced with
  swift test -j 3 --filter ReactTransformStateWebView
(measured twice, identical; also in the full suite):
  TurnedCard   rest 0.009  disabled 0.026  variant board 0.026
  FlippedCard  rest 0.008  disabled 0.009  variant board 0.009
  TurnFlipCard rest 0.011  disabled 0.039  variant board 0.039
Before the fix (same command, red run): disabled/variant 11.21/10.98 (turned), 27.06/27.06 (flipped), 26.58/26.49 (both).
Limits per case by the margin rule: 0.26–0.29.

Goldens: only ScreenLab.tsx.golden moved (rotate(45deg) -> rotate(-45deg), a flex child, no origin); no page golden changed.

Not done (out of scope): SwiftUI's inlined role-component copy drawing its plain face without the control. A turned node in a flex flow still differs from Pen (Pen grows its slot to the turned bounds).

Slots as a @ViewBuilder API, built (worktree slots, branch wt/slots, uncommitted for the integrator).

What the emitter writes now:
- Each frame of a component's own tree marked `slot` is a generic parameter (<Name>Content; `Content` for a slot named "Content"), a `private let`, and a `@ViewBuilder name: () -> NameContent` init parameter after the props and the control's members. The slot frame's stack draws `name` where Pen draws the children (SwiftUINodeEmitter+Frame, via SwiftUIComponentScope.slots).
- The frame's own children are a top-level `<Component><Slot>Default: View` (not nested: a type nested in Card<Content> is generic over Content and cannot be named in Card's own constraint). One `extension Card where Content == CardContentDefault, ...` init passes every slot its default (EmptyView for a childless slot) and forwards the props/members, so `Card()` and every #Preview still draw Pen's component.
- An instance whose `children` override targets a slot frame (InstanceOverrides.slotFills) is a call with trailing closures: first unlabelled, rest labelled (`} footer: {`); an unfilled slot passes its default view. A control's closure lands on its slot, not `action` (SE-0286 forward scan) - verified by the UploadButton render.
- Refused, with a warning, drawn as plain frames (fills inline): a slot frame with space_between/space_around, and one whose default places a child absolutely in a stack. A fill with an absolute child in a stacked slot inlines. A prop read inside a slot's default is left out with a warning.

Evidence: codegen-slots.pen (Card: 1 slot + prop; Panel: 2 slots, one empty; SlotButton: button role + slot) and six pages. Goldens under golden/swiftui/codegen-slots (no existing golden moved). SwiftUISlotRenderTests compiles the emitted module at the default floor and at iOS 18 / macOS 15 and renders all 9 boards; MAE vs Pen's exports 0.22-1.08, SlotButton 1.62 (179 vs 180 pt hugging width); limits by the margin rule.

Tests: SwiftUIEmitterSlotTests (13), InstanceOverridesSlotTests (4), SwiftUISlotRenderTests. Green-on-red, disclosed: InstanceOverridesSlotTests' undeclaredSlot / fillWithPaint / replacement and SwiftUIEmitterSlotTests.absoluteFill passed before the implementation - they guard against the slot path over-reaching (everything inlined before), not new behaviour.

Fixture change: page frames renamed `Filled Card` etc. because PageAnalyzer lowercases inner capitals (FilledCard -> Filledcard); recorded in gotchas. Names only; Pen's exports unaffected.

Docs: PenCodeGen.md *Slots*; update block in project/2026-09-26-swiftui-components.md.

data.description: Found by slots (26chl8): PageAnalyzer.sanitizeName title-cases each word, so a frame named `FilledCard` becomes the page type `Filledcard`, while a component of the same name keeps `FilledCard` (ComponentAnalyzer). The codegen-slots fixture names its pages with spaces to dodge this.

data.text:
Done in worktree cgtext (branch wt/cgtext), uncommitted, for the integrator.

The brief's cause was half right. Two faults, measured apart:
1. Optical size (the bigger one). Core Text moves Inter's opsz axis to the point size; Pen draws the default (14). Above 14 pt, CG text was 1-9 pt narrower than Pen's, so the layout was off and the boards wrapped differently. PenTextMeasurer.resolveFont now sets kCTFontOpticalSizeAttribute "none", as the SwiftUI template's PenFontFace already did. SF Pro (defaultFontFamily, Woodcase's own fallback, not a face Pen draws) is exempt: pinned, 16 pt text came out in its display cut.
2. Line placement. Pen rounds a lineHeight pitch to a whole point per line (Pen's own layout of a new probe, text-line-height-rounding.pen: 14 pt x 1.25 gives 18/36/54). It centres the glyphs by half-leading, with the baseline rounded to a whole point. Rounding scored best of six candidates; see PenTextLinePlacementTests. PenTextLines now places each CTLine itself, so Core Text's min/max line height no longer decides where a line goes. The renderer typesets once per draw: before, it measured twice and then framed.

CG MAE at 2x, before -> opsz only -> both:
  tight-wrap   13.394 -> 4.729 -> 1.574
  loose-wrap    6.395 -> 1.199 -> 1.053
  fixed-middle  5.462 -> 0.074 -> 0.074
  auto-tight    9.327 -> 1.029 -> 0.939
  stacked       7.225 -> 2.814 -> 1.272
  text-line-height-rounding (new)  -> 0.460
Reproduce: swift test -j 3 --filter PenTextLineHeightTests (each board prints its MAE and ink bands).
Gated per board by the margin rule in PenTextLineHeightTests.maeCeilings: 2.37, 1.59, 0.33, 1.41, 1.91, 0.71.

SwiftUI (swift test -j 3 --filter SwiftUIRenderTests): the template's penFont rounds the pitch and the baseline the same way. MAE 3.031/1.831/0.786/1.503/1.989 -> 1.574/1.053/0.786/0.939/1.270. That equals CG on four boards; fixed-middle stays at 0.786 (CG 0.074). The five ceilings are gone, so the boards gate at CG + 1.0. Free wins: txt-lin-h-ragged 0.268 -> 0.029 and txt-lin-v-multiline 0.441 -> 0.037.

Re-gated CG text boards (margin rule, measured this run):
- PenBankingAppTests 3.209 -> 0.891, bar 4.82 -> 1.34
- PenTextPaintTests: fixed-left 0.26, multiline 0.28, twin-lin-h 0.33, twin-radial 0.34, twin-image-stretch 0.31; icon-grad stays at its 1.9 cap
- PenWoodcaseAppTests: 12 screens, 1.25-2.39, bars 1.88-3.59

Recorded as a correction in project/2026-09-26-mae-margin-rule.md. No MAE in performance/mae-test.csv rose against mae-baseline.csv.

RapidPro (not edited): TextRasterizer copies the old pipeline (CTFrameDraw, unrounded min/max line height, 1.2 when lineHeight is unset). It uses PenTextMeasurer.resolveFont, so it picks up the optical-size change silently: its glyphs get wider. It does not pick up PenTextLines, so its explicit-lineHeight lines now differ from Woodcase CG and from the layout heights, which Woodcase now rounds per line.

data.title: React draws unfilled text and icons black; Pen draws them as nothing
data.description:
Found by PRFPX5 (2026-09-27). Pen draws a text or icon with no enabled fill as nothing (render-text-unfilled.pen). React draws both black:
- Text (ReactEmitter+TextPaint.swift): with no enabled fill PaintRoute is .none and no `color` is written, so the text inherits CSS colour (black). Evidence: golden/pages/Home.tsx.golden, "Today" (unfilled in pages.pen) gets only fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight.
- Icon (ReactEmitter+Icon.swift): colour from fills.all.first via emitFillValueRaw, which ignores `enabled` — no fill writes no color (currentColor, black), and a disabled first colour is drawn.
Fix: write color: transparent (or skip drawing) for no enabled paint; icons honour `enabled`; keep unparseable enabled solids black as Pen does. Pin in WebKit against render-text-unfilled.pen's Pen exports. Moves React goldens.

data.title: SwiftUI render batch is killed at 600 s under load and reports an empty failure
data.description: Found by Dc3tN9 (2026-09-27): SwiftUIRenderBatch.runAsync kills its child after 600 s, and the SwiftUIRenderTests batch's swiftc took 574 s alone on a loaded Mac (load ~130). In the full suite it crossed the deadline and failed both compile tests with buildFailure == nil and an EMPTY message, plus ~230 boards "the batch did not render:" with nothing after — reads like a broken emitter. Fix at source: (1) the kill must report itself ("swiftc killed after 600 s — the machine is loaded or the batch is too big"), (2) the budget is load-shaped (gotcha 2026-08-29 wall-clock budgets: 60 s budgets were raised) — raise it or bound "not hung" scale, and consider splitting the batch so one swiftc is not ~10 min. Then delete the 2026-09-27 gotcha entry about it.

Built on wt/text (worktree .claude/worktrees/text/Woodcase), uncommitted, suite green.

Fix: PenTextMeasurer.measureCFAttributedString (with a lineHeight, i.e. every layout measurement) now breaks lines once with CTTypesetterSuggestLineBreak/CTTypesetterCreateLine (PenTextMeasurer+Typesetting.swift, `typeset(_:width:)`); width = max over lines of typographic width - trailing whitespace, floored at 0. That equals CTFramesetterSuggestFrameSizeWithConstraints' width BIT FOR BIT and the line count equals a CTFrame's — proven by PenTextMeasurerTypesettingTests over 54,432 cases (Inter, IBM Plex Sans, SF Pro, Helvetica, Menlo, Times; 6 sizes; 21 strings incl. trailing/leading/only whitespace, \n, CJK, emoji, RTL, ligatures; widths nil/20/73.5/150/200.25/333; kern nil/0.5/-0.3; 4 alignments). An exploratory run over 114,048 cases (scratch) agreed. One exception found: a JUSTIFIED paragraph — a frame stretches its lines to the width and the suggested width counts that, the typesetter does not — so justified strings are measured from one frame. measure() never sets alignment, so layout always takes the typesetter path. The nil-lineHeight path of the public measureCFAttributedString still uses Suggest (its height is Core Text's frame height).

Timing: interleaved release A/B vs 4723a15, `WOODCASE_TEST_PROFILE=1 swift test -c release -j 3 --filter PerformanceBudgets.TreeTests`, 5 rounds x 2 sessions, LOADED machine (1-min load 61->19, then 10-32): tree app 290.9 -> 273.3 ms, tree synthetic 400.2 -> 393.6 ms, layout app 37.4 -> 32.1, layout synthetic 66.8 -> 55.3 (minima). scripts/text-measure-bench.swift (new), load 9.9, 122 texts of woodcase-app.pen: two passes 0.977 ms, one frame 0.857, typesetter 0.751, Suggest alone (pre-e578829 cost) 0.815. Recorded in WoodcasePerformance.md "Text measurement typesets once". Whether all of e578829's +7.9 ms is recovered needs a quiet-machine A/B against 89e43e8.

Also (for RapidPro leaf UzE2Ou): PenTextLines is public, with init(_:width:font:fontSize:lineHeight:) deriving pitch and first baseline; PenTextRenderer untouched. linePitch/firstBaseline/naturalLineHeight were already public (the brief said internal).

React glyph colour rule (ReactEmitter+TextPaint.swift): noGlyphPaint = "transparent"; glyphColor(PenValue) writes an unparseable literal (PenHexColor rejects it) as #000000, as Pen paints it; glyphColor(PenFills?) -> transparent when nothing is enabled, else the topmost enabled solid, nil when only gradients/images are enabled. Icon (ReactEmitter+Icon.swift): color = glyphColor(fills) -- honours enabled, top solid. StateEmitter's rest value for .textColor uses the same rule (it took the first fill ignoring enabled, and fell back to the *state* value when the base had none, so an unfilled text with a hover colour drew the hover colour at rest).

data.title: React WebView harness names @font-face after the file, so every page draws Times, not Inter
data.description: Found by names (K68yo3/Wo6Vni, 2026-09-27): ReactHarnessBuilder.buildFontFaceCSS names each @font-face after its file, so `Inter[opsz,wght].ttf` becomes family `Inter[opsz,wght]` and every harness page falls back to Times. That is ReactPaintWebViewTests' "the page has no Inter" and the ~3.19 MAE floor on painted text boards (ReactUnfilledPaintWebViewTests control/bad-hex/missing-variable). Fix: read the family name from the font's name table (or map file -> family), re-measure every React WebView suite (WebViewRegression screens, ReactPaint, ReactTransformState, ReactUnfilledPaint) and tighten ceilings by the margin rule. Moves many MAE baselines.

data.title: Google families draw every weight and style in the face the document asks for
data.description:
F3. On a cold cache GoogleFontResolver.downloadRegularFace fetches only weight 400 normal; on a warm cache resolveCached (GoogleFontResolver+Registration.swift:92) registers the first .ttf in directory order and stops. So static families draw bold and italic in one arbitrary file (upright Instrument Serif renders italic today, because InstrumentSerif-Italic.ttf lists first), and variable families never fetch their separate italic file. Measured with woodcase shot + scripts/png-mae against render-font-faces.pen: plexmono-700 7.32, plexmono-italic 8.54, plexmono-700-italic 11.02, spectral-700 15.76, spectral-italic 14.07, inter-italic 13.82, lora-italic 14.81 (regular controls 2.2–2.5).

Fix: resolve the (weight, style) faces a document uses; fetch each static face's file, and a variable family's italic file when italic is used; cache and register every file from its URL; replace the directory-order short-circuit with a per-face check; bundle the same set for SwiftUI (GoogleFontResolver+Bundling.swift). Test through an injected fetcher serving local files, never the network. Mind the gotcha: only one test per run may watch a family go from absent to present, so use families no other suite registers (IBM Plex Mono, Spectral and Lora are OFL; commit them, or renamed copies via scripts/rename-font-family). Update PenGoogleFonts.md.

criteria.label: A document using IBM Plex Mono at 700 and italic, rendered on an empty cache, registers the Bold, Italic and BoldItalic files and draws each board of render-font-faces.pen within MAE 3.0 of Pen's export.
With several faces cached for a family, every cached face is registered and a text's weight and style pick the right one (Instrument Serif regular draws upright).
A variable family used in italic fetches and registers its italic file (inter-italic and lora-italic within MAE 3.0).
woodcase generate swiftui bundles every face the document uses.
PenGoogleFonts.md describes per-face resolution.

data.title: A rotated node placed by x/y turns about its anchor in layout, CG and SwiftUI
data.description:
F4. Pen turns a node its parent does not lay out (layout none, or absolute) about its top-left x/y anchor. Its settled layout of render-rotated-free.pen's rectangle (200×60 at 80,60, rotation -20) is x 59.479, y 60, 208.46×124.79. Woodcase reports 80,60 with the same size: the box's corner is pinned at the anchor and CG pivots at the box's centre, so everything lands shifted. CG MAE (shot + png-mae): rrect 2.57, rtxtf 4.98, rtxta 4.98 (unrotated control 0.14). The existing render-text-fills-txt-rotated scores 7.33 in both CG and SwiftUI, the worst CG board in the repo. data.title: React writes effects on text, icons, SVG shapes and groups, in Pen's order
data.description:
F7. emitEffects is reached only from frames, rectangles, CSS ellipses and browsers. A probe's text, icon, path and group shadows and blurs are emitted as nothing. Where effects are emitted: CSS paints the first box-shadow on top while Pen draws the array bottom first; a shadow's blendMode is dropped; a layer blur is truncated with Int(radius/2); two blurs write two filter keys; and a background blur is written on a node with no visible fill (Pen and CG draw none).

Fix: text-shadow for text (cast by the glyphs); filter drop-shadow for icons and SVG shapes; a group's shadow over its content (an approximation of Pen's silhouette); mirror CG's rules as PenRendering.md lists them. data.text:
Fixed at the source, not just re-timed. SwiftUIRenderBatch.runAsync now returns a
typed ProcessOutcome (.exited / .timedOut) instead of a bare (status, output) tuple.
A .timedOut case's `output` always names the command, the deadline, and how long the
child actually ran, so a killed child can never surface as an empty message again.
The wait is now built on the existing BoundedWait (its "an await on a callback we do
not own needs a deadline we do" contract matched exactly), with a cancellation
handler that terminates the real child process rather than merely abandoning a
suspended await. Pinned red-first with SwiftUIRenderBatchRunAsyncTests.swift, which
runs runAsync directly against /bin/sleep and /bin/echo (no swiftc needed) — 3 tests,
all newly written and confirmed to fail before the fix (missing `deadline` param,
`.exited`/`.timedOut` cases didn't exist).

Deadline raised from 600 s to a 30-minute default (Duration, injectable per call),
justified in a doc comment against the 574 s worst-case alone measured earlier. Also
added `-j 3` to the swiftc invocation itself (compile(floor:)), capping the child's
own frontend parallelism to match this repo's build/test convention on the shared
8-core Mac — a deviation beyond the literal brief, disclosed in the handback, since
an unconstrained child swiftc grabbing every core is exactly the contention pattern
`project/gotchas.md`'s "Ten cold Swift builds at once panic this Mac" warns against.

Measured the real batch end-to-end (swift test --filter SwiftUIRenderTests -j 3,
load ~37-40): all 232 boards + both compile tests passed in 152 s. The batch itself
prints a build-vs-typecheck breakdown now (`SwiftUIRenderBatch: build X, typecheck
Y`): build 140.1 s vs typecheck-only 134.8 s — nearly identical. Since -typecheck
skips SILGen/IRGen/link entirely, this means type-checking the emitted SwiftUI
(ViewBuilder result-builder inference across ~230 boards) is the dominant cost, not
codegen or linking. Recommendation: do not split the batch — swiftc already
parallelizes across files (now capped -j 3), splitting into multiple invocations
would mean multiple binaries and multiple harness render passes (real architecture
change touching all 4 render batches, not "simple"), and the actual long pole
(type-checking) would not obviously shrink from splitting alone. The 30-minute
deadline plus -j 3 is the pragmatic fix; revisit only if a future measurement under
real heavy load (~130) still approaches the new deadline.

Full suite green: swift test -j 3 --quiet under a 2400 s watchdog, 3655+163+1021
tests across three targets, all passed (1 pre-existing known issue, unrelated).
swiftformat --lint clean. Removed the now-obsolete 2026-09-27 gotcha entry.

Files changed: Tests/WoodcaseTests/SwiftUIRenderBatch.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/SwiftUIScreenBatch.swift, Tests/WoodcaseTests/SwiftUISlotBatch.swift,
Tests/WoodcaseTests/SwiftUIStateBatch.swift, project/gotchas.md. New file:
Tests/WoodcaseTests/SwiftUIRenderBatchRunAsyncTests.swift.

data.title: React writes no font-optical-sizing: none, so browsers draw Inter above 14 pt narrower than Pen
data.description:
Found by reacttests (vXVtb1), 2026-09-27. With the harness now loading real Inter, WebKit applies `font-optical-sizing: auto` and draws Inter above 14 pt in its narrower display cut; Pen (like our CG renderer and SwiftUI's penFont, PenGoogleFonts.md) draws every size at the default optical size. The emitted React writes no `font-optical-sizing: none`, so a real browser draws Pen's text narrower.

Evidence: render-text-unfilled `control` (Inter 44 bold "Ink") measures 3.275 in ReactUnfilledPaintWebViewTests; the same page with `* { font-optical-sizing: none }` injected measures about a third of that (A/B with scratch script reacttests-opsz.zsh: sleepy shot + a PIL MAE, 4.37 -> 1.47 on that script's scale). Also visible in ReactPaintWebViewTests twin-lin-h (72 pt MMMM, 3.372), render-text-line-height-* and render-rotated-free-rtxts in ReactRenderWebViewTests (baselined with Gap.opticalSize).

Fix: emit `fontOpticalSizing: "none"` on text (or once in theme.css for the emitted root), in Sources/Woodcase/CodeGen/React; re-measure and tighten ReactUnfilledPaintWebViewTests' painted boards, ReactPaintWebViewTests' text boards and the opticalSize baselines in ReactRenderWebViewTests+Baselines.swift.

data.title: A React page or component named for a JavaScript global (String) shadows it
data.description:
Found by reacttests (5y8hO5), 2026-09-27. render-mesh-malformed-points.pen has a frame named `string`; emitted as a page it becomes `function String(...)`, which shadows JavaScript's global `String` in the page's scope. In the WebKit harness this broke SleepyHollow's console capture ("The page's console log could not be read: The data couldn't be read because it isn't in the correct format"), deterministically for that board. A shipped React project imports modules rather than inlining them, so there the name is scoped to its module, but any code in that module calling `String(x)` would call the component. Related to GInRSg (sanitized-name clashes).

ReactRenderWebViewTests now emits every board's page as `RenderBoard` to sidestep this; the emitter should refuse or suffix component/page names that shadow JS globals (String, Number, Object, Array, Map, Set, Date, Image, Text, ...).

data.text:
glyphs (VMKixs): Pen places an icon glyph by font metrics, not ink.

Rule: font size = min(w, h). The advance is centred across the box. The baseline is at
h/2 + size*(A - D)/28, where A and D are hhea ascent and descent at 14 pt, each rounded half-up.
- Lucide, Phosphor and Material Symbols: the baseline lands on the bottom of an em square centred in the box.
- Feather: the baseline lands at 13/14 em (0.9285 fitted at 16-128 pt).
- The reference size 14 is fitted. 28 and 42 also fit the bundled fonts; 14 is Pen's default text size.

Evidence:
- Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-icon-placement.pen plus Pen's 2x exports (pen-oracle, pen CLI 0.3.9). Six artboards, two glyphs each, in 24/48/64x32/32x64 boxes.
- scripts/icon-placement-fit.swift. Max residual of the rule is 0.08 pt vertically and 0.02 pt horizontally.

Implemented in:

- The PenIconShape template (PenSupport+Shape.swift) mirrors it.

data.title: Layout should carry a turned node's unturned size instead of the renderer solving for it
data.description: Integrator review of nAuBKh (2026-09-27): PenLayoutEngine.unturnedSize(of:bounds:) recovers a turned node's drawn size by solving W = w|cos|+h|sin|, H = w|sin|+h|cos| back from its layout rect, falling back to a solo re-layout at odd multiples of 45°. Correct today, but it reconstructs a fact the layout already had. Carry the unturned size alongside the rect (a layout-result type, or a parallel map) so the renderer, SwiftUI and RapidPro read it rather than solve for it; delete the solver. Touches every layoutRects consumer — do it when rendering/layout is quiet.

data.title: Make text ink and icon glyph placement public so RapidPro stops mirroring them
data.description:
From RapidPro caec71e (catchup, 2026-09-27): RapidPro now MIRRORS two pieces of Woodcase logic because they are internal — RenderColor.textInk(from:) mirrors PenTextRenderer.PaintRoute(fills:) + extractColor(from:), and RapidPro's IconGlyph mirrors PenIconFontRenderer.glyphOrigin(font:codepoint:box:) + font(for:size:weight:family:) + the Material default weight 200. A mirror drifts (the rule "share, don't copy"). Make one public entry point each and delete the mirrors in RapidPro:
- text ink: a public `PenGlyphPaint` (or public PaintRoute + extractColor) — `nil` for no enabled paint, else the Core Text colour;
- icons: `public struct PenIconGlyph { init?(data: PenNode.IconData, box: CGSize); let string: String; let font: CTFont; let origin: CGPoint /* y-down */ }` covering registry resolve ?? placeholder, Material wght default.
DocC 100%. Then a RapidPro leaf switches to them (side-by-side worktrees).

layout (Jg0BOv), 2026-09-27: CLASSIFICATION ONLY, no behaviour changed.

Probe: scratchpad layout-probe/layout-probe.pen (generator: scratchpad layout-gen.py), run with
`scripts/pen-oracle layout-probe.pen --scale 1` (pen CLI, sandbox off). Boards j-plain, j-clip,
j-paint, j-flex, j-fitflex, j-explicit. Each holds a `layout: "none"` frame with no width/height
(fill #808080) whose child is an 80x40 rect at (10,10) (or 50x50 at (0,0)).

What Pen does (layout.json + exports):
1. Size: 0x0, always. Pen re-saves the missing sizes as `"width": "fit_content(0)"`, and an explicit
   `"fit_content"` also settles 0x0 (J6f); `fit_content(30)` settles 30 (J6g). So in Pen, fit_content on a
   layout-none frame never measures its children: it is the fallback, default 0. Children's rects are
   unchanged (J1fa 10,10,80x40).
2. Children are drawn anyway: no clip by default, so they overhang the 0x0 box at their own x/y (j-plain).
3. With `clip: true` NOTHING of the children is drawn (j-clip is a plain black board).
4. The frame's own fill is not visible (0x0). Its outer stroke IS painted, as a 16x16 square around the
   point (strokeWidth 8, `outer`), and its outer shadow is painted too (a blurred blob off that point) -
   j-paint.
5. In a flex parent it takes no space: in a horizontal frame with gap 10, the sibling after it lands at
   x = 10 (J4s), overlapping the frame's 50x50 child. A fit_content flex parent with padding 5 around it
   settles at 10x10 (J5p), the child overhanging.
6. Editor selection box: not measurable headless; by the layout it is a zero-size box at the anchor, so
   the selection presumably shows a point/handles at (x, y), not around the children.

What Woodcase does: the union of the children from the frame's origin (PenEngine.md "Absolute
containers and fit_content", inferred, never measured) - so it paints the frame's fill across that union,
clips children to it, and grows flex slots by it. Visible differences on every one of j-plain (grey fill
drawn), j-clip (children drawn), j-flex/j-fitflex (sibling and parent move).

Prevalence: of every .pen under Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures and /Users/ben/Local/Pen, only
`layout-absolute-fit-content.pen` (Woodcase's own fixture for the inferred rule) has a sizeless
layout-none frame with children. Pen's editor never writes one (it re-saves it as fit_content(0)).

Classification: DESIGN CALL FOR BEN, leaning "Woodcase wrong".
- Not a Pen bug in any obvious sense: Pen is internally consistent (its own save spells the size
  fit_content(0), and explicit fit_content behaves identically), i.e. "fit_content" means "fit the flow"
  and an absolute container has no flow.
- Woodcase's union is friendlier for an agent-written file, but it draws differently from Pen in fill,
  clip and flex spacing, so a file looks different in the two tools - a fidelity bug by the project's
  own yardstick.

Recommendation: match Pen - resolve fit_content on a `layout: "none"` frame to its fallback (0 by
default) - and put the friendliness where it belongs: a DocumentLinter warning ("a layout-none frame with
no width/height settles 0x0 in Pen: its fill is invisible, clip hides its children, and it takes no space
in a flow; give it a size"). Correct PenEngine.md's union rule in place (it was inferred; groups keep a
union, which cqBw2i now measures). Small change (AbsoluteLayout.advance's resolveContainerSize for frames,
the layout-absolute-fit-content golden and its tests), but it changes what existing documents draw, so
Ben should rule first.

Measured with scripts/pen-oracle on a new fixture Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/render-free-groups.pen

children's rects — the anchor is not in it (group at (50,50), children at (20,30),(80,60) -> rect
(70,80) 90x60) — while the children's rects stay measured from the anchor. Free groups turn and flip
about the anchor like any free node: rect = bounds of the union box turned (rot: 82.68,70
104.28x100.62). In a flex flow the slot is the union's size grown to its turned bounds (flexrot 81.96),
and the union is drawn centred in the slot (checked against Pen's pixels).

Code: PenLayoutEngine.groupBox(of:in:) / unturnedBox(of:bounds:layoutRects:) (new file
PenLayoutEngine+UnturnedBox.swift); freeRect(of:x:y:box:) and freeRect(...size:placedIn:) in
+FreePlacement; groups lose their exemptions from freeRect, applyRotationExpansion and unturnedSize;
AbsoluteLayout sizes a group by groupBox. CG: PenRenderer.enter draws every node's box centred in its
rect, turned about its centre, then translates to a group's anchor (draw rect = box, origin non-zero
for groups); PenTransformBuilder has no group exception; renderBlur honours the rect origin. SwiftUI:
a group in a stack is PenGroupFlow (new template PenSupport+GroupFlow.swift, a Layout). tree/viewer:

Effects now follow the renderer's rules (NodeEffects: every enabled shadow in array order; the first enabled layer blur and background blur with a radius, as PenRenderer draws only the first):
- CSS boxes: one boxShadow list = stroke shadows, inner shadows top first, outer top first (main's stroke-first reorder composes with it).
- Text: textShadow top first (blur passed through; measured: text-shadow blur 8 scores 3.775 on text-inner-outer vs 5.888 at 4, so it is sigma = r/2 like box-shadow). Painted text uses drop-shadow filters (text-shadow would paint over the clipped background). No inner text shadow (CSS has none).
- Icons, SVG shapes (path, polygon, line incl. the full-width div line, arcs/donuts) and groups: one `filter` of drop-shadows (top first) then blur. FINDING: WebKit reads a drop-shadow's blur length as the Gaussian's sigma, so it is Pen blur / 2 — group-outer measured 2.496 at 12px, 0.482 at 6px (scripts/png-mae on a sleepy shot of the board page).
- Layer blur keeps its fraction (blur(2.5px)); one filter key.
- backdropFilter only with a visible fill (PenFills.hasVisiblePaint); browsers always (placeholder).
- Blend modes: a blended outer shadow on a rectangle / CSS ellipse / unclipped frame moves all that node's outer shadows to absolutely positioned layer divs with mixBlendMode (order kept). Everywhere else (inner shadows, glyphs, SVG, groups, browser, clipping frames) the blend mode is dropped with a diagnostics warning, once per node. Criterion 2nC is therefore only partly met — left pending for the integrator/Ben.

Explored and parked: an SVG filter (feComponentTransfer alpha boost -> blur -> offset -> flood -> composite out silhouette -> merge) reproduces Pen's group silhouette almost exactly in WebKit (group-translucent 0.011 vs CG 0.118), but the filter region on an HTML element is fragile: userSpaceOnUse coordinates are the page's, a region of +-100000 renders nothing, and objectBoundingBox uses a WebKit-specific content box. Not shipped; worth a leaf if group shadows matter.

Findings while building incremental settling (agent settle, wt/settle):

1. Revision hole (fixed on the branch): an instance written as slot content inside a ref's `descendants[k].children` (or rootOverrides, or a replacement node) did not fold its component into the ref's revision. Editing that component (slot-fill.pen: BTxt0 inside Badg0, drawn by Page0/Inst0's slot) moved no rev on Inst0 or Page0, and revisionCoverage missed it. componentsRendered(by:) now searches every override value for a string `ref`. Regression test: RevisionFoldTests.slotContentInstancesAreCovered.

2. Not fixed, worth a leaf: GoogleFontResolver.registerFontFile(at:) calls PenFontRegistry.didRegisterFonts() even when Core Text answers alreadyRegistered/duplicatedName, i.e. when the font set did not change. registerDeclaredFonts and registerLocalDeclaredFonts call it on every settle of a document that declares `fonts`, so every settle of such a document moves the generation: the process-wide FontResolutionCache is flushed on every read, a TextSizeCache is discarded on every settle, and incremental settling falls back to a whole settle on every read for those documents (correct, just not faster). Fix: bump only on a real registration. Left alone because font registration is process-global and its tests are order-sensitive (gotchas 2026-09-02).

3. Not fixed: TreeView.rows(expandInstances: true) over the fixture corpus ran for 14+ minutes in a debug build (sampled: deep EditableDocument.effectiveRefData(of:insideInstances:) recursion under TreeView.childSources). The equivalence test uses the default rows (no expansion) instead. Which fixture is not yet identified.

Incremental settling built: SettledTree(document:theme:textSizes:reusing:) re-lays out only roots whose revision moved (or all roots on basis/font-set change); TextSizeCache shared by a run's settles and by every writing verb's overlap before/after (RootOverlap.Baseline). This leaf is ruled (Ben: match Pen + lint warning) and ready to build; it touches PenLayoutEngine sizing and DocumentLinter. Other ready work: 0IegsD (font generation bump, perf), BpaSrF (run alone), MY1B1R, Penumbra catch-up.

Cause (55P02C): not load, a real race that load exposed. The old ParentProcessWatch read getppid() inside waitUntilOrphaned(), which Activity only reached after printing its first page and entering printFollowing's task group. followStopsWhenOrphaned's launcher (/bin/sh) exits as soon as the follower's stdout file is non-empty. If the follower was descheduled between that write and getppid(), the launcher was already gone, getppid() returned 1, the watch took itself for "born orphaned" (launcher <= 1 is deliberately never watched) and waited forever. It was never a slow notice (the 250 ms poll was fine); kqueue NOTE_EXIT would not have helped, since it would register just as late.

Fix: ParentProcessWatch is now a Friendly struct that records `launcher` at init; Activity.run() makes it before any output and passes it to printFollowing. Unit tests: Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/Support/ParentProcessWatchTests.swift (red = compile failure against the old enum API, verified by stashing only the Sources edits).

Evidence, no synthetic load (load 10-13 from other agents' builds). The script below, whose launcher polls every 0.5 ms (sleeping), SIGSTOPs the follower on its first line and exits, then SIGCONTs it:
  pre-fix binary: 1/20 and 15/100 followers still alive after 5 s
  fixed binary:   0/20 and 0/100
The test-shaped repro (sh launcher, 50 ms poll) at load ~8: 0/20 for both, which is why it only failed under heavy load.

--- 55P02C-stop.zsh ---
#!/bin/zsh
# Deterministic-ish repro for 55P02C with NO synthetic load: a launcher that polls
# the follower's output every 0.5 ms (sleeping), SIGSTOPs the follower the instant
# its first line lands, and exits. The follower is SIGCONTed only once the launcher
# is gone — standing in for a busy scheduler that parks the follower between its
# first print and its (old, late) getppid().
# usage: 55P02C-stop.zsh <binary> <runs> <grace-seconds>
set -u
BIN=$1; RUNS=$2; GRACE=$3
DIR=$(mktemp -d /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-Woodcase/7467c9f8-92c5-4600-bc83-442631e9d33a/scratchpad/55P02C-run.XXXXXX)
export WOODCASE_HOME=$DIR/home
export HOME=$DIR
unset WOODCASE_AS
cd $DIR
mkdir -p $WOODCASE_HOME
cp /Users/ben/git/Woodcase/.claude/worktrees/follow/Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/layout-vertical.pen $DIR/a.pen
WOODCASE_AS=ana $BIN set $DIR/a.pen jSUCH common.name=seeded >/dev/null || echo SEED-FAILED

pids=()
for ((i = 0; i < RUNS; i++)); do
  perl -MTime::HiRes=usleep -e '
    my ($bin, $out, $pidf) = @ARGV;
    my $pid = fork();
    if ($pid == 0) {
      open(STDOUT, ">", $out) or die; open(STDERR, ">", "/dev/null");
      exec($bin, "activity", "--follow") or die;
    }
    open(my $f, ">", $pidf); print $f "$pid\n"; close $f;
    for (1 .. 60000) { last if -s $out; usleep(500); }
    kill("STOP", $pid);
    exit 0;
  ' $BIN $DIR/out$i $DIR/pid$i
  p=$(cat $DIR/pid$i)
  pids+=($p)
  kill -CONT $p
done

sleep $GRACE
alive=0
for ((i = 0; i < RUNS; i++)); do
  p=${pids[$((i+1))]}
  if kill -0 $p 2>/dev/null; then
    alive=$((alive+1))
    kill -9 $p
  fi
done
echo "$(uptime | sed 's/.*load/load/') runs=$RUNS grace=${GRACE}s alive=$alive"
rm -rf $DIR

Cause: a cycle, not a slow function. No fixture is slow as authored — scripts/tree-expand-times (woodcase tree --json --expand, debug) finished all 208, slowest 1.13 s, 31 s total [load 60-70]. IncrementalSettleEquivalenceTests' moveToAnotherRoot write puts instances inside their own components (21 fixtures hit a depth-30 probe limit after it); PenRefExpander stops at a ref to a component already on its chain, TreeView's walk did not, so it never ended. effectiveRefData only ran on every row of the endless walk — but it also re-settled the whole chain per row, recursively (200k-element chain overflowed the stack: red test).

data.title: Pen's geometry model: which extents enter layout, and what Woodcase's rects should mean
data.description: Ben (2026-09-28) wants a geometry model that is both conceptually clear and behaviourally consistent. Since 7320cbb a turned node's PenRect carries unturnedSize (bounds first, drawn size as an annotation). Open questions: does stroke width/alignment (or shadow, blur) ever enter Pen's layout — a turned flex child's slot, a fit_content parent's size, a group's union — and what exactly does Pen's layout report for turned, flipped, stroked nodes? Establish with pen-oracle probes and Pen's own source, compare Woodcase, and propose the model (named extents: layout bounds / drawn box + transform / painted extent) in a dated finding for Ben to rule on.

data.text:
Probe fixture render-stroke-shadows.pen (scripts/gen-stroke-shadows-fixture; Pen refs by scripts/pen-oracle ... --scale 2, pen CLI, 2026-09-28): 14 boards, grey node, green 12pt stroke, white outer shadow offset 10,10 blur 8.

What Pen's exports show (read by eye from the PNGs):
- outer / centre strokes grow the silhouette by the band outside the shape; inner adds nothing.
- a translucent outer stroke (#00FF0040) shows black through the band, not the shadow: the shadow is knocked out under the whole silhouette, band included (as CG does).
- per-side widths: the shadow follows the per-side band (right 16 grows it right).
- LINES CAST NO SHADOW in Pen — neither a diagonal line nor a flat one (height 0). CG's PenShadowSilhouette draws a line's stroke as its silhouette, so CG is wrong there (out of scope: CG renderer; reported). SwiftUI already casts nothing (the open line filled is empty) and must stay that way.
- inner shadow under a 16pt inner stroke (offset 6, blur 8): fully hidden under the stroke, i.e. cast from the shape's edge, not the stroke's inner edge. No mirror problem: CG and SwiftUI both clip to the shape and draw the stroke over it.

Design: shape kinds (filledShape, frame) now apply their own background blur/outer shadows/layer blur, since only they know the box size and flat outset the band needs; placed() keeps text's. The shadow is cast by PenSilhouette(shape, stroke: <band region>) — a Path union — with penDropShadow(outset:) for a box under a point (0x0 frame).

Probes (reacteffects, 2026-09-28): four Pen-exported fixtures, scripts/pen-oracle --scale 2 (pen CLI, sandbox off): render-angular-shapes, render-inner-sides, render-unstroked-lines, render-stroke-bands; added to ReactRenderWebViewTests.gapFixtures with render-sizeless-frames.
Findings (MAE from swift test -j 3 --filter ReactRenderWebViewTests, before any fix):
- (c) Pen does NOT move children for an inner per-side stroke, and draws the stroke under them (layout.json: children at 0,0 / centred in the full box). React's CSS border shifts them: inner-sides col 10.993, row-center 5.560, none 12.863, col-padded 12.486 (CG 0.000). Fix: the overlay route, as centre/outer per-side already use.
- (d) Pen draws nothing for a line with no stroke. React writes currentColor (black): unstroked-lines fill 0.992 on the first probe; the first probe's black board hid the fixed-size case (0.000), so the fixture was regenerated on grey (#808080).
- (e) the brief's "inner shadow must be drawn over the stroke" is inverted: Pen draws it UNDER the stroke (fixture render-shadows-inner-under-stroke; CG renderShape order fills, inner shadows, stroke), and React already does: inner-under-stroke 0.383, outer-and-inner 1.181, inner-ellipse 0.447, all within CG + 1.0. Nothing to fix.
- (f) Pen casts an outer shadow from the shape grown by the stroke's outer reach on ANY box, not only 0x0 (stroke-bands box-outer/box-center/box-inner exports; CG's PenShadowSilhouette says the same). A 0x0 box: centre 8pt stroke = 8x8 square, outer = 16x16, inner = nothing, and no shadow. React: outline is not drawn on a 0x0 box (stroke-bands rect-outer 0.970, sizeless paint 0.329, centre 0.281). Fix: outer stroke as a spread box-shadow (like the centred half already is) and outer shadows spread by the outer reach.
- (b) angular on SVG shapes: 5.1-24.2 (CG 0.03-0.09); svgPaint returns nil for angular.

Probe results (scripts/gen-geometry-probe + pen-oracle --scale 2, pen CLI 0.3.9):
- Stroke (inner/centre/outer, uniform/per-side), shadow, blur, background blur never move any Pen layout rect — flex slot, sibling, fit_content parent, group union, free — unturned, turned 30/90, flipped. layoutIncludeStroke:true changes nothing either (Pen reads it into layout.includeStroke and no layout function reads that field).
- Pen's ctx.bounds = getTransformedLocalBounds = box (0,0,w,h) through translate(x,y)·rotate·flip about the anchor. Flex slot = those bounds (layoutGetOuterBounds).
- Painted extent = Pen's getVisualLocalBounds (box ∪ stroke path ∪ unclipped children, then shadow offset±1.5·blur, blur ±1.5·radius), used for export size, culling, stroke hit-test.
- Woodcase divergences: turned fill_container child (main axis f16, cross axis f20) — rotation expansion skipped after filling. Pen's FIRST layout after load undersizes fit_content parents of turned children whose other axis is unresolved (f20, f21); a relayout converges to Woodcase's numbers.
Finding in progress: project/2026-09-28-geometry-model.md

Finding written: project/2026-09-28-geometry-model.md (worktree geomodel, branch wt/geomodel, uncommitted). Both criteria met in it: e7V (stroke/shadow/blur never enter Pen's layout, unturned and turned, flex/free/group, even with layoutIncludeStroke) and gWe (three-extent model: bounds = PenRect / box+transform / painted extent; keep PenRect bounds-first, add PenPlacement + paintedExtent API; fix turned fill_container on main and cross axis; keep converged layout over Pen's first-pass artefact). New tooling: scripts/gen-geometry-probe, scripts/layout-diff; gotcha on pen-oracle's first-pass layout. Follow-up leaves to file: the two flex fixes, painted-extent API + shot --extent painted, RapidPro paintedBounds -> library, Penumbra quad + stroke-band hit-test.

data.title: The library names three extents: bounds, placement (box + transform) and painted extent
data.description: Ruled by Ben 2026-09-28 (project/2026-09-28-geometry-model.md, 'Proposed model'). Add (ii) PenPlacement: a Friendly value, box (0,0,w,h; a group's is its children's union from its anchor) + PlaneTransform into the parent, returned by one PenLayoutEngine function so readers stop composing unturnedBox + transform by hand; and (iii) paintedExtent(of:rect:layoutRects:) reproducing Pen's getVisualLocalBounds: box ∪ stroke band (alignment, per side, mitred corners) ∪ unclipped children's painted extents through their transforms, then outer shadows' offset copies ±1.5·blur (spread ignored) and layer blur ±1.5·radius, all through the node's transform. PenRect's doc states it is extent (i) and points at the other two; PenEngine.md / PenRendering.md document the three extents and their readers. Add `shot --extent painted` (opt-in; default stays layout rect), and a render-test helper that places Pen's reference by the painted extent (verify on the probe's x1–x4 export sizes: 100x60 + outer 12 + shadow (10,10) blur 8 → 148x108 pt, etc.).

data.text:
jBvokK findings (follow, 2026-09-28). Worktree .claude/worktrees/follow, branch wt/follow, uncommitted.

Cause found, test side: followStopsWhenOrphaned's wait loop checked its 30 s deadline BEFORE looking and never looked after it (the gotcha "Wall-clock assertions" trap; ViewerFixtures.waitUntil and ChildProcess.waitForExit already have the final look, this loop did not). A poll sleep that resumes past the deadline ends the wait without looking, so a follower that exited during that sleep is reported as one that never did.
Evidence: (1) regression PollingWaitTests.looksAfterTheDeadline, written against a PollingWait with the old loop shape: red ("looked 1 time(s) in 1.033 s", satisfied=false), green after adding the one look after the deadline. (2) A temporary trace in a loaded full run (swift test -j 3 --quiet, load 23-28) measured the test's own 20 ms poll sleep resuming after 2.294 s: the test process's continuations queue behind other tests' blocking work (CommandFixture.run polls a child with Thread.sleep on a cooperative thread). A 30 s stall is the same, bigger. Not proven to be the only remaining cause: no failure was caught with the diagnostics in place.

Ruled out / reasoned: pid recorded is the sh launcher (/bin/sh execs, `cmd &` forks once, no double fork); macOS has no subreaper, and ps in the forced-failure check showed PPID 1 after orphaning; stdout is a file, flushed after each page (no pipe, no SIGPIPE); stdin of an async list is /dev/null (no SIGTTIN); Follow iterator and parent watch both return on cancellation, so the task group cannot wait on a stuck child; pid reuse within the 30 s window is implausible. A remaining test-side hole also closed: the launcher gave up silently after 600 x 0.05 s and exited 0, so a follower that never printed (and so maybe never recorded a launcher) looked like a follower that failed to exit; it now waits 1200 iterations and exits 3, which the test reports separately.

Diagnostics kept in: on failure the test records the follower's ps line (pid, ppid, pgid, stat, etime), stderr (was /dev/null), stdout, the head of a 1 s `sample` call graph (with -file, so nothing lands in /tmp), how long since the launcher was seen gone, and the waiter's looks and longest gap. Verified by temporarily SIGSTOPping the follower with a 2 s budget: the message showed PPID 1, STAT T, the stack.

Files: Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/Support/PollingWait.swift, PollingWaitTests.swift, ProcessSnapshot.swift; Tests/WoodcaseCommandTests/Verbs/ActivityCommandTests+Orphan.swift (test moved here; recordRename/followEnvironment now internal). launcher.waitUntilExit() (unbounded) replaced by a bounded poll.

Runs: --filter "ActivityCommandTests|PollingWaitTests" 20/20 pass (load 6-11). Full suite (swift test -j 3 --quiet): run 1 at load 23-28, run 2 (final code) at load 18-40; the orphan test passed both times; the only failures were ReactIconPaintWebViewTests __READY__ timeout (run 1) and PerformanceSetVerbBudgetTests (run 2), both passing re-run alone (1/1 each).

ready for integration: test-side cause fixed (wait loop never looked after its deadline; PollingWait regression red then green), failure diagnostics kept in, 20/20 filter, two loaded full runs with the orphan test green. Not proven to be the only cause; leave the issue open for one more loaded wave if you want certainty.

Read Pen's own computeVisualLocalBounds overrides from /Applications/Pen.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar (grep -a -b for the identifier, dd around the offset). Facts beyond the finding:

- Effect enum: DropShadow=1, LayerBlur=2, BackgroundBlur=3, InnerShadow=4. ME() only counts type 1 (outer drop shadow) and type 2 (layer blur); inner shadows add nothing.
- Every shadow copies the extent as it stood before any shadow (n = e.clone() once), then layer blurs inflate the whole.
- Frame: box ∪ stroke band ∪ (children unless clip) then effects. Group: children only (e.reset(), no own box) then effects. Shapes (rect/ellipse/path/polygon/line): fillPath.bounds (NOT the box) ∪ stroke band, then effects — so a viewBox path that overflows its box counts (viewbox-experiment's 40 px). Text: glyph fill path bounds + effects (no stroke).
- Stroke band (DZt): inside adds nothing; centre/outside build the stroke at width w (centre) or 2w (outside, then clipped). Rectangle/frame: box grown per side by w/2 (centre) or w (outside), top/right/bottom/left, missing side 0. Every other kind: skia makeStroked of the fill path at the TOP width (per-side collapses to top), with the node's join/cap, miter limit default.
- Pen export pixel size = outward pixel-snapped painted extent at the scale (x2: 149.39 pt → 299 px; groups 366.39 → 733).

Plan: PenPlacement (Models), placement(of:rect:layoutRects:) + canvasPlacement(of:in:layoutRects:), paintedExtent(of:rect:layoutRects:) + canvasPaintedExtent(of:in:layoutRects:), PenRect.snappedOutward(toPixelsAt:), shot --extent layout|painted, test helper renderPaintedArtboard. Probe committed as Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/geometry-probe.pen with Pen's free/groups/x1–x4 exports.

Done in worktree .claude/worktrees/swiftshadow (branch wt/swiftshadow), uncommitted, for the integrator.

Both criteria met:
- EwX: SwiftUI casts an outer shadow from PenSilhouette(shape, stroke: band) (Path union) for outside/centre strokes, per side, on 0x0 boxes (penDropShadow outset:), ellipse/polygon/path; inside strokes and lines add nothing (Pen draws a line with no shadow). Regression tests: SwiftUIEmitterStrokeShadowTests (11; 8 red first, 3 guards green on first run), and the render gates below.
- Hm1: SwiftUI MAE before -> after (swift test --filter "PenStrokeShadowSnapshotTests|SwiftUIRenderTests|SwiftUIEmitter", 2x, 2026-09-28): sizeless-frames-paint 0.329 -> 0.006 (limit 1.0 -> 0.51); render-shadows-outer-and-inner 0.600 -> 0.191 (limit 1.23 -> 0.69); new render-stroke-shadows boards 4.4-14.1 -> 0.08-0.16 (rect-outer 8.888->0.089, rect-center 5.182->0.084, round 7.728->0.107, translucent 14.118->0.089, perside-outer 7.348->0.087, perside-center 4.409->0.085, frame-child 8.888->0.089, ellipse 6.567->0.155, polygon 6.352->0.123, path 6.673->0.097); inner/line/inner-under-inner-stroke unchanged (0.116/0.007/0.000/0.001). All held by ceilings (measured + 0.5).

Found: CG casts a line's outer shadow from its stroke; Pen casts none (CG MAE 2.52 line-diagonal, 4.57 line-flat). Not fixed (CG out of scope) - wants its own leaf. Inner shadows: no mirror problem (Pen hides the inner shadow under an inside stroke, as CG and SwiftUI do).

Fix in place (wt/flexturn). New file Sources/Woodcase/PenLayoutEngine+FlexFill.swift holds the filling pass: absorbFill expands the filled (unturned) size through applyRotationExpansion; a new fillCrossAxis gives each cross-axis fill child's unturned box the inner cross size and takes its turned bounds (main and cross), re-fitting the container's own main size if a main extent moved. beginFilling first settles turned cross-fill children against a provisional cross size (the container's, if known up front, else the measured siblings'), so the fill share accounts for their main extent.

Pen probe (settled, not first pass): fixture Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures/layout-turned-fill.pen, 14 rows (h1-h8 horizontal, v1-v4 vertical, e1/e2 fit_content-both rows with cross fill). New scripts/pen-settle <pen> --out <dir> writes Pen's first and settled (gap-nudged) layouts. layout-diff settled vs woodcase tree --json: before 33/58 differ, after 0/58. Geometry probe (scripts/gen-geometry-probe) vs w2er6i's pen-oracle first pass: before 10/156, after 2/156 (f20, f21 row widths, the kept first-pass artefact); vs pen-settle's settled layout: 0/156.

Finding beyond the brief: the first-pass artefact also hits a turned MAIN-axis fill in a VERTICAL column (v1: column width 80 first pass, 161.96 settled; v2: 80 -> 200) — same cause (widths fitted before heights), and also a cross fill in a fit_content-both row (e1 160 -> 200, e2 211.96 -> 231.96). Pen's settled rule for e1/e2: a cross-axis fill contributes nothing to its row's cross fit, fills the inner cross size its siblings set, and its turned bounds count in the main fit (overflowing the row's height).

data.title: React and SwiftUI give a turned fill_container child its turned slot
data.description: From YrLTHN (flexturn, 2026-09-28). The layout engine now gives a turned fill_container child its unturned box filled and its turned bounds as its slot (f16/f20, flex-turned-fill.pen). The emitters don't: SwiftUI frames only fixed-size turned nodes to their turned box (rotatedFrame in SwiftUINodeEmitter+Transform.swift), and React's new turned-slot margins (ReactEmitter+TurnedSlot.swift, Mu4JsL) apply only to fixed width and height. So a turned fill child still gets an unturned slot in both. Needs a Pen-oracle render fixture of turned fill children (flex-turned-fill.pen is layout-only; render references must come from Pen's SETTLED layout — see scripts/pen-settle and the 2026-09-28 gotcha) and a fix in each emitter, or a documented CSS/SwiftUI limit with a warning.

Both fixes implemented and green on targeted filters; full suite running.

1. CG: `PenShadowSilhouette.draw`'s `.line` case drew the line's stroke into the shadow
   silhouette's ink layer, so a line cast an outer shadow from its stroke where Pen casts
   none. Changed the `.line` case to a no-op (`break`), matching the rule
   `PenRenderer+GroupSilhouette.castsIntoGroup` already applies to a line inside a group.
   Removed the now-dead `PenShadowSilhouette.Ink` helper (its only caller was the removed
   stroke draw).
   - `render-stroke-shadows-line-diagonal` @2x MAE: 2.520 → 0.0056
   - `render-stroke-shadows-line-flat` @2x MAE: 4.569 → 0.0

     suite's own rule).

2. SwiftUI: `penDropShadow`'s silhouette fill used the default (nonzero) fill rule, so an

   filled-disc shadow instead of a ring one. A *stroked* even-odd shape was already correct

**Rounding rule.** Pen's PNG export of a painted extent keeps the extent's own —
possibly fractional — corner and rounds only the pixel *size* up
(`ceil(extent × scale)`); this was already established and implemented in the library
(`PenRect.grownToWholePixels(at:)`, leaf Wkr2Pd) but never wired into `shot`.
`ShotCommand+Pipeline.swift`'s `render` now grows the region to whole pixels when
`--extent painted` and no `--crop`, and `ShotRegionRenderer.image` rounds instead of
truncating its own pixel-size math (a second, independent source of the 298-vs-299 bug:
even a pre-grown region loses a pixel to floating-point noise under truncation).
`ShotCommandTests` pins six boards from `geometry-probe.pen` against `pen-oracle`'s real
2x exports (previously red: 298x269 vs Pen's 299x270 on x2).

**ShotCommand split.** `ShotCommand.swift` (was ~450 lines) → `ShotCommand.swift` (292,
the CLI surface: doc, options, validate, run) + `ShotCommand+Request.swift` (46) +
`ShotCommand+Pipeline.swift` (128, the render pipeline) + `ShotCommand+Scale.swift` (19).
Purely mechanical; `Request`/`render`/`buildAttributedString` widened from `private` to
internal where a different file now calls them.

**Scope addition (integrator message mid-task):** RapidPro reported Woodcase's
`paintedExtent` bounds text by its box where Pen may count glyph ink. Confirmed from
Pen's own JS (`app.asar`'s text class overrides `computeVisualLocalBounds` to return its
Skia fill path's *tight bounds*, not the box) and from three new `pen-oracle` exports
(x5 unbreakable-word overflow, x6 italic overhang, x7 paragraph wrap overflow — all
added to `scripts/gen-geometry-probe`/`geometry-probe.pen`, Inter, per the brief). Fixed:
`PenLayoutEngine.textInkBounds(of:box:)` (new file) lays out the same lines
`PenTextRenderer` draws and unions each line's Core Text image bounds; wired into
`ownInk`'s `fillBounds` for `.text`. MAE against Pen's real exports dropped from
15.6/22.1/20.0 (box) to 3.4/6.9/8.6 (ink) — order-of-magnitude improvement, not exact:
Core Text and Pen's Skia disagree on Inter's glyph metrics at these sizes even with
optical sizing off (the same gap `PenTextOpticalSizeTests` already measures elsewhere,
~3-9pt at 32-56pt). A dedicated tolerant test (`textExtentApproachesPensExport`, 20px)
replaces the exact-pixel one x1-x4 get, since cross-engine text metrics were never going

data.title: BoundedWait's deadline cannot fire while the cooperative pool is saturated
data.description: SwiftUIRenderBatchRunAsyncTests fails in full-suite runs (17:11 and 18:3x on 2026-09-28), passes alone: `sleep 20` under a 1 s deadline came back `.exited(status: 0, elapsed: 74 s)`. data.title: SwiftUI instances are calls: a component's fixed root size is its ideal size, and variant refs call the merged view
data.description: Ben, 2026-09-28: most instances in woodcase-app's SwiftUI export are inlined copies (30 copies vs 10 calls), mostly because an instance's root size override (fill_container on a fixed-width component) inlines (project/2026-09-26-swiftui-components.md choice 5). Ruling: a component's fixed root size becomes its ideal size — `.frame(idealWidth: 354, maxWidth: .infinity)` style — so the parent sizes it; a call site states a fixed instance size with `.frame(width:)`; previews/catalog show the component at its own size. Also route a ref to a state variant (`TabBar:home`) to the merged view's call (`TabBar(selected: .home)`), which needs the size change. PencilListItem's unmapped overrides (image prop typed Color, icon/score) are out of scope.

data.title: Props carry icons, root fills, recolored text and image types read from instances
data.description:
Ben, 2026-09-28: after the ideal-size change (RNSV2z), woodcase-app's 10 remaining SwiftUI copies are overrides no prop can carry, mostly for the system's reasons, not the file's (project/2026-09-28-swiftui-instance-calls.md, cause 3). Widen what a prop carries, in the shared analyzer (ComponentAnalyzer, PropType, PropMapper, InstanceOverrides) so React gets the same props:
1. An icon prop kind: an icon node's glyph (`icon`, and `iconFontName` on older icon_font nodes), with its color carried alongside (woodcase-app PencilListItem's star/heart, M71FY).
2. A prop that targets the component's root (today an empty `_props` path names nothing): the root's fill (the red Delete ActionButton, the status bars' page fill).
3. A text prop whose instances also recolor the text: carry the color beside the content, or a second color prop on the same node (PencilListItem's gray "Med" score, P90YD). Decide which; a designer-drawn state is the alternative.
4. An image prop's type read from what the instances pass, not only the component's own fill (PencilListItem's image prop is typed Color because its thumbnail's own fill is a color).
Evidence of frequency: tally of override keys across 185 .pen files (fixtures, ~/Local/Pen, Penumbra samples).

data.title: serve should ride through a file deleted and recreated, and through missing artboards and nodes, without page errors
data.description:
Human feedback from Ben, 2026-09-30, while watching an agent design in c41x:

> Sometimes the agent deletes the file and recreates it completely, which leads to JSON errors in the Woodcase dashboard. `woodcase serve` should handle things like missing nodes, artboards and files seamlessly, as this churn is a normal part of agentic design.

Context: c41x's design build (`design/build/rebuild.sh`) runs `rm -f design/directions.pen` → `woodcase new` → `woodcase js …`. A subagent was running that rebuild in a loop while the dashboard watched the file with `woodcase serve <file> --port 7333` (woodcase 0.1.2, .pen 2.19). While the file was missing, empty, or half-built, the page showed JSON errors instead of riding through the churn. The serve process itself stayed up, and its stdout showed no errors.

Expected behavior:
- A watched file that vanishes is a transient state, not an error. Keep showing the last good render, perhaps with a quiet "waiting for file" mark, and pick the file up again when it reappears. Re-arm the watch on the path, not on the old inode, since `rm` followed by a create gives a new inode.
- A file that reads as truncated or invalid JSON mid-write should keep the last good state and retry on the next change. It should never push a parse error to the page.
- Artboards and nodes that disappear or are renamed should drop out, or be replaced, without client-side errors. A page holding a stale artboard id should fall back cleanly.
- Debounce bursts of changes, such as a whole rebuild, into a single render of the settled file.

data.text: Second symptom, 2026-09-30: after the agent finished its rebuild loop, the dashboard showed only 2 of the file's 12 artboards (the two R1-L-A boards, which the last rebuild had written last), and it stayed that way. The file on disk held all 12. The serve log showed no errors. Restarting woodcase serve showed all 12. So serve can get stuck on a partial snapshot taken mid-rebuild, not only show JSON errors while one is running.

data.title: PDF export writes a zero MediaBox, so Preview shows every page blank
data.description:
Found 2026-10-03 from c41x (its spec sheets, design/renders/specs/*.pdf, rendered by `woodcase render --format pdf`, woodcase 0.1.2 / .pen 2.19, macOS 27).

Symptom: Preview (and any Core Graphics / PDFKit reader) shows the exported PDF as an empty, unsized page. poppler (pdftoppm, pdftotext) renders it in full, because it falls back to Letter for a zero box, which is why the export looked fine in non-Apple checks.

Cause: the page tree carries `/MediaBox [0 0 0 0]` and the page object carries no MediaBox of its own, so every page inherits a zero box:
  2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /MediaBox [0 0 0 0] /Count 1 /Kids [ 1 0 R ] >>
  1 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /Resources 3 0 R /Contents 4 0 R >>
Core Graphics reads page 1's mediaBox and cropBox as (0, 0, 0, 0).

Where: Sources/Woodcase/Rendering/PDFExporter.swift:78-87. The context is created with `var mediaBox = CGRect.zero` (written onto the Pages node), and each page calls `context.beginPage(mediaBox: &pageBox)`, which on this macOS does not write a per-page /MediaBox. The comment above it records an earlier attempt: a bridged CGRect in the beginPDFPage dictionary was ignored.

Proposed fix: (1) create the context with the first page's box as the initial mediaBox, so the page tree has a real default; (2) set each page's own box through `context.beginPDFPage([kCGPDFContextMediaBox: Data(bytes: &pageBox, count: MemoryLayout<CGRect>.size) as CFData] as CFDictionary)`: the key's value must be CFData wrapping the CGRect, which is likely why the bridged CGRect was ignored. (3) Regression test: export a 612 x 792 page (and a two-page document of two sizes), reopen it with CGPDFDocument and assert each page's getBoxRect(.mediaBox) equals its size.

Repro: any .pen with a 612 x 792 frame, `woodcase render x.pen --format pdf`, then `open x.pdf` (blank), or a Swift script: CGPDFDocument(url)!.page(at: 1)!.getBoxRect(.mediaBox) == .zero.

data.text:
2026-10-03: fixed on main by d23c0ff (per-page `context.beginPage(mediaBox:)`); the c41x export was made with the Homebrew 0.1.2 build, tagged at 8cebb0a, one commit before that fix.

Evidence: `woodcase render c41x-technical-report.pen --format pdf` (5 pages, 612x792). 0.1.2: CGPDFDocument reads every page's mediaBox as (0,0,0,0), and pdftoppm draws pages 2-5 blank. main (.build/release): every page reads (0,0,612,792) and all five draw. PDFExporterTests already asserts per-page boxes.

Residue: the page tree still carries the context's initial `/MediaBox [0 0 0 0]`. Readers use the per-page box, but a reader that trusts the inherited default would see a zero page. Tidy it in the 2.20 / 0.1.3 work: create the context with the first page's box. Ships to Homebrew as 0.1.3.
